import type { ComponentProps, MouseEvent, ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Icon, type IconName } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Alert.module.css'

export interface AlertProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'div'>, 'title'> {
  variant?: 'info' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger'
  appearance?: 'subtle' | 'outlined' | 'solid'
  title?: ReactNode
  /** Replaces the variant's icon; `false` shows none. */
  icon?: ReactNode | false
  /** Buttons or links under the message, e.g. "Retry". */
  action?: ReactNode
  /** Shows a close button that calls this. The alert does not hide itself: remove it when this fires. */
  onClose?: (event: MouseEvent<HTMLButtonElement>) => void
  /** Accessible name of the close button. */
  closeLabel?: string
  /**
   * Announce the alert when it appears. `danger` and `warning` interrupt
   * (`role="alert"`), the others wait their turn (`role="status"`). Leave it
   * off for an alert that is on the page from the start.
   */
  isLive?: boolean
}

const icons: Record<NonNullable<AlertProps['variant']>, IconName> = {
  info: 'info-filled',
  success: 'success-filled',
  warning: 'warning-filled',
  danger: 'danger-filled',
}

export function Alert({
  variant = 'info',
  appearance = 'subtle',
  title,
  icon,
  action,
  onClose,
  closeLabel = 'Dismiss',
  isLive = false,
  className,
  children,
  ...props
}: AlertProps) {
  const urgent = variant === 'danger' || variant === 'warning'
  return (
    <div
      role={isLive ? (urgent ? 'alert' : 'status') : undefined}
      className={cn(styles.alert, styles[variant], styles[appearance], className)}
      {...props}
    >
      {icon !== false && (
        <span className={styles.icon} aria-hidden="true">
          {icon ?? <Icon name={icons[variant]} />}
        </span>
      )}
      <div className={styles.body}>
        {title && <div className={styles.title}>{title}</div>}
        {children && <div className={styles.description}>{children}</div>}
        {action && <div className={styles.action}>{action}</div>}
      </div>
      {onClose && (
        <button type="button" aria-label={closeLabel} className={styles.close} onClick={onClose}>
          <Icon name="close" />
        </button>
      )}
    </div>
  )
}

# Alert A message about a page or a section that stays until the situation changes or the ...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import * as AlertStories from './Alert.stories'

<Meta of={AlertStories} />

# Alert

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A message about a page or a section that stays until the situation changes
or the reader dismisses it: something went wrong, needs attention, or worked.

<Status of={AlertStories} />

<Canvas of={AlertStories.WithAction} />

## Variants

`variant` is the colour, by meaning; `appearance` is the emphasis. Any
variant takes any appearance.

<Canvas of={AlertStories.Variants} />

| Variant | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `info` | Something worth knowing that changes nothing: a plan change, scheduled maintenance. |
| `success` | Something finished and stays true: a domain verified, an import done. |
| `warning` | Something that will go wrong if nobody acts: a card expiring, a quota nearly used. |
| `danger` | Something that went wrong and needs a next step: a failed upload, a lost connection. |

<Canvas of={AlertStories.Appearances} />

| Appearance | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `subtle` | The default. Sits on the page without shouting. |
| `outlined` | On a tinted or busy background, where a tint would disappear. |
| `solid` | The one message nobody should miss, such as an outage banner. Rarely more than one per page. |

<Canvas of={AlertStories.Dismissible} />

<Canvas of={AlertStories.WithoutIcon} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Alert } from 'zweihander/alert'
```

npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/alert.json
```

- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/alert](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/alert)
- Behaviour: a plain element, no Base UI part
- Figma: not in the library yet

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={AlertStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={AlertStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

Only the description is required. The icon is one line of body text tall,
so it sits on the title's line.

## Measurements

One size. The text is body text, so an alert sits in running content
without a jump in size.

<SpecTable
  caption="Every alert"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Padding, from the outer edge', token: '--space-group' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-lg' },

    { part: 'Title and description', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body' },
    { part: 'Title and description', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body' },
    { part: 'Title and description', property: 'Gap', token: '--space-inline' },
    { part: 'Action', property: 'Space above, and between actions', token: '--space-inline' },
    { part: 'Close button', property: 'Size', token: '--box-sm' },
    { part: 'Close button', property: 'Icon size', token: '--icon-md' },
    { part: 'Close button', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-sm' },
    { part: 'Close button', property: 'Minimum hit area on touch screens', token: '--target-coarse' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Width', token: '--focus-width' },

  ]}
/>

The border is always there, 1px and transparent unless `outlined`, so
switching appearance never moves the content. The padding counts that
pixel: the content sits 16px from the alert's edge. The close button is 24px,
flush with the padding and top-aligned with the icon. No shadow: an alert is
part of the page.

## Color

Each variant reads four tokens, the same four as a Tag of that variant, so
the two always agree. Subtle and outlined keep the description in
`--color-text`: a paragraph in the variant's colour is tiring to read, so
the colour goes on the icon, the title and the close button.

## States

The alert itself has no states. Its close button does.

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Close hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Close focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={AlertStories.Dismissible} />
</States>

- **Hover** tints the close button with 15% of the alert's own text
  colour, so it reads on every variant and appearance.
- **Focus** is a 2px `--color-border-focused` outline, inside the button's edge.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={AlertStories} />
</div>

Every other `<div>` attribute passes through, including `ref`.

### Differences from the spec

- **Sized after Atlassian's section message**: 16px padding, 16px from
  the icon to the text, 8px between title, description and actions, 8px
  corners, no shadow, a semibold 14/20 title, a 24px close button.

- **Placed in the content, not at the top of the screen.** The spec
  describes a prominent message at the top; here an alert goes where the
  thing it is about is. An outage banner is a `solid` alert placed at the
  top by the page.
- **Closing is the parent's job.** `onClose` reports the click and the
  alert stays until whoever rendered it removes it, so "dismissed" lives in
  your state and can be remembered across visits.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use an Alert for a message about a page or a section that should stay put
until it is dealt with: a failed save, a card about to expire, an import
that finished. The title says what happened; the description says what it
means and what to do.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={AlertStories.DoSayWhatHappened} />}
  doCaption="Say what happened and offer the next step."
  dont={<Story of={AlertStories.DontVague} />}
  dontCaption="“Something went wrong” leaves the red box to do the talking, and the reader with nothing to do."
/>

The icon is decorative, so the variant has to be clear from the words too:
"Upload failed", not just a red box.

## When not to use

- **For news about something that just happened and needs nothing more.**
  Use a [Toast](?path=/docs/components-notifications-toast--docs): it goes
  away by itself.
- **For a one-line message under a form or a group of fields.** Use an
  [Inline Alert](?path=/docs/components-notifications-inlinealert--docs).
- **For an error on one field.** Use the field's own `validationState` and
  `helperText`, tied to it with `aria-describedby`.
- **For a decision the reader must make before going on.** Use a Modal.

## Accessibility

- A plain `<div>` by default: an alert on the page when it loads is read in
  order, like the text around it, and does not interrupt.
- An alert that **appears** in response to something (a failed save) needs
  `isLive`. `danger` and `warning` become `role="alert"` and are read at
  once; `info` and `success` become `role="status"` and wait for the screen
  reader to finish.

  <Canvas of={AlertStories.Live} />

- The icon is `aria-hidden`: the words carry the meaning.
- The close button is a native `<button>` named `Dismiss` (change it with
  `closeLabel`). Tab reaches it, Enter and Space press it.
- Focus ring: 2px `--color-border-focused` on the close button. On touch screens its hit
  area grows to 44×44px without the button growing.
- Every variant and appearance passes the story tests' contrast check
  (light mode).

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

'use client'

import { useState, type ComponentProps } from 'react'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import type { AccentColor } from '@/theme/palettes'
import { Tooltip, TooltipGroup } from '../overlays/Tooltip'
import { Badge, type BadgeProps } from './Badge'
import styles from './Avatar.module.css'

type AvatarStatus = 'online' | 'away' | 'busy' | 'offline'

// Badge's presence colours, so a dot on an avatar and a dot beside a name match.
const STATUS: Record<AvatarStatus, { variant: BadgeProps['variant']; label: string }> = {
  online: { variant: 'success', label: 'Online' },
  away: { variant: 'warning', label: 'Away' },
  busy: { variant: 'destructive', label: 'Busy' },
  offline: { variant: 'secondary', label: 'Offline' },
}

export interface AvatarProps extends ComponentProps<'span'> {
  /** 16, 24, 32, 40, 96 or 128px across: Atlassian's avatar sizes. */
  size?: 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl' | '2xl'
  imageSrc?: string
  /** Who this is. Without it the avatar is decorative and hidden from assistive tech. */
  imageAlt?: string
  /** Shown when there is no image, or it fails to load. One or two letters; `xs` has room for the first only. */
  initials?: string
  /** Any accent hue. Unset is the neutral gray. */
  color?: AccentColor
  /** `subtle` is a tint of the hue; `solid` is its 600 step (400 in dark). */
  variant?: 'subtle' | 'solid'
  /** A presence dot at the bottom-end corner. Joins the name as ", Online" when there is `imageAlt`. */
  status?: AvatarStatus
  /** The status word in the name, for another language. Defaults to Online, Away, Busy or Offline. */
  statusLabel?: string
}

export function Avatar({
  size = 'md',
  imageSrc,
  imageAlt,
  initials,
  color,
  variant = 'subtle',
  status,
  statusLabel = status && STATUS[status].label,
  className,
  ...props
}: AvatarProps) {
  // Keyed by src, so a new imageSrc gets a fresh attempt instead of staying
  // on the fallback from the last one that failed.
  const [failedSrc, setFailedSrc] = useState<string>()
  // An empty string is no image, not a request for the page's own URL.
  const showImage = !!imageSrc && failedSrc !== imageSrc
  // 16px holds one letter at the smallest type size. A count ("+3", "9+")
  // stays whole: half of it would be a different number.
  const letters = size === 'xs' && initials && !initials.includes('+') ? Array.from(initials)[0] : initials

  return (
    <span
      // The label lives on the container so the image, the initials and the silhouette
      // all announce the same thing: the person, not "S R" or nothing.
      role={imageAlt ? 'img' : undefined}
      // Children of role="img" are not read, so the status joins the name.
      aria-label={imageAlt && status ? `${imageAlt}, ${statusLabel}` : imageAlt}
      aria-hidden={imageAlt ? undefined : true}
      // The Theme's own palette switch: on the avatar it remaps --color-background-brand-bold and
      // its tints to this hue, already measured for contrast.
      data-accent={color}
      // A CSS class cannot start with a digit.
      className={cn(styles.avatar, styles[size === '2xl' ? 'xxl' : size], styles[variant], status && styles.hasStatus, className)}
      {...props}
    >
      {showImage ? (
        <img
          src={imageSrc}
          alt=""
          className={styles.image}
          onError={() => setFailedSrc(imageSrc)}
        />
      ) : letters ? (
        <span className={styles.initials}>{letters}</span>
      ) : (
        <Icon name="user" className={styles.silhouette} />
      )}
      {status && (
        <Badge
          isDot
          variant={STATUS[status].variant}
          // 8px from sm to lg, as Figma; xl and 2xl size it in CSS, xs hides it.
          size="md"
          className={styles.status}
        />
      )}
    </span>
  )
}

export interface AvatarGroupProps extends ComponentProps<'span'> {
  /** The people, in order. Each takes Avatar's props; the group's `size` wins. */
  avatars: AvatarProps[]
  /** The most circles in the row, the "+n" included. Unset shows everyone. */
  max?: number
  size?: AvatarProps['size']
  /** The name of the "+n" avatar, for another language. Used only when the avatars are named. */
  moreLabel?: (count: number) => string
  /** Each named avatar shows its name on hover, and the "+n" lists the people it stands for, on hover or focus. */
  hasTooltips?: boolean
}

/** Avatars overlapping in a row, with a "+n" for the ones past `max`. */
export function AvatarGroup({
  avatars,
  max,
  size = 'md',
  moreLabel = (count) => `${count} more`,
  hasTooltips = false,
  className,
  ...props
}: AvatarGroupProps) {
  // The "+n" takes the last slot, so it always stands for two or more: never "+1"
  // where the person would have fitted.
  const shown = max !== undefined && avatars.length > max ? avatars.slice(0, Math.max(max - 1, 0)) : avatars
  const hidden = avatars.length - shown.length
  // Named avatars get a named "+n"; decorative ones (the names are printed) a decorative one.
  const isNamed = avatars.some((a) => a.imageAlt)

  // With tooltips, the "+n" lists who it stands for, and takes focus so
  // that list can be read by keyboard too.
  const hiddenNames = hasTooltips
    ? avatars
        .slice(shown.length)
        .map((a) => a.imageAlt)
        .filter(Boolean)
        .join(', ')
    : ''
  const more = hidden > 0 && (
    // A 16px circle holds two characters, so past nine the xs count reads "9+".
    // ponytail: larger sizes are not capped; an sm circle outgrows +99.
    <Avatar
      size={size}
      initials={size === 'xs' && hidden > 9 ? '9+' : `+${hidden}`}
      imageAlt={isNamed ? moreLabel(hidden) : undefined}
      tabIndex={hiddenNames ? 0 : undefined}
    />
  )

  const group = (
    <span className={cn(styles.group, className)} {...props}>
      {shown.map((avatar, i) => {
        const el = <Avatar {...avatar} size={size} style={{ zIndex: shown.length - i, ...avatar.style }} />
        return hasTooltips && avatar.imageAlt ? (
          <Tooltip key={i} content={avatar.imageAlt}>
            {el}
          </Tooltip>
        ) : (
          <Avatar key={i} {...avatar} size={size} style={{ zIndex: shown.length - i, ...avatar.style }} />
        )
      })}
      {more && hiddenNames ? <Tooltip content={hiddenNames}>{more}</Tooltip> : more}
    </span>
  )
  // One shared delay: once a name shows, the next shows as the pointer moves on.
  return hasTooltips ? <TooltipGroup>{group}</TooltipGroup> : group
}

# Avatar A picture of a person or account, with initials or a silhouette when there is no ...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import { Avatar, AvatarGroup } from './Avatar'
import * as AvatarStories from './Avatar.stories'

<Meta of={AvatarStories} />

# Avatar

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A picture of a person or account, with initials or a silhouette when there
is no picture, an optional presence dot, and a group that overlaps several.

<Status of={AvatarStories} />

<Canvas of={AvatarStories.Fallbacks} />

## Variants

Neutral by default. `color` picks any accent hue, and `variant` how strong
it is. Behind a photo the colour only shows while it loads or where the
image is transparent.

<Canvas of={AvatarStories.Colors} />

| Variant | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| <Avatar initials="SR" /> `subtle` | Most places: lists, comments, a byline. A tint that sits quietly next to text. |
| <Avatar initials="SR" variant="solid" /> `solid` | Where the avatar has to stand out on its own: a header, an account menu trigger. |

Colour tells people apart in a list; it carries no meaning. Pick it from the
person (a hash of their id), never from a status.

### Sizes

Atlassian's six. `md` is the default.

<Canvas of={AvatarStories.Sizes} />

| `size` | Across | Use for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `xs` | 16px | Inline with a line of small text: a mention, a dense table cell. One initial. |
| `sm` | 24px | Beside a name in a row, a field or a table cell. |
| `md` | 32px | The default: a comment, a feed event, the account button in a top bar. |
| `lg` | 40px | The leading visual of a list row or a card. |
| `xl` | 96px | A profile header. |
| `2xl` | 128px | A profile page, or the picture being edited. |

With initials, `xs` shows the first letter only: two do not fit in 16px.

<Canvas of={AvatarStories.InitialsSizes} />

### Status

`status` puts a presence dot on the bottom-end corner, in Badge's presence
colours: online, away, busy, offline.

<Canvas of={AvatarStories.Status} />

The dot grows with the avatar, and at `xl` and `2xl` it sits on the curve:

<Canvas of={AvatarStories.StatusSizes} />

### Group

`AvatarGroup` overlaps a row of avatars, for the people on a record or a
thread. `max` is the most circles in the row, the "+n" included.

<Canvas of={AvatarStories.Group} />

With `hasTooltips`, each named avatar shows its name on hover, and the
"+n" lists the people it stands for, on hover or keyboard focus:

<Canvas of={AvatarStories.GroupTooltips} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Avatar, AvatarGroup } from 'zweihander/avatar'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/avatar.json
```

- Source: [src/components/atomic-elements/Avatar.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/atomic-elements/Avatar.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/avatar](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/avatar)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={AvatarStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={AvatarStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

One avatar shows one of image, initials or silhouette, in that order of
preference. A broken image falls back to the next. The status dot and the
group are optional.

## Measurements

The circle ignores the Theme's radius preset: a circle is the shape, not a
corner setting.

<SpecTable
  caption="xs"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Size', token: '--avatar-xs' },
    { part: 'Initials', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body-sm' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="sm"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Size', token: '--avatar-sm' },
    { part: 'Initials', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body-sm' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="md"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Size', token: '--avatar-md' },
    { part: 'Initials', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body-sm' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="lg"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Size', token: '--avatar-lg' },
    { part: 'Initials', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="xl"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Size', token: '--avatar-xl' },
    { part: 'Initials', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-heading-xl' },
    { part: 'Status dot', property: 'Size', token: '--box-2xs' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="2xl"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Size', token: '--avatar-2xl' },
    { part: 'Initials', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-heading-2xl' },
    { part: 'Status dot', property: 'Size', token: '--box-xs' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable caption="Every size" rows={[{ part: 'Container', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-pill' }]} />

The image fills the circle edge to edge. The silhouette is the kit's
`user` icon at 60% of the circle, centred.

Initials are 12px up to `md`, where `xs` keeps only the first letter, 14px
on `lg`, then 28px and 32px: the type scale stops at 32px, so on `xl` and
`2xl` the letters are a smaller share of the circle. They are medium (500)
up to `lg` and semibold (600) on `xl` and `2xl`, Figma's Heading/xl and
Heading/2xl.

An `xs` avatar draws no status dot, as in Atlassian: at 16px the dot would
cover most of the picture, so the status is in the accessible name only.
The status dot is an 8px Badge dot (`md`) on the sm, md and lg avatars,
flush on the corner of the avatar's box, outside the curve. On `xl` and `2xl` that corner is far off the circle and a Badge dot
is a speck, so the dot is 16px and 20px, and its centre sits on the circle
at 45°.

<SpecTable
  caption="Status dot and group"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Status dot', property: 'Ring', token: '--color-surface' },
    { part: 'Group', property: 'Ring around each avatar', token: '--color-surface' },
    { part: 'Group', property: 'Overlap, every size but sm', token: '--space-1' },
  ]}
/>

The ring is 2px at every size, as on a floating Badge. The overlap is
Atlassian's: 4px, and none at `sm`, where the 24px circles only touch.

## Color

`color` sets the Theme's own `data-accent` on the avatar, so a hue avatar
reads the accent tokens of that hue: switch the accent in the toolbar to see
the values for another one.

<SpecTable
  caption="subtle, neutral"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Background', token: '--color-background-neutral' },
    { part: 'Initials', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text' },
    { part: 'Silhouette', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-subtlest' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="subtle, with a hue"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Background', token: '--color-background-brand-subtlest' },
    { part: 'Initials and silhouette', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-brand-bold' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="solid, neutral"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Background', token: '--color-background-neutral-bold' },
    { part: 'Initials and silhouette', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-inverse' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="solid, with a hue"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Background', token: '--color-background-brand-bold' },
    { part: 'Initials and silhouette', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-brand-inverse' },
  ]}
/>

The status dot takes Badge's presence colours: online `success`, away
`warning`, busy `destructive`, offline `secondary`. The "+n" in a group is a
neutral subtle avatar.

## States

An avatar is not interactive: no hover, focus or pressed. Its states are
which part it can show.

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Image', content: <Avatar size="lg" imageSrc={AvatarStories.default.args.imageSrc} imageAlt="Mary Thompson" /> },
    { label: 'Initials', content: <Avatar size="lg" initials="SR" imageAlt="Sam Rivera" /> },
    { label: 'Silhouette', content: <Avatar size="lg" imageAlt="Unknown user" /> },
    { label: 'Broken image', content: <Story of={AvatarStories.BrokenImage} /> },
    { label: 'Online', content: <Avatar size="lg" initials="SR" imageAlt="Sam Rivera" status="online" /> },
    { label: 'Offline', content: <Avatar size="lg" initials="SR" imageAlt="Sam Rivera" status="offline" /> },
  ]}
/>

- **Image** shows while `imageSrc` loads and after.
- **Broken image** drops the `<img>` and shows the initials, or the
  silhouette when there are none, instead of the browser's broken-image
  icon. A new `imageSrc` is tried again. An empty `imageSrc` is no image.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={AvatarStories} />
</div>

Every other `<span>` attribute passes through to the container, including
`ref`.

### AvatarGroup

<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={AvatarGroup} />
</div>

Every other `<span>` attribute passes through to the row.

### Differences from the spec

- **`initials` is added.** The spec's Anatomy has an Initials part but
  its prop list has no way to set them. Pass the letters, not a name:
  how to abbreviate a name depends on the language, and the kit should
  not guess.
- **A broken image falls back** to initials or the silhouette instead
  of showing the browser's broken-image icon.
- **Sizes follow Atlassian Design**: 16, 24, 32, 40, 96 and
  128px, with `md` (32px) the default, so an avatar lines up with the
  kit's 32px controls. There is no 48px.
- **`xs` shows one initial.** Two letters do not fit in 16px at the
  smallest type size.
- **No square, no `appearance`.** Always a circle, so a person never
  reads as a product or workspace logo.
- **The placeholder is the kit's `user` icon** at 60% of the circle,
  centred, as in Figma. It takes `color` and `variant` like initials do.
- **`color` and `variant` are added**, to tell people apart in a list.
- **The circle ignores the radius preset.**
- **`status` and `AvatarGroup` are added.** The status words and the
  "+n" name are English by default; `statusLabel` and `moreLabel` translate
  them.
- **`max` counts the "+n".** The row never grows past `max` circles, and
  the "+n" always stands for two or more: never "+1" where the person
  would have fitted.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use an Avatar to show who: the author of a comment, the people on a
project, the account that is signed in. Give it `imageAlt` when the avatar
is the only thing that says who it is. When the name is printed next to
it, leave `imageAlt` out: the avatar is decorative, and the name is read
once.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={AvatarStories.DoDecorativeBesideName} />}
  doCaption="The name is printed, so the avatar has no imageAlt. A screen reader hears “Mary Thompson” once."
  dont={<Story of={AvatarStories.DontRepeatName} />}
  dontCaption="imageAlt repeats the printed name: “Mary Thompson, image, Mary Thompson”."
/>

## When not to use

- **For a product, team or workspace logo.** An Avatar is always round, so
  it reads as a person. Use an image with its own shape.
- **For status through colour.** The avatar's `color` means nothing. Use
  `status` for presence, and print the status where people act on it (an
  assignee picker): a dot is a glance, not the only cue.
- **For a long list of people.** A group shows who at a glance; past a
  handful, show the count or a list of names instead.
- **For an icon in a circle.** Use the icon itself, or an icon-only
  [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs) when it acts.

## Accessibility

- `imageAlt` names the **whole avatar** (`role="img"`), not just the
  image, so the image, the initials and the silhouette all announce the
  same person. The inner `<img>` has `alt=""`.
- Without `imageAlt` the avatar is **decorative** and hidden
  (`aria-hidden`), its status dot with it.
- With `status`, the status **joins the name**: "Mary Thompson, Online".
  The dot itself is not read.
- In a group, the "+n" is named "3 more" when the avatars are named, and
  decorative when they are not.
- With `hasTooltips`, the "+n" is the one avatar that takes focus, with
  the focus ring, and its tooltip of hidden names is its description. The
  other avatars' tooltips open on hover only: their names are already
  their accessible names.
- Initials are never read out: with `imageAlt` the avatar's name replaces
  them, without it the avatar is hidden. They are uppercased with CSS, so
  the text keeps the letters as passed.
- Initials meet 4.5:1 in every colour and variant, on every gray ramp in
  both modes, measured by the `Contrast` story. Neutral solid is gray 600
  under gray 50, 6.5:1 or more.
- The silhouette uses the initials colour (neutral subtle uses
  `--color-text-subtlest`), past the 3:1 a graphic needs in every colour
  and variant, measured by the `Contrast` story.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

import type { ComponentProps, ReactNode } from 'react'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Badge.module.css'

export interface BadgeProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'span'>, 'children'> {
  count?: number
  variant?: 'primary' | 'accent' | 'secondary' | 'destructive' | 'success' | 'warning'
  /**
   * Size of a dot: 8px (`md`) or 6px (`sm`). A count is 16px tall at either.
   * `sm` on a count is deprecated: it renders the `md` badge. In the next
   * release `sm` is for dots only.
   */
  size?: 'sm' | 'md'
  /** A dot with no number: "something new", not "how many". */
  isDot?: boolean
  /** Counts above this show as `maxCount+`. */
  maxCount?: number
  /** Pins the badge to a corner of `children` instead of sitting inline. */
  isFloating?: boolean
  floatingPlacement?: 'top-start' | 'top-end' | 'bottom-start' | 'bottom-end'
  /** The element a floating badge is pinned to. */
  children?: ReactNode
}

let hasWarned = false

export function Badge({
  count,
  variant = 'primary',
  size = 'md',
  isDot = false,
  maxCount,
  isFloating = false,
  floatingPlacement = 'top-end',
  children,
  className,
  ...props
}: BadgeProps) {
  const hasBadge = isDot || count !== undefined
  if (import.meta.env.DEV && !hasWarned && size === 'sm' && hasBadge && !isDot) {
    hasWarned = true
    console.warn('Badge: `size="sm"` on a count is deprecated and renders as `md`. Keep it for dots only.')
  }
  const badge = hasBadge && (
    <span
      // A labelled badge is an image of a state: a plain span may not carry
      // aria-label. An unlabelled dot says nothing, and a floating badge sits
      // outside the element it describes, so both are hidden — the meaning
      // belongs in the anchor's own name.
      role={props['aria-label'] ? 'img' : undefined}
      aria-hidden={!props['aria-label'] && (isDot || isFloating) ? true : undefined}
      className={cn(
        styles.badge,
        styles[variant],
        styles[size],
        isDot && styles.dot,
        isFloating && [styles.floating, styles[floatingPlacement]],
        className,
      )}
      {...props}
    >
      {isDot ? null : maxCount !== undefined && count! > maxCount ? `${maxCount}+` : count}
    </span>
  )

  if (children === undefined) return badge
  return (
    <span className={styles.anchor}>
      {children}
      {badge}
    </span>
  )
}

# Badge A small count or dot that flags something new on another element: unread messages ...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import { Badge } from './Badge'
import * as BadgeStories from './Badge.stories'

<Meta of={BadgeStories} />

# Badge

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A small count or dot that flags something new on another element: unread
messages on an inbox, a status on an avatar.

<Status of={BadgeStories} />

<Canvas of={BadgeStories.Variants} />

## Variants

Each variant comes as a count or, with `isDot`, a dot.

| Variant | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| <Badge count={8} /> `primary` | The default: new items in the brand colour. |
| <Badge count={8} variant="accent" /> `accent` | Strong and neutral, where the brand colour would clash. |
| <Badge count={8} variant="secondary" /> `secondary` | Low emphasis: a total, not news. As a dot, Offline. |
| <Badge count={8} variant="destructive" /> `destructive` | Something needs attention: failures, overdue items. As a dot, Busy. |
| <Badge count={8} variant="success" /> `success` | As a dot, Online. |
| <Badge count={8} variant="warning" /> `warning` | As a dot, Away or Pending. |

<Canvas of={BadgeStories.Status} />

<Canvas of={BadgeStories.Sizes} />

`maxCount` keeps a large number from stretching the badge past its anchor.

<Canvas of={BadgeStories.MaxCount} />

`isFloating` pins the badge to a corner of the element it wraps.

<Canvas of={BadgeStories.Floating} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Badge } from 'zweihander/badge'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/badge.json
```

- Source: [src/components/atomic-elements/Badge.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/atomic-elements/Badge.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/badge](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/badge)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={BadgeStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={BadgeStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The anchor only exists when the badge has `children`. A badge on its own
is just the container.

## Measurements

One count badge, Atlassian's: 16px tall and at least 24px wide, so a
column of one- and two-digit counts lines up. `size` picks the dot: 8px
(`md`) or 6px (`sm`).

`size="sm"` on a count is deprecated. It renders the same badge as `md`
and warns once in development; in the next release `sm` is for dots only.
`size="md"` on a count, the default written out, and `sm` on a dot are
silent.

<SpecTable
  caption="md"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Height', token: '--badge-md' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Minimum width', token: '--box-sm' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Inline padding', token: '--space-1' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-xs' },
    { part: 'Count', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body-sm' },
    { part: 'Count', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body-sm' },
    { part: 'Dot', property: 'Size', token: '--badge-dot-md' },
    { part: 'Dot', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-pill' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable caption="sm" rows={[{ part: 'Dot', property: 'Size', token: '--badge-dot-sm' }]} />

A floating badge is centred on its corner of the anchor, half in and half
out, with a 2px ring.

## Color

    { part: 'Count', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-warning-inverse' },

  ]}
/>

<SpecTable caption="Floating, every variant" rows={[{ part: 'Ring', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-surface' }]} />

A dot has no text to carry it, so it must reach 3:1 against the page on its
own. That is why the `secondary` and `warning` dots step to a darker colour
than their count badge.

## States

A badge is not interactive: no hover, focus or pressed. Its states are what
it shows.

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Count', content: <Badge count={8} /> },
    { label: 'Over maxCount', content: <Badge count={120} maxCount={99} /> },
    { label: 'Zero', content: <Badge count={0} /> },
    { label: 'Dot', content: <Badge isDot /> },
  ]}
/>

`count={0}` shows "0". Hide the badge yourself if nothing new should mean
no badge.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={BadgeStories} />
</div>

Every other `<span>` attribute passes through to the badge, not to the
anchor.

### Differences from the spec

- **Atlassian's box, not a pill.** A count is 16px tall, at least 24px
  wide, with a 2px corner, in one size. Only the dot is round.
- **`children` is added.** A floating badge needs something to float on.
  The badge wraps it in a `position: relative` span rather than asking
  every consumer to position the anchor themselves.
- **`accent` is the inverted neutral.** The token set has one brand hue,
  which `primary` already uses, so `accent` is foreground-on-background:
  the strongest contrast available without inventing a colour.
- **`success` and `warning` are added** from the status tokens, for
  presence and state dots.
- **`floatingPlacement` defaults to `top-end`**, the usual notification
  corner; the spec gives no default.
- **Start and end are physical** (left and right). RTL pages would get
  mirrored placement.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Badge to say something is new, or how many, on the element it
belongs to: unread messages on an inbox button, a status dot on an avatar.
A floating badge is hidden from assistive tech, so the element it sits on
carries the meaning in its own name.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={BadgeStories.DoNameTheAnchor} />}
  doCaption="The button is named “Notifications, 4 unread”: the count reaches a screen reader too."
  dont={<Story of={BadgeStories.DontCountOnlyInBadge} />}
  dontCaption="The count lives only in the badge, which is hidden: a screen reader hears “Notifications”."
/>

Colour is never the only signal. A destructive badge still needs words
somewhere that say what is wrong, and a status dot needs `aria-label` or
a name beside it.

## When not to use

- **For a label or category.** Use a
  [Tag](?path=/docs/components-atomic-elements-tag--docs): it holds words,
  a badge holds a number.
- **For a message that needs reading.** Use an Alert or a Toast.
- **On every item of a list.** A badge flags what is new; if everything
  is, nothing stands out.

## Accessibility

- An **inline count** is plain text and is read where it sits. Inside a
  button it becomes part of the name ("Inbox 12").
- A **floating** badge is hidden from assistive tech: it sits *outside*
  the element it decorates, so it would be read as a stray number after
  it. Put the meaning in that element's name instead:
  `aria-label="Notifications, 4 unread"`.
- A **dot** has no text and is hidden too.
- Pass `aria-label` to any badge to expose it as an image with that name
  instead, e.g. a status dot on an avatar: `aria-label="Online"`.
- Contrast is checked by addon-a11y in error mode for every story.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

'use client'

import { useEffect, useRef, useState, type ComponentProps, type ReactElement, type ReactNode } from 'react'
import { useRender } from '@base-ui/react/use-render'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Breadcrumbs.module.css'

export interface BreadcrumbItem {
  label: ReactNode
  href?: string
  /** Replaces the `<a>`, e.g. a router's `<Link to="…" />`. */
  render?: ReactElement
}

export interface BreadcrumbsProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'nav'>, 'children'> {
  /** From the top level down. The last one is the current page. */
  items: BreadcrumbItem[]
  /**
   * Collapse the middle when there are more than this many: the first item,
   * "…", and the last `maxItems - 1`. The "…" expands them in place.
   */
  maxItems?: number
  separator?: ReactNode
  size?: 'sm' | 'md'
  /** The nav landmark's name. */
  'aria-label'?: string
}

function Crumb({ item }: { item: BreadcrumbItem }) {
  return useRender({
    render: item.render,
    defaultTagName: 'a',
    props: { href: item.href, className: styles.link, children: item.label },
  })
}

export function Breadcrumbs({
  items,
  maxItems,
  separator,
  size = 'md',
  'aria-label': ariaLabel = 'Breadcrumb',
  className,
  ...props
}: BreadcrumbsProps) {
  const [expanded, setExpanded] = useState(false)
  const listRef = useRef<HTMLOListElement>(null)
  // The "…" button is gone once pressed: move focus to the first item it
  // revealed, rather than dropping it on <body>.
  const justExpanded = useRef(false)
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!justExpanded.current) return
    justExpanded.current = false
    listRef.current?.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('li')[1]?.querySelector<HTMLElement>('a, [href], button')?.focus()
  }, [expanded])
  const collapse = !expanded && maxItems !== undefined && maxItems >= 2 && items.length > maxItems
  const shown: (BreadcrumbItem | 'ellipsis')[] = collapse
    ? [items[0], 'ellipsis', ...items.slice(items.length - (maxItems - 1))]
    : items
  const sep = (
    <span className={styles.separator} aria-hidden="true">
      {separator ?? <Icon name="chevron-right" />}
    </span>
  )

  return (
    <nav aria-label={ariaLabel} className={cn(styles.breadcrumbs, styles[size], className)} {...props}>
      <ol ref={listRef} className={styles.list}>
        {shown.map((item, i) => {
          const last = i === shown.length - 1
          return (
            <li key={i} className={styles.item}>
              {item === 'ellipsis' ? (
                <button
                  type="button"
                  className={styles.ellipsis}
                  aria-label={`Show ${items.length - maxItems!} more`}
                  onClick={() => {
                    justExpanded.current = true
                    setExpanded(true)
                  }}
                >
                  <Icon name="more" />
                </button>
              ) : last ? (
                // The current page: text, not a link to itself.
                <span className={styles.current} aria-current="page">
                  {item.label}
                </span>
              ) : (
                <Crumb item={item} />
              )}
              {!last && sep}
            </li>
          )
        })}
      </ol>
    </nav>
  )
}

# Breadcrumbs The trail from the top of a hierarchy down to the current page, each step a ...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import * as BreadcrumbsStories from './Breadcrumbs.stories'

<Meta of={BreadcrumbsStories} />

# Breadcrumbs

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

The trail from the top of a hierarchy down to the current page, each step a
link back up.

<Status of={BreadcrumbsStories} />

<Canvas of={BreadcrumbsStories.Default} />

## Variants

Breadcrumbs has one look. What changes is the size, how a long trail
collapses, and what sits between the steps.

| Form | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `md` | Under a page title, at body size. The default. |
| `sm` | Dense headers, panels and side sheets, at `body-sm`. |
| `maxItems` | Deep hierarchies, or a trail in a narrow place: the middle collapses to "…", which expands in place. |
| `separator` | A slash or other glyph, where a chevron would clash with nearby icons. |

<Canvas of={BreadcrumbsStories.Small} />

<Canvas of={BreadcrumbsStories.Collapsed} />

<Canvas of={BreadcrumbsStories.CustomSeparator} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Breadcrumbs } from 'zweihander/breadcrumbs'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/breadcrumbs.json
```

- Behaviour: a plain `<nav>` and `<ol>`, after the [APG breadcrumb pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/breadcrumb/)
- Figma: not in the library yet

<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={BreadcrumbsStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={BreadcrumbsStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

Each step is a list item: its link (or the ellipsis), then a separator.
The last item has no separator after it.

## Measurements

Breadcrumbs is text, not a row of controls. At `md` each item sits in a
24px box around its 14/20 text, with 8px either side of the separator, as
Atlassian Design's breadcrumb items.
Atlassian Design has no small breadcrumb; `sm` is the kit's own, and its
height is its line height.

/>

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={BreadcrumbsStories.StatesExample} />
</States>

- **Hover** turns a link to `--color-text` and underlines it; on the
  ellipsis it fills an `--color-background-neutral` chip.
- **Focus** is a 2px `--color-border-focused` outline, 2px outside the link or the
  ellipsis.
- There is no disabled state: a level the reader cannot open is left out
  of the trail.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={BreadcrumbsStories} />
</div>

Every other `<nav>` attribute passes through.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use Breadcrumbs on pages three or more levels deep, under the page title,
so a reader can see where they are and jump back up any number of levels.
It is a secondary aid: the main navigation still has to get people
everywhere.

Keep the trail on one line. When it would wrap, collapse the middle with
`maxItems`; the first level and the nearest ones stay in view.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={BreadcrumbsStories.DoCollapseLongTrail} />}
  doCaption="Collapse a long trail with maxItems: one line, and the levels that matter most stay visible."
  dont={<Story of={BreadcrumbsStories.DontWrapLongTrail} />}
  dontCaption="A trail that wraps reads as two rows and pushes the page down."
/>

Write each label as the title of the page it opens, short enough to scan.
The last item is the current page, as text: a link to the page you are on
does nothing useful.

## When not to use

- **For history.** Breadcrumbs shows where a page sits, not how the reader
  got there. For "go back", use a Back link or
  [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs).
- **On a flat site.** One or two levels need no trail; the main
  navigation already says where you are.
- **For the steps of a task.** Use a Stepper: it shows the steps ahead
  too, and which are done.
- **As the main navigation.** Use a side navigation of links, or Tabs.

## Accessibility

- A `<nav>` landmark named "Breadcrumb" (change it with `aria-label`),
  around an ordered list: screen readers announce the number of items and
  the position of each.
- Each level above the current page is a real `<a href>`, in the tab
  order.
- The last item is text with `aria-current="page"`, not a link.
- Separators are `aria-hidden`, so they are not read between items.
- The ellipsis is a button named "Show 3 more". Enter or Space expands the
  trail and moves focus to the first item it revealed, rather than
  dropping it on the page.
- The ellipsis is under 44px; on touch screens (`pointer: coarse`) its hit
  area grows to 44×44px without it growing.
- Focus ring: 2px `--color-border-focused`, 2px offset.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

# Breakpoints Five breakpoints, inherited from the underlying CSS framework without modifi...
import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as BreakpointsStories from './Breakpoints.stories'

<Meta of={BreakpointsStories} />

# Breakpoints

Five breakpoints, inherited from the underlying CSS framework without
modification. Zweihänder declares no `--breakpoint-*` of its own.

| Prefix | Min width | At a 16px root |
| --- | --- | --- |
| *(none)* | `0` | 0px |
| `sm:` | `40rem` | 640px |
| `md:` | `48rem` | 768px |
| `lg:` | `64rem` | 1024px |
| `xl:` | `80rem` | 1280px |
| `2xl:` | `96rem` | 1536px |

<Canvas of={BreakpointsStories.Scale} />

The box below reports the breakpoint currently in effect. Resize the
preview — or use Storybook's viewport toolbar — and it changes.

<Canvas of={BreakpointsStories.Active} />

## They are min-width, and that has a direction

`md:flex` means "flex at 768px **and above**". There is no maximum, so
rules outside a media query are the small-screen case and every
`@media (width >= …)` is an override for larger screens. Write the phone
layout first and widen it; writing the desktop layout first means every
breakpoint has to undo something.

The other direction is expressible — `@media (width < 48rem)` caps a rule
below a breakpoint — but mixing both in one component is where responsive
CSS usually becomes unreadable. Pick min-width and stay there.

## Breakpoints are in rem

`40rem`, not `640px`. A reader who raises their browser's default font
size gets the layout to break earlier, because the layout responds to how
large the text actually is rather than to the device. That is the correct
behaviour and it is worth not overriding: a `px` breakpoint holds a
multi-column layout together long after its text has stopped fitting.

The px column above is only true at the default 16px root.

## The kit has no opinion yet

**No component here uses a breakpoint.** Controls such as Button and Text
Input are inline-sized — they fill whatever their container gives them and have no
layout of their own to rearrange. The stories on this page are the only
responsive code in the repo.

That is expected: breakpoints are a **layout** concern, and the kit ships
components, not page layouts. Marketing sections, dashboards and checkout
flows are where these will actually get used, and where the kit will need an opinion about
which of the five are load-bearing. Most design systems end up leaning on
two or three.

## Container queries are usually the better tool

A breakpoint asks how wide the *viewport* is. A component almost always
wants to know how wide **its own container** is — the same card is narrow
in a sidebar and wide in a main column at one identical viewport width.

Container queries are in every current browser, and they are plain CSS:

```css
.card {
  container-type: inline-size;
}

.cardBody {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
}

@container (width >= 28rem) {
  .cardBody {
    flex-direction: row;
  }
}
```

When a component is built here that needs to reflow, it should reach for
`@container` first and a viewport breakpoint only when the thing being
arranged really is the page.

## Customization

Breakpoints are theme keys like any other, redefined in the `@theme`
block:

```css
@theme {
  --breakpoint-sm: 30rem;
  --breakpoint-3xl: 120rem;
}
```

Two cautions. These generate utility *variants*, so they cannot be
overridden per-scope by `Theme` the way a color can — a variant is
compiled into a media query at build time, and there is no runtime
variable to swap. And removing a default breakpoint removes its prefix
entirely, so any existing `lg:` becomes a silent no-op rather than an
error.

'use client'

import type { ComponentProps, ReactNode, Ref } from 'react'
import { Button as BaseButton } from '@base-ui/react/button'
import { mergeProps } from '@base-ui/react/merge-props'
import { useRender } from '@base-ui/react/use-render'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Button.module.css'

interface ButtonBaseProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'button'>, 'ref'> {
  ref?: Ref<HTMLElement>
  variant?: 'primary' | 'accent' | 'secondary' | 'destructive'
  appearance?: 'contained' | 'outlined' | 'ghost'
  size?: 'sm' | 'md'
  startIcon?: ReactNode
  endIcon?: ReactNode
  /** Shows a spinner, blocks clicks and keeps focus, so a keyboard user is not dropped. On a link it behaves as disabled. */
  isLoading?: boolean
  isFullWidth?: boolean
  /** Renders an `<a>` instead of a `<button>`: it navigates, it does not act. */
  href?: string
  target?: string
  rel?: string
  /** Replaces the rendered element, e.g. a router's `<Link />`. */
  render?: useRender.RenderProp
}

/** An icon-only button has no text to name it, so `aria-label` is required. */
export type ButtonProps =
  | (ButtonBaseProps & { isIconOnly?: false })
  | (ButtonBaseProps & { isIconOnly: true; 'aria-label': string })

export function Button({
  variant = 'primary',
  appearance = 'contained',
  size = 'md',
  startIcon,
  endIcon,
  isLoading = false,
  isFullWidth = false,
  isIconOnly = false,
  href,
  target,
  rel,
  render,
  disabled,
  type = 'button',
  className,
  children,
  ...props
}: ButtonProps) {
  const content = (
    <>
      {isLoading && <span className={styles.spinner} aria-hidden="true" />}
      {startIcon && (
        <span className={styles.icon} aria-hidden="true">
          {startIcon}
        </span>
      )}
      {children}
      {endIcon && (
        <span className={styles.icon} aria-hidden="true">
          {endIcon}
        </span>
      )}
    </>
  )
  const own = {
    className: cn(
      styles.button,
      styles[variant],
      styles[appearance],
      styles[size],
      isIconOnly && styles.iconOnly,
      isFullWidth && styles.fullWidth,
      isLoading && styles.loading,
      className,
    ),
    'aria-busy': isLoading || undefined,
    children: content,
  }

  // `href` or `render` means someone else's element — an <a>, a router's
  // Link — whose semantics must survive: Base UI's Button would stamp
  // role="button" on it. Props are merged onto it instead.
  //
  // Disabled (or loading, which a link cannot show) drops the render
  // element too and leaves a bare <a> with no href: removing the href is
  // the only thing that stops an <a> navigating, and a router's Link keeps
  // its own. aria-disabled says why it is inert.
  const inert = disabled || isLoading
  const custom = useRender({
    enabled: href !== undefined || render !== undefined,
    render: inert ? undefined : render,
    defaultTagName: 'a',
    props: mergeProps<'a'>(own, props as ComponentProps<'a'>, {
      ...(!inert && href !== undefined && { href }),
      target,
      rel,
      'aria-disabled': inert || undefined,
    }),
  })
  if (custom) return custom

  return (
    <BaseButton
      {...props}
      {...own}
      type={type}
      disabled={disabled || isLoading}
      focusableWhenDisabled={isLoading}
    />
  )
}

# Button Triggers an action on the current page, or, with `href`, navigates. ## Variants `...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'

# Button

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

Triggers an action on the current page, or, with `href`, navigates.

<Status of={ButtonStories} />

<Canvas of={ButtonStories.Default} />

## Variants

`variant` is the colour, by meaning; `appearance` is the emphasis. Any
variant takes any appearance.

<Canvas of={ButtonStories.Matrix} />

| Variant | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| <Button>Primary</Button> | The next step: Save, Continue, Create. One per view. |
| <Button variant="accent">Accent</Button> | A strong action in neutral black or white, where the brand colour would clash or already means something else. |
| <Button variant="secondary">Secondary</Button> | Everything else: Cancel, Back, Export. |
| <Button variant="destructive">Destructive</Button> | Deleting, or anything that cannot be undone. |

| Appearance | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| <Button>Contained</Button> | The action to take, filled so it is found first. |
| <Button appearance="outlined">Outlined</Button> | Actions that matter but are not the next step. |
| <Button appearance="ghost">Ghost</Button> | Low emphasis and dense places: toolbars, table rows, a card's corner. |

<Canvas of={ButtonStories.Sizes} />

<Canvas of={ButtonStories.WithIcons} />

<Canvas of={ButtonStories.IconOnly} />

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={ButtonStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={ButtonStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

While `isLoading`, a spinner takes the content's place; the content stays,
invisible, so the button keeps its width and its name.

## Measurements

Each size is a control tier (Foundations / Sizing), with Atlassian
Design's numbers: 32px by default, 24px for tables and dense rows. Buttons
take the spacious inline padding, 12px at both sizes: a centred label
needs more room either side than a field's left-aligned text. The 12px is
measured from the button's outer edge to its label or icon, border
included, as in Atlassian Design, and is the same with or without an icon
on that side; icon and label sit 6px apart. Ghost has no border, so it is
11px from edge to label, as Figma binds it. The label is 14/20 at both
sizes.

## Color

Each variant has a solid (the contained fill), a colour on that solid, and
a tone that outlined and ghost use for their label. Switch the theme and the
accent in the toolbar: the values follow.

Ghost and outlined have no fill at rest. Contained is lit from above: a
lighter top, a highlight on the top edge, a bottom-edge inner shadow
(black at 18%, 1px up, 1.2px blur, 0.35px spread) and a hairline border a
step darker than the solid. The hairline is the variant's solid moved in
lightness, so it has no token of its own and follows the accent and the
mode; the highlight and the shadow are light, the same on every fill.

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
    { label: 'Pressed', pseudo: 'active' },
    { label: 'Disabled', content: <Story of={ButtonStories.Disabled} /> },
    { label: 'Loading', content: <Story of={ButtonStories.Loading} /> },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={ButtonStories.Default} />
</States>

- **Hover and pressed** are mixed from the variant's own colours, not a
  token each. A coloured solid (primary, destructive) moves away from its
  label and gains contrast; accent and secondary move toward it. Outlined
  and ghost tint the background with their tone, 8% on hover and 14% when
  pressed, and their label moves 25% and 40% toward `--color-text`. Every state keeps the label at 4.5:1, measured by the
  `StateContrast` story under all seventeen accents in both modes.
- **Pressed**, on contained, turns the light over: shade on the top edge,
  no drop shadow, no gradient, as if pushed in.
- **Focus** is a 2px `--color-border-focused` outline, 2px outside the button.
- **Disabled** is the enabled look at 50% opacity.
- **Loading** keeps the full colour: the button is busy, not unavailable.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={ButtonStories} />
</div>

Every other `<button>` attribute passes through, including `ref`.

### Differences from the spec

- **Two sizes, not four.** The sizes follow Atlassian Design: 32px (`md`) by default, 24px (`sm`) for tables and dense rows. Both take 12px from the outer edge to the label (11px on ghost, which has no border), a 6px gap and a 14/20 label; `sm` is a shorter box, not smaller type. The spec's larger steps were dropped; a big call to action is `md` with more room around it, not a taller box.
- **`disabled`, not `isDisabled`**: the native attribute keeps its name.
- **`isIconOnly` is added.** The spec has no icon-only button, and a
  square button that still requires a name is common enough to need one.
- **`render` is added** for composition with routers and other elements,
  matching Base UI and shadcn. It replaced `asChild` in 0.8.
- **`accent` is the inverted neutral** (foreground on background), as on
  Badge: the token set has one brand hue and `primary` uses it.
- Outlined and ghost `primary` use `--color-text-brand`, a step of the accent
  measured to read at 4.5:1 on the page. The solid step would not, for
  warm accents.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Button for an action on the current page: save, submit, open a
dialog, delete. Use one `primary contained` button per view, for the thing
to do next. Everything else steps down to `outlined` or `ghost`, or to
`secondary`.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={ButtonStories.DoOnePrimary} />}
  doCaption="One primary button: the thing to do next. The rest step down."
  dont={<Story of={ButtonStories.DontTwoPrimaries} />}
  dontCaption="Two primary buttons compete for the same click."
/>

**Loading** keeps the button's width and focus and blocks it from acting
again, so a double-submit is impossible and a keyboard user is not dropped
back to the top of the page.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={ButtonStories.Loading} />}
  doCaption="Show progress with isLoading: the button stays where focus is, and cannot fire twice."
  dont={<Story of={ButtonStories.DontDisableWhileSaving} />}
  dontCaption="Disabling it to show progress drops keyboard focus and reads as unavailable."
/>

## When not to use

- **To navigate.** A link is not a button. Pass `href` and Button renders a
  real `<a>`: it keeps link semantics, opens in a new tab on middle-click,
  and gets the link cursor. A plain Button with an `onClick` that changes
  the page does none of that.
- **For a setting that stays on or off.** Use a
  [Toggle Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-togglebutton--docs), a
  Switch or a Checkbox.
- **For a link inside running text.** Use Link.

<Canvas of={ButtonStories.Href} />

## Accessibility

- A native `<button>`, `type="button"` by default so it never submits a
  form by accident. Enter and Space both activate it.
- `isIconOnly` needs `aria-label`; TypeScript refuses it without one.
  Icons are `aria-hidden` everywhere else, so they never double the name.
- `isLoading` sets `aria-busy` and `aria-disabled` but keeps the button
  focusable. `disabled` removes it from the tab order, as native buttons
  do.
- A disabled or loading link renders a bare `<a>` with no `href` (the
  only thing that stops an `<a>` navigating) and `aria-disabled`. With
  `render`, the render element is dropped too, since a router's Link would
  keep its own `href`.
- `render` is for elements that are already interactive: a link or a
  router's Link. It merges props onto the element and adds no role or
  keyboard handling, so do not render a `<div>` through it.
- Hover and pressed keep the label at 4.5:1 too. The `StateContrast`
  story measures every variant × appearance × state under all seventeen
  accents in both modes, from the CSS that ships.
- `sm` and `md` are under 44px; on touch screens (`pointer: coarse`) the
  hit area grows to 44×44px without the button growing.
- Focus ring: 2px `--color-border-focused`, 2px offset, at 3:1 or better on the page.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

'use client'

import type { ComponentProps } from 'react'
import { ToggleGroup } from '@base-ui/react/toggle-group'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './ButtonGroup.module.css'

export interface ButtonGroupProps
  extends Omit<ComponentProps<'div'>, 'defaultValue' | 'onChange' | 'dir'> {
  /** `separate`: ToggleButtons 4px apart. `joined`: one bar, inner corners square, borders shared. */
  type?: 'separate' | 'joined'
  /** Controlled: the `value` of the ToggleButton that is on. Pair with `onValueChange`. */
  value?: string
  /** Uncontrolled: the value on at first. */
  defaultValue?: string
  /** Called with the value of the ToggleButton just turned on. */
  onValueChange?: (value: string) => void
  /** Disables every toggle in the group. */
  disabled?: boolean
}

/** ToggleButtons that share one selection, exactly one on at a time, like Tabs. */
export function ButtonGroup({
  type = 'separate',
  value,
  defaultValue,
  onValueChange,
  className,
  ...props
}: ButtonGroupProps) {
  return (
    <ToggleGroup
      {...props}
      value={value === undefined ? undefined : [value]}
      defaultValue={defaultValue === undefined ? undefined : [defaultValue]}
      onValueChange={(next, details) => {
        // Once one is on, pressing it again does not leave none on.
        if (next.length === 0) return details.cancel()
        onValueChange?.(next[0])
      }}
      className={cn(styles[type], className)}
    />
  )
}

# Button Group

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A selection control, like Tabs without the panel:
[Toggle Buttons](?path=/docs/components-buttons-togglebutton--docs) that
share one selection, exactly one on at a time. `type="separate"` sets them
4px apart; `type="joined"` makes them one bar.

<Status of={ButtonGroupStories} />

Button Group is outside the 1.0 component list; it is beta from 0.9.0.

<Canvas of={ButtonGroupStories.Default} />

## Variants

| `type` | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `separate` | The default. Outlined toggles 4px apart: one view, one mode, one period at a time. |
| `joined` | A segmented control: one bar, where the options read as one control. |

<Canvas of={ButtonGroupStories.Joined} />

<Canvas of={ButtonGroupStories.IconToggles} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { ButtonGroup } from 'zweihander/button-group'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/button-group.json
```

- Source: [src/components/buttons/ButtonGroup.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/buttons/ButtonGroup.tsx)
- Spec: none on uiguideline.com; after [shadcn/ui Button Group](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/button-group) and [Toggle Group](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/toggle-group)
- Behaviour: [Base UI Toggle Group](https://base-ui.com/react/components/toggle-group)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={ButtonGroupStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={ButtonGroupStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The toggles keep their own anatomy; the container only spaces them
(`separate`) or joins them (`joined`).

## Measurements

The group adds no size of its own. Each button keeps its tier, so a group
of `sm` buttons is `--control-sm` tall.

`joined`: the inner corners are square and each toggle after the first
overlaps the one before by its 1px border, so two outlined toggles share
one line. The outer corners keep the toggles' radius.

`separate` leaves its toggles whole: every toggle keeps its four corners
and its border, and they stand `--space-1` (4px) apart in one row that does
not wrap. In a group wider than its content the toggles share the extra
width.

  caption="separate"
  rows={[

  ]}
/>

<SpecTable

## Color

The group paints nothing: off and on colours are the Toggle Button's. In
a joined group the toggle that is on is raised over its neighbours so its
own border wins where they overlap.

<SpecTable

  rows={[

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
    { label: 'Disabled', content: <Story of={ButtonGroupStories.Disabled} /> },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={ButtonGroupStories.Default} />
</States>

Hover and focus are each toggle's own; a toggle has no press-and-hold
state. In a joined group the focused toggle is raised over its neighbours
so the ring is never cut; in a separate group the ring fits in the gap.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={ButtonGroupStories} />
</div>

Every other `<div>` attribute passes through.

### Differences from the spec

- **A selection control, not a row of actions.** As in the Figma library,
  ButtonGroup holds ToggleButtons with exactly one on, in a `separate` or
  `joined` `type`. In 0.9 it replaced both the old action-row
  `ButtonGroup` and `ToggleGroup`. There is no `multiple`: for settings
  that combine, use separate ToggleButtons. For related actions, lay out
  Buttons yourself.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a ButtonGroup when the toggles answer one question with one answer:
which view, which mode, which period. Give every toggle in a group the
same variant and appearance, so the one that is on is the only one that
stands out.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={ButtonGroupStories.DoSameLook} />}
  doCaption="One look across the group: only the toggle that is on stands out."
  dont={<Story of={ButtonGroupStories.DontMixLooks} />}
  dontCaption="A different variant per button reads as several states at once."
/>

<Canvas of={ButtonGroupStories.Controlled} />

## When not to use

- **To switch between panels of content.** Use Tabs: they own the panel
  and its `tabpanel` role.
- **For a choice submitted with a form.** Use a Radio group or Checkboxes:
  a toggle applies at once, a form field waits for Submit.
- **For actions.** A ButtonGroup keeps one option on; for previous and
  next, or zoom in and out, lay out Buttons side by side.
- **For settings that combine** (status filters, Bold and Italic). Use
  separate ToggleButtons: a ButtonGroup keeps exactly one on.
- **For more than a handful of options.** Use a Select.

## Accessibility

- The container has `role="group"`; name it with `aria-label`.
- Each toggle is a native `<button>` with `aria-pressed`, so a screen reader
  announces "Board, toggle button, pressed".
- The group is one tab stop. Arrow keys move between its toggles and
  wrap, Home and End jump to the first and last; Space or Enter turns one
  on. This is the APG toolbar pattern Base UI's Toggle Group follows.
- Exactly one stays on: pressing the one that is on again does not
  release it.
- A disabled group disables every toggle in it.
- An icon-only toggle needs its own `aria-label`, as on Button. A
  [Tooltip](?path=/docs/components-overlays-tooltip--docs) can show that
  label to sighted users: it merges onto the toggle instead of wrapping
  it, so the group still holds only its toggles.

  <Canvas of={ButtonGroupStories.WithTooltips} />

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

/* ------------------------------------------------------------ plain dates
   Calendar dates carry no time: every Date here is local midnight. */

export const startOfDay = (d: Date) => new Date(d.getFullYear(), d.getMonth(), d.getDate())
export const isSameDay = (a: Date | null | undefined, b: Date | null | undefined) =>
  !!a && !!b && a.getFullYear() === b.getFullYear() && a.getMonth() === b.getMonth() && a.getDate() === b.getDate()
export const addDays = (d: Date, n: number) => new Date(d.getFullYear(), d.getMonth(), d.getDate() + n)
/** Adds months, keeping the day where it exists: 31 Jan + 1 month is 28/29 Feb. */
export const addMonths = (d: Date, n: number) => {
  const first = new Date(d.getFullYear(), d.getMonth() + n, 1)
  const last = new Date(first.getFullYear(), first.getMonth() + 1, 0).getDate()
  return new Date(first.getFullYear(), first.getMonth(), Math.min(d.getDate(), last))
}
const startOfMonth = (d: Date) => new Date(d.getFullYear(), d.getMonth(), 1)
const clamp = (d: Date, min?: Date | null, max?: Date | null) =>
  min && d < startOfDay(min) ? startOfDay(min) : max && d > startOfDay(max) ? startOfDay(max) : d

/** The locale's first day of the week (0 = Sunday), where the browser knows it. */
export function firstDayOfWeek(locale?: string) {
  try {
    const l = new Intl.Locale(locale ?? navigator.language) as Intl.Locale & {
      getWeekInfo?: () => { firstDay: number }
      weekInfo?: { firstDay: number }
    }
    const info = l.getWeekInfo?.() ?? l.weekInfo
    if (info) return info.firstDay % 7
  } catch {
    /* fall through */
  }
  return 1
}

  max,
  isDateDisabled,
  range,
  locale,
  weekStartsOn,
  autoFocus = false,
  className,
}: CalendarProps) {
  const today = startOfDay(new Date())
  const [valueState, setValueState] = useState(defaultValue)
  const selected = range ? range.start : value !== undefined ? value : valueState
  const rangeEnd = range?.end ?? null
  const [monthState, setMonthState] = useState(() => startOfMonth(defaultMonth ?? selected ?? today))
  const month = monthProp ? startOfMonth(monthProp) : monthState
  // The day with the roving tab stop, and where the keyboard moves from.
  const [focused, setFocused] = useState(() => clamp(selected ?? (isSameMonth(today, month) ? today : month), min, max))
  const gridRef = useRef<HTMLTableElement>(null)
  const moveFocus = useRef(autoFocus)

  const first = weekStartsOn ?? firstDayOfWeek(locale)
  const fmt = useMemo(() => {
    return {
      title: new Intl.DateTimeFormat(locale, { month: 'long', year: 'numeric', calendar: 'gregory' }),
      weekday: new Intl.DateTimeFormat(locale, { weekday: 'short', calendar: 'gregory' }),
      weekdayNarrow: new Intl.DateTimeFormat(locale, { weekday: 'narrow', calendar: 'gregory' }),
      weekdayLong: new Intl.DateTimeFormat(locale, { weekday: 'long', calendar: 'gregory' }),
      day: new Intl.DateTimeFormat(locale, { day: 'numeric', calendar: 'gregory' }),
      full: new Intl.DateTimeFormat(locale, { dateStyle: 'full', calendar: 'gregory' }),
    }
  }, [locale])

  const disabled = (d: Date) =>
    (!!min && d < startOfDay(min)) || (!!max && d > startOfDay(max)) || (isDateDisabled?.(d) ?? false)

  const setMonth = (m: Date) => {
    const next = startOfMonth(m)
    setMonthState(next)
    onMonthChange?.(next)
  }
  const focusDay = (d: Date) => {
    const next = clamp(d, min, max)
    setFocused(next)
    if (!isSameMonth(next, month)) setMonth(next)
    moveFocus.current = true
  }
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!moveFocus.current) return
    moveFocus.current = false
    gridRef.current?.querySelector<HTMLElement>('[tabindex="0"]')?.focus()
  })
  // Keep the tab stop inside the month when it changes from outside.
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!isSameMonth(focused, month)) setFocused(clamp(selected && isSameMonth(selected, month) ? selected : month, min, max))
  }, [month.getTime()]) // eslint-disable-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps

  const select = (d: Date) => {
    if (disabled(d)) return
    setValueState(d)
    onValueChange?.(d)
    setFocused(d)
  }

  const onKeyDown = (e: KeyboardEvent<HTMLElement>) => {
    const dow = (focused.getDay() - first + 7) % 7
    // Right to left mirrors the grid, so the arrows follow what is on screen.
    const ahead = getComputedStyle(e.currentTarget).direction === 'rtl' ? -1 : 1
    const moves: Record<string, () => Date> = {
      ArrowLeft: () => addDays(focused, -ahead),
      ArrowRight: () => addDays(focused, ahead),
      ArrowUp: () => addDays(focused, -7),
      ArrowDown: () => addDays(focused, 7),
      Home: () => addDays(focused, -dow),
      End: () => addDays(focused, 6 - dow),
      PageUp: () => addMonths(focused, e.shiftKey ? -12 : -1),
      PageDown: () => addMonths(focused, e.shiftKey ? 12 : 1),
    }
    if (moves[e.key]) {
      e.preventDefault()
      focusDay(moves[e.key]())
    } else if (e.key === 'Enter' || e.key === ' ') {
      e.preventDefault()
      select(focused)
    }
  }

  // Six rows of seven days, starting on the week's first day.
  const lead = (month.getDay() - first + 7) % 7
  const start = addDays(month, -lead)
  const weeks = Array.from({ length: 6 }, (_, w) => Array.from({ length: 7 }, (_, d) => addDays(start, w * 7 + d)))
  const weekdays = weeks[0]
  // Two letters where the short names are short ("Mon" → "Mo", "lun." →
  // "lu"); the narrow ones where they are not ("Thứ 2" → "T2").
  const weekdayName = (d: Date) => {
    const short = fmt.weekday.format(d)
    return weekdays.every((w) => fmt.weekday.format(w).length <= 4) ? short.slice(0, 2) : fmt.weekdayNarrow.format(d)
  }
  const minMonth = min ? startOfMonth(min) : null
  const maxMonth = max ? startOfMonth(max) : null
  const nav = (label: string, months: number) => {
    const back = months < 0
    return (
      <button
        type="button"
        className={styles.nav}
        aria-label={label}
        disabled={back ? !!minMonth && minMonth >= month : !!maxMonth && maxMonth <= month}
        onClick={() => setMonth(clamp(addMonths(month, months), minMonth, maxMonth))}
      >
        <Icon name={back ? 'chevron-left' : 'chevron-right'} className={styles.dirIcon} />
      </button>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className={cn(styles.calendar, className)}>
      {/* Month back at the start, the month centred, month on at the end.
          Years are Shift+Page Up and Shift+Page Down. */}
      <div className={styles.header}>
        {nav('Previous month', -1)}
        {/* Not a heading: a calendar can sit anywhere in a page's outline.
            It announces the month as it changes. */}
        <div className={styles.title} aria-live="polite">
          {fmt.title.format(month)}
        </div>
        {nav('Next month', 1)}
      </div>
      <table ref={gridRef} role="grid" aria-label={fmt.title.format(month)} className={styles.grid} onKeyDown={onKeyDown}>
        <thead>
          <tr>
            {weekdays.map((d) => (
              <th key={d.getDay()} scope="col" abbr={fmt.weekdayLong.format(d)} className={styles.weekday}>
                {weekdayName(d)}
              </th>
            ))}
          </tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
          {weeks.map((week, w) => (
            <tr key={w}>
              {week.map((d, col) => {
                const outside = !isSameMonth(d, month)
                // Selection and the band stay inside the month: a day of the month
                // either side is only there for shape, and two months side by
                // side would otherwise both draw the days where they overlap.
                const isSelected = !outside && (isSameDay(d, selected) || isSameDay(d, rangeEnd))
                const between = !outside && !!selected && !!rangeEnd && d > selected && d < rangeEnd
                const banded = !!rangeEnd && !isSameDay(selected, rangeEnd) && (isSelected || between)
                const isDisabled = disabled(d)
                return (
                  <td
                    key={d.getTime()}
                    role="gridcell"
                    aria-selected={isSelected || between || undefined}
                    className={cn(
                      styles.cell,
                      banded && styles.inRange,
                      banded && isSameDay(d, selected) && styles.rangeStart,
                      banded && isSameDay(d, rangeEnd) && styles.rangeEnd,
                      // Rounded off where a week or the month starts or ends.
                      banded && (col === 0 || d.getDate() === 1) && styles.bandStart,
                      banded && (col === 6 || addDays(d, 1).getDate() === 1) && styles.bandEnd,
                    )}
                  >
                    {outside ? (
                      // The months either side are shape, not content: hidden from
                      // assistive tech, not pickable, and faded past muted. Arrow
                      // keys still cross into them, by moving the month.
                      <span aria-hidden="true" data-outside="" className={cn(styles.day, styles.outside)}>
                        {fmt.day.format(d)}
                      </span>
                    ) : (
                      <button
                        type="button"
                        tabIndex={isSameDay(d, focused) ? 0 : -1}
                        aria-label={fmt.full.format(d)}
                        aria-current={isSameDay(d, today) ? 'date' : undefined}
                        aria-disabled={isDisabled || undefined}
                        className={cn(
                          styles.day,
                          isSelected && styles.selected,
                          between && styles.between,
                          isSameDay(d, today) && styles.today,
                        )}
                        onClick={() => select(d)}
                        onFocus={() => setFocused(d)}
                      >
                        {fmt.day.format(d)}
                      </button>
                    )}
                  </td>
                )
              })}
            </tr>
          ))}
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </div>
  )
}

function isSameMonth(a: Date, b: Date) {
  return a.getFullYear() === b.getFullYear() && a.getMonth() === b.getMonth()
}
