# Colors Every color in the system is a CSS custom property declared in `src/tokens.css`, ...
import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as ColorsStories from './Colors.stories'

<Meta of={ColorsStories} />

# Colors

Every color in the system is a CSS custom property declared in
`src/tokens.css`, with a counterpart under the `.dark` class. The source is
`tokens/semantic.json`; `npm run tokens` generates the stylesheet from it
and measures the contrast pairs listed below. One stylesheet holds both
modes, so a rule that reads `var(--color-text)` switches theme without a
conditional.

**The swatches on this page read their values out of the live document**,
so a color shown here is the value the components get. The token *names*
are listed by hand in `Colors.stories.tsx`.

## Naming

Names follow Atlassian's design tokens:

```
--color-<category>-<role>[-<emphasis>]
```

The **category** says what the color is painted on: `surface`, `text`,
`icon`, `border`, `background`, `interaction`, `blanket` or `chart`. Pick
the category by the CSS property you are setting — a `color` on a label is
a `text` token, a `fill` on a glyph is an `icon` token, a `background` on a
button is a `background` token. The bare category (`--color-text`,
`--color-border`) is the default for it.

The **role** says what it means: `brand`, `neutral`, `input`, `selected`,
a status (`info`, `success`, `warning`, `danger`), or `accent-<hue>`.

The **emphasis** says how strong it is, from weakest to strongest:
`subtlest`, `subtle`, (none), `bold`, `bolder`. `-inverse` is text or an
icon that sits on a `bold` fill of the same role.

In Figma the Color collection mirrors this as `<category>/<role>`:
`text/subtlest`, `background/brand-bold`, and `text/default` for the bare
`--color-text`. Each variable's code syntax is its `var(--color-…)`, so
Dev Mode shows the CSS name.

## Surfaces

What a region of the page is. `--color-surface` is the page;
`--color-surface-raised` is a card or panel set into it;
`--color-surface-overlay` is anything that floats above it — a menu,
popover, modal or toast. In light mode the page is gray-50 and the two
raised surfaces are white, so a panel separates by being lighter and needs
a border at most. In dark mode the page is the darkest step and both
raised surfaces are lifted one step toward the viewer.

| Token | Role | Light | Dark |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--color-surface` | The page | gray-50 | gray-950 |
| `--color-surface-raised` | A card or panel in the page | white | gray-900 |
| `--color-surface-overlay` | A menu, popover, modal or toast | white | gray-900 |

Text on any surface is `--color-text` (or a quieter text token below).
There is no per-surface foreground: one text token works on all three.

<Canvas of={ColorsStories.Surfaces} />

## Text

| Token | Role | Light | Dark |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--color-text` | Body text, headings, labels | gray-950 | gray-50 |
| `--color-text-subtle` | Text that recedes until hovered or current: navigation labels | gray-600 | gray-300 |
| `--color-text-subtlest` | Secondary text: descriptions, hints, captions, placeholders | gray-500 | gray-400 |
| `--color-text-inverse` | Text on `--color-background-neutral-bold` | gray-50 | gray-50 |
| `--color-text-brand` | Brand-coloured text: an outlined or ghost primary button, a link | accent text step | accent text step |
| `--color-text-brand-bold` | Text on `--color-background-brand-subtlest` | accent-800 or darker | accent-300 or lighter |
| `--color-text-brand-inverse` | Label on `--color-background-brand-bold` | white or near-black, per accent | near-black |
| `--color-text-<status>` | Status text on the page or on its tint | 800 | 300 |
| `--color-text-<status>-inverse` | Label on `--color-background-<status>-bold` | neutral-50 (warning: neutral-900) | neutral-900 |
| `--color-text-accent-<hue>` | Hue text on the page or on its tint | 800 | 300 |
| `--color-text-accent-<hue>-inverse` | Label on `--color-background-accent-<hue>-bolder` | neutral-50 | neutral-50 |

`--color-text-subtle` is body-safe (7.24:1 on the light page). Use
`--color-text-subtlest` for genuinely secondary text; it still clears 4.5:1
on every surface and fill it is allowed on (see Contrast).

`--color-text-brand` is a separate step from the brand fill. The fill is
picked so its label reads; read as text on the page, amber-500 is barely
2:1, so the build picks the first step of the accent that clears 4.5:1
against the page instead.

## Icons

Glyphs take `icon` tokens, not `text` tokens. They are separate so an icon
can sit at a different step from the text beside it: a status icon is the
saturated hue, its text the darker 800 step.

| Token | Role | Light | Dark |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--color-icon` | Default glyph | gray-950 | gray-50 |
| `--color-icon-subtle` | A glyph that recedes: a chevron, a field's leading icon | gray-500 | gray-400 |
| `--color-icon-inverse` | A glyph on a bold neutral fill | gray-50 | gray-50 |
| `--color-icon-brand` | A brand-coloured glyph | accent text step | accent text step |
| `--color-icon-info` | Info glyph | blue-600 | blue-400 |
| `--color-icon-success` | Success glyph | green-700 | green-400 |
| `--color-icon-warning` | Warning glyph | amber-600 | amber-400 |
| `--color-icon-danger` | Danger glyph | red-600 | red-400 |

## Borders

| Token | Role | Light | Dark |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--color-border` | A divider or container edge | gray-200 | white 10% |
| `--color-border-input` | A text field's edge | gray-300 | white 18% |
| `--color-border-bold` | A checkbox, radio or switch track outline | gray-500 | gray-400 |
| `--color-border-focused` | The focus indicator | accent-700 | accent-400 |

Choose by what the edge has to do. `--color-border` separates things and
is never the only sign something is there. `--color-border-input` is the
light hairline of a text field: about 1.5:1, a deliberate exception to 3:1
because a field also has its label, placeholder, fill and focus ring. A
product that needs 3:1 on fields sets
`--color-border-input: var(--color-border-bold)`. `--color-border-bold` is
for controls that have nothing else showing they are there, so it clears
3:1 against the page (WCAG 1.4.11). `--color-border-focused` follows the
accent one step darker than its fill, because the lighter solids miss 3:1
against the page — yellow-600 measures 2.93:1.

In dark mode the two lighter borders are translucent white, so an edge
reads the same on `--color-surface` and on a lifted
`--color-surface-raised`.

<Canvas of={ColorsStories.LinesAndFocus} />

## Backgrounds

Fills behind content that is not a surface: a button, a selected row, a
filled field, a status message.

| Token | Role | Light | Dark |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--color-background-neutral` | A quiet fill: secondary button, a disabled field, a zebra stripe | gray-100 | gray-800 |
| `--color-background-neutral-bold` | A solid neutral fill (a neutral Avatar) | gray-600 | gray-600 |
| `--color-background-selected` | The current item: a selected row, the active nav item | gray-200 | white 10% |
| `--color-background-input` | A filled panel or field that subtlest text can sit on | gray-50 | gray-800 |
| `--color-background-brand-bold` | The default button: **the brand hue** | accent solid | accent solid |
| `--color-background-brand-subtlest` | A brand tint | accent-100 | accent-950 |
| `--color-background-<status>-bold` | Solid status fill | 600 (success 700, warning 500) | 400 |
| `--color-background-<status>` | Status tint | 100 | 950 |
| `--color-background-accent-<hue>-bolder` | Solid hue fill (a solid Tag) | 600 | 600 |
| `--color-background-accent-<hue>-subtler` | Hue tint | 100 | 950 |

`--color-background-brand-bold` is the one fill the
[`accentColor`](?path=/docs/foundations-overview--docs) setting moves, with
`--color-text-brand`, `--color-icon-brand`, the brand tint and
`--color-border-focused`. The accent solid is step 600 for most hues and
700 for sky, fuchsia, pink and rose in light mode, and its label is white
or near-black, whichever clears 4.5:1 on it.

<Canvas of={ColorsStories.SubtleSurfaces} />

<Canvas of={ColorsStories.SolidActions} />

## Interaction, blanket

| Token | Role | Light | Dark |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--color-interaction-hovered` | Hover overlay, laid over whatever fill the item already has | black 5% | white 6% |
| `--color-blanket` | Behind a modal | black 50% | black 50% |

`--color-interaction-hovered` is translucent so one token works on any
surface or fill: lay it on top (a second background layer or a
pseudo-element), do not swap the fill for it.

## Status and hue

Four status roles carry meaning about state: `info` (blue), `success`
(green), `warning` (amber), `danger` (red). They are fixed hues and do not
follow the accent: a status colour that changes with the brand stops being
a status. Each role has a solid fill and its label, a tint, text that reads
on the tint or the page, and an icon:

```
--color-background-<status>-bold   --color-text-<status>-inverse
--color-background-<status>        --color-text-<status>
--color-icon-<status>
```

`danger` is also the destructive action: a delete button is
`--color-background-danger-bold` with `--color-text-danger-inverse`. If the
accent is already red, tell a destructive action apart by wording and
placement, not by colour alone.

The 17 hues (`red` to `rose`, as in the primitives below) carry category,
not state — a Tag colour, an Avatar's initials. Each has a solid, its
label, a tint, and text:

```
--color-background-accent-<hue>-bolder   --color-text-accent-<hue>-inverse
--color-background-accent-<hue>-subtler  --color-text-accent-<hue>
```

Every hue's solid is step 600 with a white label in both modes, so a row of
solid tags reads as one set. The warm hues fall below 4.5:1 there, and the
build does not measure hue labels on purpose (decision of 2026-10-08).
`--color-text-accent-orange-contrast` is a near-black label (neutral-900)
for orange, for a place that has to pass 4.5:1 on the orange solid; nothing
in the kit reads it yet.

## Chart

`--color-chart-1` to `--color-chart-8` colour series in the charts, in
order. They are separate from the hue tokens so the series order can be
tuned for neighbours that stay distinguishable.

| Token | Light | Dark |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--color-chart-1` | blue-600 | blue-400 |
| `--color-chart-2` | yellow-700 | yellow-400 |
| `--color-chart-3` | pink-600 | pink-400 |
| `--color-chart-4` | teal-600 | teal-500 |
| `--color-chart-5` | violet-600 | violet-400 |
| `--color-chart-6` | orange-600 | orange-500 |
| `--color-chart-7` | cyan-600 | cyan-500 |
| `--color-chart-8` | lime-700 | lime-500 |

## Contrast

Measured, not assumed. `npm run tokens` computes each pair below from the
OKLCH values and stops the build if one drops under its floor. WCAG AA
wants 4.5:1 for text and 3:1 for the edge of a control or a chart mark.

- **Brand labels:** for each of the 17 accents, the solid and its label are
  picked together so `--color-text-brand-inverse` clears 4.5:1 on
  `--color-background-brand-bold`. `--color-text-brand` clears 4.5:1
  against the page, and `--color-border-focused` clears 3:1 against it.
- **Status:** for each of info, success, warning and danger, in both modes,
  `--color-text-<status>-inverse` on the bold fill, and
  `--color-text-<status>` on its tint and on the page, all at 4.5:1.
- **Hues:** `--color-text-accent-<hue>` on its subtler tint and on the
  page, at 4.5:1. Labels on the bolder fill are not measured (see above).
- **Secondary text:** `--color-text-subtlest` on `--color-surface`,
  `--color-surface-raised`, `--color-background-input` and
  `--color-background-neutral`, at 4.5:1 on all nine gray ramps in both
  modes.
- **Neutral solid:** `--color-text-inverse` on
  `--color-background-neutral-bold`, at 4.5:1 on all nine gray ramps.
- **Control outlines:** `--color-border-bold` against the page, at 3:1 on
  all nine gray ramps.
- **Chart marks:** each `--color-chart-<n>` against `--color-surface-raised`,
  at 3:1 on all nine gray ramps. This is why yellow and lime take step 700
  in light.

The values on the defaults (blue accent, gray ramp):

| Pair | Light | Dark |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--color-text` on `--color-surface` | 19.28:1 | 19.28:1 |
| `--color-text` on `--color-surface-raised` | 20.13:1 | 17.00:1 |
| `--color-text-subtle` on `--color-surface` | 7.24:1 | 13.67:1 |
| `--color-text-subtlest` on `--color-surface` | 4.85:1 | 7.73:1 |
| `--color-text-subtlest` on `--color-background-neutral` | 4.60:1 | 5.64:1 |
| `--color-text-brand-inverse` on `--color-background-brand-bold` | 5.03:1 | 6.79:1 |
| `--color-text-brand` on `--color-surface` | 5.04:1 | 7.63:1 |
| `--color-text-inverse` on `--color-background-neutral-bold` | 7.24:1 | 7.24:1 |
| `--color-border-focused` on `--color-surface` | 6.54:1 | 7.63:1 |
| `--color-border-bold` on `--color-surface` | 4.85:1 | 7.73:1 |

| Status pair | info | success | warning | danger |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| label on bold, light | 5.03:1 | 4.73:1 | 8.35:1 | 4.56:1 |
| text on tint, light | 7.25:1 | 6.45:1 | 6.41:1 | 6.86:1 |
| text on page, light | 8.47:1 | 6.80:1 | 6.83:1 | 8.02:1 |
| label on bold, dark | 6.79:1 | 10.09:1 | 10.43:1 | 6.19:1 |
| text on tint, dark | 8.13:1 | 10.67:1 | 10.37:1 | 8.40:1 |
| text on page, dark | 11.11:1 | 14.40:1 | 13.92:1 | 10.48:1 |

The tightest pair is `--color-text-subtlest` on
`--color-background-neutral` in light mode, at 4.60:1: gray-500 on every
ramp is the lightest value that clears 4.6:1 on its own gray-100. Dark
`--color-text-danger-inverse` is neutral-900, not near-white: the danger
fill lightens to red-400 in dark mode, and near-white on red-400 is 2.77:1.

## Color is never the only signal

`--color-background-danger-bold` on a button does not say what will be
destroyed, and a red tag means nothing to a reader who cannot tell it from
a neutral one. Pair colour with words, an icon or a shape every time it
carries meaning. The numbers above are a floor, not a design review.

## Dark mode

Every token has a counterpart under `.dark`, switched by a class. Dark is
not an inversion of light: surfaces go *up*, and strong fills get lighter
so their labels flip to dark text. The mechanism and how to follow the OS
setting are on their own page:
**[Dark mode](?path=/docs/foundations-dark-mode--docs)**.

## Primitives

The palette underneath: 17 hues and 9 gray ramps, 11 shades each. Two ramps feed the semantic
tokens and each can be swapped on its own: an **accent** (blue by default)
for the brand tokens, and a **gray** (`gray` by default) for surfaces,
text, borders and neutral fills. The status, hue and chart tokens pin
their own ramps. The exceptions to "every value is a ramp step" are the
white raised surfaces in light mode and the translucent tokens: the dark
borders, dark selected fill, hover overlay and blanket.

This is raw material, not a palette to build UI from. Reach for a
primitive when you are defining the *next* semantic token; if a primitive
shows up in a component, a token is missing. The classes are generated by
an `@source inline(...)` directive in `src/index.css` only so this page
can render them.

<Canvas of={ColorsStories.Primitives} />

## Migrating from 0.8

0.9.0 renamed every colour token and removed the old names. The main ones:

{/* docs:check allow --background --card --popover --foreground --card-foreground --popover-foreground --secondary-foreground --accent-foreground --muted-foreground --subtle-foreground --primary --primary-foreground --primary-text --secondary --muted --accent --selected --surface-filled --border --input --field-border --control-border --ring --destructive --destructive-foreground --neutral-solid --neutral-solid-foreground --hover-overlay --scrim --warning-indicator -- old 0.8 names, listed for migration */}

| 0.8 | 0.9 |
| --- | --- |
| `--background` | `--color-surface` |
| `--card` | `--color-surface-raised` |
| `--popover` | `--color-surface-overlay` |
| `--foreground`, `--card-foreground`, `--popover-foreground`, `--secondary-foreground`, `--accent-foreground` | `--color-text` |
| `--subtle-foreground` | `--color-text-subtle` |
| `--muted-foreground` | `--color-text-subtlest` |
| `--primary` | `--color-background-brand-bold` |
| `--primary-foreground` | `--color-text-brand-inverse` |
| `--primary-text` | `--color-text-brand` |
| `--secondary`, `--muted`, `--accent` | `--color-background-neutral` |
| `--selected` | `--color-background-selected` |
| `--surface-filled` | `--color-background-input` |
| `--neutral-solid`, `--neutral-solid-foreground` | `--color-background-neutral-bold`, `--color-text-inverse` |
| `--border`, `--input` | `--color-border` |
| `--field-border` | `--color-border-input` |
| `--control-border` | `--color-border-bold` |
| `--ring` | `--color-border-focused` |
| `--destructive`, `--destructive-foreground` | `--color-background-danger-bold`, `--color-text-danger-inverse` |
| `--hover-overlay` | `--color-interaction-hovered` |
| `--scrim` | `--color-blanket` |
| `--warning-indicator` | `--color-icon-warning` |
| --&lt;status&gt;, --&lt;status&gt;-foreground | `--color-background-<status>-bold`, `--color-text-<status>-inverse` |
| --&lt;status&gt;-subtle, --&lt;status&gt;-text | `--color-background-<status>`, `--color-text-<status>` |
| --&lt;hue&gt;, --&lt;hue&gt;-foreground | `--color-background-accent-<hue>-bolder`, `--color-text-accent-<hue>-inverse` |
| --&lt;hue&gt;-subtle, --&lt;hue&gt;-text | `--color-background-accent-<hue>-subtler`, `--color-text-accent-<hue>` |
| --chart-N | `--color-chart-<n>` |

Glyphs that used a text token now have their own: `--color-icon`,
`--color-icon-subtle` and the status icons.

## Customization

Redeclare a token after Zweihänder's stylesheet, or edit
`tokens/semantic.json` and run `npm run tokens` if you own the source.
Nothing that reads `var(--color-background-brand-bold)` changes, because
every rule points at the variable rather than the value.

Two things to carry through a rebrand: re-measure the pairs above — a
brand hue at the same lightness as another will not hit the same ratios —
and keep light and dark as separate decisions. Reusing the light value of
a fill in dark mode is what produced the 2.77:1 failure described under
Contrast.

Projects that install through the registry get these values merged into
their own stylesheet; projects on the npm package import
`zweihander/tokens.css` and override afterwards.

# Column Chooser A button above a table that opens a list of its columns, each with a chec...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import * as ColumnChooserStories from './ColumnChooser.stories'

<Meta of={ColumnChooserStories} />

# Column Chooser

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A button above a table that opens a list of its columns, each with a
checkbox to show or hide it, and a Reset columns row that brings back the
default set.

<Status of={ColumnChooserStories} />

<Canvas of={ColumnChooserStories.Open} />

## Variants

| Variant | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| Every column shown (default) | Tables whose columns all matter at first, where people hide what they do not need. |
| `defaultVisibleKeys` | Tables with more columns than fit: show the essentials, let people add the rest. Reset goes back to this set. |

The chooser does not touch the table: it reports the shown keys and you
filter the Table's `columns` with them. That keeps the choice yours to
store, per user or per view. With a resizable Table, pass `onReset` to put
the widths back too:

<Canvas of={ColumnChooserStories.Default} />

<Canvas of={ColumnChooserStories.SomeHiddenByDefault} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { ColumnChooser } from 'zweihander/column-chooser'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/column-chooser.json
```

- Source: [src/components/data-display/ColumnChooser.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/data-display/ColumnChooser.tsx)
- Spec: none on uiguideline.com; built from the Application UI catalogue, whose source for widths is shadcn's Resizable. Widths are Table's `isResizable` instead, a handle in each header rather than resizable panels
- Behaviour: the kit's [Popover](?path=/docs/components-overlays-popover--docs), [Checkbox](?path=/docs/components-controls-checkbox--docs) and [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs); the popup is styled as a [Select](?path=/docs/components-inputs-select--docs) list's shell and options
- Figma: the Column Chooser component in the library

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={ColumnChooserStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={ColumnChooserStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The open popovers on this tab and the next are pictures: real choosers
rendered in place with `container` and inert, the popup laid out under the
button where it opens.

## Measurements

<SpecTable
  caption="Every chooser"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Popup', property: 'Block padding', token: '--space-2' },
    { part: 'Column checkbox', property: 'Row block padding', token: '--space-1-5' },
    { part: 'Column checkbox', property: 'Row inline padding', token: '--space-3' },
    { part: 'Column checkbox', property: 'Row minimum height', token: '--control-md' },
    { part: 'Column checkbox', property: 'Gap, box to name', token: '--space-2' },
    { part: 'Separator', property: 'Space above and below', token: '--space-1' },
    { part: 'Separator', property: 'Thickness', token: '--border-width' },
    { part: 'Reset', property: 'Inline start padding, past a box', token: '--choice-box' },
    { part: 'Reset', property: 'Hit area on touch screens', token: '--target-coarse' },
  ]}
/>

The button is a medium Button. The popup is a list's shell, as Select's,
with Popover's border, `--radius-lg` corner and `--shadow-overlay`:
240px wide (or the screen's width, if narrower), 8px above and below the
rows and none at the sides, so a row's hover fill runs edge to edge. Each
column is an option's row, 32px, and the whole row is the click target:
it is the checkbox's label, stretched. Reset columns is one more row, its
text in line with the column names. Rows grow to 44px on touch screens.

## Color

The button is an outlined secondary Button and the popup's surface is
Popover's `--color-surface-overlay`; see those pages for their tokens.

<SpecTable
  caption="Rows"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Column checkbox, hover', property: 'Background', token: '--color-background-neutral' },
    { part: 'Reset', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text' },
    { part: 'Reset, hover', property: 'Background', token: '--color-background-neutral' },
    { part: 'Separator', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-border' },
    { part: 'Reset, focus', property: 'Ring', token: '--color-border-focused' },
  ]}
/>

## States

The chooser is open or closed. The button keeps Button's states; each box
keeps Checkbox's, and a locked column shows Checkbox's disabled look. A
row and Reset take `--color-background-neutral` on hover; Reset's focus
ring is drawn inside it:

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
    { label: 'Pressed', pseudo: 'active' },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={ColumnChooserStories.StateButton} />
</States>

- **Locked**: the row header column, and the last column left, are ticked
  and disabled: a table needs a name per row and at least one column.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>

</div>

### Differences from the spec

There is no uiguideline spec. The catalogue's anatomy lists drag to
reorder as optional; it is left out until a table needs it, because it
needs a keyboard way to move as well. The popup is a dialog with no
visible title, named by `label`: it holds checkboxes and a button, which a
`listbox` cannot.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Column Chooser on a table with more columns than most people need at
once, typically six or more, where different people read different ones.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={ColumnChooserStories.DoFewColumns} />}
  doCaption="A few optional columns beside a locked name column."
  dont={<Story of={ColumnChooserStories.DontTwoColumns} />}
  dontCaption="A chooser for two columns: one is locked, so there is nothing to choose."
/>

## When not to use

- **To switch between whole layouts** (a summary and a detailed set): use
  saved views, so one choice changes several columns at once.
- **To filter rows.** Hiding a column does not hide rows; use filters in
  the table's toolbar.
- **For a table that fits.** If every column fits on the screens it is
  used on, leave them all shown.

## Accessibility

- The button reports `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and `aria-expanded`. The
  popup is a `role="dialog"` named by the label, "Columns", through
  `aria-label`: it shows no title.
- Opening moves focus into the dialog; Escape closes it and returns focus
  to the button.
- Each column is a checkbox named by its header, in table order; Space
  toggles it, and so does a click anywhere on its row. The shown keys are
  reported in column order, the row header always among them.
- The row header column's checkbox, and the last checked one, are
  `aria-disabled`: ticked and unchangeable.
- Reset is a button named "Reset columns" that brings back the default
  columns, after a `role="separator"`.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

'use client'

import { useId, useRef, useState, type ReactNode, type Ref } from 'react'
import { Combobox as BaseCombobox } from '@base-ui/react/combobox'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import {
  InputField,
  boxClass,
  inputStyles as s,
  type InputSize,
  type ValidationState,
} from './InputField'
import styles from './Combobox.module.css'

/** Labels are strings here: they are what is typed, matched and shown in the input. */
export type ComboboxOption = string | { value: string; label: string; disabled?: boolean }
type Item = { value: string; label: string; disabled?: boolean }

export interface ComboboxProps {
  ref?: Ref<HTMLInputElement>
  options: ComboboxOption[]
  value?: string | null
  defaultValue?: string | null
  /** The spec's `onChange`. `null` when cleared. */
  onValueChange?: (value: string | null) => void
  placeholder?: string
  label?: ReactNode
  helperText?: ReactNode
  validationState?: ValidationState
  size?: InputSize
  isFullWidth?: boolean
  /** Options are still arriving: a spinner, and "Loading…" in the list. */
  isLoading?: boolean
  /** Show a button that clears the selection. */
  isClearable?: boolean
  /** Shown in the list when nothing matches. */
  emptyText?: string
  name?: string
  disabled?: boolean
  readOnly?: boolean
  required?: boolean
  autoFocus?: boolean
  id?: string
  /** Where the popup renders instead of `<body>`, e.g. an element in fullscreen or a scope with its own theme. */
  container?: HTMLElement | null
  className?: string
  'aria-label'?: string
}

/** The first case-insensitive match of the query, marked. */
function Highlight({ text, query }: { text: string; query: string }) {
  const at = query ? text.toLowerCase().indexOf(query.toLowerCase()) : -1
  if (at < 0) return <>{text}</>
  return (
    <>
      {text.slice(0, at)}
      <mark className={styles.match}>{text.slice(at, at + query.length)}</mark>
      {text.slice(at + query.length)}
    </>
  )
}

export function Combobox({
  ref,
  options,
  value,
  defaultValue,
  onValueChange,
  placeholder,
  label,
  helperText,
  validationState,
  size = 'md',
  isFullWidth,
  isLoading,
  isClearable = true,
  emptyText = 'No matches',
  name,
  disabled,
  readOnly,
  required,
  autoFocus,
  id,
  className,
  container,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel,
}: ComboboxProps) {
  const items: Item[] = options.map((o) => (typeof o === 'string' ? { value: o, label: o } : o))
  const find = (v: string | null | undefined) => (v == null ? v : (items.find((i) => i.value === v) ?? null))
  // Only for highlighting the typed text in each option; Base UI owns the
  // input's value and the filtering.
  const [query, setQuery] = useState('')
  // A pointer pick sends the field back to rest: no caret, no ring, as a
  // native select after a click. A keyboard pick keeps focus where the user is.
  const inputRef = useRef<HTMLInputElement | null>(null)
  const labelId = useId()

  return (
    <InputField
      label={label}
      labelId={labelId}
      helperText={helperText}
      validationState={validationState}
      required={required}
      disabled={disabled}
      name={name}
      isFullWidth={isFullWidth}
      className={className}
    >
      <BaseCombobox.Root
        items={items}
        value={find(value)}
        defaultValue={find(defaultValue)}
        onValueChange={(next, details) => {
          // After Base UI's own refocus of the input, hence the timeout.
          if (details.event instanceof MouseEvent) setTimeout(() => inputRef.current?.blur())
          onValueChange?.((next as Item | null)?.value ?? null)
        }}
        // Highlight only what was typed. When an option is chosen the input
        // takes its label, which is not a query to mark in other options.
        onInputValueChange={(next, details) => setQuery(details.reason === 'input-change' ? next : '')}
        // items are rebuilt each render, so compare by value, not identity,
        // or the selection loses its check on the next keystroke.
        isItemEqualToValue={(a: Item, b: Item) => a.value === b.value}
        readOnly={readOnly}
        required={required}
        autoHighlight
      >
        <BaseCombobox.InputGroup className={cn(boxClass(size), s.picker)}>
          <BaseCombobox.Input
            ref={(el) => {
              inputRef.current = el
              if (typeof ref === 'function') ref(el)
              else if (ref) ref.current = el
            }}
            id={id}
            placeholder={placeholder}
            autoFocus={autoFocus}
            aria-label={ariaLabel}
            aria-busy={isLoading || undefined}
            className={s.control}
          />
          {isLoading && <span className={cn(s.icon, s.spinner)} aria-hidden="true" />}
          {isClearable && !readOnly && (
            <BaseCombobox.Clear className={cn(s.iconButton, s.bare)} aria-label="Clear selection">
              <Icon name="clear" />
            </BaseCombobox.Clear>
          )}
          <BaseCombobox.Trigger
            className={s.iconButton}
            // Field labels every control in it with the field's label; this
            // button is not the field, so it keeps its own name rather than
            // being a second "Team member".
            render={(props) => <button {...props} aria-labelledby={undefined} aria-label="Show options" />}
          >
            <Icon name="chevron-down" />
          </BaseCombobox.Trigger>
        </BaseCombobox.InputGroup>
        <BaseCombobox.Portal container={container}>
          <BaseCombobox.Positioner className={s.positioner} sideOffset={4}>
            <BaseCombobox.Popup className={s.popup}>
              {isLoading ? (
                <BaseCombobox.Status className={s.status}>Loading…</BaseCombobox.Status>
              ) : (
                <BaseCombobox.Empty className={s.empty}>{emptyText}</BaseCombobox.Empty>
              )}
              {/* A listbox needs a name of its own: the field's. */}
              <BaseCombobox.List aria-labelledby={label ? labelId : undefined} aria-label={label ? undefined : ariaLabel}>
                {(item: Item) => (
                  <BaseCombobox.Item key={item.value} value={item} disabled={item.disabled} className={s.option}>
                    <BaseCombobox.ItemIndicator className={s.check}>
                      <Icon name="check" />
                    </BaseCombobox.ItemIndicator>
                    <span>
                      <Highlight text={item.label} query={query} />
                    </span>
                  </BaseCombobox.Item>
                )}
              </BaseCombobox.List>
            </BaseCombobox.Popup>
          </BaseCombobox.Positioner>
        </BaseCombobox.Portal>
      </BaseCombobox.Root>
    </InputField>
  )
}

# Combobox

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A field you type into to filter a list of options, then choose one.

<Status of={ComboboxStories} />

<Canvas of={ComboboxStories.Default} />

## Variants

Two sizes, and the field's validation states. Typing filters the list and
marks the match; the chosen option carries a check.

<Canvas of={ComboboxStories.Sizes} />

| Size | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `md` | Forms and settings: the default. |
| `sm` | Dense places: a toolbar filter, a table row. As tall as a default Button. |

<Canvas of={ComboboxStories.Validation} />

<Canvas of={ComboboxStories.Clear} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Combobox } from 'zweihander/combobox'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/combobox.json
```

- Source: [src/components/inputs/Combobox.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/inputs/Combobox.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/combobox](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/combobox)
- Behaviour: [Base UI Combobox](https://base-ui.com/react/components/combobox)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={ComboboxStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={ComboboxStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The options list opens under the field, at least as wide as it:

- **Option**: the label, with the typed text marked by weight and
  underline. Options are inset by the field's padding, so their text
  starts where the input's does.
- **Check**: before the chosen option's label, in a column kept for every
  option so labels never shift.
- **Message**: "No matches" (`emptyText`) when nothing matches,
  "Loading…" while `isLoading`.

<Canvas of={ComboboxStories.OpenButton} />

## Measurements

A field is one step taller than a Button, after Atlassian Design: `sm` is
32px and `md` is 40px (Foundations / Sizing). The sizes share the rest:
10px of padding at each end, the 16px icons, 12px apart, the field
radius, which never becomes a pill, and body type. The clear button is
the bare 16px icon; the open button is a 24px target round its icon,
which ends 10px inside the edge. The text stops 12px short of the first
icon.

wide as the field, 4px under it, and scrolls after 20rem (about ten

## Color

<SpecTable
  caption="Field"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Field', property: 'Background', token: '--color-surface-raised' },
    { part: 'Field', property: 'Border', token: '--color-border-input' },
    { part: 'Label, input', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text' },
    { part: 'Placeholder, helper, icons', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-subtlest' },
    { part: 'Required asterisk', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-danger' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-border-focused' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Validation and read-only"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Border, helper, focus ring, error', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-danger' },
    { part: 'Border, helper, success', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-success' },
    { part: 'Field, read-only', property: 'Background', token: '--color-background-input' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Options list"
  rows={[
    { part: 'List', property: 'Background', token: '--color-surface-overlay' },
    { part: 'List', property: 'Border', token: '--color-border' },
    { part: 'List', property: 'Shadow', token: '--shadow-overlay' },
    { part: 'Option', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text' },
    { part: 'Option, highlighted', property: 'Background', token: '--color-background-neutral' },
    { part: 'Option, highlighted', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text' },
    { part: 'Check', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-brand' },
    { part: 'No matches, Loading…', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-subtlest' },
  ]}
/>

The field's edge is a light hairline, about 1.5:1, as in the Claude apps:
an approved exception to WCAG 1.4.11. The label, placeholder and focus
ring still mark the field. The matched text keeps the option's own colour,
so it holds full contrast on the highlighted row.

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus' },
    { label: 'Filled', content: <Fit><Story of={ComboboxStories.Clear} /></Fit> },
    { label: 'Error', content: <Fit><Story of={ComboboxStories.Validation} /></Fit> },
    { label: 'Read-only', content: <Fit><Combobox label="Team member" options={['Miya Burns']} defaultValue="Miya Burns" readOnly /></Fit> },
    { label: 'Disabled', content: <Fit><Story of={ComboboxStories.Disabled} /></Fit> },
    { label: 'Loading', content: <Fit><Story of={ComboboxStories.Loading} /></Fit> },
  ]}
>
  <Fit><Story of={ComboboxStories.Default} /></Fit>
</States>

- **Focus** is a 2px `--color-border-focused` outline, 2px outside the field, drawn while
  the input has focus, by pointer too: that is where typing goes. In the
  error state the ring is `--color-text-danger`. The clear and open buttons draw
  their own ring when tabbed to, so the field never shows two.
- **Hover** changes nothing on the field; the clear and open buttons
  darken from `--color-text-subtlest` to `--color-text`.
- **Error** turns the edge and the helper `--color-text-danger` together; the
  words are the message, the colour only points at it.
- **Read-only** fills the field with `--color-background-input`; there is no clear
  button.
- **Disabled** is the enabled look at 50% opacity.
- **Loading** adds a spinner before the buttons and says "Loading…" in the
  list.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={ComboboxStories} />
</div>

### Differences from the spec

- **Labels must be strings**, not components: they are what is typed,
  matched and shown in the input.
- **`emptyText`** is added: an empty list needs to say why.
- **`onValueChange`, not `onChange`**, and native names (`disabled`,
  `readOnly`, `required`), as on Select.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Combobox to choose one option from a long list, when people already
know what they are looking for: a person, a country, a project. Typing a
few letters is faster than scrolling. It chooses from the list only; free
text that is not an option is not a value.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={ComboboxStories.DoLongList} />}
  doCaption="A long list people know an entry of: type a few letters, pick it."
  dont={<Story of={ComboboxStories.DontFewOptions} />}
  dontCaption="Three options hidden behind typing. A Select or a radio group shows them all."
/>

## When not to use

- **For a handful of options.** Under about seven, use a
  [Select](?path=/docs/components-inputs-select--docs), or a
  [Radio](?path=/docs/components-controls-radio--docs) group when they
  should all be visible.
- **For free text.** If any answer is valid, use a
  [Text Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textinput--docs); to filter
  a page, use [Search](?path=/docs/components-inputs-search--docs).
- **For several values.** It holds one; a multi-select is not built yet.

## Accessibility

- The input has `role="combobox"`, `aria-autocomplete="list"` and
  `aria-expanded`; the list is a `listbox` named by the field's label (or
  `aria-label` when there is no visible label), as the input is.
- **Keyboard:** typing opens and filters; the first match is highlighted
  so Enter picks it; Up and Down move; Escape closes, then clears.
- The match is marked by weight and underline, not colour, so it keeps
  the option's full contrast on the highlighted row.
- The open button is named "Show options" and is out of the tab order
  (the input already opens the list); the clear button is "Clear
  selection".
- `validationState="error"` sets `aria-invalid`, and the helper text is
  the input's description.
- Loading and empty states are announced from the list.
- After an option is picked with the pointer, the input loses focus and the
  field returns to rest (no caret, no ring). A keyboard pick keeps focus in
  the input, so keyboard and screen reader users are not dropped to the page.
- Options are 32px tall; on touch screens (`pointer: coarse`) they grow to
  44px, and the clear and open buttons get a 44×44px hit area.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

# Confirm Dialog Asks before something that cannot be undone: a warning, the action as a q...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import * as ConfirmDialogStories from './ConfirmDialog.stories'

<Meta of={ConfirmDialogStories} />

# Confirm Dialog

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

Asks before something that cannot be undone: a warning, the action as a
question, what it will destroy, then Cancel or the action. A press outside
does nothing, so the reader has to choose.

<Status of={ConfirmDialogStories} />

<Canvas of={ConfirmDialogStories.Default} />

## Variants

| Variant | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| Default | An everyday delete: a comment, a file, a saved view. One question, two buttons. |
| Non-destructive (`kind="default"`) | A decision that destroys nothing: sign out everywhere, leave without saving. No warning icon, and the action is a primary button. |
| Type to confirm (`confirmText`) | A large delete that cannot be undone: a workspace, an account, a project with its files. The action waits until the reader types the name. |

<Canvas of={ConfirmDialogStories.KindDefault} />

<Canvas of={ConfirmDialogStories.TypeToConfirm} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { ConfirmDialog } from 'zweihander/confirm-dialog'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/confirm-dialog.json
```

- Source: [src/components/overlays/ConfirmDialog.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/overlays/ConfirmDialog.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/modal](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/modal) (the alert dialog)
- Built on: [Modal](?path=/docs/components-overlays-modal--docs) with `isAlert`, on [Base UI Alert Dialog](https://base-ui.com/react/components/alert-dialog)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={ConfirmDialogStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={ConfirmDialogStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The open dialogs on this tab and the next are pictures: rendered in a frame
with `container` and `isModal={false}`, inert, so they do not lock this page
or take its focus.

## Measurements

It is a Modal at `size="sm"` (at most 400px wide): container, title,
body and footer take Modal's measurements, except the 16px from the title
to the description (8px in a Modal). Its own parts:

<SpecTable
  caption="Icon and field"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Title to description', property: 'Gap', token: '--space-group' },
    { part: 'Warning icon', property: 'Width', token: '--icon-md' },
    { part: 'Icon to title', property: 'Gap', token: '--space-inline' },
    { part: 'Text to type', property: 'Font family', token: '--font-mono' },
  ]}
/>

The icon is one line of the title tall, so it stays on the first line when
the title wraps.

## Color

<SpecTable
  caption="Its own parts"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Warning icon', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-background-danger-bold' },
  ]}
/>

Everything else takes Modal's colours, and the buttons keep their own:
Cancel is `secondary` outlined, the action `destructive` (`primary` with
`kind="default"`, which has no warning icon).

## States

The dialog is open or closed. With `confirmText`, the action is disabled
until the field matches, then enabled; without it, it is enabled from the
start.

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Waiting for the name', content: <Story of={ConfirmDialogStories.StateWaiting} /> },
    { label: 'Ready', content: <Story of={ConfirmDialogStories.DoEverydayDelete} /> },
  ]}
/>

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={ConfirmDialogStories} />
</div>

### Differences from the spec

- **Destructive by default.** `kind="default"` drops the warning icon and
  makes the action primary; for anything more custom, use a
  [Modal](?path=/docs/components-overlays-modal--docs) with `isAlert`, where
  you choose the buttons.
- **No pending state.** The dialog closes on confirm. If the delete can fail,
  control `open` and keep it open until your request settles.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Before an action that destroys something the reader cannot get back. Put
the object's name in the title, say in the description what goes with it,
and name the action button after what it does.

Type to confirm is for the few deletes that are both large and final. Used
on every delete, it becomes a chore readers do without reading.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={ConfirmDialogStories.DoEverydayDelete} />}
  doCaption="Ask once for an everyday delete, with the action on the button."
  dont={<Story of={ConfirmDialogStories.DontTypeForSmall} />}
  dontCaption="Do not make the reader type for a small delete: it teaches them to type without reading."
/>

## When not to use

- **When the action can be undone.** Do it, then offer Undo in a
  [Toast](?path=/docs/components-notifications-toast--docs): no question
  is faster than a good one.
- **For a decision that destroys nothing**, such as Sign out or Leave
  without saving. Use a [Modal](?path=/docs/components-overlays-modal--docs)
  with `isAlert`.
- **To show a warning.** Use an
  [Inline Alert](?path=/docs/components-notifications-inlinealert--docs).

## Accessibility

- `role="alertdialog"`, named by the title (the icon is hidden from
  assistive tech) and described by the consequence.
- Focus starts on Cancel, so Enter on open cannot delete. With
  `confirmText` it starts in the field, which is named "To confirm, type"
  and the name.
- The action stays disabled until the field matches exactly, case
  included; spaces around the text are ignored. Enter in the field confirms
  once it matches.
- A press outside does nothing. Cancel and Escape close it without
  confirming, and focus goes back to the trigger.
- Reopened, the field starts empty.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

# Cursors Three tokens, and a convention that surprises most people: **buttons do not get ...
import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as CursorsStories from './Cursors.stories'

<Meta of={CursorsStories} />

# Cursors

Three tokens, and a convention that surprises most people: **buttons do
not get `cursor: pointer`. Links do.**

## The convention

`cursor: pointer` means "this navigates" — it is the hand that appears
over a link. Browsers have never applied it to `<button>`, `<select>` or a
checkbox, and neither does this kit. Interactive elements that act on the
current page keep the regular arrow; only a link gets the hand. This is a
deliberate departure from the very common `button { cursor: pointer }`
reset.

It is worth knowing the argument on the other side: a large body of
usability opinion holds that the hand cursor is now such a widespread
affordance for "clickable" that removing it costs more than the semantic
purity gains. If your product takes that view, this is a one-line change —
see **Customization** below. The point of making it a token is that it is
one line, in one place, rather than a decision re-litigated per component.

<Canvas of={CursorsStories.Tokens} />

## `--cursor-button`

`default` — the regular arrow. Applied by Button.

Note this changes nothing visually today: a native `<button>` already
shows the arrow. **The token's job is not its current value; it is that
the value is reachable.** Without it, switching the kit to `pointer` means
editing every component; with it, it is one declaration.

## `--cursor-link`

`pointer` — the hand.

This one exists because the convention above has a second half that is
easy to state and easy to get wrong. Button takes `href`, so it can
render as a real `<a href>` — and when it did, it inherited
`--cursor-button` and lost the hand that the browser gives every other
link on the page. A link styled as a button is still a link.

```css
a[href].button {
  cursor: var(--cursor-link);
}
```

The `a[href]` part is doing real work. An `<a>` without `href` is not a
link and browsers do not give it the hand either, so matching on the
attribute rather than the element keeps the rule honest.

The distinction the kit draws is navigation versus action, not
appearance: a `<button>` styled as a link would still act on the current
page, so it would keep the arrow.

| | Element | Cursor |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<Button>` | `<button>` | arrow |
| `<Button href="/x">` | `<a href>` | hand |

The Button `Href` story asserts this, and compares against a bare
`<a href>` rather than the literal `pointer` — so overriding
`--cursor-link` moves the assertion with it instead of breaking it.

## `--cursor-disabled`

`not-allowed` — used by TextInput, and **not** by Button. That asymmetry
is not an oversight.

A disabled `<input>` stays hit-testable, so a cursor set on it renders and
the user gets feedback on hover. Button's disabled state is
`pointer-events: none`, which makes the element untargetable; an
untargetable element is never hovered, so a cursor there would be dead
CSS. The `pointer-events: none` is not incidental — because Button
can render as an `<a>`, which ignores the `disabled` attribute entirely. Blocking pointer events is what actually disables it
in that case.

So the token applies to the pattern where a control stays hoverable while
disabled — including a control deliberately wrapped so a tooltip can
explain *why*. That trade-off, between a disabled control you can
interrogate and one that is inert, is a real design choice, and the two
components here happen to sit on opposite sides of it.

## Adding tokens

A mature system ends up with a token per interactive component —
checkboxes, menu items, radios, switches, slider thumbs. This kit has
three, because it has two components and one of them can render as two
different things.

{/* docs:check allow --cursor-slider-thumb -- an example of a token not to add */}

**Add a token when the component that needs it is built, not before.** A
`--cursor-slider-thumb` with no Slider is a value nobody can verify and
that the eventual Slider may not want.

## Customization

All three are plain CSS keywords, not colors, so they override like any
other custom property:

```css
:root {
  --cursor-button: pointer;
}
```

Load any override after Zweihänder's own stylesheet so the cascade picks it
up. Setting `--cursor-button: pointer` is the one-line version of adopting
the mainstream convention; it leaves `--cursor-link` alone, which is
already `pointer`, so the two simply converge.

# Dark mode Dark mode is **a class, not a media query.** `tokens.css` declares the light v...
import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as DarkModeStories from './DarkMode.stories'

<Meta of={DarkModeStories} />

# Dark mode

Dark mode is **a class, not a media query.** `tokens.css` declares the
light values on `:root, .light` and the dark values on `.dark`, and
every rule in the kit reads those variables, so the class is the only
switch there is. The same scopes set `color-scheme`, so the UI the browser
draws itself (scrollbars, date and select popups, autofill) switches with
them.

Nothing is automatic about it. Adding `class="dark"` to `<html>` is what
switches the document; without that, a device set to dark mode gets the
light theme. That is the trade — see **Following the system** below.

<Canvas of={DarkModeStories.SideBySide} />

## Components don't know about it

No component stylesheet — `Button.module.css`, `InputField.module.css` or any other — mentions `.dark`.
They write `background: var(--color-background-brand-bold)`, and it is the variable that
changes; the rule is identical in both modes.

This is the main reason to reach for a token rather than a literal. A
hard-coded `#0a0a0a` is near-black in both modes and needs a `.dark`
override beside it to survive a theme switch; `var(--color-background-brand-bold)` needs
nothing. Every theme conditional in a codebase is a place a value was
hardcoded and then patched.

## Dark is not an inversion

Flipping lightness would produce the wrong result in three places, and the
palette deliberately doesn't:

- **`--color-surface` is gray-950, not black.** A pure-black page makes
  the halation around light text worse and leaves no room to sit a surface
  *below* the page level.
- **Surfaces go up, not down.** `--color-surface-raised` and
  `--color-surface-overlay` are a step *lighter* than the page in dark
  mode (gray-900 on gray-950), as they are in light mode (white on
  gray-50). Elevation in dark mode is carried by lightness, because a drop shadow
  has almost nothing left to darken (see
  [Shadows](?path=/docs/foundations-shadows--docs)).
- **Strong fills become light, so their labels become dark.**
  `--color-background-brand-bold` goes from the accent's 600 step to its
  400, and `--color-text-brand-inverse` turns near-black with it.
  `--color-background-danger-bold` does the same, red-600 to red-400 —
  which is exactly where the palette's one contrast bug lived: keeping the
  near-white `--color-text-danger-inverse` on the lightened red measured
  2.77:1. It is now neutral-900 at 6.19:1. Lightening a fill without
  flipping its `-inverse` label is the single easiest dark-mode mistake to
  make.

Full measurements for both modes are in
[Color → Contrast](?path=/docs/foundations-colors--docs).

## Alpha for edges

`--color-border` and `--color-border-input` are opaque gray-200 and
gray-300 in light, and `white / 10%` and `white / 18%` in dark;
`--color-background-selected` is `white / 10%` in dark too. An opaque dark
border would have to be re-chosen for every surface it sits on; a
translucent white edge lightens whatever is underneath, so the same token
reads correctly on `--color-surface` and on a lifted
`--color-surface-raised`. `--color-interaction-hovered` and
`--color-blanket` are translucent in both modes for the same reason.

## Scoping

`Theme` switches an appearance for a subtree rather than the document —
a dark footer on a light page, a light popover inside a dark shell. See
[Overview → Nesting](?path=/docs/foundations-overview--docs) for how the
nesting resolves and the one caveat that comes with it.

```tsx
<Theme appearance="dark">
  <Footer />
</Theme>
```

## Following the system

The kit ships no `prefers-color-scheme` handling, because the choice
between "follow the OS" and "remember what the user picked" belongs to the
app, not the component library. The usual shape:

```ts
const media = window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)')
const stored = localStorage.getItem('theme') // 'light' | 'dark' | null
const dark = stored ? stored === 'dark' : media.matches
document.documentElement.classList.toggle('dark', dark)
```

Two things worth getting right. Run it **before first paint** — in a
blocking inline script in `<head>`, not in a `useEffect` — or the page
renders light and flips, which is the flash every themed site has had at
some point. And keep listening to `media` afterwards so a user changing
their OS setting mid-session is followed, unless they have made an
explicit choice.

In this Storybook, the **Theme** toolbar control does the class toggle for
you; there is no persistence and no system detection.

/** The locale's numeric date format, its field order and a placeholder pattern. */
function useDateFormat(locale?: string) {
  return useMemo(() => {
    // Gregorian and Western digits whatever the locale's defaults: the grid is
    // Gregorian, and the parser reads ASCII digits. Without this, th-TH shows
    // the Buddhist year (2569) and fa-IR Persian digits, and neither reads back.
    const format = new Intl.DateTimeFormat(locale, {
      day: '2-digit',
      month: '2-digit',
      year: 'numeric',
      calendar: 'gregory',
      numberingSystem: 'latn',
    })
    const parts = format.formatToParts(new Date(2026, 10, 22))
    const order = parts.filter((p) => p.type === 'day' || p.type === 'month' || p.type === 'year').map((p) => p.type)
    const pattern = parts
      .map((p) => (p.type === 'day' ? 'dd' : p.type === 'month' ? 'mm' : p.type === 'year' ? 'yyyy' : p.value))
      .join('')
    /** Reads the three numbers in the locale's order; any separator will do. */
    const parse = (text: string): Date | null | undefined => {
      const nums = text.match(/\d+/g)
      if (!text.trim()) return null
      if (!nums || nums.length !== 3) return undefined
      const v: Record<string, number> = {}
      order.forEach((type, i) => (v[type] = Number(nums[i])))
      const year = v.year < 100 ? 2000 + v.year : v.year
      const d = new Date(year, v.month - 1, v.day)
      // Rejects 31/02 and the like, which Date would roll into March.
      return d.getFullYear() === year && d.getMonth() === v.month - 1 && d.getDate() === v.day ? d : undefined
    }
    return { format: (d: Date) => format.format(d), parse, pattern }
  }, [locale])
}

export function DatePicker({
  value,
  defaultValue = null,
  onValueChange,
  label,
  helperText,
  validationState,
  size = 'md',
  min,
  max,
  isDateDisabled,
  locale,
  weekStartsOn,
  placeholder,
  isFullWidth,
  name,
  disabled,
  readOnly,
  required,
  id,
  className,
  container,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel,
}: DatePickerProps) {
  const { format, parse, pattern } = useDateFormat(locale)
  const today = startOfDay(new Date())
  const [valueState, setValueState] = useState(defaultValue)
  const date = value !== undefined ? value : valueState
  const [text, setText] = useState(() => (date ? format(date) : ''))
  const [invalid, setInvalid] = useState(false)
  const [month, setMonth] = useState(() => date ?? today)
  // Follow a controlled value that changes from outside.
  const [shown, setShown] = useState(date)
  if (!isSameDay(shown, date) && !(shown === null && date === null)) {
    setShown(date)
    setText(date ? format(date) : '')
    setInvalid(false)
  }

  const allowed = (d: Date) =>
    !(min && d < startOfDay(min)) && !(max && d > startOfDay(max)) && !(isDateDisabled?.(d) ?? false)
  const commit = (next: Date | null) => {
    setValueState(next)
    setShown(next)
    setText(next ? format(next) : '')
    setInvalid(false)
    if (next) setMonth(next)
    onValueChange?.(next)
  }
  const commitText = () => {
    const parsed = parse(text)
    if (parsed === undefined || (parsed && !allowed(parsed))) setInvalid(true)
    else if (parsed === null ? date !== null : !isSameDay(parsed, date)) commit(parsed)
    else setInvalid(false)
  }

  return (
    <PickerField
      text={text}
      onTextChange={(t) => {
        setText(t)
        setInvalid(false)
      }}
      onCommit={commitText}
      onShow={() => setMonth(date ?? today)}
      triggerLabel={date ? `Choose date, ${format(date)} selected` : 'Choose date'}
      popupLabel="Choose date"
      hidden={name && <input type="hidden" name={name} value={date ? iso(date) : ''} />}
      label={label}
      helperText={invalid ? `Enter a date as ${pattern}${min || max ? ', within the allowed range' : ''}.` : helperText}
      validationState={invalid ? 'error' : validationState}
      size={size}
      placeholder={placeholder ?? pattern}
      isFullWidth={isFullWidth}
      disabled={disabled}
      readOnly={readOnly}
      required={required}
      id={id}
      className={className}
      container={container}
      aria-label={ariaLabel}
    >
      {({ autoFocus, close }) => (
        <Calendar
          value={date}
          month={month}
          onMonthChange={setMonth}
          onValueChange={(d) => {
            commit(d)
            close()
          }}
          min={min}
          max={max}
          isDateDisabled={isDateDisabled}
          locale={locale}
          weekStartsOn={weekStartsOn}
          autoFocus={autoFocus}
          className={styles.body}
        />
      )}
    </PickerField>
  )
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------ range */

export interface DateRangePreset {
  label: string
  start: Date
  end: Date
}

/** The built-in presets, whole periods around today: Today … Last year. */
export function rangePresets(weekStartsOn: number, today = startOfDay(new Date())): DateRangePreset[] {
  const week = addDays(today, -((today.getDay() - weekStartsOn + 7) % 7))
  const y = today.getFullYear()
  const m = today.getMonth()
  return [
    { label: 'Today', start: today, end: today },
    { label: 'Yesterday', start: addDays(today, -1), end: addDays(today, -1) },
    { label: 'This week', start: week, end: addDays(week, 6) },
    { label: 'Last week', start: addDays(week, -7), end: addDays(week, -1) },
    { label: 'This month', start: new Date(y, m, 1), end: new Date(y, m + 1, 0) },
    { label: 'Last month', start: new Date(y, m - 1, 1), end: new Date(y, m, 0) },
    { label: 'This year', start: new Date(y, 0, 1), end: new Date(y, 11, 31) },
    { label: 'Last year', start: new Date(y - 1, 0, 1), end: new Date(y - 1, 11, 31) },
  ]
}

export interface DateRangePickerProps extends Omit<DatePickerProps, 'value' | 'defaultValue' | 'onValueChange' | 'name'> {
  /** Both ends set, or `null`. */
  value?: DateRange | null
  defaultValue?: DateRange | null
  onValueChange?: (range: DateRange | null) => void
  /** A list beside the calendars: `true` for the built-in one (Today … Last year), or your own. */
  presets?: boolean | DateRangePreset[]
  /** Submitted as `yyyy-mm-dd/yyyy-mm-dd`, an ISO 8601 interval. */
  name?: string
}

const NO_RANGE: DateRange = { start: null, end: null }
const monthIndex = (d: Date) => d.getFullYear() * 12 + d.getMonth()
/** The range's first month on the left, its last on the right; the next month when it spans one. */
const monthsFor = (r: DateRange | null, today: Date): [Date, Date] => {
  const left = r?.start ?? today
  const right = r?.end && monthIndex(r.end) > monthIndex(left) ? r.end : addMonths(left, 1)
  return [left, right]
}
/** The two days as a range, earlier first. */
const ordered = (a: Date | null, b: Date | null): DateRange => (a && b && b < a ? { start: b, end: a } : { start: a, end: b })
const sameRange = (a: DateRange | null, b: DateRange | null) =>
  a === b || (!!a && !!b && isSameDay(a.start, b.start) && isSameDay(a.end, b.end))

export function DateRangePicker({
  value,
  defaultValue = null,
  onValueChange,
  label,
  helperText,
  validationState,
  size = 'md',
  min,
  max,
  isDateDisabled,
  locale,
  weekStartsOn,
  placeholder,
  presets = false,
  isFullWidth,
  name,
  disabled,
  readOnly,
  required,
  id,
  className,
  container,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel,
}: DateRangePickerProps) {
  const { format, parse, pattern } = useDateFormat(locale)
  const today = startOfDay(new Date())
  const [valueState, setValueState] = useState(defaultValue)
  const range = value !== undefined ? value : valueState
  const show = (r: DateRange | null) => (r?.start && r.end ? `${format(r.start)} – ${format(r.end)}` : '')
  const [text, setText] = useState(() => show(range))
  const [invalid, setInvalid] = useState(false)
  const [draft, setDraft] = useState<DateRange>(range ?? NO_RANGE)
  // The two calendars page on their own; the left one always shows the
  // earlier month. Moving one past the other pushes the other along.
  const [months, setMonths] = useState(() => monthsFor(range, today))
  const [shown, setShown] = useState(range)
  if (!sameRange(shown, range)) {
    setShown(range)
    setText(show(range))
    setInvalid(false)
  }

  const presetList = presets === true ? rangePresets(weekStartsOn ?? firstDayOfWeek(locale), today) : presets || []
  const allowed = (d: Date) =>
    !(min && d < startOfDay(min)) && !(max && d > startOfDay(max)) && !(isDateDisabled?.(d) ?? false)
  const commit = (next: DateRange | null) => {
    setValueState(next)
    setShown(next)
    setText(show(next))
    setInvalid(false)
    onValueChange?.(next)
  }
  /** Two dates, each in the locale's order: six numbers, any separators. */
  const commitText = () => {
    const nums = text.match(/\d+/g)
    let parsed: DateRange | null | undefined = null
    if (text.trim()) {
      const a = nums?.length === 6 ? parse(nums.slice(0, 3).join(' ')) : undefined
      const b = nums?.length === 6 ? parse(nums.slice(3).join(' ')) : undefined
      parsed = a && b && allowed(a) && allowed(b) ? ordered(a, b) : undefined
    }
    if (parsed === undefined) setInvalid(true)
    else if (!sameRange(parsed, range)) commit(parsed)
    else setText(show(range))
  }

  return (
    <PickerField
      text={text}
      onTextChange={(t) => {
        setText(t)
        setInvalid(false)
      }}
      onCommit={commitText}
      onShow={() => {
        setDraft(range ?? NO_RANGE)
        setMonths(monthsFor(range, today))
      }}
      triggerLabel={range ? `Choose dates, ${show(range)} selected` : 'Choose dates'}
      popupLabel="Choose dates"
      popupClassName={styles.rangePopup}
      hidden={
        name && <input type="hidden" name={name} value={range?.start && range.end ? `${iso(range.start)}/${iso(range.end)}` : ''} />
      }
      label={label}
      helperText={
        invalid ? `Enter two dates as ${pattern} – ${pattern}${min || max ? ', within the allowed range' : ''}.` : helperText
      }
      validationState={invalid ? 'error' : validationState}
      size={size}
      // Words, not the pattern twice: the pattern stays with assistive tech
      // as the description, and in the error message.
      placeholder={placeholder ?? 'Start – End'}
      formatHint={`${pattern} – ${pattern}`}
      isFullWidth={isFullWidth}
      disabled={disabled}
      readOnly={readOnly}
      required={required}
      id={id}
      className={className}
      container={container}
      aria-label={ariaLabel}
    >
      {({ autoFocus, close }) => {
        // A range applies as soon as both ends are in.
        const choose = (r: DateRange) => {
          setDraft(r)
          if (!r.start || !r.end) return
          if (!sameRange(r, range)) commit(r)
          close()
        }
        // The first click starts a range, the second ends it, either way round.
        const pick = (d: Date) => choose(!draft.start || draft.end ? { start: d, end: null } : ordered(draft.start, d))
        const calendar = { range: draft, onValueChange: pick, min, max, isDateDisabled, locale, weekStartsOn }
        return (
          <>
            {presetList.length > 0 && (
              <div role="group" aria-label="Presets" className={styles.presets}>
                {presetList.map((p) => (
                  <button
                    key={p.label}
                    type="button"
                    aria-pressed={isSameDay(p.start, draft.start) && isSameDay(p.end, draft.end)}
                    className={styles.preset}
                    onClick={() => {
                      setMonths(monthsFor(p, today))
                      choose({ start: p.start, end: p.end })
                    }}
                  >
                    {p.label}
                  </button>
                ))}
              </div>
            )}
            <div className={styles.months}>
              <Calendar
                {...calendar}
                month={months[0]}
                onMonthChange={(m) => setMonths(([, right]) => [m, monthIndex(m) < monthIndex(right) ? right : addMonths(m, 1)])}
                autoFocus={autoFocus}
                className={styles.body}
              />
              {/* Hidden on a narrow screen, where one month fits. */}
              <Calendar
                {...calendar}
                month={months[1]}
                onMonthChange={(m) => setMonths(([left]) => [monthIndex(left) < monthIndex(m) ? left : addMonths(m, -1), m])}
                className={cn(styles.body, styles.second)}
              />
            </div>
          </>
        )
      }}
    </PickerField>
  )
}

# Date Picker A date field: type the date, or pick it from a calendar. ## Variants Two siz...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'

# Date Picker

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A date field: type the date, or pick it from a calendar.

<Status of={DatePickerStories} />

<Canvas of={DatePickerStories.Default} />

## Variants

Two sizes, `sm` and `md`, and the field's validation states, as on
[Text Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textinput--docs). The typed
order follows `locale`: day first in `en-GB` and `vi-VN`, month first in
`en-US`. The form always gets `yyyy-mm-dd`.

| Locale | Typed as |
| --- | --- |
| `en-GB`, `vi-VN` | `dd/mm/yyyy` |
| `en-US` | `mm/dd/yyyy` |

<Canvas of={DatePickerStories.UnitedStates} />

<Canvas of={DatePickerStories.Vietnamese} />

`min`, `max` and `isDateDisabled` limit what can be picked or typed:

<Canvas of={DatePickerStories.Range} />

For a span of days, see
[Date Range Picker](?path=/docs/components-inputs-daterangepicker--docs).

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { DatePicker } from 'zweihander/date-picker'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/date-picker.json
```

- Source: [src/components/inputs/DatePicker.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/inputs/DatePicker.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/date-picker](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/date-picker)
- Behaviour: [Base UI Popover](https://base-ui.com/react/components/popover), and the kit's [Calendar](?path=/docs/components-data-display-calendar--docs)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={DatePickerStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={DatePickerStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The calendar opens in a popover 8px under the field, aligned to its
start: a [Calendar](?path=/docs/components-data-display-calendar--docs)
in a panel. Its days, header and paging buttons are specified there.

## Measurements

The field is the kit's field: `sm` is 32px and `md` is 40px, one step
taller than a Button, with the same 10px padding, icon and type in both.
The calendar button is a 16px icon in a 24px target, pulled into the
padding so the icon ends 10px inside the edge, 8px after the date.

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Empty', content: <DatePicker label="Start date" locale="en-GB" /> },
    { label: 'Filled' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus' },
    {
      label: 'Error',
      content: <DatePicker label="Start date" locale="en-GB" validationState="error" helperText="Enter a date as dd/mm/yyyy." />,
    },
    { label: 'Read-only', content: <DatePicker label="Start date" locale="en-GB" defaultValue={new Date(2026, 8, 18)} readOnly /> },
    { label: 'Disabled', content: <DatePicker label="Start date" locale="en-GB" defaultValue={new Date(2026, 8, 18)} disabled /> },
  ]}
>
  <DatePicker label="Start date" locale="en-GB" defaultValue={new Date(2026, 8, 18)} />
</States>

- **Focus** is a 2px `--color-border-focused` outline, 2px outside the field, drawn while
  the input has focus, by pointer too. In the error state the ring is
  `--color-text-danger`. The calendar button draws its own ring when tabbed to.
- **Error** turns the edge and the helper `--color-text-danger`. It is also
  shown on its own while the typed text is not a date, or is outside
  `min` and `max`: the helper then gives the expected pattern.
- **Hover** changes nothing on the field; the calendar icon darkens from
  `--color-text-subtlest` to `--color-text`.
- **Read-only** fills the box with `--color-background-input`, as every
  Zweihänder field does. The input stays focusable and copyable and its
  value is submitted; the calendar icon stays but is not a button, so the
  calendar never opens. Say why in `helperText`.
- **Disabled** is the enabled look at 50% opacity; the calendar button is
  disabled with it.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={DatePickerStories} />
</div>

### Design notes

- **Typing is first-class.** Many people type a known date faster than
  they can page to it. Any separator works (`3.10.26`, `3/10/2026`); the
  field reformats on blur or Enter.
- **An impossible date is kept, not guessed.** `31/02/2026` stays as
  typed, the field turns to its error state and the helper shows the
  expected pattern; nothing is reported until it is a real date.
- **A click in the input opens the calendar, and keeps focus there.**
  Typing carries on with the month in view; the calendar button and
  Alt+Down move focus into the calendar instead.
- **The form gets ISO.** Whatever the display order, `name` submits
  `yyyy-mm-dd`, so the server never has to guess the locale.
### Differences from the spec

- **`onValueChange`, not `onChange`**, with a `Date` or `null`, as the
  kit's other value fields.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Date Picker for one date: a start date, a due date, a booking. Let
people type it when they know it, and pick it when they want to see the
week around it. Set `min`, `max` or `isDateDisabled` so a date that cannot
be used cannot be chosen, rather than refusing it after submit.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={DatePickerStories.DoPatternPlaceholder} />}
  doCaption="The empty field shows the pattern to type, in the locale's order."
  dont={<Story of={DatePickerStories.DontExamplePlaceholder} />}
  dontCaption="An example date as the placeholder reads as a value already filled in."
/>

## When not to use

- **For a span of days.** Use a
  [Date Range Picker](?path=/docs/components-inputs-daterangepicker--docs):
  one field, both ends, never back to front.
- **To show a month on the page.** Use a
  [Calendar](?path=/docs/components-data-display-calendar--docs) inline.
- **For a time of day.** The picker holds a date only.

## Accessibility

- The input is a labelled text box with `inputmode="numeric"` for a
  number keypad; while the text is not a valid date it has
  `aria-invalid` and the helper explains the format. Without a visible
  label, pass `aria-label` to name the input.
- The calendar button is named "Choose date", with the current date when
  there is one. Alt+Down in the input opens it too.
- `readOnly` puts `readonly` on the input: screen readers announce it,
  it stays in the tab order, and there is no calendar button; a click or
  Alt+Down opens nothing.
- The calendar opens as a dialog named "Choose date" with focus on the
  selected day; Escape closes it without a change.
- **After a pick the field goes back to rest.** Picked with the pointer,
  focus leaves the field (no caret, no ring), as in Combobox. Picked with
  the keyboard, focus returns to where it came from (the button, or the
  input), so keyboard and screen reader users are not dropped to the page.
- The field and calendar's own labels ("Choose date", "Previous month")
  are in English, like the rest of the kit's built-in labels.
- On touch screens (`pointer: coarse`) the calendar button gets a 44×44px
  hit area without the field growing.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

const iso = (d: Date) =>
  `${d.getFullYear()}-${String(d.getMonth() + 1).padStart(2, '0')}-${String(d.getDate()).padStart(2, '0')}`

/** The locale's numeric date format, its field order and a placeholder pattern. */
function useDateFormat(locale?: string) {
  return useMemo(() => {
    // Gregorian and Western digits whatever the locale's defaults: the grid is
    // Gregorian, and the parser reads ASCII digits. Without this, th-TH shows
    // the Buddhist year (2569) and fa-IR Persian digits, and neither reads back.
    const format = new Intl.DateTimeFormat(locale, {
      day: '2-digit',
      month: '2-digit',
      year: 'numeric',
      calendar: 'gregory',
      numberingSystem: 'latn',
    })
    const parts = format.formatToParts(new Date(2026, 10, 22))
    const order = parts.filter((p) => p.type === 'day' || p.type === 'month' || p.type === 'year').map((p) => p.type)
    const pattern = parts
      .map((p) => (p.type === 'day' ? 'dd' : p.type === 'month' ? 'mm' : p.type === 'year' ? 'yyyy' : p.value))
      .join('')
    /** Reads the three numbers in the locale's order; any separator will do. */
    const parse = (text: string): Date | null | undefined => {
      const nums = text.match(/\d+/g)
      if (!text.trim()) return null
      if (!nums || nums.length !== 3) return undefined
      const v: Record<string, number> = {}
      order.forEach((type, i) => (v[type] = Number(nums[i])))
      const year = v.year < 100 ? 2000 + v.year : v.year
      const d = new Date(year, v.month - 1, v.day)
      // Rejects 31/02 and the like, which Date would roll into March.
      return d.getFullYear() === year && d.getMonth() === v.month - 1 && d.getDate() === v.day ? d : undefined
    }
    return { format: (d: Date) => format.format(d), parse, pattern }
  }, [locale])
}
