export function DatePicker({
  value,
  defaultValue = null,
  onValueChange,
  label,
  helperText,
  validationState,
  size = 'md',
  min,
  max,
  isDateDisabled,
  locale,
  weekStartsOn,
  placeholder,
  isFullWidth,
  name,
  disabled,
  readOnly,
  required,
  id,
  className,
  container,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel,
}: DatePickerProps) {
  const { format, parse, pattern } = useDateFormat(locale)
  const today = startOfDay(new Date())
  const [valueState, setValueState] = useState(defaultValue)
  const date = value !== undefined ? value : valueState
  const [text, setText] = useState(() => (date ? format(date) : ''))
  const [invalid, setInvalid] = useState(false)
  const [month, setMonth] = useState(() => date ?? today)
  // Follow a controlled value that changes from outside.
  const [shown, setShown] = useState(date)
  if (!isSameDay(shown, date) && !(shown === null && date === null)) {
    setShown(date)
    setText(date ? format(date) : '')
    setInvalid(false)
  }

  const allowed = (d: Date) =>
    !(min && d < startOfDay(min)) && !(max && d > startOfDay(max)) && !(isDateDisabled?.(d) ?? false)
  const commit = (next: Date | null) => {
    setValueState(next)
    setShown(next)
    setText(next ? format(next) : '')
    setInvalid(false)
    if (next) setMonth(next)
    onValueChange?.(next)
  }
  const commitText = () => {
    const parsed = parse(text)
    if (parsed === undefined || (parsed && !allowed(parsed))) setInvalid(true)
    else if (parsed === null ? date !== null : !isSameDay(parsed, date)) commit(parsed)
    else setInvalid(false)
  }

  return (
    <PickerField
      text={text}
      onTextChange={(t) => {
        setText(t)
        setInvalid(false)
      }}
      onCommit={commitText}
      onShow={() => setMonth(date ?? today)}
      triggerLabel={date ? `Choose date, ${format(date)} selected` : 'Choose date'}
      popupLabel="Choose date"
      hidden={name && <input type="hidden" name={name} value={date ? iso(date) : ''} />}
      label={label}
      helperText={invalid ? `Enter a date as ${pattern}${min || max ? ', within the allowed range' : ''}.` : helperText}
      validationState={invalid ? 'error' : validationState}
      size={size}
      placeholder={placeholder ?? pattern}
      isFullWidth={isFullWidth}
      disabled={disabled}
      readOnly={readOnly}
      required={required}
      id={id}
      className={className}
      container={container}
      aria-label={ariaLabel}
    >
      {({ autoFocus, close }) => (
        <Calendar
          value={date}
          month={month}
          onMonthChange={setMonth}
          onValueChange={(d) => {
            commit(d)
            close()
          }}
          min={min}
          max={max}
          isDateDisabled={isDateDisabled}
          locale={locale}
          weekStartsOn={weekStartsOn}
          autoFocus={autoFocus}
          className={styles.body}
        />
      )}
    </PickerField>
  )
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------ range */

export interface DateRangePreset {
  label: string
  start: Date
  end: Date
}

/** The built-in presets, whole periods around today: Today … Last year. */
export function rangePresets(weekStartsOn: number, today = startOfDay(new Date())): DateRangePreset[] {
  const week = addDays(today, -((today.getDay() - weekStartsOn + 7) % 7))
  const y = today.getFullYear()
  const m = today.getMonth()
  return [
    { label: 'Today', start: today, end: today },
    { label: 'Yesterday', start: addDays(today, -1), end: addDays(today, -1) },
    { label: 'This week', start: week, end: addDays(week, 6) },
    { label: 'Last week', start: addDays(week, -7), end: addDays(week, -1) },
    { label: 'This month', start: new Date(y, m, 1), end: new Date(y, m + 1, 0) },
    { label: 'Last month', start: new Date(y, m - 1, 1), end: new Date(y, m, 0) },
    { label: 'This year', start: new Date(y, 0, 1), end: new Date(y, 11, 31) },
    { label: 'Last year', start: new Date(y - 1, 0, 1), end: new Date(y - 1, 11, 31) },
  ]
}

export interface DateRangePickerProps extends Omit<DatePickerProps, 'value' | 'defaultValue' | 'onValueChange' | 'name'> {
  /** Both ends set, or `null`. */
  value?: DateRange | null
  defaultValue?: DateRange | null
  onValueChange?: (range: DateRange | null) => void
  /** A list beside the calendars: `true` for the built-in one (Today … Last year), or your own. */
  presets?: boolean | DateRangePreset[]
  /** Submitted as `yyyy-mm-dd/yyyy-mm-dd`, an ISO 8601 interval. */
  name?: string
}

const NO_RANGE: DateRange = { start: null, end: null }
const monthIndex = (d: Date) => d.getFullYear() * 12 + d.getMonth()
/** The range's first month on the left, its last on the right; the next month when it spans one. */
const monthsFor = (r: DateRange | null, today: Date): [Date, Date] => {
  const left = r?.start ?? today
  const right = r?.end && monthIndex(r.end) > monthIndex(left) ? r.end : addMonths(left, 1)
  return [left, right]
}
/** The two days as a range, earlier first. */
const ordered = (a: Date | null, b: Date | null): DateRange => (a && b && b < a ? { start: b, end: a } : { start: a, end: b })
const sameRange = (a: DateRange | null, b: DateRange | null) =>
  a === b || (!!a && !!b && isSameDay(a.start, b.start) && isSameDay(a.end, b.end))

export function DateRangePicker({
  value,
  defaultValue = null,
  onValueChange,
  label,
  helperText,
  validationState,
  size = 'md',
  min,
  max,
  isDateDisabled,
  locale,
  weekStartsOn,
  placeholder,
  presets = false,
  isFullWidth,
  name,
  disabled,
  readOnly,
  required,
  id,
  className,
  container,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel,
}: DateRangePickerProps) {
  const { format, parse, pattern } = useDateFormat(locale)
  const today = startOfDay(new Date())
  const [valueState, setValueState] = useState(defaultValue)
  const range = value !== undefined ? value : valueState
  const show = (r: DateRange | null) => (r?.start && r.end ? `${format(r.start)} – ${format(r.end)}` : '')
  const [text, setText] = useState(() => show(range))
  const [invalid, setInvalid] = useState(false)
  const [draft, setDraft] = useState<DateRange>(range ?? NO_RANGE)
  // The two calendars page on their own; the left one always shows the
  // earlier month. Moving one past the other pushes the other along.
  const [months, setMonths] = useState(() => monthsFor(range, today))
  const [shown, setShown] = useState(range)
  if (!sameRange(shown, range)) {
    setShown(range)
    setText(show(range))
    setInvalid(false)
  }

  const presetList = presets === true ? rangePresets(weekStartsOn ?? firstDayOfWeek(locale), today) : presets || []
  const allowed = (d: Date) =>
    !(min && d < startOfDay(min)) && !(max && d > startOfDay(max)) && !(isDateDisabled?.(d) ?? false)
  const commit = (next: DateRange | null) => {
    setValueState(next)
    setShown(next)
    setText(show(next))
    setInvalid(false)
    onValueChange?.(next)
  }
  /** Two dates, each in the locale's order: six numbers, any separators. */
  const commitText = () => {
    const nums = text.match(/\d+/g)
    let parsed: DateRange | null | undefined = null
    if (text.trim()) {
      const a = nums?.length === 6 ? parse(nums.slice(0, 3).join(' ')) : undefined
      const b = nums?.length === 6 ? parse(nums.slice(3).join(' ')) : undefined
      parsed = a && b && allowed(a) && allowed(b) ? ordered(a, b) : undefined
    }
    if (parsed === undefined) setInvalid(true)
    else if (!sameRange(parsed, range)) commit(parsed)
    else setText(show(range))
  }

  return (
    <PickerField
      text={text}
      onTextChange={(t) => {
        setText(t)
        setInvalid(false)
      }}
      onCommit={commitText}
      onShow={() => {
        setDraft(range ?? NO_RANGE)
        setMonths(monthsFor(range, today))
      }}
      triggerLabel={range ? `Choose dates, ${show(range)} selected` : 'Choose dates'}
      popupLabel="Choose dates"
      popupClassName={styles.rangePopup}
      hidden={
        name && <input type="hidden" name={name} value={range?.start && range.end ? `${iso(range.start)}/${iso(range.end)}` : ''} />
      }
      label={label}
      helperText={
        invalid ? `Enter two dates as ${pattern} – ${pattern}${min || max ? ', within the allowed range' : ''}.` : helperText
      }
      validationState={invalid ? 'error' : validationState}
      size={size}
      // Words, not the pattern twice: the pattern stays with assistive tech
      // as the description, and in the error message.
      placeholder={placeholder ?? 'Start – End'}
      formatHint={`${pattern} – ${pattern}`}
      isFullWidth={isFullWidth}
      disabled={disabled}
      readOnly={readOnly}
      required={required}
      id={id}
      className={className}
      container={container}
      aria-label={ariaLabel}
    >
      {({ autoFocus, close }) => {
        // A range applies as soon as both ends are in.
        const choose = (r: DateRange) => {
          setDraft(r)
          if (!r.start || !r.end) return
          if (!sameRange(r, range)) commit(r)
          close()
        }
        // The first click starts a range, the second ends it, either way round.
        const pick = (d: Date) => choose(!draft.start || draft.end ? { start: d, end: null } : ordered(draft.start, d))
        const calendar = { range: draft, onValueChange: pick, min, max, isDateDisabled, locale, weekStartsOn }
        return (
          <>
            {presetList.length > 0 && (
              <div role="group" aria-label="Presets" className={styles.presets}>
                {presetList.map((p) => (
                  <button
                    key={p.label}
                    type="button"
                    aria-pressed={isSameDay(p.start, draft.start) && isSameDay(p.end, draft.end)}
                    className={styles.preset}
                    onClick={() => {
                      setMonths(monthsFor(p, today))
                      choose({ start: p.start, end: p.end })
                    }}
                  >
                    {p.label}
                  </button>
                ))}
              </div>
            )}
            <div className={styles.months}>
              <Calendar
                {...calendar}
                month={months[0]}
                onMonthChange={(m) => setMonths(([, right]) => [m, monthIndex(m) < monthIndex(right) ? right : addMonths(m, 1)])}
                autoFocus={autoFocus}
                className={styles.body}
              />
              {/* Hidden on a narrow screen, where one month fits. */}
              <Calendar
                {...calendar}
                month={months[1]}
                onMonthChange={(m) => setMonths(([left]) => [monthIndex(left) < monthIndex(m) ? left : addMonths(m, -1), m])}
                className={cn(styles.body, styles.second)}
              />
            </div>
          </>
        )
      }}
    </PickerField>
  )
}

# Date Range Picker A field for a span of days: a report period, a booking. Typed like [Da...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'

import * as DateRangePickerStories from './DateRangePicker.stories'

<Meta of={DateRangePickerStories} />

# Date Range Picker

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A field for a span of days: a report period, a booking. Typed like
[Date Picker](?path=/docs/components-inputs-datepicker--docs), or picked
from two months side by side.

<Status of={DateRangePickerStories} />

<Canvas of={DateRangePickerStories.Default} />

## Variants

Two sizes, `sm` and `md`, and the field's validation states, as on Date
Picker. With `presets`, whole periods sit beside the calendars.

| Option | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| No presets | Ranges that rarely line up with a calendar period: a booking, a leave request. |
| `presets` | Reports and filters, where people mostly want "Last month" or "This year". |

<Canvas of={DateRangePickerStories.Presets} />

<Canvas of={DateRangePickerStories.Vietnamese} />

## Resources

Shipped in the same file as Date Picker, which it shares its field and
popover with. From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { DateRangePicker } from 'zweihander/date-picker'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/date-picker.json
```

- Source: [src/components/inputs/DatePicker.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/inputs/DatePicker.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/date-picker](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/date-picker)
- Behaviour: [Base UI Popover](https://base-ui.com/react/components/popover), and the kit's [Calendar](?path=/docs/components-data-display-calendar--docs)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={DateRangePickerStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={DateRangePickerStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The popover holds:

- **Presets**, with `presets`: whole periods, Today to Last year, in a
  column beside the calendars, or a row above them on a narrow screen.
- **Calendars**: two months that page on their own, opening on the
  range's first and last months (this month and the next when empty). The
  left one always stays before the right: paging one past the other
  pushes the other along. One month on a screen narrower than 50rem.

<Canvas of={DateRangePickerStories.PagingApart} />

## Measurements

The field is Date Picker's: `sm` is 32px and `md` is 40px, with the same
padding, icon and type in both.

Presets are 2px apart and at least 7rem wide in the column. The field is
20rem wide unless `isFullWidth`; a range is longer than one date, so give
it room or `isFullWidth`.

## States

  states={[
    { label: 'Empty', content: <DateRangePicker label="Period" locale="en-GB" /> },
    { label: 'Filled' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus' },
    {
      label: 'Error',
      content: <DateRangePicker label="Period" locale="en-GB" validationState="error" helperText="Choose both ends." />,
    },
    {
      label: 'Read-only',
      content: <DateRangePicker label="Period" locale="en-GB" defaultValue={{ start: new Date(2026, 8, 7), end: new Date(2026, 8, 13) }} readOnly />,
    },
    {
      label: 'Disabled',
      content: <DateRangePicker label="Period" locale="en-GB" defaultValue={{ start: new Date(2026, 8, 7), end: new Date(2026, 8, 13) }} disabled />,
    },
  ]}
>
  <DateRangePicker label="Period" locale="en-GB" defaultValue={{ start: new Date(2026, 8, 7), end: new Date(2026, 8, 13) }} />
</States>

The field's states are Date Picker's: a `--color-border-focused` outline while the input
has focus, `--color-text-danger` in error (also while the typed text is not a
range), `--color-background-input` and no calendar button when read-only, 50%
opacity when disabled. A preset matching the picked range
stays in its pressed look.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={DateRangePickerStories} />
</div>

### Design notes

- **Either way round.** The first click starts the range, the second
  ends it; a second click before the first swaps them. So does typing
  the later date first.
- **Presets are whole periods.** "This month" is the 1st to the last
  day, not the 1st to today, so a preset reads the same all month.
- **No Cancel or Apply.** A range applies, and the popover closes, once
  both ends are in; Escape before the second click leaves the value as
  it was.
- **No hover preview.** The band shows once both ends are in; add a
  preview if testing shows people lose track of the first click.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Date Range Picker when the two dates are one thing: a period to
report on, a stay, a sprint. Both ends are set together, start never after
end, and the value is complete or `null`.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={DateRangePickerStories.DoOneField} />}
  doCaption="One field for one period: it cannot be half filled or set back to front."
  dont={<Story of={DateRangePickerStories.DontTwoFields} />}
  dontCaption="Two Date Pickers for one period: here the end is before the start, and nothing stops it."
/>

## When not to use

- **For one date.** Use a
  [Date Picker](?path=/docs/components-inputs-datepicker--docs).
- **When one end is optional**, such as a contract with no end date. The
  range needs both ends; use two Date Pickers and check their order
  yourself.

## Accessibility

- As Date Picker: a labelled text box, an error state with the expected
  pattern, and the calendars in a dialog named "Choose dates". Without a
  visible label, pass `aria-label` to name the input.
- The calendar button is named "Choose dates", with the current range
  when there is one.
- `readOnly` works as on Date Picker: `readonly` on the input, no
  calendar button, and a click or Alt+Down opens nothing.
- Every day in the range has `aria-selected`, so the span is announced,
  not only its ends.
- A day of the month either side is decoration: hidden from assistive
  tech and not pickable, so each day is one button.
- Presets are toggle buttons in a group named "Presets"; the one that
  matches the picked range is `aria-pressed`.
- After both ends are in, the field goes back to rest, as Date Picker's
  does after a pick.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

export interface DividerProps extends ComponentProps<'hr'> {
  orientation?: 'horizontal' | 'vertical'
  /** Indents both ends so the line stops short of its container's edges. */
  inset?: boolean
  /** Line thickness: 1px, 2px, 4px. */
  size?: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'
  /** uiguideline calls this `variant`; renamed because `variant` means color here. */
  appearance?: 'solid' | 'dashed'

  orientation = 'horizontal',
  inset = false,

      className={cn(

        styles[orientation],
        styles[size],

      )}

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import { Divider } from './Divider'
import * as DividerStories from './Divider.stories'

export const Stack = ({ children }) => (
  <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 'var(--space-3)', inlineSize: '8rem' }}>
    <span>Above</span>
    {children}
    <span>Below</span>
  </div>
)

<Meta of={DividerStories} />

# Divider

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A thin line that separates content into groups: sections of a card, items
in a toolbar, blocks of a page.

<Status of={DividerStories} />

<Canvas of={DividerStories.Default} />

## Variants

| Appearance | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `solid` | Almost everywhere: the quiet default. |
| `dashed` | A boundary that is softer or provisional: a drop zone, a "more below" break, a draft section. |

<Canvas of={DividerStories.Dashed} />

A **vertical** divider separates items in a row: toolbar groups, links in
a footer. It has no fixed height and stretches to its flex row.

<Canvas of={DividerStories.Vertical} />

**Inset** stops the line short of the container's edges, so it aligns with
the text in a padded list rather than running edge to edge.

<Canvas of={DividerStories.Inset} />

<Canvas of={DividerStories.Sizes} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Divider } from 'zweihander/divider'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/divider.json
```

- Source: [src/components/atomic-elements/Divider.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/atomic-elements/Divider.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/divider](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/divider)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={DividerStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={DividerStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

One part. The line is a border, top for horizontal and start for
vertical, and the box shrinks to it: a vertical divider is exactly as
wide as its line.

## Measurements

Thickness is whole pixels, not a token: `--border-width` covers 1px and
`--border-width-selected` 2px, and a divider's three weights stay its own.

| Size | Thickness |
| --- | --- |
| `sm` | 1px |
| `md` | 2px |
| `lg` | 4px |

<SpecTable
  caption="inset, every size"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Horizontal line', property: 'Inline margin', token: '--space-4' },
    { part: 'Vertical line', property: 'Block margin', token: '--space-2' },
  ]}
/>

## Color

Every size and appearance uses the same colour.

<SpecTable caption="Every appearance" rows={[{ part: 'Line', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-border' }]} />

## States

A divider is not interactive: no hover, focus or pressed. It looks the same
whether it is announced or decorative; only a screen reader tells them
apart.

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Solid', content: <Stack><Divider /></Stack> },
    { label: 'Dashed', content: <Stack><Divider appearance="dashed" size="md" /></Stack> },
    { label: 'Inset', content: <Stack><Divider inset /></Stack> },
    { label: 'Decorative', content: <Stack><Divider aria-hidden /></Stack> },
  ]}
/>

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={DividerStories} />
</div>

Every other `<hr>` attribute passes through, including `ref` and
`aria-hidden`.

### Differences from the spec

- **`appearance`, not `variant`.** In this kit `variant` always means a
  colour by intent (primary, destructive…) and `appearance` means a style.
  Solid versus dashed is a style.
- **Thickness is raw px.** `--border-width` and `--border-width-selected`
  cover 1px and 2px strokes; a divider is the only component that needs a
  third, so its three weights stay its own.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Divider between groups that spacing alone does not separate: the
sections of a menu, the blocks of a settings page, groups in a toolbar.
Divide groups, not every item: a line after each row turns a list into
stripes and makes the real breaks harder to see.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={DividerStories.DoDivideGroups} />}
  doCaption="One line between two groups: the break carries meaning."
  dont={<Story of={DividerStories.DontDivideEveryItem} />}
  dontCaption="A line after every item: nothing stands out as a group."
/>

## When not to use

- **Where space already separates.** Cards, list items with padding and
  headed sections are grouped by their own whitespace; a line adds noise.
- **As the only thing that tells groups apart.** The line is faint on
  purpose (see Accessibility). Pair it with a heading or space.
- **For a border of a component.** Draw that with the component's own
  border, not a Divider beside it.

## Accessibility

- `<hr>` is announced as a separator. Vertical dividers add
  `aria-orientation="vertical"`; horizontal ones don't, because that is
  already the default.
- If the line is purely decorative, e.g. between two icons that are
  already grouped, pass `aria-hidden` so it isn't announced at all.
- The `--color-border` colour is below 3:1 against the background on purpose: a
  divider is decoration and is not required to meet the non-text contrast
  ratio. Never let a divider be the only thing that tells groups apart.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-vite'
import { STORY_RENDERED } from 'storybook/internal/core-events'
import { addons } from 'storybook/preview-api'
import { expect, userEvent, waitFor, within } from 'storybook/test'
import { Button } from '@/components/buttons/Button'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '.'

/* Stories for the docs blocks themselves, tagged !dev: they run as tests (and
   a11y) like any story, but stay out of the sidebar and the Playground. The
   Internal / Docs blocks page shows them in use. */
const meta = {
  title: 'Internal/Docs blocks',
  tags: ['!dev'],
} satisfies Meta

export default meta
type Story = StoryObj<typeof meta>

const example = (
  <Button startIcon={<Icon name="plus" />} size="md">
    Add item
  </Button>
)

const tabs = (
  <DocTabs>
    <DocTab value="overview">
      <p>What it is.</p>
    </DocTab>
    <DocTab value="specs">
      <p>How it is built.</p>
    </DocTab>
    <DocTab value="guidelines">
      <p>How to use it.</p>
    </DocTab>
  </DocTabs>
)

export const Tabs: Story = {
  render: () => tabs,
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    await expect(canvas.getByRole('tablist', { name: 'Documentation' })).toBeVisible()
    const [overview, specs, guidelines] = canvas.getAllByRole('tab')
    await expect([overview, specs, guidelines].map((t) => t.textContent)).toEqual(['Overview', 'Specs', 'Guidelines'])
    // Overview first, always.
    await expect(overview).toHaveAttribute('aria-selected', 'true')
    await expect(canvas.getByRole('tabpanel')).toHaveTextContent('What it is.')
    // Mouse.
    await userEvent.click(specs)
    await waitFor(() => expect(canvas.getByRole('tabpanel')).toHaveTextContent('How it is built.'))
    // Arrow keys select as they move: a docs page, not a toolbar.
    await userEvent.keyboard('{ArrowRight}')
    await waitFor(() => expect(guidelines).toHaveAttribute('aria-selected', 'true'))
    await waitFor(() => expect(canvas.getByRole('tabpanel')).toHaveTextContent('How to use it.'))
    await userEvent.keyboard('{ArrowLeft}{ArrowLeft}')
    await waitFor(() => expect(overview).toHaveAttribute('aria-selected', 'true'))
    await expect(overview).toHaveFocus()
  },
}

const anatomy = (
  <Anatomy
    parts={[
      { name: 'Container', selector: 'button', description: 'The box.' },
      { name: 'Start icon', selector: 'svg', description: 'Decorative: `aria-hidden`.' },
    ]}
  >
    {example}
  </Anatomy>
)

export const AnatomyMarkers: Story = {
  name: 'Anatomy',
  render: () => anatomy,
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    // One marker per part, each named by number and part.
    const markers = await canvas.findAllByRole('img', { name: /^\d: / })
    await expect(markers.map((m) => m.getAttribute('aria-label'))).toEqual(['1: Container', '2: Start icon'])
    await expect(markers.map((m) => m.textContent)).toEqual(['1', '2'])
    // Each sits above its part, centred on it, with a line down to the part.
    for (const [marker, part] of [
      [markers[0], canvas.getByRole('button')],
      [markers[1], canvas.getByRole('button').querySelector('svg')!],
    ] as const) {
      const m = marker.getBoundingClientRect()
      const p = part.getBoundingClientRect()
      await expect(Math.abs(m.left + m.width / 2 - (p.left + p.width / 2))).toBeLessThanOrEqual(1)
      await expect(m.bottom).toBeLessThan(p.top)
      const line = (marker.previousElementSibling as HTMLElement).getBoundingClientRect()
      await expect(Math.abs(line.bottom - p.top)).toBeLessThanOrEqual(1)
    }
    // The key lists every part.
    const key = canvas.getByRole('table')
    await expect(within(key).getByRole('rowheader', { name: 'Start icon' })).toBeVisible()
    await expect(key).not.toHaveTextContent('Not found')
    // Backticks in a description become inline code.
    await expect(within(key).getByText('aria-hidden').tagName).toBe('CODE')
    await expect(key).not.toHaveTextContent('`')
  },
}

export const AnatomyCrowded: Story = {
  render: () => (
    <Anatomy
      parts={[
        { name: 'Container', selector: 'button' },
        { name: 'Label', selector: 'button' },
        { name: 'Again', selector: 'button' },
      ]}
    >
      {example}
    </Anatomy>
  ),
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    // Parts with the same centre still get three markers that do not overlap:
    // one above, one below, one slid aside.
    const boxes = (await canvas.findAllByRole('img', { name: /^\d: / })).map((m) => m.getBoundingClientRect())
    await expect(boxes).toHaveLength(3)
    for (const [i, a] of boxes.entries())
      for (const b of boxes.slice(i + 1))
        await expect(a.right <= b.left || b.right <= a.left || a.bottom <= b.top || b.bottom <= a.top).toBe(true)
  },
}

export const AnatomyMissingPart: Story = {
  render: () => (
    <Anatomy
      parts={[
        { name: 'Container', selector: 'button' },
        { name: 'Badge', selector: '[data-badge]' },
      ]}
    >
      {example}
    </Anatomy>
  ),
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    // A selector that matches nothing gets no marker, and says so in the key.
    await expect(await canvas.findAllByRole('img', { name: /^\d: / })).toHaveLength(1)
    await expect(canvas.getByRole('table')).toHaveTextContent('Not found: [data-badge] matches nothing in the example.')
  },
}

const spec = (
  <SpecTable
    caption="Measurements, md"
    rows={[
      { part: 'Container', property: 'Height', token: '--control-md' },
      { part: 'Container', property: 'Background', token: '--color-surface' },
      { part: 'Label', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body' },
    ]}
  />
)

export const Spec: Story = {
  render: () => spec,
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    const rows = canvas.getAllByRole('row').slice(1) as HTMLTableRowElement[]
    const value = (row: HTMLTableRowElement) => row.cells[3]
    // A length resolves to px, calc() and all.
    await expect(value(rows[0])).toHaveTextContent(/^32px$/)
    await expect(value(rows[0])).toHaveAttribute('data-kind', 'length')
    // A colour shows a swatch and the computed colour.
    const background = value(rows[1])
    await expect(background).toHaveAttribute('data-kind', 'color')
    await expect(background.querySelector('[aria-hidden="true"]')).not.toBeNull()
    // Anything else shows its declared value.
    await expect(value(rows[2])).toHaveAttribute('data-kind', 'raw')
    // The value follows the theme.
    const html = document.documentElement
    const wasDark = html.classList.contains('dark')
    const before = background.textContent
    html.classList.toggle('dark')
    try {
      await waitFor(() => expect(background.textContent).not.toBe(before))
    } finally {
      html.classList.toggle('dark', wasDark)
    }
    await waitFor(() => expect(background.textContent).toBe(before))
  },
}

const states = (
  <States
    states={[
      { label: 'Enabled' },
      { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
      { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
      { label: 'Pressed', pseudo: 'active' },
      {
        label: 'Disabled',
        content: (
          <Button startIcon={<Icon name="plus" />} disabled>
            Add item
          </Button>
        ),
      },
    ]}
  >
    {example}
  </States>
)

export const StateRow: Story = {
  name: 'States',
  render: () => states,
  play: async ({ canvasElement }) => {
    // Storybook announces each render, and the addon rewrites the stylesheets
    // then (docs pages included). The test runner announces nothing, so play
    // Storybook's part.
    addons.getChannel().emit(STORY_RENDERED)
    const cells = within(canvasElement).getAllByRole('listitem')
    await expect(cells.map((c) => c.lastElementChild!.textContent)).toEqual(['Enabled', 'Hover', 'Focus', 'Pressed', 'Disabled'])
    const stage = (label: string) => canvasElement.querySelector<HTMLElement>(`[data-state="${label}"]`)!
    await expect(stage('Hover')).toHaveClass('pseudo-hover-all')
    await expect(stage('Focus')).toHaveClass('pseudo-focus-visible-all')
    await expect(stage('Pressed')).toHaveClass('pseudo-active-all')
    await expect(stage('Disabled').querySelector('button')).toBeDisabled()
    // The forced states actually paint: the addon rewrote :hover and friends.
    const look = (label: string) => {
      const s = getComputedStyle(stage(label).querySelector('button')!)
      return `${s.backgroundColor} ${s.outlineStyle}`
    }
    // What the addon did to the stylesheets, for the failure message.
    const rewritten = () => {
      const button = stage('Hover').querySelector('button')!
      const rules = [...document.styleSheets].flatMap((sheet) => {
        try {
          return [...sheet.cssRules]
        } catch {
          return []
        }
      })
      const hover = rules.filter((r): r is CSSStyleRule => r instanceof CSSStyleRule && r.selectorText.includes(':hover'))
      const forced = hover.filter((r) => r.selectorText.includes('pseudo-hover-all'))
      const engaged = forced.filter((r) => button.matches(r.selectorText))
      return `${document.styleSheets.length} sheets, ${hover.length} :hover rules, ${forced.length} rewritten, ${engaged.length} reach the button: ${engaged.map((r) => r.cssText).join(' | ').slice(0, 300) || hover.find((r) => r.selectorText.includes('button'))?.cssText.slice(0, 300)}`
    }
    await waitFor(() => {
      // Again on each try: a stylesheet Vite injects late is rewritten too.
      addons.getChannel().emit(STORY_RENDERED)
      expect(look('Hover'), rewritten()).not.toBe(look('Enabled'))
    })
    // No transition to wait out: each state shows its end value at once.
    await expect(getComputedStyle(stage('Hover').querySelector('button')!).transitionDuration).toBe('0s')
    await expect(look('Pressed')).not.toBe(look('Hover'))
    await expect(getComputedStyle(stage('Focus').querySelector('button')!).outlineStyle).toBe('solid')
  },
}

}

# Empty State What a list, a table or a page shows when there is nothing in it yet: why it...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import * as EmptyStateStories from './EmptyState.stories'

<Meta of={EmptyStateStories} />

# Empty State

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

What a list, a table or a page shows when there is nothing in it yet: why
it is empty, and what to do about it.

<Status of={EmptyStateStories} />

<Canvas of={EmptyStateStories.FirstUse} />

## Variants

There are three kinds of empty, and they need three kinds of copy. The
component is the same; the words and the action are not.

| Kind | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| First use | Nothing has been made yet. Say what will live here, and offer the way in: "No projects yet", New project. |
| No results | A search or a filter matched nothing. Say what was searched, and offer to clear it: "No projects match", Clear search. |
| Cleared out | Everything is done. Often no action at all: "All caught up". |

<Canvas of={EmptyStateStories.Default} />

<Canvas of={EmptyStateStories.TitleOnly} />

`size="sm"` fits a panel or a table body; `md` fills a page or a section.

<Canvas of={EmptyStateStories.Small} />

- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/empty-state](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/empty-state)
- Behaviour: a plain element, no Base UI part
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>

<Anatomy parts={EmptyStateStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={EmptyStateStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

Only the title is required. [Error State](?path=/docs/components-states-errorstate--docs)
and [Success State](?path=/docs/components-states-successstate--docs) are
this layout with the disc in their own tone.

## Measurements

The icon is half the disc's size. Title and description are at most
464px wide at `md` and 304px at `sm` (29rem and 19rem, Atlassian's wide
and narrow empty state), so they stay a short paragraph on a wide page.
`md` keeps Atlassian's rhythm: 48px above and below, 24px under the
image, 16px under the heading, 24px above the buttons, 8px between them.
`sm` keeps the 16px and 24px and is 16px under a smaller image.

Empty State itself is static: it has no hover, focus or pressed look. Its
action does, and those are the action's own (here, an outlined Button).

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use an Empty State wherever a list, a table or a page can have nothing in
it: before the first item is made, after a search matches nothing, when
everything is done. Write the title for the reader's situation, and give
them the next step.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={EmptyStateStories.FirstUse} />}
  doCaption="Say what is empty and what will live here, and offer the way in."
  dont={<Story of={EmptyStateStories.DontNoData} />}
  dontCaption="“No data” says neither why nor what to do next."
/>

## When not to use

- **When loading failed.** Use an
  [Error State](?path=/docs/components-states-errorstate--docs): "No
  projects" when the request failed tells the reader their work is gone.
- **When a flow has finished.** Use a
  [Success State](?path=/docs/components-states-successstate--docs).
- **While content is loading.** Use a Skeleton or a Spinner: an empty
  state shown before the data arrives flashes the wrong message.

## Accessibility

- The title is a real heading, so a screen reader user jumping by
  headings finds out the area is empty. Set `headingLevel` to fit the
  outline: `3` inside a section headed by an `h2`.
- The icon is `aria-hidden`; the title has to say it all.
- It is not a live region, so it is not announced when it replaces
  results. If a search updates as you type, announce the count elsewhere,
  in a `role="status"` line such as "0 results".

</DocTab>

import type { ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import { EmptyState, type EmptyStateProps } from './EmptyState'
import styles from './ErrorState.module.css'

export interface ErrorStateProps extends Omit<EmptyStateProps, 'title'> {
  /** What failed, in the reader's words. */
  title?: ReactNode
  /** A reference for support, e.g. an error code or request id. Shown small, selectable. */
  details?: ReactNode
  /** Announce it when it replaces content that was loading (`role="alert"`). */
  isLive?: boolean
}

/**
 * What a list, panel or page shows when loading it failed: why, and a way
 * forward, usually a retry. Empty State's layout in the danger tone.
 */
export function ErrorState({
  title = 'Something went wrong',
  icon = <Icon name="danger" />,
  description,
  details,
  isLive = false,
  className,
  ...props
}: ErrorStateProps) {
  return (
    <EmptyState
      role={isLive ? 'alert' : undefined}
      title={title}
      icon={icon}
      description={
        (description || details) && (
          <>
            {description}
            {details && <span className={styles.details}>{details}</span>}
          </>
        )
      }
      className={cn(styles.error, className)}
      {...props}
    />
  )
}

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use an Error State in place of content that failed to load: a list, a
panel, a whole page. Say what failed in the reader's words, say that
nothing is lost when that is true, and offer a way forward.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={ErrorStateStories.Default} />}
  doCaption="Say what failed, that nothing is lost, and offer to try again."
  dont={<Story of={ErrorStateStories.DontRawError} />}
  dontCaption="A raw error is for developers, and with no action the reader is stuck."
/>

Details are for support, not for the reader: keep them small and
selectable so they can be pasted into a message.

## When not to use

- **When there is simply nothing there.** Use an
  [Empty State](?path=/docs/components-states-emptystate--docs).
- **When an action failed but the screen is fine**, such as a save. Use an
  Alert or a Toast and keep the reader's work on screen.
- **For a field's error.** Show it on the field, through its own error
  message.

## Accessibility

- The title is a real heading, as on Empty State. Set `headingLevel` to
  fit the outline.
- The icon is `aria-hidden`; the title says what failed.
- `isLive` makes it a `role="alert"`: use it when the error replaces
  content that was loading, so a screen reader hears that it failed.
  Without it, nothing is announced.

<Canvas of={ErrorStateStories.Live} />

# Field The label, required mark, info note and helper text for a control that has none of...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import { Field, FieldControl } from './Field'
import { boxClass, inputStyles } from './InputField'
import * as FieldStories from './Field.stories'

<Meta of={FieldStories} />

# Field

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

The label, required mark, info note and helper text for a control
that has none of its own.

<Status of={FieldStories} />

Every Zweihänder control (Text Input, Select, Checkbox and the rest)
already carries this anatomy. Field is for the control that does not: a
native element the kit has no component for, a Base UI primitive, or one
of your own. It wires the label, description and invalid state to it
through Base UI Field.

<Canvas of={FieldStories.Default} />

## Variants

There is one appearance. What changes is which optional parts are there.

<Canvas of={FieldStories.Validation} />

| Part | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `helperText` | The format, limits or purpose, in a line; the error message when invalid. |
| `labelInfo` | A longer rule or explanation most people do not need every time: behind an info button, so the form stays short. |
| `validationState` | `error` when the value cannot be accepted: the helper text says what to change, and it and the edge turn red. `success` for a value checked and accepted. |
| `required` | An asterisk after the label. |

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Field } from 'zweihander/field'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/field.json
```

- Source: [src/components/inputs/Field.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/inputs/Field.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/text-input](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/text-input) (the label and helper parts)
- Behaviour: [Base UI Field](https://base-ui.com/react/components/field)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={FieldStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={FieldStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The control is whatever you put inside; in these stories it is a native
time input in the same box as Text Input.

The field is 20rem wide, capped at its container; with `isFullWidth` it
fills the container. The info note is at most 22rem wide and opens above
the button.

## Color

  caption="default"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Label', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text' },
    { part: 'Required asterisk', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-danger' },

    { part: 'Helper text', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-subtlest' },

    { part: 'Info note', property: 'Border', token: '--color-border' },
    { part: 'Info note', property: 'Shadow', token: '--shadow-overlay' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable

/>

<SpecTable
  caption="error"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Helper text', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-danger' },
    { part: 'Field box edge', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-danger' },
  ]}
/>

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    {
      label: 'Error',
      content: (
        <Field label="Start time" validationState="error" helperText="Enter a time between 06:00 and 22:00.">
          <span className={boxClass('md')}>
            <FieldControl type="time" className={inputStyles.control} />
          </span>
        </Field>
      ),
    },
    {
      label: 'Read-only',
      content: (
        <Field label="Start time" helperText="Set by the rota.">
          <span className={boxClass('md')}>
            <FieldControl defaultValue="09:00" readOnly className={inputStyles.control} />
          </span>
        </Field>
      ),
    },
    {
      label: 'Disabled',
      content: (
        <Field label="Start time" helperText="Pick a shift first." disabled>
          <span className={boxClass('md')}>
            <FieldControl type="time" className={inputStyles.control} />
          </span>
        </Field>
      ),
    },
  ]}
>
  <Field label="Start time" labelInfo="When the shift starts." helperText="HH:MM">
    <span className={boxClass('md')}>
      <FieldControl type="time" className={inputStyles.control} />
    </span>
  </Field>
</States>

- **Hover** and **focus** belong to the control. The info button turns
  `--color-text` on hover and draws the `--color-border-focused` outline on keyboard focus.
- **Error** colours the helper text, which then says what to change, and
  the edge of a field box inside.
- **Read-only** is set on the control (`readOnly`), not on the Field.
  A field box with a read-only control inside is filled with
  `--color-background-input`; the edge, label and helper stay as they are.
- **Disabled** disables the control; how it dims is the control's own. The
  info button stays active: the note may say why the field is disabled.

## API

<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={FieldStories} />
</div>

`FieldControl` is Base UI's `Field.Control`: an `<input>` by default, any
element through `render`, with the label, description and invalid state
wired to it. A Base UI control (Slider, Number Field, Checkbox) inside a
Field wires itself.

### Differences from the spec

- **No separate error part.** As in every Zweihänder control, the error
  is the helper text in the error state (the kit's API convention), so a
  field never shows a hint and an error at once.
- **The info note is a toggletip**, opened by press or Enter, not a
  hover tooltip: tooltips do not open on touch.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Field round a control that has no label of its own. Keep the helper
text to a line; put a longer rule behind `labelInfo`.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={FieldStories.DoLongNoteInInfo} />}
  doCaption="The format in a line under the control; the full rule behind the info button."
  dont={<Story of={FieldStories.DontLongHelper} />}
  dontCaption="A paragraph of helper text pushes every field below it down, on every visit."
/>

An **error** says what to change, not only that something is wrong.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={FieldStories.DoSayWhatToFix} />}
  doCaption="The error names the allowed range."
  dont={<Story of={FieldStories.DontVagueError} />}
  dontCaption="'Invalid value' leaves people guessing what to change."
/>

### Read-only

A value people need to see but cannot change here (set by a rule,
another team or their role) stays a field: put `readOnly` on the control
and say in `helperText` why, and who can change it. Every Zweihänder
control takes `readOnly`. The boxed fields (Text Input, Textarea,
Search, Number Input, Select, Combobox, Date Picker, Date Range Picker)
all look the same: a filled box, still focusable, the value selectable
and submitted with the form. Checkbox, Radio, Switch and Rating keep
their look, since their mark is the value, and only stop changing.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={FieldStories.DoReadOnlyWithReason} />}
  doCaption="Read-only: readable, focusable, copyable, and it says who can change it."
  dont={<Story of={FieldStories.DontDisableToLock} />}
  dontCaption="Disabled: dimmed below readable contrast, skipped by Tab, not submitted."
/>

- **Not disabled.** A locked value is still read and copied; a disabled
  one is not (Disabled, below, is for "not yet").
- **No lock icon by default.** The fill already marks the state, and an
  icon would need its own name for screen readers; the helper text says
  more than a lock.
- **A whole record that cannot be edited** is not a form of read-only
  fields: show it as a description list (`<dl>`), label and value with no
  box.

### Disabled

Disable a control only while it does not apply yet, and people can change
that on the same screen: a choice earlier in the form, a step not done.
Say what turns it on, in `helperText` or in the control that does it.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={FieldStories.DoDisableWithReason} />}
  doCaption="Disabled for now, and the helper text says what turns it on."
  dont={<Story of={FieldStories.DontDisableWithoutReason} />}
  dontCaption="Nothing says why it is off or how to turn it on."
/>

- **Disable for "not yet", hide for "not you", read-only for "not
  changeable here".** An action or a field people's role never lets them
  use, and that they do not need to read, is left out, not shown disabled:
  a control they can never turn on is noise and a support ticket. A value
  they need to see but may not change is read-only.
- **No tooltip for the reason.** A disabled control leaves the tab order,
  so a tooltip on it never opens by keyboard or on touch. Put the reason
  in text people can see; `labelInfo` stays active on a disabled Field.
- **Dimmed on purpose.** Disabled controls are exempt from contrast
  rules and drop below readable contrast, one more reason not to disable
  a value people need to read.
- **Fields that turn off together** each take `disabled`, and one line of
  text near them says what turns them on.

## When not to use

- **Round a Zweihänder control.** Text Input, Textarea, Number Input,
  Select, Combobox, Date Picker, Checkbox, Switch and Radio have their own
  label, helper text and validation; a Field round one gives it two labels.
- **For a group of controls** under one name, use a `<fieldset>` and
  `<legend>`, or Radio's own group.

## Accessibility

- The label is a real `<label>` for the control: it is the control's
  accessible name, and clicking it focuses the control.
- `helperText` is the control's description (`aria-describedby`), read
  after its name.
- A read-only control keeps its place in the tab order and has the
  `readonly` attribute, so screen readers announce it as read-only;
  typing does not change the value, and the reason in `helperText` is read
  as its description.
- A disabled control is left out of the tab order; its helper text is still its description, so a screen reader browsing to it
  hears why.
- `validationState="error"` sets `aria-invalid="true"` on the control.
  Colour is never the only signal: the helper text says what is wrong.
- The required asterisk is `aria-hidden`; put `required` on the control so
  screen readers announce it.
- The info button is named by `infoLabel` ("More information") and
  described by the label, so a list of buttons tells which field each is
  for. It sits outside the `<label>`: pressing it opens the note without
  focusing the control. Enter or a press opens the note, a dialog named by
  the label; Escape closes it and returns focus to the button.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

'use client'

import { useEffect, useId, useRef, useState, type DragEvent, type ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import { Button } from '../buttons/Button'
import { Spinner } from '../loaders/Spinner'
import styles from './FileUploader.module.css'

export interface FileRejection {
  file: File
  reason: 'type' | 'size' | 'count'
  /** Ready to show, e.g. "photo.gif is not an accepted type." */
  message: string
}

export interface FileStatus {
  /** 0–100 while uploading: a ring beside the remove button, hidden at 100. */
  progress?: number
  /** Short, beside the remove button in the danger colour, e.g. "Upload failed". */
  error?: string
}

export interface FileUploaderProps {
  files?: File[]
  defaultFiles?: File[]
  /** The list after an add or a remove. Rejected files are never in it. */
  onFilesChange?: (files: File[]) => void
  /** Files that were dropped or chosen but did not pass `accept`, `maxSize` or `maxFiles`. */
  onReject?: (rejections: FileRejection[]) => void
  /** As the native attribute: extensions and MIME types, e.g. `".pdf,image/*"`. Also checked on drop. */
  accept?: string
  multiple?: boolean
  /** In bytes. */
  maxSize?: number
  maxFiles?: number
  label?: ReactNode
  /** Inside the drop zone, under the button, e.g. "PNG or JPG, up to 5 MB." */
  helperText?: ReactNode
  /** Upload progress or a server error per file. The uploader does not upload: you do. */
  getFileStatus?: (file: File) => FileStatus | undefined
  /** Submitted with the form, as a native file input. */
  name?: string
  disabled?: boolean
  required?: boolean
  isFullWidth?: boolean
  className?: string
}

const sizeFormat = (bytes: number) => {
  const [value, unit] =
    bytes >= 1e6 ? [bytes / 1e6, 'megabyte'] : bytes >= 1e3 ? [bytes / 1e3, 'kilobyte'] : [bytes, 'byte']
  return new Intl.NumberFormat(undefined, { style: 'unit', unit, unitDisplay: 'short', maximumFractionDigits: 1 }).format(value)
}

/** Does the file match the `accept` list? Extensions, exact MIME types and `type/*`. */
function accepts(file: File, accept?: string) {
  if (!accept) return true
  const name = file.name.toLowerCase()
  const type = file.type.toLowerCase()
  return accept
    .split(',')
    .map((t) => t.trim().toLowerCase())
    .filter(Boolean)
    .some((t) => (t.startsWith('.') ? name.endsWith(t) : t.endsWith('/*') ? type.startsWith(t.slice(0, -1)) : type === t))
}

function syncInput(input: HTMLInputElement | null, files: File[]) {
  if (!input || typeof DataTransfer === 'undefined') return
  const transfer = new DataTransfer()
  files.forEach((f) => transfer.items.add(f))
  input.files = transfer.files
}

type FileKind = 'word' | 'excel' | 'powerpoint' | 'pdf' | 'image' | 'audio'

function fileKind(file: File): FileKind | undefined {
  const ext = file.name.split('.').pop()?.toLowerCase() ?? ''
  const type = file.type.toLowerCase()
  if (ext === 'pdf' || type === 'application/pdf') return 'pdf'
  if (['doc', 'docx', 'odt', 'rtf'].includes(ext)) return 'word'
  if (['xls', 'xlsx', 'csv', 'ods'].includes(ext)) return 'excel'
  if (['ppt', 'pptx', 'odp'].includes(ext)) return 'powerpoint'
  if (type.startsWith('image/')) return 'image'
  if (type.startsWith('audio/') || ['mp3', 'wav', 'm4a', 'ogg', 'flac'].includes(ext)) return 'audio'
}

const badgeText: Record<FileKind, string> = {
  word: 'DOC',
  excel: 'XLS',
  powerpoint: 'PPT',
  pdf: 'PDF',
  image: 'IMG',
  audio: 'MP3',
}

/**
 * A page with a coloured type badge, after Microsoft 365's file icons, on
 * the Figma library's 20px grid. Unknown types get the bare page. DOC and
 * MP3 are wider letters, so their badge is 16px, the rest 14px.
 */
function FileTypeIcon({ file }: { file: File }) {
  const kind = fileKind(file)
  const badgeWidth = kind === 'word' || kind === 'audio' ? 16 : 14
  return (
    <svg className={styles.fileIcon} data-kind={kind} viewBox="0 0 20 20" aria-hidden="true">
      <path className={styles.page} d="M4 1h8l5 5v13H4Z" />
      <path className={styles.fold} d="M12 1l5 5h-5Z" />
      {kind && (
        <g>
          <rect className={styles.badge} x="1" y="10" width={badgeWidth} height="8" rx="1.5" />
          <text className={styles.badgeText} x={1 + badgeWidth / 2} y="14" textAnchor="middle" dominantBaseline="central">
            {badgeText[kind]}
          </text>
        </g>
      )}
    </svg>
  )
}

const sameFile = (a: File, b: File) => a.name === b.name && a.size === b.size && a.lastModified === b.lastModified

export function FileUploader({
  files: filesProp,
  defaultFiles = [],
  onFilesChange,
  onReject,
  accept,
  multiple = false,
  maxSize,
  maxFiles,
  label,
  helperText,
  getFileStatus,
  name,
  disabled = false,
  required,
  isFullWidth,
  className,
}: FileUploaderProps) {
  const id = useId()
  const inputRef = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null)
  const chooseRef = useRef<HTMLElement>(null)
  const listRef = useRef<HTMLUListElement>(null)
  const [filesState, setFilesState] = useState(defaultFiles)
  const files = filesProp ?? filesState
  const [rejections, setRejections] = useState<FileRejection[]>([])
  const [dragging, setDragging] = useState(false)
  const [announcement, setAnnouncement] = useState('')
  const limit = multiple ? (maxFiles ?? Infinity) : 1

  const [missing, setMissing] = useState(false)

  // The native input carries the list, so a plain form post sends it. Also
  // after a controlled `files` changes from outside, e.g. cleared after upload.
  useEffect(() => syncInput(inputRef.current, files), [files])

  const update = (next: File[]) => {
    setFilesState(next)
    syncInput(inputRef.current, next)
    onFilesChange?.(next)
  }

  const add = (incoming: File[]) => {
    const rejected: FileRejection[] = []
    const accepted: File[] = []
    for (const file of incoming) {
      if (!accepts(file, accept)) rejected.push({ file, reason: 'type', message: `${file.name} is not an accepted type.` })
      else if (maxSize !== undefined && file.size > maxSize)
        rejected.push({ file, reason: 'size', message: `${file.name} is larger than ${sizeFormat(maxSize)}.` })
      else accepted.push(file)
    }
    // A single-file uploader replaces its file, but only with one that passed:
    // a rejected drop leaves the chosen file where it is. A multiple one appends.
    let next = multiple ? [...files] : []
    for (const file of accepted) {
      if (next.some((f) => sameFile(f, file))) continue
      if (next.length >= limit)
        rejected.push({
          file,
          reason: 'count',
          message: multiple ? `${file.name} was not added: the limit is ${limit} files.` : `${file.name} was not added: only one file can be added.`,
        })
      else next.push(file)
    }
    if (!multiple && next.length === 0) next = files
    const added = next.filter((f) => !files.some((g) => sameFile(f, g))).length
    setRejections(rejected)
    if (rejected.length) onReject?.(rejected)
    if (next.length) setMissing(false)
    if (added || next.length !== files.length) update(next)
    else syncInput(inputRef.current, files)
    setAnnouncement(
      [added ? `${added} ${added === 1 ? 'file' : 'files'} added.` : '', rejected.length ? `${rejected.length} not added.` : '']
        .filter(Boolean)
        .join(' '),
    )
  }

  const remove = (index: number) => {
    const removed = files[index]
    const next = files.filter((_, i) => i !== index)
    update(next)
    setAnnouncement(`${removed.name} removed.`)
    // Focus goes to the next remove button, else the previous, else Choose.
    requestAnimationFrame(() => {
      const buttons = listRef.current?.querySelectorAll<HTMLButtonElement>('button[data-remove]')
      const target = buttons?.[Math.min(index, buttons.length - 1)] ?? chooseRef.current
      target?.focus()
    })
  }

  const onDrop = (e: DragEvent) => {
    e.preventDefault()
    setDragging(false)
    if (!disabled) add([...e.dataTransfer.files])
  }

  const helperId = `${id}-helper`
  const errorId = `${id}-errors`

  return (
    // A group named by the label: the control inside is a button with its own
    // name ("Choose files"), so a <label> would have nothing to label.
    <div
      role="group"
      aria-labelledby={label ? `${id}-label` : undefined}
      className={cn(styles.uploader, isFullWidth && styles.fullWidth, disabled && styles.disabled, className)}
    >
      {label && (
        <div id={`${id}-label`} className={styles.label}>
          {label}
          {required && (
            <>
              <span className={styles.required} aria-hidden="true">
                *
              </span>
              {/* A group cannot be aria-required; the name says it instead. */}
              <span className={styles.srOnly}> (required)</span>
            </>
          )}
        </div>
      )}
      <div
        className={cn(styles.dropzone, dragging && styles.dragging, (rejections.length > 0 || missing) && styles.invalid)}
        data-disabled={disabled || undefined}
        onDragEnter={(e) => {
          e.preventDefault()
          if (!disabled) setDragging(true)
        }}
        onDragOver={(e) => {
          e.preventDefault()
          e.dataTransfer.dropEffect = disabled ? 'none' : 'copy'
        }}
        onDragLeave={(e) => {
          if (!e.currentTarget.contains(e.relatedTarget as Node)) setDragging(false)
        }}
        onDrop={onDrop}
      >
        <span className={styles.icon} aria-hidden="true">
          <Icon name="upload" />
        </span>
        <p className={styles.prompt}>
          {/* Dragging is a shortcut; the button is the way in for everyone. */}
          Drag {multiple ? 'files' : 'a file'} here or
        </p>
        <Button
          ref={chooseRef}
          variant="accent"
          size="sm"
          disabled={disabled}
          aria-describedby={[helperText ? helperId : '', rejections.length || missing ? errorId : ''].filter(Boolean).join(' ') || undefined}
          onClick={() => inputRef.current?.click()}
        >
          {multiple ? 'Choose files' : 'Choose a file'}
        </Button>
        {helperText && (
          <p id={helperId} className={styles.helper}>
            {helperText}
          </p>
        )}
        <input
          ref={inputRef}
          type="file"
          className={styles.srOnly}
          tabIndex={-1}
          name={name}
          accept={accept}
          multiple={multiple}
          disabled={disabled}
          required={required && files.length === 0}
          aria-hidden="true"
          onChange={(e) => add([...(e.target.files ?? [])])}
          // The browser would focus this hidden input and pin its bubble to
          // it. Show the message ourselves and send focus to Choose instead.
          onInvalid={(e) => {
            e.preventDefault()
            setMissing(true)
            chooseRef.current?.focus()
          }}
        />
      </div>
      {(rejections.length > 0 || missing) && (
        <ul id={errorId} className={styles.errors}>
          {missing && <li>{multiple ? 'Choose at least one file.' : 'Choose a file.'}</li>}
          {rejections.map((r, i) => (
            <li key={i}>{r.message}</li>
          ))}
        </ul>
      )}
      {files.length > 0 && (
        <ul ref={listRef} className={styles.list} aria-label={multiple ? 'Chosen files' : 'Chosen file'}>
          {files.map((file, i) => {
            const status = getFileStatus?.(file)
            const uploading = status?.progress !== undefined && status.progress < 100 && !status.error
            return (
              <li key={`${file.name}-${file.size}-${file.lastModified}`} className={styles.item}>
                <FileTypeIcon file={file} />
                {/* The name truncates; the size always shows in full. */}
                <span className={styles.nameRow}>
                  <span className={styles.name}>{file.name}</span>
                  <span className={styles.size}>{sizeFormat(file.size)}</span>
                </span>
                {uploading && (
                  <Spinner value={status?.progress} variant="primary" size="sm" aria-label={`Uploading ${file.name}`} />
                )}
                {status?.error && (
                  <span className={styles.fileError} title={status.error}>
                    {status.error}
                  </span>
                )}
                <Button
                  isIconOnly
                  data-remove=""
                  className={styles.remove}
                  aria-label={`Remove ${file.name}`}
                  variant="secondary"
                  appearance="ghost"
                  size="sm"
                  disabled={disabled}
                  onClick={() => remove(i)}
                >
                  <Icon name="close" />
                </Button>
              </li>
            )
          })}
        </ul>
      )}
      <p role="status" className={styles.srOnly}>
        {announcement}
      </p>
    </div>
  )
}

# File Uploader

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

Choose files to send: drag them onto the drop zone or pick them with the
button. It checks type, size and count, lists what was chosen, and shows
progress or an error per file. It does not upload: your code does, and
tells it how that is going.

<Status of={FileUploaderStories} />

<Canvas of={FileUploaderStories.WithStatus} />

## Variants

| Mode | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `multiple` | Attachments, a batch of photos: files are appended, up to `maxFiles`. |
| Single | One document: an invoice, a CV. A new file replaces the chosen one, if it passes the checks. |

<Canvas of={FileUploaderStories.Single} />

Each file gets a type icon: a page with a coloured badge for Word, Excel,
PowerPoint, PDF, image and audio, after Microsoft 365, from the extension
or MIME type. Anything else is the bare page.

<Canvas of={FileUploaderStories.FileTypes} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { FileUploader } from 'zweihander/file-uploader'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/file-uploader.json
```

- Source: [src/components/inputs/FileUploader.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/inputs/FileUploader.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/file-uploader](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/file-uploader)
- Behaviour: a native `<input type="file">` behind a kit [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={FileUploaderStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={FileUploaderStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

Two more parts show only when needed:

- **Errors**: one line per file that was not added, under the drop zone,
  e.g. "raw-scan.png is larger than 5 MB."
- **File error**: in place of the progress ring, a short message from
  `getFileStatus`, e.g. "Upload failed". A long one truncates.

<Canvas of={FileUploaderStories.Rejected} />

## Measurements

One size. The buttons inside are `sm` Buttons, 24px tall.

  rows={[

    { part: 'Icon', property: 'Padding', token: '--space-inline' },

    { part: 'File row', property: 'Block padding', token: '--space-stack' },

The uploader is 24rem wide unless `isFullWidth`. A file row has no
inline padding, so its icon and remove button line up with the drop
zone's edges. The type icon is 20px: a 13 × 18 page with a folded corner,
and a badge 8px tall (14px wide, 16px for DOC and MP3) naming the type
in 6px bold: DOC, XLS, PPT, PDF, IMG or MP3.

The type badges keep fixed colours in both modes: they are each file
type's identity, not the theme's, and white on each is above 4.5:1. The
page is an 18% tint of the badge colour and the fold a 40% one; an
unknown type gets a fixed light gray page (#e3e5e8, fold #c2c5cc). The
Choose button is an `accent contained` Button and the remove buttons
`secondary ghost`; their states are Button's.

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
    { label: 'Uploading', content: <Fit><Story of={FileUploaderStories.Anatomy} /></Fit> },
    { label: 'Disabled', content: <Fit><Story of={FileUploaderStories.Disabled} /></Fit> },
  ]}
>
  <Fit><Story of={FileUploaderStories.DoStateTheRules} /></Fit>
</States>

- **Dragging**: while a file is over the drop zone its edge turns solid
  `--color-border-focused` and it fills with `--color-background-neutral`, so the change is not colour
  alone.
- **Rejected or required and empty**: the drop zone's edge turns
  `--color-text-danger` and the errors list why, one line per file.
- **Focus** is the Choose button's and the remove buttons' own ring.
- **Uploading**: a progress ring beside the remove button while
  `progress` is under 100; it goes at 100. An `error` takes its place.
- **Disabled** fades the icon and the buttons, not the text: none of it
  is a native label, so faded text would fail contrast rather than be
  exempt.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={FileUploaderStories} />
</div>

### Design notes

- **Checks on every path in.** The system picker filters by `accept`, but
  a drop, or "All files" in the picker, does not. The uploader checks the
  type, size and count of everything and says why a file was left out.
- **A rejected file never replaces a good one.** In single-file mode a
  new file replaces the chosen one only if it passes the checks.
- **The same file twice is one file.** Name, size and modified time
  match, so it is skipped rather than listed again.
- **Uploading is yours.** Start it in `onFilesChange` and report through
  `getFileStatus`.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a File Uploader to attach files to a form: receipts to a claim,
documents to an application. Say what is allowed in `helperText`, and set
`accept`, `maxSize` and `maxFiles` to match, so the rules are read before
a file is turned away.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={FileUploaderStories.DoStateTheRules} />}
  doCaption="The rules up front: types and size in the helper text, checked by accept and maxSize."
  dont={<Story of={FileUploaderStories.DontHideTheRules} />}
  dontCaption="No rules shown: people learn them one rejection at a time."
/>

Report upload progress per file with `getFileStatus`, and keep errors
short ("Upload failed"): the row has room for a few words.

## When not to use

- **For text people could paste.** Use a
  [Textarea](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textarea--docs).
- **For a link to a file.** Use a
  [Text Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textinput--docs) with
  `type="url"`.

## Accessibility

- Dragging is a shortcut, never the only way: the Choose button is a
  real button, reached by Tab, and opens the system picker. The file
  input itself is hidden from assistive tech so there is one control, not
  two.
- The uploader is a `group` named by its label; `required` adds
  "(required)" to that name, since a group cannot be `aria-required`.
  Submitting it empty shows "Choose at least one file." (or "Choose a
  file.") in the errors and moves focus to the Choose button, instead of
  the browser's bubble on the hidden input.
- The helper text and any errors describe the Choose button, so they
  are read when focus lands on it.
- The chosen files are a list named "Chosen files" ("Chosen file" when
  `multiple` is off), one item per file.
- A polite status line announces "2 files added. 1 not added." and
  "report.pdf removed."
- Remove buttons are named "Remove report.pdf". After a remove, focus
  moves to the next file's button, or back to Choose when the list is
  empty, so it is never lost.
- The progress ring is a `progressbar` named "Uploading report.pdf",
  with its value.
- While dragging, the drop zone's edge turns solid as well as changing
  colour.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

  { name: '--focus-offset', use: 'Ring outside the element: buttons, fields, links, free-standing controls' },
  { name: '--focus-offset-inset', use: 'Ring inside the element: tabs, rows, close buttons in a panel' },
]

const SAMPLE: React.CSSProperties = {

./src/foundations/Focus.mdx
# Focus One ring for the whole kit: `outline: var(--focus-width) solid var(--color-border-...
import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as FocusStories from './Focus.stories'

<Meta of={FocusStories} />

# Focus

One ring for the whole kit: `outline: var(--focus-width) solid var(--color-border-focused)`,
shown on `:focus-visible` only. Its colour is `--color-border-focused`, measured at 3:1
against the page (see [Colors](?path=/docs/foundations-colors--docs)).

<Canvas of={FocusStories.Rings} />

## Outside or inside

There are two offsets and the choice is mechanical.

**`--focus-offset`** draws the ring outside the element. It is the default
for anything that stands on its own: buttons, fields, links, checkboxes.

**`--focus-offset-inset`** draws it inside. Use it when the element sits
flush against the edge of a container that clips its overflow, or when an
outside ring would run into a neighbour: tabs, table rows and sortable
headers, the close button in a modal, popover, alert
or toast, the remove button in a tag, the steppers in a number input.

A third value is a smell. The one exception is a selected colour swatch,
which already carries a selection ring at `--focus-offset`, so its focus
ring sits one pixel further out to stay visible.

## Why the ring is in pixels

`--focus-width` and both offsets are plain pixels, not `rem`. A ring is a
stroke, and WCAG 2.4.13 measures it in CSS pixels.

# Icons One module, `src/lib/icon.tsx`, and one component: ``. Every component in the kit ...
import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as IconStories from './Icon.stories'

<Meta of={IconStories} />

# Icons

One module, `src/lib/icon.tsx`, and one component: `<Icon name="close" />`.
Every component in the kit imports its icons from here and nowhere else.

<Canvas of={IconStories.Catalog} />

## Why names say what an icon is for

`close`, `danger`, `success` — not `x`, `alert-circle`, `check-circle`.
The set is temporary: it is Boxicons for now, and may be
replaced by the kit's own set. Named by purpose, that swap is an edit to this one file.
Named by shape, it would be a search through every component for which
shape meant what. Navigation shapes (`chevron-down`, `search`, `plus`)
keep their plain names because the shape *is* the purpose.

## Sizing and colour

The icon is a `1em` square filled with `currentColor`, so it takes both
from the text around it. Set `font-size` on a wrapper, or on the icon
itself, to size it; never pass a colour.

```tsx
<span style={{ fontSize: 20 }}><Icon name="warning" /></span>
```

## Accessibility

- Without `label` an icon is decorative: `aria-hidden`, and not focusable
  in old Edge. This is almost always right, because the icon sits next to
  words that already say the same thing.
- With `label` it is exposed as an image with that name. Use it only when
  the icon stands alone and carries meaning, e.g. a status with no text.
- An icon-only *button* is named on the button (`aria-label`), not on
  the icon.

## Source and licence

Path data is copied from Boxicons free (`@boxicons/core` 1.0.6): the basic
set, and the filled set where the table says *filled*. MIT. The licence
notice is in the file header, so it travels with the file when the registry
copies it into another project. There is no npm dependency on Boxicons, and
no icon font.

The paths use Boxicons' own `0 0 24 24` viewBox; keep it when adding icons.

## Names in Boxicons

Each purpose name in code is one Boxicon, so designers can find the same
glyph at [boxicons.com](https://boxicons.com):

| Code (`name`) | Boxicon |
| --- | --- |
| `calendar` | `bx-calendar` |
| `check` | `bx-check` |
| `chevron-down` | `bx-chevron-down` |
| `chevron-left` | `bx-chevron-left` |
| `chevron-right` | `bx-chevron-right` |
| `chevron-up` | `bx-chevron-up` |
| `chevrons-up-down` | `bx-chevrons-up-down` |
| `clear` | `bx-x-circle` (filled) |
| `close` | `bx-x` |
| `danger` | `bx-alert-circle` |
| `danger-filled` | `bx-alert-circle` (filled) |
| `edit` | `bx-pencil` |
| `external` | `bx-arrow-out-up-right-square` |
| `file` | `bx-file` |
| `help` | `bx-help-circle` |
| `info` | `bx-info-circle` |
| `info-filled` | `bx-info-circle` (filled) |
| `menu` | `bx-menu` |
| `minus` | `bx-minus` |
| `more` | `bx-dots-horizontal-rounded` |
| `notifications` | `bx-bell` |
| `pause` | `bx-pause` |
| `play` | `bx-play` |
| `plus` | `bx-plus` |
| `search` | `bx-search` |
| `sidebar-collapse` | `bx-dock-left-arrow` |
| `sidebar-expand` | `bx-dock-left-arrow` (chevron mirrored) |
| `star` | `bx-star` |
| `star-filled` | `bx-star` (filled) |
| `success` | `bx-check-circle` |
| `success-filled` | `bx-check-circle` (filled) |
| `upload` | `bx-arrow-up-stroke` |
| `user` | `bx-user` |
| `warning` | `bx-alert-triangle` |
| `warning-filled` | `bx-alert-triangle` (filled) |

To add an icon: find it at boxicons.com, copy the `d` attribute(s) from
`svg/basic/<name>.svg` (or `svg/filled/<name>.svg`) in `@boxicons/core`
into the `paths` map under a purpose name, add a row to this table, and add
the name to the catalog story.

import type { ComponentProps, ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Icon, type IconName } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './InlineAlert.module.css'

export interface InlineAlertProps extends ComponentProps<'div'> {
  variant?: 'info' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger'
  size?: 'sm' | 'md'
  /** Replaces the variant's icon; `false` shows none. */
  icon?: ReactNode | false
  /** A short link or button after the message, e.g. "Retry". */
  action?: ReactNode
  /**
   * Announce it when it appears: `danger` and `warning` interrupt
   * (`role="alert"`), the others wait (`role="status"`).
   */
  isLive?: boolean
}

const icons: Record<NonNullable<InlineAlertProps['variant']>, IconName> = {
  info: 'info-filled',
  success: 'success-filled',
  warning: 'warning-filled',
  danger: 'danger-filled',
}

/**
 * A one-line message in the flow of a form or a section: no box, no title,
 * no close button. For a message about a whole page or region, use Alert.
 */
export function InlineAlert({
  variant = 'info',
  size = 'md',
  icon,
  action,
  isLive = false,
  className,
  children,
  ...props
}: InlineAlertProps) {
  const urgent = variant === 'danger' || variant === 'warning'
  return (
    <div
      role={isLive ? (urgent ? 'alert' : 'status') : undefined}
      className={cn(styles.inlineAlert, styles[variant], styles[size], className)}
      {...props}
    >
      {icon !== false && (
        <span className={styles.icon} aria-hidden="true">
          {icon ?? <Icon name={icons[variant]} />}
        </span>
      )}
      <span className={styles.message}>{children}</span>
      {action && <span className={styles.action}>{action}</span>}
    </div>
  )
}
