# Spacing Pick a spacing token by **what the gap does**, not by its size. Six roles cover ...
import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as SpacingStories from './Spacing.stories'

<Meta of={SpacingStories} />

# Spacing

Pick a spacing token by **what the gap does**, not by its size. Six roles
cover every gap and pad in the kit, and each role has one value. A
designer never chooses between 12 and 16 pixels: they choose
`--space-cluster` or `--space-group`.

<Canvas of={SpacingStories.Roles} />

## The six roles

| Token | Use for | Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--space-stack` | Lines of text under each other: title to description, label to value | 4 |
| `--space-inline` | Small things side by side: icon to text, label to value on one line, breadcrumb items | 8 |
| `--space-cluster` | Controls or parts that sit together: filters in a toolbar, an avatar to its content, the parts of a page heading, inside a small card | 12 |
| `--space-group` | Items and blocks that belong together: cards in a row, toolbar to table, table cell sides | 16 |
| `--space-container` | Inside the edge of a card, panel or page heading | 24 |
| `--space-section` | Page edge and between page sections | 24 |

The scale is short on purpose: 4, 8, 12, 16, 24. Section and container
share 24px, so separate sections with a card edge or a rule, not with
extra white space. Apply `--space-section` to the page edge from 64rem
up; below that, keep the edge at its narrow value.

The numeric steps (`--space-0-5` to `--space-20`) still exist for the few
places no role fits, such as the size of an icon disc.

## Controls

The control tier binds a control's height, padding and icon gap, so a
control never reads a spacing role for its own box.

| Control token | lg | md | sm | xs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--control-{tier}` height | 40 | 32 | 24 | 20 |
| `--control-{tier}-pad` (rows, menu items) | – | 10 | 8 | 6 |
| `--control-{tier}-pad-spacious` (buttons, from the outer edge to the label) | – | 12 | 12 | 6 |
| `--control-{tier}-gap` (icon to label) | – | 6 | 6 | 4 |

A field is `lg` tall by default and `md` at `size="sm"`, one step above a
button. It takes the numeric step `--space-1-5` (6px) inside its edge at
both sizes, and `--space-stack` between its label, box and helper text.

A small control inside a component (a table's sort button, a modal's
close button, a badge, the number input's steppers) reads the control tier
of its own size, like any other control, not a spacing role.

## One scale

The kit has one set of numbers: there is no density mode and no scaling
factor. Where a screen needs a tighter control, such as a button in a
table row or a filter in a toolbar, use that component's `size="sm"`.

## Touch and rem

Controls are below the 44px touch minimum on purpose: on coarse pointers
every control widens its hit area to 44px without growing the box. Every
value is in `rem`, so it follows the user's root font size; "32px" is 32px
at the default 16px root.

import type { ComponentProps } from 'react'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import { colorVar, type ChartColor } from './chart-utils'
import styles from './Chart.module.css'

export interface SparklineProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'div'>, 'children'> {
  /** Values in order, oldest first. Empty or null shows "No data". */
  data: number[] | null | undefined
  color?: ChartColor
  /** `area` fills under the line; `bar` draws one bar per value, for counts. */
  appearance?: 'line' | 'area' | 'bar'
  /**
   * Off by default: next to a figure and its change the trend is decoration.
   * Give it a name when the spark is the only place the trend is shown.
   */
  'aria-label'?: string
}

/**
 * A trend with no axes, 96 × 24 unless a class or style sizes it otherwise.
 * The viewBox stretches to any width without measuring, and
 * non-scaling-stroke keeps the line 1.5px. Bars are placed in percentages
 * instead, so their 1px corners stay round at any width.
 */
export function Sparkline({ data, color = 'chart-1', appearance = 'area', className, 'aria-label': ariaLabel, ...props }: SparklineProps) {
  const isEmpty = !data?.length
  let line = ''
  // A zero baseline: a spark that starts at its minimum exaggerates small swings.
  const max = isEmpty ? 1 : Math.max(...data, 0) || 1
  if (!isEmpty && appearance !== 'bar') {
    const step = data.length > 1 ? 100 / (data.length - 1) : 0
    line = 'M' + data.map((v, i) => `${(i * step).toFixed(2)},${(29 - (v / max) * 27).toFixed(2)}`).join('L')
    if (data.length === 1) line += 'L100,' + line.split(',')[1]
  }
  const a11y = ariaLabel ? { role: 'img', 'aria-label': ariaLabel } : { 'aria-hidden': true }
  return (
    <div {...props} className={cn(styles.spark, className)}>
      {!isEmpty && appearance === 'bar' ? (
        <svg fill={colorVar(color)} {...a11y}>
          {data.map((v, i) => {
            // Each bar fills three quarters of its slot, centred; a zero keeps a sliver so its slot still reads.
            const h = Math.max(4, (Math.max(v, 0) / max) * 100)
            return <rect key={i} x={`${((i + 0.125) * 100) / data.length}%`} width={`${75 / data.length}%`} y={`${100 - h}%`} height={`${h}%`} rx={1} />
          })}
        </svg>
      ) : (
        <svg viewBox="0 0 100 30" preserveAspectRatio="none" {...a11y}>
          {isEmpty ? (
            <path className={styles.sparkEmpty} d="M0,20 C25,14 40,24 60,18 S90,12 100,16" />
          ) : (
            <>
              {appearance === 'area' && <path className={styles.sparkArea} d={`${line}L100,30L0,30Z`} fill={colorVar(color)} />}
              <path className={styles.sparkLine} d={line} stroke={colorVar(color)} />
            </>
          )}
        </svg>
      )}
      {isEmpty && <span className={styles.badge}>No data</span>}
    </div>
  )
}

'use client'

import { useEffect, useState, type ComponentProps } from 'react'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Spinner.module.css'

export interface SpinnerProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'span'>, 'children'> {
  size?: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'
  /** Colour of the indicator. `accent` is the foreground, as on Button. */
  variant?: 'primary' | 'accent' | 'secondary'
  /** Wait this many milliseconds before showing, so a fast load never flashes a spinner. */
  delay?: number
  /** 0–100. Omit for an indeterminate, spinning indicator. */
  value?: number
  /** Spin even when `value` is given. */
  isIndeterminate?: boolean
  /** Shown under the indicator and used as its accessible name ("Loading" when omitted). */
  label?: string
}

export function Spinner({
  size = 'md',
  variant = 'accent',
  delay = 0,
  value,
  isIndeterminate = false,
  label,
  className,
  ...props
}: SpinnerProps) {
  const [elapsed, setElapsed] = useState(false)
  // Always after mount, even with no delay: the live region below has to be
  // in the page before its text arrives for the text to be announced.
  useEffect(() => {
    const timer = setTimeout(() => setElapsed(true), Math.max(0, delay))
    return () => clearTimeout(timer)
  }, [delay])

  const determinate = value !== undefined && !isIndeterminate
  const clamped = determinate ? Math.min(100, Math.max(0, value)) : 0
  const name = label || 'Loading'

  const indicator = (
    // No viewBox: the ring is sized in CSS so its stroke stays 2.25px at
    // every size. pathLength 100 lets the dash read as a percentage.
    <svg className={cn(styles.svg, !determinate && styles.spinning)} aria-hidden="true">
      <circle className={styles.track} />
      <circle
        className={styles.indicator}
        pathLength={100}
        strokeDasharray={100}
        // Indeterminate shows 30% of the ring; determinate shows the value.
        strokeDashoffset={determinate ? 100 - clamped : 70}
      />
    </svg>
  )

  // Determinate: a progressbar that says how far along it is.
  if (determinate) {
    if (delay > 0 && !elapsed) return null
    return (
      <span
        role="progressbar"
        aria-valuenow={clamped}
        aria-valuemin={0}
        aria-valuemax={100}
        aria-label={name}
        className={cn(styles.spinner, styles[size], styles[variant], className)}
        {...props}
      >
        {indicator}
        {label && <span className={styles.label}>{label}</span>}
      </span>
    )
  }

  // Indeterminate: a polite live region that is in the page from the first
  // render, empty through the delay. Screen readers announce text inserted
  // into a live region that already exists, not a region that mounts full.
  return (
    <span
      role="status"
      aria-label={name}
      className={cn(styles.spinner, styles[size], styles[variant], className)}
      {...props}
    >
      {elapsed && (
        <>
          {indicator}
          <span className={label ? styles.label : styles.hiddenLabel}>{name}</span>
        </>
      )}
    </span>
  )
}

# Spinner Says that something is loading when there is no telling how long it will take, o...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import { Spinner } from './Spinner'
import * as SpinnerStories from './Spinner.stories'

<Meta of={SpinnerStories} />

# Spinner

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

Says that something is loading when there is no telling how long it will
take, or, given a value, how far along it is.

<Status of={SpinnerStories} />

<Canvas of={SpinnerStories.WithLabel} />

## Variants

`variant` is the colour of the indicator. The track and the label are the
same in all three.

<Canvas of={SpinnerStories.Variants} />

| Variant | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| <Spinner variant="accent" /> `accent` | The default: a quiet placeholder in `--color-text`, inside content that has its own colour. |
| <Spinner variant="primary" /> `primary` | A load the page is about, where the brand colour helps it be found: the first load of a view. |
| <Spinner variant="secondary" /> `secondary` | Low emphasis: a spinner beside other muted text, or in a dense list. |

With a `value` it stops spinning and becomes a progress ring, which reads
better than a bar in a small space such as a thumbnail.

<Canvas of={SpinnerStories.Determinate} />

<Canvas of={SpinnerStories.Sizes} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Spinner } from 'zweihander/spinner'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/spinner.json
```

- Source: [src/components/loaders/Spinner.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/loaders/Spinner.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/spinner](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/spinner)
- Behaviour: a plain element; there is no behaviour here worth Base UI
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={SpinnerStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={SpinnerStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

While spinning, the indicator is 30% of the ring turning once every
`--duration-spin`. With no `label`, a visually hidden "Loading" stands in
for it.

## Measurements

The ring is a 2.25px stroke at every size, its outer edge on the box's
edge. There is no token for 2.25px, so the thickness is not in the tables.

<SpecTable caption="sm" rows={[{ part: 'Ring', property: 'Width and height', token: '--space-4' }]} />

<SpecTable caption="md" rows={[{ part: 'Ring', property: 'Width and height', token: '--space-6' }]} />

<SpecTable caption="lg" rows={[{ part: 'Ring', property: 'Width and height', token: '--space-8' }]} />

<SpecTable
  caption="Every size"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Ring to label', property: 'Gap', token: '--space-2' },
    { part: 'Label', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body' },
    { part: 'Label', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body' },
    { part: 'Indicator', property: 'One turn', token: '--duration-spin' },
    { part: 'Indicator', property: 'One turn, reduced motion', token: '--duration-spin-reduced' },
  ]}
/>

## Color

The indicator is the part that has to be seen, so each variant takes a
colour that clears 3:1 on the page. Switch the theme and the accent in the
toolbar: the values follow.

<SpecTable caption="primary" rows={[{ part: 'Indicator', property: 'Stroke', token: '--color-text-brand' }]} />

<SpecTable caption="accent" rows={[{ part: 'Indicator', property: 'Stroke', token: '--color-text' }]} />

<SpecTable caption="secondary" rows={[{ part: 'Indicator', property: 'Stroke', token: '--color-text-subtlest' }]} />

<SpecTable
  caption="Every variant"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Track', property: 'Stroke', token: '--color-border' },
    { part: 'Label', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-subtlest' },
  ]}
/>

## States

A spinner is not interactive: it has no hover, focus or pressed state.

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Spinning' },
    { label: 'Progress', content: <Spinner value={40} label="Uploading" variant="primary" /> },
    { label: 'Complete', content: <Spinner value={100} label="Uploaded" variant="primary" /> },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={SpinnerStories.WithLabel} />
</States>

- **Spinning** is the default, and what it shows with `isIndeterminate`
  even when given a `value`.
- **Progress** fills the ring clockwise from twelve o'clock, easing
  between values over `--duration-slow`.
- **Delayed**: with `delay`, nothing shows until it has passed. The live
  region is in the page, empty, from the start.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={SpinnerStories} />
</div>

Every other `<span>` attribute passes through to the outer element.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Spinner when something is loading and you cannot say what its result
will look like or how long it will take. Use one per region that is
loading, labelled with what is coming.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={SpinnerStories.DoOneForTheRegion} />}
  doCaption="One spinner for the region, named for what is coming."
  dont={<Story of={SpinnerStories.DontOnePerItem} />}
  dontCaption="A spinner per card says the same thing three times, and three screen-reader announcements."
/>

Give a load you expect to be fast a `delay` of 300–500ms. The spinner only
appears if the wait turns out to be long enough to notice.

<Canvas of={SpinnerStories.Delay} />

## When not to use

- **When you know the shape of what is coming.** A
  [Skeleton](?path=/docs/components-loaders-skeleton--docs) keeps the
  layout and says more.
- **For a long task with a known size**: an upload, an install. Use a
  [Progress Bar](?path=/docs/components-loaders-progressbar--docs), or a
  `value` here when space is tight.
- **Inside a button.** Use the Button's `isLoading`: it keeps the button's
  width and focus and stops a second click.

## Accessibility

- **Spinning, it is `role="status"`**, a polite live region, named by
  `label` or "Loading". The region renders empty and its text (the label,
  or a visually hidden "Loading") is inserted just after, or once `delay`
  has passed: screen readers announce text added to a live region that is
  already in the page, not a region that mounts full.
- **With a value, it is `role="progressbar"`** with `aria-valuenow`,
  `aria-valuemin="0"` and `aria-valuemax="100"`. Values outside 0–100 are
  clamped.
- The SVG is hidden.
- The indicator clears 3:1 on the page in every variant: `--color-text-brand`
  (measured at 4.5:1 per accent), `--color-text-subtlest`, `--color-text`.
  The track is decoration and may be faint.
- Under `prefers-reduced-motion` it slows to one turn in 2.5s rather than
  stopping, since a frozen arc reads as "stuck", and the progress ring
  stops easing between values.
- Put `aria-busy="true"` on the region that is loading, and remove the
  spinner when the load ends, so the change is announced.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

import type { ComponentProps, ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Stepper.module.css'

export interface StepperStep {
  label: ReactNode
  description?: ReactNode
  /** Override the status worked out from `current`, e.g. to flag a step with an error. */
  status?: 'complete' | 'current' | 'upcoming' | 'error'
}

export interface StepperProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'nav'>, 'children'> {
  steps: StepperStep[]
  /** 0-based index of the step the reader is on. Steps before it are complete. */
  current: number
  /** Ignored with `appearance="bullets"`, which is always one row. */
  orientation?: 'horizontal' | 'vertical'
  /**
   * `circles` shows every step's marker and label. `bullets` shows only
   * the current step's label ("Step 2 of 4: Workspace") over a row of
   * dots, for a narrow space or a longer flow.
   */
  appearance?: 'circles' | 'bullets'
  size?: 'sm' | 'md'
  /**
   * Makes finished steps (and the current one) buttons that go back to
   * them. Upcoming steps stay plain: they cannot be skipped to.
   */
  onStepClick?: (index: number) => void
  /** The nav landmark's name. */
  'aria-label'?: string
}

const statusText = { complete: 'completed', current: 'current', upcoming: 'not started', error: 'has an error' }

export function Stepper({
  steps,
  current,
  orientation = 'horizontal',
  appearance = 'circles',
  size = 'md',
  onStepClick,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel = 'Progress',
  className,
  ...props
}: StepperProps) {
  const bullets = appearance === 'bullets'
  const currentStep = steps[current]
  return (
    <nav
      aria-label={ariaLabel}
      className={cn(styles.stepper, bullets ? styles.bullets : styles[orientation], styles[size], className)}
      {...props}
    >
      {/* Hidden from screen readers: the list already says each step's position and status. */}
      {bullets && currentStep && (
        <p className={styles.summary} aria-hidden="true">
          <span className={styles.count}>
            Step {current + 1} of {steps.length}:
          </span>{' '}
          <span className={styles.label}>{currentStep.label}</span>
        </p>
      )}
      <ol className={styles.list}>
        {steps.map((step, i) => {
          const status = step.status ?? (i < current ? 'complete' : i === current ? 'current' : 'upcoming')
          const clickable = onStepClick !== undefined && status !== 'upcoming'
          const marker = (
            <span className={styles.marker} aria-hidden="true">
              {bullets ? null : status === 'complete' ? <Icon name="check" /> : status === 'error' ? <Icon name="danger" /> : i + 1}
            </span>
          )
          // Bullets show only the dot: the label and status are said, not shown.
          const text = (
            <span className={cn(styles.text, bullets && styles.srOnly)}>
              <span className={styles.label}>
                {step.label}
                {/* Said, not shown: the marker carries it visually. */}
                <span className={styles.srOnly}>, {statusText[status]}</span>
              </span>
              {step.description && <span className={styles.description}>{step.description}</span>}
            </span>
          )
          return (
            <li
              key={i}
              className={cn(styles.step, styles[status])}
              // An error on the current step does not stop it being where the reader is.
              aria-current={status === 'current' || i === current ? 'step' : undefined}
            >
              {clickable ? (
                <button type="button" className={styles.target} onClick={() => onStepClick(i)}>
                  {marker}
                  {text}
                </button>
              ) : (
                <span className={styles.target}>
                  {marker}
                  {text}
                </span>
              )}
              {!bullets && i < steps.length - 1 && <span className={styles.connector} aria-hidden="true" />}
            </li>
          )
        })}
      </ol>
    </nav>
  )
}

# Stepper Shows where the reader is in a flow of a few ordered steps: sign-up, checkout, a...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import * as StepperStories from './Stepper.stories'

<Meta of={StepperStories} />

# Stepper

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

Shows where the reader is in a flow of a few ordered steps: sign-up,
checkout, a setup wizard.

<Status of={StepperStories} />

<Canvas of={StepperStories.Default} />

## Variants

| Variant | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| Horizontal (default) | Three to five steps above a form. The label sits under its marker, so every step gets the same width whatever its label. |
| Vertical | Steps with long descriptions, or a narrow column beside the form. |
| `sm` | Dense places: a dialog, a side panel. |
| Bullets (`appearance="bullets"`) | A phone, a narrow dialog, or more steps than fit with labels: only the current step's label shows, "Step 3 of 4: Invite", over a row of dots. |
| Navigable (`onStepClick`) | Flows where going back to fix an earlier step is normal. Finished steps become buttons. |

<Canvas of={StepperStories.Navigable} />

<Canvas of={StepperStories.Vertical} />

<Canvas of={StepperStories.Small} />

<Canvas of={StepperStories.Bullets} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Stepper } from 'zweihander/stepper'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/stepper.json
```

- Source: [src/components/navigation/Stepper.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/navigation/Stepper.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/stepper](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/stepper)
- Behaviour: a plain `<nav>` around an ordered list
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>

/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Error"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Marker', property: 'Background', token: '--color-background-danger' },
    { part: 'Marker ring, icon, label', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-danger' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Bullets"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Dot, complete', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-background-brand-bold' },
    { part: 'Dot and ring, current', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-brand' },
    { part: 'Dot, upcoming', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-border' },
    { part: 'Dot, error', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-danger' },
    { part: 'Ring gap, current', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-surface' },
    { part: 'Dot hit area, hover', property: 'Background', token: '--color-background-neutral' },
    { part: '"Step 3 of 4"', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-subtlest' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Every status"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Description', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-subtlest' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-border-focused' },
  ]}
/>

Complete and current share the primary colour: the filled disc says done,
the ring says here. The current ring uses `--color-text-brand`, the step of
the accent that reads at 4.5:1 on the page, because it frames a number.

## States

A step's status is its state. With `onStepClick`, finished steps and the
current one are buttons, with hover and focus of their own.

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Statuses', content: <Story of={StepperStories.Statuses} /> },
    { label: 'Clickable' },
    { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={StepperStories.Clickable} />
</States>

- **Hover** underlines the label of a clickable step.
- **Focus** is a 2px `--color-border-focused` outline, 2px outside the step.
- **Upcoming** steps are never buttons, so they have no hover or focus.
- With bullets, **hover** fills the dot's hit area with `--color-background-neutral`, since
  there is no visible label to underline.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={StepperStories} />
</div>

Every other `<nav>` attribute passes through.

A step's `status` is only for the exception, such as an error: the rest
is worked out from `current`. Only finished steps can be clicked; upcoming
ones stay text, because a flow that can be skipped ahead is a set of Tabs.

Bullets ignore `orientation` and draw no connectors: the dots sit close
enough to read as one line. When `current` is past the last step, the
"Step 3 of 4" line is left out. A step with an error that is also
`current` keeps `aria-current` and the ring.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Stepper when a task is split into a few steps that must be done in
order, and it helps to know how many are left: checkout, onboarding, an
import wizard. Keep it to three to five steps with a word or two each.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={StepperStories.DoFewShortSteps} />}
  doCaption="Four steps, one word each: the whole flow at a glance."
  dont={<Story of={StepperStories.DontTooManySteps} />}
  dontCaption="Ten steps squeeze every label and make the flow look longer than it is. Merge steps, or drop the stepper."
/>

## When not to use

- **For sections the reader can visit in any order.** Use
  [Tabs](?path=/docs/components-navigation-tabs--docs).
- **For progress with no steps to name**, such as an upload. Use a
  [Progress Bar](?path=/docs/components-loaders-progressbar--docs).
- **For a single-page form.** Headings do the job; a stepper over one page
  promises steps that are not there.

## Accessibility

- A `<nav>` landmark named "Progress" around an ordered list: screen
  readers announce the number of steps and the position of each.
- The current step has `aria-current="step"`.
- The marker is decorative, so each label carries its status in visually
  hidden text: "Account, completed", "Invite, not started", "Workspace,
  has an error". Bullets hide every label but the current one, and still
  say each in the same hidden text. Their visible "Step 3 of 4: Invite"
  is hidden from screen readers, which hear the list instead.
- An error on the current step keeps `aria-current="step"`.
- Without `onStepClick` nothing is focusable. With it, complete and
  current steps are real buttons: reached with Tab, pressed with Enter or
  Space, showing the focus ring, and 44px tall on touch screens
  (`pointer: coarse`).

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

# Success State

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

What a flow shows when it has finished: the invites are sent, the import
is done, the inbox is empty. It confirms what happened and offers the
next step.

<Status of={SuccessStateStories} />

<Canvas of={SuccessStateStories.Default} />

## Variants

| Variant | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `md` | The end of a flow that filled the page or a dialog: a sent form, a finished import. Lead with the next step. |
| `sm` | A panel or a list that is done: "All caught up". Often no action. |

<Canvas of={SuccessStateStories.Small} />

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

import { SuccessState } from 'zweihander/success-state'
```

## States

Success State itself is static. Its action has the states of its own
Buttons.

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },

## API

  <ArgTypes of={SuccessStateStories} />
</div>

Every other `<div>` attribute passes through, including `ref`.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Success State when the screen the reader was on is finished and
needs replacing: a sent form, a completed import, an emptied inbox. Say
what was done, and lead with the next step.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={SuccessStateStories.Default} />}
  doCaption="The flow is over: say what was done and where to go next."
  dont={<Story of={SuccessStateStories.DontForQuickSave} />}
  dontCaption="A quick save is not the end of a flow. This hides the form; a Toast would leave it in place."
/>

## When not to use

- **To confirm a quick action** such as Save, Copy or Move. Use a Toast:
  it confirms and leaves the screen as it was.
- **When there is nothing there yet.** Use an
  [Empty State](?path=/docs/components-states-emptystate--docs).

## Accessibility

- The title is a real heading, as on Empty State. Set `headingLevel` to
  fit the outline.
- The icon is `aria-hidden`; the title says what was done.
- `isLive` makes it a `role="status"`, read politely when it replaces a
  form or a progress view. Without it, nothing is announced.

<Canvas of={SuccessStateStories.AfterSubmit} />

</DocTab>

import type { ReactNode, Ref } from 'react'
import { Switch as BaseSwitch } from '@base-ui/react/switch'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import { ChoiceField, choiceStyles, type ValidationState } from './ChoiceField'
import styles from './Switch.module.css'

export interface SwitchProps {
  ref?: Ref<HTMLElement>
  /** Controlled state. */
  checked?: boolean
  /** Uncontrolled starting state (the spec's `defaultValue`). */
  defaultChecked?: boolean
  /** The spec's `onChange`. Base UI's event details are dropped. */
  onCheckedChange?: (checked: boolean) => void
  label?: ReactNode
  helperText?: ReactNode
  name?: string
  /** Submitted when on; "on" by default, like a checkbox. */
  value?: string
  /**
   * Track 32×16 (`md`) or 40×20px (`lg`).
   * `sm` is deprecated: it draws the `md` track and goes in the next release.
   */
  size?: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'
  /** Colour of the on state. */
  variant?: 'primary' | 'accent' | 'destructive'
  disabled?: boolean
  required?: boolean
  readOnly?: boolean
  validationState?: ValidationState
  id?: string
  className?: string
  'aria-label'?: string
}

let hasWarned = false

export function Switch({
  label,
  helperText,
  name,
  size = 'md',
  variant = 'primary',
  disabled,
  required,
  validationState,
  className,
  onCheckedChange,
  ...props
}: SwitchProps) {
  if (import.meta.env.DEV && !hasWarned && size === 'sm') {
    hasWarned = true
    console.warn('Switch: `size="sm"` is deprecated and renders as `md`. It will be removed in the next release.')
  }
  return (
    <ChoiceField
      label={label}
      helperText={helperText}
      validationState={validationState}
      required={required}
      disabled={disabled}
      name={name}
      className={cn(styles[size === 'lg' ? 'lg' : 'md'], className)}
    >
      <BaseSwitch.Root
        {...props}
        required={required}
        onCheckedChange={onCheckedChange && ((next) => onCheckedChange(next))}
        className={cn(choiceStyles.control, styles.track, styles[variant])}
      >
        <BaseSwitch.Thumb className={styles.thumb} />
      </BaseSwitch.Root>
    </ChoiceField>
  )
}

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'

# Switch

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

Turns a setting on or off, taking effect immediately.

<Status of={SwitchStories} />

<Canvas of={SwitchStories.Default} />

## Variants

`variant` is the colour of the on state. Off is the same in every variant.

<Canvas of={SwitchStories.Variants} />

| Variant | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| <Switch defaultChecked label="Primary" /> | The default: most settings. |
| <Switch variant="accent" defaultChecked label="Accent" /> | Neutral black or white, where the brand colour would clash or already means something else. |
| <Switch variant="destructive" defaultChecked label="Destructive" /> | A setting that is risky to leave on: public sharing, deleting old data automatically. |

<Canvas of={SwitchStories.Sizes} />

<Canvas of={SwitchStories.Validation} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Switch } from 'zweihander/switch'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/switch.json
```

- Source: [src/components/controls/Switch.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/controls/Switch.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/switch](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/switch)
- Behaviour: [Base UI Switch](https://base-ui.com/react/components/switch) and [Field](https://base-ui.com/react/components/field)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={SwitchStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={SwitchStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The label wraps the track, so the whole label is part of the click target.

## Measurements

Two tracks, Atlassian's: 32×16px (`md`, the default) and 40×20px (`lg`).
Each is twice as wide as it is tall, so the thumb travels one track
height. The thumb sits 2px inside the track at both sizes.

`size="sm"` is deprecated. It draws the `md` track, warns once in
development, and will be removed in the next release: drop the prop.
`md` (the default, written out or not) and `lg` are silent.

<SpecTable
  caption="md, 32×16px"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Track', property: 'Height', token: '--switch-md-h' },
    { part: 'Track', property: 'Width', token: '--switch-md-w' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="lg, 40×20px"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Track', property: 'Height', token: '--switch-lg-h' },
    { part: 'Track', property: 'Width', token: '--switch-lg-w' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Every size"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Track and thumb', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-pill' },
    { part: 'Label', property: 'Gap from the track', token: '--space-inline' },
    { part: 'Label', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body' },
    { part: 'Label', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body' },
    { part: 'Helper text', property: 'Gap from the label', token: '--space-1' },
    { part: 'Thumb', property: 'Slide duration', token: '--duration-base' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Width', token: '--focus-width' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Offset', token: '--focus-offset' },
    { part: 'Hit area', property: 'Minimum', token: '--box-sm' },
    { part: 'Hit area', property: 'Minimum on touch screens', token: '--target-coarse' },
  ]}
/>

## Color

Off is a `--color-border-bold` track (3:1 on the page, so the control is
visible at all) with a page-coloured thumb. On takes the variant's solid,
and the thumb its label colour, measured at 4.5:1 against it.

<SpecTable
  caption="Off, every variant"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Track', property: 'Background', token: '--color-border-bold' },
    { part: 'Thumb', property: 'Background', token: '--color-surface' },

/>

<SpecTable

    { part: 'Track', property: 'Background', token: '--color-background-brand-bold' },

/>

<SpecTable

/>

<SpecTable

  rows={[
    { part: 'Track', property: 'Background', token: '--color-background-danger-bold' },

<SpecTable

    { part: 'Helper text, error', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-danger' },
    { part: 'Helper text, success', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-success' },

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Off' },
    { label: 'On', content: <Switch defaultChecked label="Email notifications" /> },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
    { label: 'Disabled', content: <Switch disabled defaultChecked label="Email notifications" /> },
    { label: 'Error', content: <Switch validationState="error" label="Email notifications" /> },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={SwitchStories.Default} />
</States>

- **Hover** changes only the cursor: the track has no lighter or darker
  step to move to without losing its 3:1.
- **Focus** is a 2px `--color-border-focused` outline, 2px outside the track.
- **Disabled** dims the track and the label to 50%.
- **Error** draws a 2px `--color-text-danger` ring outside the track, as
  Figma's outside stroke. It fills the 2px focus offset, so the focus ring
  draws just beyond it and both show.
- **Read-only** looks enabled, with an arrow cursor.
- The thumb slides over `--duration-base`, and stops animating under
  `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={SwitchStories} />
</div>

`id`, `className`, `aria-label` and `ref` pass through to the track.

### Differences from the spec

- **Atlassian's two tracks.** 32×16px and 40×20px; `sm` is deprecated and
  draws the `md` track.
- **The label sits beside the track at regular weight**, as a Checkbox's
  does. Atlassian's toggle draws no visible label of its own (its `label`
  is hidden text for a screen reader); a form there puts a separate form
  Label next to it.
- **Base UI's names:** `checked`, `defaultChecked`, `onCheckedChange` for
  the spec's `defaultValue` and `onChange`; native `disabled`,
  `required`, `readOnly` for `isDisabled`, `isRequired`, `isReadOnly`.
- **`helperText` is added.** `validationState="error"` needs somewhere to
  say what is wrong; colour alone is not a message.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a switch for a setting that takes effect the moment it is flipped,
like a light switch: dark mode, notifications, auto-save.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={SwitchStories.DoApplyAtOnce} />}
  doCaption="The setting applies as soon as the switch moves."
  dont={<Story of={SwitchStories.DontWaitForSave} />}
  dontCaption="A switch that waits for Save looks done when it is not. Use a checkbox in a form."
/>

<Canvas of={SwitchStories.Controlled} />

## When not to use

- **For a choice submitted with a form.** Use a
  [Checkbox](?path=/docs/components-controls-checkbox--docs).
- **For more than two options.** Use a
  [Radio](?path=/docs/components-controls-radio--docs) group or a Select.
- **For a toggle in a toolbar** (Bold, a filter). Use a
  [Toggle Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-togglebutton--docs).

## Accessibility

- `role="switch"` with `aria-checked`; Space toggles it.
- The label wraps the control, so it names it and clicking it toggles it.
  Without a visible label, pass `aria-label`: it goes to the switch itself.
- `helperText` is the switch's description (`aria-describedby`); in the
  error state the switch has `aria-invalid`.
- The off track is `--color-border-bold`, measured at 3:1 on the page on
  every gray ramp; the thumb is 4.5:1 or more against its track in both
  states.
- A hidden `<input type="checkbox">` carries `name`, `value` and
  `required` into native form submission and validation.
- On is the end side: in a right-to-left page the thumb travels left.
- The hit area is at least 24px tall, 44×44px on coarse pointers.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

export default meta
type Story = StoryObj<typeof meta>

/** Heights of a row's cell and its header cell, without the header's rule. */
const cellHeights = (canvas: ReturnType<typeof within>) =>
  [canvas.getAllByRole('rowheader')[0], canvas.getAllByRole('columnheader')[0]].map((c: HTMLElement) => c.clientHeight)

/** Text only: a row of these is one 20px line tall. */
const textColumns = columns.filter((c) => c.key !== 'status')

/** Where an element's content is drawn, without its own padding. */
const contentBox = (el: Element) => {
  const range = document.createRange()
  range.selectNodeContents(el)
  return range.getBoundingClientRect()
}

const names = (canvas: ReturnType<typeof within>) => canvas.getAllByRole('rowheader').map((c: HTMLElement) => c.textContent)

export const Default: Story = {
  play: async ({ args, canvas }) => {
    const table = canvas.getByRole('table', { name: 'Projects' })
    await expect(within(table).getAllByRole('row')).toHaveLength(5)
    // 8px above and below the header's 16px line: the sort button adds nothing.
    await expect(cellHeights(canvas)[1]).toBe(32)
    // The header ends on a 1px rule; the rows have no divider.
    await expect(getComputedStyle(canvas.getAllByRole('columnheader')[0]).borderBottomWidth).toBe('1px')
    await expect(getComputedStyle(canvas.getAllByRole('rowheader')[0]).borderBottomWidth).toBe('0px')
    // A table with rows closes on the same rule: 1px, the header's colour, right under the last row.
    const closing = getComputedStyle(table)
    await expect(closing.borderBottomWidth).toBe('1px')
    await expect(closing.borderBottomColor).toBe(getComputedStyle(canvas.getAllByRole('columnheader')[0]).borderBottomColor)
    await expect(table.getBoundingClientRect().bottom - within(table).getAllByRole('row').at(-1)!.getBoundingClientRect().bottom).toBe(1)
    // So a one-line row is 36px all told, and the Tag in it adds nothing.
    const atlas = canvas.getByRole('rowheader', { name: 'Atlas' }).closest('tr')!
    await expect(within(atlas).getByText('Active')).toBeVisible()
    await expect(atlas.getBoundingClientRect().height).toBe(36)
    await expect(names(canvas)).toEqual(['Atlas', 'Billing revamp', 'Onboarding', 'Design tokens'])
    // Sort: ascending, descending, then back to unsorted. aria-sort follows.
    const files = canvas.getByRole('columnheader', { name: /Files/ })
    await expect(files).toHaveAttribute('aria-sort', 'none')
    await userEvent.click(within(files).getByRole('button'))
    await expect(files).toHaveAttribute('aria-sort', 'ascending')
    await expect(args.onSortChange).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith({ key: 'files', direction: 'ascending' })
    await expect(names(canvas)).toEqual(['Design tokens', 'Billing revamp', 'Atlas', 'Onboarding'])
    await userEvent.click(within(files).getByRole('button'))
    await expect(files).toHaveAttribute('aria-sort', 'descending')
    await expect(names(canvas)).toEqual(['Onboarding', 'Atlas', 'Billing revamp', 'Design tokens'])
    await userEvent.click(within(files).getByRole('button'))
    await expect(files).toHaveAttribute('aria-sort', 'none')
    await expect(names(canvas)).toEqual(['Atlas', 'Billing revamp', 'Onboarding', 'Design tokens'])
    // Dates sort as dates, text by locale with numbers in order.
    await userEvent.click(within(canvas.getByRole('columnheader', { name: /Updated/ })).getByRole('button'))
    await expect(names(canvas)[0]).toBe('Design tokens')
  },
}

    await userEvent.click(canvas.getByRole('checkbox', { name: 'Select Atlas' }))

    await userEvent.click(all)
    await expect(args.onSelectionChange).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith(['p2', 'p1', 'p3', 'p4'])
    await expect(all).toHaveAttribute('aria-checked', 'true')
    await userEvent.click(all)
    await expect(args.onSelectionChange).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith([])
  },

function PagedTable(props: { onSelectionChange: (ids: string[]) => void }) {
  const [page, setPage] = useState(0)
  return (
    <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 'var(--space-3)', justifyItems: 'start' }}>
      <Table
        columns={columns}
        rows={projects.slice(page * 2, page * 2 + 2)}
        getRowId={(p) => p.id}
        caption={`Projects, page ${page + 1} of 2`}
        isSelectable
        onSelectionChange={props.onSelectionChange}
      />
      <Button variant="secondary" appearance="outlined" size="sm" onClick={() => setPage(1 - page)}>
        {page === 0 ? 'Next page' : 'Previous page'}
      </Button>
    </div>
  )
}

/** Selection with getRowId survives paging: "Select all" adds or removes this page's rows only. */
export const Paged: Story = {
  render: (args) => <PagedTable onSelectionChange={args.onSelectionChange!} />,
  play: async ({ args, canvas }) => {
    await userEvent.click(canvas.getByRole('checkbox', { name: 'Select Atlas' }))
    await userEvent.click(canvas.getByRole('button', { name: 'Next page' }))
    const all = canvas.getByRole('checkbox', { name: 'Select all rows' })
    await userEvent.click(all)
    await expect(args.onSelectionChange).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith(['p1', 'p3', 'p4'])
    await userEvent.click(all)
    await expect(args.onSelectionChange).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith(['p1'])
  },
}

/**
 * Every cell, the first and last included, is padded 8px all round. The
 * header has no fill.
 */
export const EdgeCells: Story = {
  tags: ['!dev'],
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    const table = canvas.getByRole('table', { name: 'Projects' }).getBoundingClientRect()
    const row = canvas.getByRole('rowheader', { name: 'Atlas' }).closest('tr')!
    const head = canvas.getAllByRole('columnheader')
    // The first cell's text, and its header's label, start 8px in from the table's left edge.
    await expect(contentBox(row.firstElementChild!).left).toBeCloseTo(table.left + 8, 0)
    await expect(contentBox(within(head[0]).getByRole('button')).left).toBeCloseTo(table.left + 8, 0)
    // The last column is end-aligned: its figures and its label end 8px in from the right edge.
    await expect(contentBox(row.lastElementChild!).right).toBeCloseTo(table.right - 8, 0)
    await expect(contentBox(within(head.at(-1)!).getByRole('button')).right).toBeCloseTo(table.right - 8, 0)
    // Every cell: 8px each side, the edge cells too.
    for (const cell of [row.firstElementChild!, row.children[1], row.lastElementChild!, head[0], head[1], head.at(-1)!]) {
      const { paddingLeft, paddingRight } = getComputedStyle(cell)
      await expect([paddingLeft, paddingRight]).toEqual(['8px', '8px'])
    }
    // No header fill: the container's colour shows through.
    await expect(getComputedStyle(head[0]).backgroundColor).toBe('rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)')
  },
}

/** Sorted by the caller (e.g. a server): the table reports the sort and shows the rows as given. */
export const ControlledSort: Story = {
  render: function Render(args) {
    const [sort, setSort] = useState<{ key: string; direction: 'ascending' | 'descending' } | null>(null)
    const rows = sort ? [...projects].sort((a, b) => a.owner.localeCompare(b.owner) * (sort.direction === 'ascending' ? 1 : -1)) : projects
    return <Table {...args} rows={rows} sort={sort} onSortChange={setSort} />
  },
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    await userEvent.click(within(canvas.getByRole('columnheader', { name: /Owner/ })).getByRole('button'))
    await expect(canvas.getAllByRole('row')[1]).toHaveTextContent('Ava Stone')

  play: async ({ args, canvas, step }) => {
    const atlas = canvas.getByRole('button', { name: 'Expand Atlas' })
    await step('A row with no content has no button', async () => {
      await expect(canvas.queryByRole('button', { name: 'Expand Design tokens' })).toBeNull()
    })
    await step('Click opens and closes, aria-expanded follows', async () => {
      await expect(atlas).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false')
      await userEvent.click(atlas)
      await expect(atlas).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true')
      await expect(args.onExpandedChange).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith(['p1'])
      const content = canvas.getByText(/Sam Rivera owns Atlas/)
      await expect(atlas).toHaveAttribute('aria-controls', content.closest('td')!.id)
      // The content spans the whole row, checkbox and button columns included.
      await expect(content.closest('td')).toHaveAttribute('colspan', String(columns.length + 2))
      await userEvent.click(atlas)
      await expect(atlas).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false')
      await expect(canvas.queryByText(/Sam Rivera owns Atlas/)).toBeNull()
    })
    await step('Enter and Space toggle from the keyboard', async () => {
      const billing = canvas.getByRole('button', { name: 'Expand Billing revamp' })
      billing.focus()
      await userEvent.keyboard('{Enter}')
      await expect(billing).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true')
      await userEvent.keyboard(' ')
      await expect(billing).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false')
      await userEvent.keyboard('{Enter}')
    })
    await step('Sorting keeps the same row open, its content right under it', async () => {
      await userEvent.click(within(canvas.getByRole('columnheader', { name: /Files/ })).getByRole('button'))
      await expect(names(canvas)).toEqual(['Design tokens', 'Billing revamp', 'Atlas', 'Onboarding'])
      const texts = rowTexts(canvas)
      const at = texts.findIndex((t) => t.includes('Billing revamp') && !t.includes('owns'))
      await expect(texts[at + 1]).toMatch(/Mia Chen owns Billing revamp/)
      await expect(canvas.getByRole('button', { name: 'Expand Billing revamp' })).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true')
      await expect(canvas.getByRole('button', { name: 'Expand Atlas' })).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false')
    })
    await step('Selecting a row leaves expansion alone', async () => {
      await userEvent.click(canvas.getByRole('checkbox', { name: 'Select Billing revamp' }))
      await userEvent.click(canvas.getByRole('checkbox', { name: 'Select all rows' }))
      await expect(args.onSelectionChange).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith(['p2', 'p4', 'p1', 'p3'])
      await expect(canvas.getByRole('button', { name: 'Expand Billing revamp' })).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true')
      await expect(args.onExpandedChange).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith(['p2'])
    })
  },
}

/** Opened from outside the table: `expandedIds` is the source of truth. */
export const ControlledExpansion: Story = {
  args: { expandedContent: details },
  render: function Render(args) {
    const [open, setOpen] = useState<string[]>([])
    return (
      <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 'var(--space-3)', justifyItems: 'start' }}>
        <Button variant="secondary" appearance="outlined" size="sm" onClick={() => setOpen(open.includes('p3') ? [] : ['p3'])}>
          {open.includes('p3') ? 'Close Onboarding' : 'Open Onboarding'}
        </Button>
        <Table
          {...args}
          expandedIds={open}
          onExpandedChange={(ids) => {
            setOpen(ids)
            args.onExpandedChange?.(ids)
          }}
        />
      </div>
    )
  },
  play: async ({ args, canvas }) => {
    const onboarding = canvas.getByRole('button', { name: 'Expand Onboarding' })
    await userEvent.click(canvas.getByRole('button', { name: 'Open Onboarding' }))
    await expect(onboarding).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true')
    await expect(canvas.getByText(/Leo Park owns Onboarding/)).toBeVisible()
    // The row's own button reports back; the caller decides.
    await userEvent.click(onboarding)
    await expect(args.onExpandedChange).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith([])
    await expect(onboarding).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false')
    await expect(canvas.getByRole('button', { name: 'Open Onboarding' })).toBeVisible()
  },
}

/** What each row's menu does; archived projects have no actions, so no button. */
const onAction = fn()
const actions = (p: Project): MenuEntry[] =>
  p.status === 'Archived'
    ? []
    : [
        { label: 'Edit', onSelect: () => onAction('edit', p.id) },
        { label: 'Duplicate', onSelect: () => onAction('duplicate', p.id) },
        { type: 'separator' },
        { label: 'Archive', isDestructive: true, onSelect: () => onAction('archive', p.id) },
      ]

/**
 * A row is as tall as what it holds. One line of text is 36px, and the
 * checkbox, the expand button and the actions button all fit in that; a
 * 32px button in a cell makes its row 48px.
 */
export const RowWithControl: Story = {
  tags: ['!dev'],
  args: {
    isSelectable: true,
    expandedContent: details,
    rowActions: actions,
    columns: [...textColumns, { key: 'open', header: 'Open', cell: (p) => (p.id === 'p1' ? <Button appearance="outlined">Open</Button> : null) }],
  },
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    const [atlas, billing] = canvas.getAllByRole('rowheader')
    await expect([atlas.clientHeight, billing.clientHeight]).toEqual([48, 36])
    await expect(cellHeights(canvas)[1]).toBe(32)
    // No divider: the row is exactly as tall as its cells.
    await expect(billing.closest('tr')!.getBoundingClientRect().height).toBe(36)
  },
}

/** The control columns at the edges: the expand button first, the actions button last, each 8px in from the edge. */
export const EdgeControls: Story = {
  tags: ['!dev'],
  args: { expandedContent: details, defaultExpandedIds: ['p1'], rowActions: actions },
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    const table = canvas.getByRole('table', { name: 'Projects' }).getBoundingClientRect()
    const expand = canvas.getByRole('button', { name: 'Expand Atlas' })
    const more = canvas.getByRole('button', { name: 'Actions for Atlas' })
    await expect(expand.getBoundingClientRect().left).toBeCloseTo(table.left + 8, 0)
    await expect(more.getBoundingClientRect().right).toBeCloseTo(table.right - 8, 0)
    // The open row's content lines up with the cells' text.
    await expect(contentBox(canvas.getByText(/Sam Rivera owns Atlas/)).left).toBeCloseTo(table.left + 8, 0)
    // The cell has no room for an outset ring: the rings are drawn inside the buttons.
    // Tab first, so the focus that follows counts as keyboard focus.
    await userEvent.tab()
    for (const button of [expand, more]) {
      button.focus()
      await expect(getComputedStyle(button).outlineStyle).toBe('solid')
      await expect(getComputedStyle(button).outlineOffset).toBe('-2px')
    }
  },
}

/** The menu renders into <body>, outside the story's canvas. */
const page = (el: HTMLElement) => within(el.ownerDocument.body)

/** A menu at the end of each row, for actions on that one record. */
export const RowActions: Story = {
  args: { rowActions: actions, isSelectable: true },
  play: async ({ canvas, step }) => {
    await step('The column has a hidden header, and a row with no items has no button', async () => {
      await expect(canvas.getByRole('columnheader', { name: 'Actions' })).toBeInTheDocument()
      await expect(canvas.queryByRole('button', { name: 'Actions for Design tokens' })).toBeNull()
    })
    await step('The button is named after the row and opens its menu', async () => {
      const atlas = canvas.getByRole('button', { name: 'Actions for Atlas' })
      await expect(atlas).toHaveAttribute('aria-haspopup', 'menu')
      await userEvent.click(atlas)
      await userEvent.click(await page(atlas).findByRole('menuitem', { name: 'Archive' }))
      await expect(onAction).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith('archive', 'p1')
      await waitFor(() => expect(atlas).toHaveFocus())
    })
    await step('Enter opens it from the keyboard; Escape closes it', async () => {
      const billing = canvas.getByRole('button', { name: 'Actions for Billing revamp' })
      billing.focus()
      await userEvent.keyboard('{Enter}')
      const menu = await page(billing).findByRole('menu')
      await waitFor(() => expect(menu).toBeVisible())
      await userEvent.keyboard('{Escape}')
      await waitFor(() => expect(billing).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false'))
      await waitFor(() => expect(billing).toHaveFocus())
    })
  },
}

/** Files summed in a footer row that sorting leaves at the bottom. */
const totalled: TableColumn<Project>[] = columns.map((c) =>
  c.key === 'name'
    ? { ...c, footer: 'Total' }
    : c.key === 'files'
      ? { ...c, footer: projects.reduce((n, p) => n + p.files, 0).toLocaleString('en') }
      : c,
)

export const TotalRow: Story = {
  args: { columns: totalled, isSelectable: true, expandedContent: details },
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    const [, body, foot] = canvas.getAllByRole('rowgroup')
    await expect(within(body).getAllByRole('row')).toHaveLength(4)
    // The label is the total row's header, so its cells read "Total, Files".
    await expect(within(foot).getByRole('rowheader', { name: 'Total' })).toBeInTheDocument()
    await expect(within(foot).getAllByRole('cell').map((c) => c.textContent)).toContain('1,464')
    // One cell per column, the checkbox and expand columns included, so it lines up.
    await expect(within(foot).getByRole('row').children).toHaveLength(canvas.getAllByRole('columnheader').length)
    // The header's 1px rule, over the total: 36px of row under it.
    const total = within(foot).getByRole('rowheader', { name: 'Total' })
    await expect(getComputedStyle(total).borderTopWidth).toBe('1px')
    // The table's closing rule sits under the total row.
    const table = canvas.getByRole('table')
    await expect(getComputedStyle(table).borderBottomWidth).toBe('1px')
    await expect(table.getBoundingClientRect().bottom - total.getBoundingClientRect().bottom).toBe(1)
    await expect(total.clientHeight).toBe(36)
    // Sorting moves the rows, never the total.
    await userEvent.click(within(canvas.getByRole('columnheader', { name: /Files/ })).getByRole('button'))
    await expect(canvas.getAllByRole('row').at(-1)).toHaveTextContent('Total')
  },
}

/** Drag or arrow-key a header's end edge to resize its column. */
export const Resizable: Story = {
  args: { isResizable: true, onColumnWidthsChange: fn() },
  play: async ({ args, canvas, step }) => {
    const owner = canvas.getByRole('columnheader', { name: /Owner/ })
    const handle = canvas.getByRole('separator', { name: 'Resize Owner' })
    await step('Every column header has a focusable vertical separator with its width as the value', async () => {
      await expect(canvas.getAllByRole('separator')).toHaveLength(columns.length)
      await expect(handle).toHaveAttribute('aria-orientation', 'vertical')
      await expect(handle).toHaveAttribute('aria-valuemin', '48')
      await expect(handle).toHaveAttribute('aria-valuemax', '1200')
      await waitFor(() => expect(Number(handle.getAttribute('aria-valuenow'))).toBe(Math.round(owner.getBoundingClientRect().width)))
    })
    await step('Arrow Right widens the column by 16px, Arrow Left narrows it', async () => {
      handle.focus()
      const before = Number(handle.getAttribute('aria-valuenow'))
      await userEvent.keyboard('{ArrowRight}')
      await expect(handle).toHaveAttribute('aria-valuenow', String(before + 16))
      await expect(args.onColumnWidthsChange).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith({ owner: before + 16 })
      await waitFor(() => expect(Math.round(owner.getBoundingClientRect().width)).toBe(before + 16))
      await userEvent.keyboard('{ArrowLeft}{ArrowLeft}')
      await expect(handle).toHaveAttribute('aria-valuenow', String(before - 16))
    })
    await step('End sets the widest width, Home the narrowest', async () => {
      await userEvent.keyboard('{End}')
      await expect(handle).toHaveAttribute('aria-valuenow', '1200')
      await userEvent.keyboard('{Home}')
      await expect(handle).toHaveAttribute('aria-valuenow', '48')
      await waitFor(() => expect(Math.round(owner.getBoundingClientRect().width)).toBe(48))
    })
    await step('Dragging the handle resizes by the distance moved', async () => {
      const files = canvas.getByRole('separator', { name: 'Resize Files' })
      const th = canvas.getByRole('columnheader', { name: /Files/ })
      const from = Math.round(th.getBoundingClientRect().width)
      const { x, y } = files.getBoundingClientRect()
      await userEvent.pointer([
        { keys: '[MouseLeft>]', target: files, coords: { clientX: x, clientY: y } },
        { target: files, coords: { clientX: x + 40, clientY: y } },
        { keys: '[/MouseLeft]', target: files, coords: { clientX: x + 40, clientY: y } },
      ])
      await expect(files).toHaveAttribute('aria-valuenow', String(from + 40))
      await waitFor(() => expect(Math.round(th.getBoundingClientRect().width)).toBe(from + 40))
    })
  },
}

/** Right to left: the handle is on the header's left edge, so Arrow Left widens. */
export const ResizableRtl: Story = {
  args: { isResizable: true },
  render: (args) => (
    <div dir="rtl">
      <Table {...args} />
    </div>
  ),
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    const handle = canvas.getByRole('separator', { name: 'Resize Owner' })
    await waitFor(() => expect(Number(handle.getAttribute('aria-valuenow'))).toBeGreaterThan(48))
    const before = Number(handle.getAttribute('aria-valuenow'))
    handle.focus()
    await userEvent.keyboard('{ArrowLeft}')
    await expect(handle).toHaveAttribute('aria-valuenow', String(before + 16))
    await userEvent.keyboard('{ArrowRight}{ArrowRight}')
    await expect(handle).toHaveAttribute('aria-valuenow', String(before - 16))
  },
}

/** Widths owned by the caller: the handle reports, the caller decides. */
export const ControlledWidths: Story = {
  args: { isResizable: true, columnWidths: { name: 200 }, onColumnWidthsChange: fn() },
  play: async ({ args, canvas }) => {
    const handle = canvas.getByRole('separator', { name: 'Resize Project' })
    await expect(handle).toHaveAttribute('aria-valuenow', '200')
    handle.focus()
    await userEvent.keyboard('{ArrowRight}')
    await expect(args.onColumnWidthsChange).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith({ name: 216 })
    // Not stored by the caller, so it stays where it was.
    await expect(handle).toHaveAttribute('aria-valuenow', '200')
  },
}

/** The parts the Specs tab numbers, each found by a selector inside the `Anatomy` story. */
export const anatomyParts = [
  { name: 'Caption', selector: 'caption', description: 'Names the table. Visually hidden unless showCaption.' },
  { name: 'Header row', selector: 'thead tr', description: 'Small semibold labels over a 1px rule, with no fill. Stays in view with hasStickyHeader.' },
  { name: 'Sort button', selector: 'th[aria-sort] button', description: 'The whole header label, with an icon for the sort. Only on sortable columns.' },
  { name: 'Select all', selector: 'thead [role="checkbox"]', description: 'With isSelectable. Selects or clears every row shown, and shows mixed when some are selected.' },
  { name: 'Row', selector: 'tbody tr', description: 'As tall as what it holds: 36px for one line of text. No divider: tinted when hovered or selected.' },
  { name: 'Row checkbox', selector: 'tbody [role="checkbox"]', description: 'Named after the row header: "Select Atlas".' },
  { name: 'Expand button', selector: 'tbody [aria-expanded]', description: 'With expandedContent: a ghost icon button. The chevron turns down when open.' },
  { name: 'Row header', selector: 'tbody th[scope="row"]', description: 'The column marked isRowHeader, medium weight: the name a row is known by.' },
  { name: 'Row actions', selector: 'tbody [aria-haspopup="menu"]', description: 'With rowActions: a ghost "more" button at the end of the row that opens a Menu.' },
  {
    name: 'Expanded row',
    selector: 'tbody td[colspan]',
    description: 'One cell spanning every column, under its row. Holds any layout.',
  },
  { name: 'Total row', selector: 'tfoot tr', description: 'With a footer on any column: a semibold row under a 1px rule, outside the sort.' },
]

/** Every part present: caption shown, a sortable column, selection, one row open, row actions, a total. */
export const Anatomy: Story = {
  tags: ['!dev'],
  args: {
    showCaption: true,
    isSelectable: true,
    expandedContent: details,
    defaultExpandedIds: ['p1'],
    rowActions: actions,
    // Every project, so the total matches the rows on screen.
    columns: totalled,
  },
  play: async ({ canvasElement, canvas }) => {
    const found = await expectAnatomy(canvasElement, anatomyParts)
    await expect(found[7]).toHaveTextContent('Atlas')
    await expect(found[9]).toHaveTextContent(/Sam Rivera owns Atlas/)
    await expect(found[10]).toHaveTextContent('Total')
    // Cells padded 8px all round, the caption 24px from the top and 8px from the table.
    const cell = getComputedStyle(found[7])
    await expect([cell.paddingTop, cell.paddingRight, cell.paddingBottom, cell.paddingLeft]).toEqual(['8px', '8px', '8px', '8px'])
    const caption = getComputedStyle(found[0])
    await expect([caption.paddingTop, caption.paddingBottom]).toEqual(['24px', '8px'])
    // 8px in from the table's edges, as the cells' text: the caption and the checkbox at the start, the actions button at the end.
    const table = canvas.getByRole('table').getBoundingClientRect()
    await expect(contentBox(found[0]).left).toBeCloseTo(table.left + 8, 0)
    await expect(found[5].getBoundingClientRect().left).toBeCloseTo(table.left + 8, 0)
    await expect(found[8].getBoundingClientRect().right).toBeCloseTo(table.right - 8, 0)
    // The checkbox column is the 16px box with 8px either side; the expand column, its 24px button with 8px either side.
    await expect([found[5].closest('td')!.clientWidth, found[6].closest('td')!.clientWidth]).toEqual([32, 40])
    await expect(canvas.getByRole('columnheader', { name: 'Actions' })).toBeInTheDocument()
    // The expand column is announced like the others, by a hidden header.
    await expect(canvas.getByRole('columnheader', { name: 'Details' })).toBeInTheDocument()
  },
}

/** Two columns and two rows, small enough for the Specs tab's States to sit side by side. */
const brief = { columns: columns.filter((c) => c.key === 'name' || c.key === 'files'), rows: projects.slice(0, 2) }

/** Specs, States: the plain table. */
export const StateEnabled: Story = { tags: ['!dev'], args: brief }

/** Specs, States: sorted by Files, ascending. */
export const StateSorted: Story = { tags: ['!dev'], args: { ...brief, defaultSort: { key: 'files', direction: 'ascending' } } }

/** Specs, States: Atlas selected. */
export const StateSelected: Story = { tags: ['!dev'], args: { ...brief, isSelectable: true, defaultSelectedIds: ['p1'] } }

/** Specs, States: Atlas open. */
export const StateExpanded: Story = { tags: ['!dev'], args: { ...brief, expandedContent: details, defaultExpandedIds: ['p1'] } }

/** Guidelines, Don't: numbers at the start, so the digits do not line up. */
export const DontNumbersAtStart: Story = {
  tags: ['!dev'],
  args: { columns: columns.map(({ align: _align, ...c }) => c) },
}

/** Guidelines, Don't: no row header, so a row's checkbox can only say which number it is. */
export const DontNoRowHeader: Story = {
  tags: ['!dev'],
  args: { isSelectable: true, columns: columns.map(({ isRowHeader: _isRowHeader, ...c }) => c) },
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    // Counted from `rows`, so a sort does not rename it; but "row 1" says nothing.
    await expect(canvas.getByRole('checkbox', { name: 'Select row 1' })).toBeInTheDocument()
    await expect(canvas.queryByRole('rowheader')).toBeNull()
    // Sorted by Files, Atlas moves to the third row and keeps its name.
    await userEvent.click(within(canvas.getByRole('columnheader', { name: /Files/ })).getByRole('button'))
    await expect(canvas.getByRole('checkbox', { name: 'Select row 1' }).closest('tr')).toHaveTextContent('Atlas')
    await expect(canvas.getAllByRole('row')[3]).toHaveTextContent('Atlas')
  },
}

Controlled Sort incomplete example
Sorted by the caller (e.g. a server): the table reports the sort and shows the rows as given.
const ControlledSort = () => {
    const [sort, setSort] = useState<{ key: string; direction: 'ascending' | 'descending' } | null>(null)
    const rows = sort ? [...projects].sort((a, b) => a.owner.localeCompare(b.owner) * (sort.direction === 'ascending' ? 1 : -1)) : projects

    return (
        <Table
            columns={[
              { key: 'name', header: 'Project', sortable: true, isRowHeader: true },
              { key: 'owner', header: 'Owner', sortable: true },
              { key: 'status', header: 'Status', cell: (p) => <Tag variant={tone[p.status]} text={p.status} /> },
              { key: 'files', header: 'Files', sortable: true, align: 'end', cell: (p) => p.files.toLocaleString('en') },
              { key: 'updated', header: 'Updated', sortable: true, align: 'end', cell: (p) => date.format(p.updated) },
            ]}
            getRowId={(p: Project) => p.id}
            caption="Projects"
            onSelectionChange={fn()}
            onExpandedChange={fn()}
            rows={rows}
            sort={sort}
            onSortChange={setSort} />
    );
};
