# Table Rows of records with the same fields, to scan and compare: projects, invoices, mem...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import * as TableStories from './Table.stories'

<Meta of={TableStories} />

# Table

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

Rows of records with the same fields, to scan and compare: projects,
invoices, members. Columns can sort, rows can be selected, expanded and
acted on, and a total row can sum them up.

<Status of={TableStories} />

<Canvas of={TableStories.Selectable} />

## Variants

Table has one size: 8px round each cell, so a row of text is
36px, and a row that holds a button or a field grows to fit it. Any table
takes any of these together: a selectable table can also expand its rows
and keep its header in view.

| Variant | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `isSelectable` | Acting on several rows at once: archive, export, assign. |
| `expandedContent` | Details that belong to one row but do not fit in a column: a description, a timeline, line items. |
| `hasStickyHeader` | Long tables that scroll inside a fixed height, so the column names stay in view. |
| `rowActions` | Actions on one record (edit, duplicate, archive) that do not earn a column: a menu at the row's end. |
| `footer` on a column | A total row under the rows: sums, counts, averages. |
| `isResizable` | Tables whose columns hold text of unknown length (names, notes, emails), so people can widen what they read. |
| `emptyState` | Saying why there are no rows, and what to do: clear a search, add the first one. |

<Canvas of={TableStories.Default} />

Rows with details open under themselves. Expansion is independent of
selection and survives sorting:

<Canvas of={TableStories.ExpandableRows} />

A menu at the end of each row. A row with nothing to do gets no button:

<Canvas of={TableStories.RowActions} />

A total row under the rows, which sorting leaves at the bottom. The table
does not add anything up: you pass each column's `footer`, so you decide
whether it totals this page or every row.

<Canvas of={TableStories.TotalRow} />

A handle on each header's end edge resizes its column, by dragging or by
the arrow keys. The table is then laid out by its header widths: give the
columns a starting `width`, and keep `columnWidths` if they should last.
Pair it with a [Column Chooser](?path=/docs/components-data-display-column-chooser--docs)
to hide columns as well.

<Canvas of={TableStories.Resizable} />

<Canvas of={TableStories.StickyHeader} />

<Canvas of={TableStories.Empty} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Table, type TableColumn } from 'zweihander/table'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/table.json
```

- Source: [src/components/data-display/Table.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/data-display/Table.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/table](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/table)
- Behaviour: a native `<table>`; selection uses the kit's [Checkbox](?path=/docs/components-controls-checkbox--docs), expansion its [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs), row actions its [Menu](?path=/docs/components-navigation-menu--docs)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={TableStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={TableStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The table sits in a container that scrolls sideways on a narrow screen
rather than squeezing the columns. The selection column comes first, then
the expand column; the actions column comes last. A row whose
`expandedContent` or `rowActions` returns nothing leaves that cell empty.
The total row is a `<tfoot>`, so it stays at the bottom whatever the sort.

## Measurements

A row has no height of its own: it is as tall as what its cells hold.

| What the row holds | Row height |
| --- | --- |
| One line of text (20px), or a Tag | 36px |
| A checkbox, an expand button or an actions button (24px) | 36px |
| A 24px button | 40px |
| A 32px button or field | 48px |
| Header (one 16px line) | 32px |

A body row is exactly that tall: there is no divider under it. The header
and the total row add their 1px rule, and a table that has rows adds one
more under its last row. The checkbox, expand and actions
columns take 2px less block padding than the other cells, so their 24px
buttons do not make a row of text taller.

<SpecTable
  caption="Every table"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Cell', property: 'Padding, all round', token: '--space-2' },
    { part: 'Header cell', property: 'Padding, all round', token: '--space-2' },
    { part: 'Header row', property: 'Rule under it', token: '--border-width' },
    { part: 'Total row', property: 'Rule above it', token: '--border-width' },
    { part: 'Table', property: 'Rule under it, with rows', token: '--border-width' },
    { part: 'Cell', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body' },
    { part: 'Cell', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body' },
    { part: 'Header cell', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body-sm' },
    { part: 'Header cell', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body-sm' },
    { part: 'Sort button', property: 'Block padding', token: '--space-0-5' },
    { part: 'Sort button', property: 'Inline padding', token: '--space-1' },
    { part: 'Sort button', property: 'Gap', token: '--space-1' },
    { part: 'Sort button', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-sm' },
    { part: 'Sort icon', property: 'Size', token: '--icon-md' },
    { part: 'Selection column', property: 'Width', token: '--box-md' },
    { part: 'Expand column', property: 'Width', token: '--box-lg' },
    { part: 'Expand icon', property: 'Size', token: '--icon-md' },
    { part: 'Actions column', property: 'Width', token: '--box-lg' },
    { part: 'Expanded row', property: 'Block start padding', token: '--space-2' },
    { part: 'Expanded row', property: 'Block end padding', token: '--space-4' },
    { part: 'Caption', property: 'Block start padding', token: '--space-6' },
    { part: 'Caption', property: 'Block end padding', token: '--space-2' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Width', token: '--focus-width' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Offset, inside the button', token: '--focus-offset-inset' },
    { part: 'Sort button', property: 'Hit area on touch screens', token: '--target-coarse' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Resize handle (isResizable)"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Handle', property: 'Width', token: '--box-2xs' },
    { part: 'Handle line', property: 'Inset from the header edges', token: '--space-1' },
    { part: 'Handle line, hover and drag', property: 'Width', token: '--focus-width' },
    { part: 'Handle', property: 'Hit area on touch screens', token: '--target-coarse' },
  ]}
/>

The handle line is 1px at rest; no token covers a hairline. Its strip is 16px wide (44px on touch screens), at the
header's end, over the header's own padding. The last column's handle sits on the table's edge and shows its line
only on hover and drag. A column is 48px to 1200px wide; the arrow
keys move it 16px at a time.

Rows have no divider between them: the hover tint and the selection fill
tell them apart. The header ends on a 1px rule and its labels are
semibold; the total row sits under the same rule, so the sum reads as a
sum. A table that has rows closes on that rule too, as Atlassian's dynamic
table: under the last row, an open row's content or the total row,
whichever comes last. It is the table's own border, so under a sticky
header it scrolls with the rows, and whatever a page puts under the table
(a Pagination, a footer) keeps its own gap below the rule. An empty table
has no closing rule: the header's is the only one over the empty state.
The sort button pulls itself out
by its own padding, so its label lines up with the cells below and its
hover fill adds nothing to the header's height.

**Every cell is padded 8px all round**, the first and last of a row
included: the first column's text, the caption and an open row's content
all start 8px in from the table's left edge, and an end-aligned last
column ends 8px short of its right edge. The control columns are their
control with 8px either side: 32px for the 16px checkbox, 40px for the
24px expand and actions buttons. Focus rings in the control columns are
drawn inside the control, because the cell has no room for an outset
ring. Figures are tabular, so numbers line up column-wide.

## Color

Switch the theme and the accent in the toolbar: the values follow.

<SpecTable
  caption="Header"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Header row', property: 'Background when sticky', token: '--color-surface-raised' },
    { part: 'Header label', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text' },
    { part: 'Sort icon', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-subtlest' },
    { part: 'Sort icon, sorted column', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-icon-brand' },
    { part: 'Header row', property: 'Rule under it', token: '--color-border' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Row"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Background', token: '--color-surface-raised' },
    { part: 'Cell', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text' },
    { part: 'Total row', property: 'Rule above it', token: '--color-border' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Hover"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Row', property: 'Background', token: '--color-background-neutral' },
    { part: 'Sort button', property: 'Background', token: '--color-background-neutral' },
    { part: 'Sort button', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Selected"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Row', property: 'Background', token: '--color-background-brand-subtlest' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Resize handle"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Handle line', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-border' },
    { part: 'Handle line, hover and drag', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-background-brand-bold' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable caption="Every part" rows={[{ part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-border-focused' }]} />

- The header has no fill. With `hasStickyHeader` it takes the container's
  own `--color-surface-raised`, only so the rows scroll under it.
- Rows are not striped, and have no divider: hover and selection tint
  the row under the pointer or the checkbox, from edge to edge.
- The sort icon of a column that is not sorted is `--color-text-subtlest`;
  the sorted column's is the brand colour.
- **Two selected rows next to each other** read as one filled block;
  each row's checkbox says which are in it.
- **An open row and its content read as one block**: the content row
  shares its row's hover and selected tint, and its 16px block-end padding
  sets the pair apart from the next row.

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={TableStories.StateEnabled} />
</States>

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
    { label: 'Pressed', pseudo: 'active' },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={TableStories.StateEnabled} />
</States>

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Sorted', content: <Story of={TableStories.StateSorted} /> },
    { label: 'Selected', content: <Story of={TableStories.StateSelected} /> },
  ]}
/>

<States states={[{ label: 'Expanded', content: <Story of={TableStories.StateExpanded} /> }]} />

Each example forces the state on every row and button at once; on screen
it is the one under the pointer or the keyboard.

- **Hover** tints the row with `--color-background-neutral`, and the sort button too. The
  content row of an open row takes no hover of its own, only its row's.
- **Focus** is a 2px `--color-border-focused` outline, drawn 2px inside the sort button.
  The checkboxes and the expand button keep
  their own focus rings.
- **Pressed** has no look of its own: the click sorts, selects or opens,
  and that state's look follows.
- **Resize handle**: hover and drag thicken its line to 2px `--color-background-brand-bold`;
  focus draws the `--color-border-focused` outline inside the handle.
- **Disabled**: Table has none. A row that cannot be acted on is a row
  without the control.
- **Sorted** shows the column's icon at full colour, pointing up or down.
- **Selected** tints the row with `--color-background-brand-subtlest`.
- **Expanded** turns the chevron to point down and opens the content row
  under it.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={TableStories} />
</div>

`TableColumn<Row>` describes one column:

- `key`: unique; also the row field shown when there is no `cell`.
- `header`: the column's label.
- `cell`: renders the cell; defaults to `row[key]`.
- `sortable`: adds a sort button to the header. It sorts by `sortValue`,
  or by `row[key]`.
- `align`: `start`, `center` or `end`. `end` for numbers and dates, so the
  digits line up.
- `width`: any CSS width, e.g. `8rem` or `20%`.
- `isRowHeader`: makes the column's cells `<th scope="row">`, the name a
  row is known by. Usually the first column.
- `footer`: this column's cell in the total row, e.g. a sum. Any column
  with one adds the row; put the label ("Total") on the row header column.
  Hidden while there are no rows.

`TableSort` is `{ key, direction }`, with direction `ascending` or
`descending`.

`size` and `density` are deprecated. Table has one size, as Atlassian's
does: `size="sm"` (and `density="sm"`) renders the same table as `md`.
Both are still accepted for one release; drop them. The kit's rule for a
deprecated prop: it warns in the development console when it is passed a
value that is not its documented default, and a renamed prop warns
whenever it is used. So `size="sm"` and any `density` warn, and
`size="md"`, the default written out, is silent.

With `sort` controlled, the table leaves the order to you. `sortRows(rows,
columns, sort)` returns the rows in the order the table would sort them,
so you can sort every row before slicing out a page.

### Differences from the spec

Cell sizing follows the Figma library: Atlassian's dynamic table with 8px
round every cell.

- **No row height, and one size.** A cell has 8px padding all round
  and the row is as tall as its content; rows were a fixed 48px
  and 40px before, picked by `density` and then `size`, which are
  deprecated.
- **No row dividers.** Only the 1px rule under the header and the one
  that closes a table with rows, as Atlassian draws them; rows are told
  apart by the hover tint and the selection fill.
- **The total row has a 1px rule above it.** Atlassian's table has no
  total row; the rule is the header's, turned over. The table's closing
  rule then sits under the total row.
- **No header fill, and padded edges.** The header is its labels over the
  rule, as Atlassian's dynamic table. Unlike Atlassian's, the first and
  last cells keep their 8px at the table's edge. The hover and selection
  tints run edge to edge.
- **The caption** sits 24px from the top and 8px above the table, 8px in
  from the edge where the cells' text starts. Its type stays the cells' size,
  semibold; Atlassian's is a 20px heading.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Table for records that share their fields, when people compare them
or look one up: projects, invoices, members. Align numbers and dates to the
end, and mark the column a row is known by with `isRowHeader`.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={TableStories.Default} />}
  doCaption="Numbers and dates aligned to the end, in tabular figures: the digits line up column-wide."
  dont={<Story of={TableStories.DontNumbersAtStart} />}
  dontCaption="Aligned to the start, 9 sits under the 1 of 1,203, and the column cannot be compared at a glance."
/>

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={TableStories.Selectable} />}
  doCaption="A row header names each row, so its checkbox reads “Select Atlas”."
  dont={<Story of={TableStories.DontNoRowHeader} />}
  dontCaption="Without one, every checkbox is “Select row 1”, “Select row 2”: a screen reader user cannot tell what they select."
/>

**Sort cycles ascending, descending, off.** The third click returns to the
original order, which is often the one that meant something. Uncontrolled,
the table sorts a copy: dates as dates, numbers as numbers, text by locale
with "file 2" before "file 10". Empty values sort last both ways.

<Canvas of={TableStories.EmptyValuesSortLast} />

With server-side sorting, pass `sort` and `onSortChange` and hand back the
rows already sorted:

<Canvas of={TableStories.ControlledSort} />

**Paging is not built in.** Put a
[Pagination](?path=/docs/components-navigation-pagination--docs) under the
table and pass it one page of `rows`. With `getRowId`, selection keeps
working across pages: "Select all" adds or removes this page's rows only.

<Canvas of={TableStories.Paged} />

Pass `expandedIds` to open rows from outside the table:

<Canvas of={TableStories.ControlledExpansion} />

## When not to use

- **For records that do not share fields**, or that are read one at a
  time, like products in a shop. Use [Cards](?path=/docs/components-data-display-card--docs).
- **For layout.** A table announces rows and columns to a screen reader;
  use CSS grid to place things side by side.
- **For a spreadsheet**, where arrow keys move between cells and cells
  are edited in place. Table is a plain table, not an ARIA grid; the kit
  has no data grid yet.

## Accessibility

- A real `<table>` named by its `<caption>`, with `<th scope="col">`
  headers and a `<th scope="row">` for the row header column: screen
  readers announce the column and the row for every cell.
- Sortable headers carry `aria-sort` (`ascending`, `descending` or
  `none`); the sort control is a button inside the header.
- Row checkboxes are named after the row header ("Select Atlas"), or
  "Select row 1" without one, counted from `rows` so a sort does not
  rename them. The header checkbox is "Select all rows" and reports
  `mixed` when some are selected. A selected row has `aria-selected`.
- Each expand button is named after the row header ("Expand Atlas"),
  reports `aria-expanded`, and while open points at the content cell with
  `aria-controls`. Enter and Space toggle it. The name stays the same open
  or closed; `aria-expanded` carries the state.
- A row with nothing to expand has no button.
- The expand column's header is "Details", visually hidden, so the column
  is announced like the others.
- The content cell spans every column, so it is read as one cell under its
  row.
- Each row actions button is named after the row header ("Actions for
  Atlas") and reports `aria-haspopup="menu"`. Enter opens the menu,
  Escape closes it, and focus returns to the button. A row with no items
  has no button.
- The actions column's header is "Actions", visually hidden.
- When the table is wider than its box and nothing in it takes focus, the
  scroll box becomes a tab stop with a focus ring: `role="region"` named by
  the caption, which the browser scrolls with the arrow keys. A table that
  fits, or whose cells hold a control (a sort button, a checkbox), gets no
  extra tab stop.
- With `isResizable`, each column header holds a focusable
  `role="separator"` with `aria-orientation="vertical"`, named "Resize"
  and the header ("Resize Owner"), or the column's `key` when the header
  is not plain text. Its `aria-valuenow` is the column's
  width in px, between `aria-valuemin` 48 and `aria-valuemax` 1200.
- Arrow Right widens the column 16px and Arrow Left narrows it (mirrored
  in right-to-left); Home sets the narrowest width and End the widest.
  Dragging the handle does the same with a pointer.
- The total row is in a `<tfoot>` with one cell per column, so each total
  is announced under its column; the label column is its row header.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

import type { ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Tabs as BaseTabs } from '@base-ui/react/tabs'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Tabs.module.css'

export interface TabItem {
  value: string
  label: ReactNode
  /** The panel shown while this tab is selected. */
  content?: ReactNode
  icon?: ReactNode
  disabled?: boolean
}

export interface TabsProps {
  items: TabItem[]
  value?: string
  defaultValue?: string
  onValueChange?: (value: string) => void
  /** `underline`: a line under the selected tab. `pills`: a filled segment, for switching views in a toolbar. */
  appearance?: 'underline' | 'pills'
  size?: 'sm' | 'md'
  orientation?: 'horizontal' | 'vertical'
  /** Tabs share the full width equally. */
  isFullWidth?: boolean
  /** Select a tab as soon as it gets focus, rather than on Enter or Space. */
  activateOnFocus?: boolean
  /** Keep hidden panels in the DOM, e.g. to preserve their state. */
  keepMounted?: boolean
  /** Names the tab list when nothing on the page does. */
  'aria-label'?: string
  className?: string
}

export function Tabs({
  items,
  value,
  defaultValue,
  onValueChange,
  appearance = 'underline',
  size = 'md',
  orientation = 'horizontal',
  isFullWidth = false,
  activateOnFocus = false,
  keepMounted = false,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel,
  className,
}: TabsProps) {
  return (
    <BaseTabs.Root
      value={value}
      defaultValue={defaultValue ?? (value === undefined ? items.find((i) => !i.disabled)?.value : undefined)}
      onValueChange={onValueChange && ((v) => onValueChange(v as string))}
      orientation={orientation}
      className={cn(styles.tabs, styles[appearance], styles[size], styles[orientation], isFullWidth && styles.fullWidth, className)}
    >
      <BaseTabs.List className={styles.list} activateOnFocus={activateOnFocus} aria-label={ariaLabel}>
        {items.map((item) => (
          <BaseTabs.Tab key={item.value} value={item.value} disabled={item.disabled} className={styles.tab}>
            {item.icon && (
              <span className={styles.icon} aria-hidden="true">
                {item.icon}
              </span>
            )}
            {item.label}
          </BaseTabs.Tab>
        ))}
        <BaseTabs.Indicator className={styles.indicator} />
      </BaseTabs.List>
      {items.map(
        (item) =>
          item.content !== undefined && (
            <BaseTabs.Panel key={item.value} value={item.value} keepMounted={keepMounted} className={styles.panel}>
              {item.content}
            </BaseTabs.Panel>
          ),
      )}
    </BaseTabs.Root>
  )
}

# Tabs Switches between views of the same thing without leaving the page: Overview, Activi...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import * as TabsStories from './Tabs.stories'

<Meta of={TabsStories} />

# Tabs

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

Switches between views of the same thing without leaving the page:
Overview, Activity, Settings of one project.

<Status of={TabsStories} />

<Canvas of={TabsStories.Default} />

## Variants

`appearance` is the look. Either takes either size and orientation.

| Appearance | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `underline` | The sections of a page or a panel. Tabs sit on a 1px rule; a bar slides under the selected one. The default. |
| `pills` | A compact view switch in a toolbar, such as List / Board. A segmented track with the selected tab lifted. |

<Canvas of={TabsStories.Pills} />

| Form | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `isFullWidth` | Two to four tabs that should fill a narrow container, such as a side panel or a phone screen. |
| `vertical` | Many sections, or labels too long for a row: settings pages, a panel beside its content. |
| Icons | Recognisable icons beside the label. Never an icon alone: the label is the tab's name. |

<Canvas of={TabsStories.FullWidth} />

<Canvas of={TabsStories.Vertical} />

<Canvas of={TabsStories.WithIcons} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Tabs } from 'zweihander/tabs'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/tabs.json
```

- Source: [src/components/navigation/Tabs.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/navigation/Tabs.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/tabs](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/tabs)
- Behaviour: [Base UI Tabs](https://base-ui.com/react/components/tabs)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={TabsStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={TabsStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The indicator is one element for the whole list. It moves to the selected
tab rather than each tab drawing its own, so a change of tab slides it
across.

## Measurements

Each size is a control tier (Foundations / Sizing). `md` follows Atlassian
Design's tabs: 32px tall, 8px inline padding, no gap between tabs, a
14/20 label and a 2px indicator as wide as the label (8px in from the
tab's edges). The `underline` list is pulled out by those 8px, so the
first label lines up with the content below it; inside a container that
clips (a modal body, a card with hidden overflow) leave 8px of room on
that side, or the first tab's focus ring is cut, as with Atlassian's.
The 16px from the list
to the panel is the kit's own: Atlassian leaves that to the panel's
content. Atlassian Design has no small tab; `sm` is the kit's own, the
same tab in a 24px box for dense panels.

<SpecTable
  caption="sm"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Tab', property: 'Height', token: '--control-sm' },
    { part: 'Tab', property: 'Inline padding', token: '--space-2' },
    { part: 'Tab', property: 'Gap between icon and label', token: '--control-sm-gap' },
    { part: 'Tab', property: 'Corner radius (the focus ring follows it)', token: '--control-sm-radius' },
    { part: 'Tab, pills', property: 'Track corner radius', token: '--control-sm-radius-field' },
    { part: 'Icon', property: 'Size', token: '--icon-sm' },
    { part: 'Label', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body' },
    { part: 'Label', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="md"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Tab', property: 'Height', token: '--control-md' },
    { part: 'Tab', property: 'Inline padding', token: '--space-2' },
    { part: 'Tab', property: 'Gap between icon and label', token: '--control-md-gap' },
    { part: 'Tab', property: 'Corner radius (the focus ring follows it)', token: '--control-md-radius' },
    { part: 'Tab, pills', property: 'Track corner radius', token: '--control-md-radius-field' },
    { part: 'Icon', property: 'Size', token: '--icon-md' },

    { part: 'Label', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body' },

/>

<SpecTable

  rows={[
    { part: 'Tab list, pills', property: 'Gap between tabs', token: '--space-stack' },
    { part: 'Tab list', property: 'Gap to the panel', token: '--space-group' },
    { part: 'Indicator, underline', property: 'Thickness', token: '--border-width-selected' },
    { part: 'Tab', property: 'Focus ring offset (inside the tab)', token: '--focus-offset-inset' },

  ]}
/>

In `pills`, the track has a 2px inset
and the chip's corner is the track's minus 2px, so the two stay concentric
at every size.

## Color

Each appearance has its own label colours and indicator. Switch the theme
and the accent in the toolbar: the values follow.

<SpecTable
  caption="underline"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Tab', property: 'Label colour', token: '--color-text-subtlest' },
    { part: 'Tab, hover', property: 'Label colour', token: '--color-text' },
    { part: 'Selected tab', property: 'Label colour', token: '--color-text-brand' },
    { part: 'Indicator', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-background-brand-bold' },
    { part: 'Tab list', property: 'Rule', token: '--color-border' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="pills"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Tab list', property: 'Track', token: '--color-background-neutral' },
    { part: 'Tab', property: 'Label colour', token: '--color-text-subtle' },
    { part: 'Tab, hover, and selected tab', property: 'Label colour', token: '--color-text' },
    { part: 'Indicator', property: 'Background', token: '--color-surface' },
    { part: 'Indicator', property: 'Border', token: '--color-border' },
    { part: 'Indicator', property: 'Shadow', token: '--shadow-raised' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable caption="Every appearance" rows={[{ part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-border-focused' }]} />

Pill labels use `--color-text-subtle`, not `--color-text-subtlest`: that is
4.3:1 on the `--color-background-neutral` track, under 4.5:1.

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={TabsStories.StatesUnderline} />
</States>

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled, pills' },
    { label: 'Hover, pills', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Focus, pills', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={TabsStories.StatesPills} />
</States>

- **Selected**: the label takes the selected colour and the indicator
  slides under it (`underline`) or behind it (`pills`).
- **Hover** brings an unselected label up to `--color-text`. It adds no
  fill.
- **Focus** is a 2px `--color-border-focused` outline drawn just inside the tab, so it is
  not clipped by the list.
- **Disabled** (Archive, above) is the enabled look at 50% opacity. It
  still takes focus.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={TabsStories} />
</div>

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use Tabs to split one thing into views the reader moves between freely,
in any order: the overview, activity and settings of a project. Every
panel is about the same object, and only one is needed at a time.

Label each tab with a word or two. Labels do not wrap or shrink, so long
ones push the row past its container.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={TabsStories.DoShortLabels} />}
  doCaption="Short labels, a word or two: the row fits, and each reads at a glance."
  dont={<Story of={TabsStories.DontLongLabels} />}
  dontCaption="Long labels run past the edge of the container. Shorten them, or go vertical."
/>

Use `underline` for the sections of a page and `pills` for a view switch
in a toolbar. Name the tab list with `aria-label` when no heading does.
Selection is manual by default: arrow keys move focus, Enter or Space
selects, so a slow panel does not load on every keypress. Turn on
`activateOnFocus` only for light panels.

## When not to use

- **For a sequence.** Steps that must be done in order belong in a
  Stepper.
- **To compare content side by side.** Tabs show one panel at a time; put
  things that are read together on the same view.
- **To go to another page.** Use links, a side navigation or Breadcrumbs: a tab
  changes the view, not the URL.
- **For one setting with two or three options.** Use a radio group or a
  [Toggle Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-togglebutton--docs) group:
  that changes a value, not the view.

## Accessibility

- `role="tablist"` of `role="tab"` buttons with `aria-selected` and
  `aria-controls`; each panel is a `role="tabpanel"` labelled by its tab.
- One tab stop: Tab moves into the list on the selected tab and the next
  Tab moves on to the panel.
- Arrow keys move between tabs (Left and Right, or Up and Down when
  vertical, with `aria-orientation` set); Home and End jump to the ends.
- Arrows move focus without selecting; Enter or Space selects. With
  `activateOnFocus`, arrows select as they go.
- A disabled tab still takes focus, marked `aria-disabled`, so it is
  found and announced, but it cannot be selected.
- Tabs are 24 or 32px tall and grow to 44px on touch screens
  (`pointer: coarse`).
- Focus ring: 2px `--color-border-focused`, drawn inside the tab.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

import type { ComponentProps, MouseEvent, ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Tag.module.css'

/** Status first, then every hue the accent ramps offer, for categories. */
export const TAG_VARIANTS = [
  'neutral',
  'info',
  'success',
  'warning',
  'danger',
  'red',
  'orange',
  'amber',
  'yellow',
  'lime',
  'green',
  'emerald',
  'teal',
  'cyan',
  'sky',
  'blue',
  'indigo',
  'violet',
  'purple',
  'fuchsia',
  'pink',
  'rose',
] as const
export type TagVariant = (typeof TAG_VARIANTS)[number]

export interface TagProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'span'>, 'children'> {
  text: string
  startIcon?: ReactNode
  /** Image URL for a small avatar before the text, e.g. a person in a filter. */
  startAvatar?: string
  /**
   * One size: every tag is 20px tall.
   * @deprecated `sm` renders the same tag as `md` and warns in development; `md`, the default, is
   * silent. The prop goes in the next release: drop it.
   */
  size?: 'sm' | 'md'
  appearance?: 'subtle' | 'outlined' | 'solid'
  variant?: TagVariant
  hasRemoveButton?: boolean
  onRemove?: (event: MouseEvent<HTMLButtonElement>) => void
}

let hasWarned = false

export function Tag({
  text,
  startIcon,
  startAvatar,
  size = 'md',
  appearance = 'subtle',
  variant = 'info',
  hasRemoveButton = false,
  onRemove,
  className,
  ...props
}: TagProps) {
  if (import.meta.env.DEV && !hasWarned && size === 'sm') {
    hasWarned = true
    console.warn('Tag: `size="sm"` is deprecated and renders as `md`. `size` will be removed in the next release.')
  }
  return (
    <span
      className={cn(
        styles.tag,
        styles[appearance],
        styles[variant],
        className,
      )}
      {...props}
    >
      {startAvatar ? (
        // A plain image, not <Avatar>: the tag only needs a round crop, and a
        // cross-component import would not survive the copy-source install.
        <img src={startAvatar} alt="" className={styles.avatar} />
      ) : (
        startIcon && (
          <span className={styles.icon} aria-hidden="true">
            {startIcon}
          </span>
        )
      )}
      <span className={styles.text}>{text}</span>
      {hasRemoveButton && (
        <button
          type="button"
          // "Remove" alone is ambiguous in a list of tags, each with its own.
          aria-label={`Remove ${text}`}
          className={styles.remove}
          onClick={onRemove}
        >
          <Icon name="close" />
        </button>
      )}
    </span>
  )
}

# Tag A short label that categorises or marks something: a status, a filter chip, a person...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import { Tag } from './Tag'
import * as TagStories from './Tag.stories'

<Meta of={TagStories} />

# Tag

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A short label that categorises or marks something: a status, a filter
chip, a person picked in a field.

<Status of={TagStories} />

<Canvas of={TagStories.Matrix} />

## Variants

`variant` is the colour: a status, or a hue for categories. `appearance`
is the emphasis. Any variant takes any appearance.

| Variant | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| <Tag text="Neutral" variant="neutral" /> | A plain label with no status: a type, a version. |
| <Tag text="Info" variant="info" /> | Informational status: In review, Scheduled. The default. |
| <Tag text="Success" variant="success" /> | Done or healthy: Paid, Verified, Live. |
| <Tag text="Warning" variant="warning" /> | Needs attention soon: Expiring, Pending. |
| <Tag text="Danger" variant="danger" /> | Failed or blocked: Overdue, Error. |
| <Tag text="Violet" variant="violet" /> | A hue: one per category, label or owner. It carries no meaning. |

| Appearance | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| <Tag text="Subtle" /> | Most places: a tint that sits in a row of text. |
| <Tag text="Outlined" appearance="outlined" /> | Dense tables and busy surfaces, where many tints would be loud. |
| <Tag text="Solid" appearance="solid" /> | One tag that must stand out: a single status on a card. |

<Canvas of={TagStories.Colors} />

<Canvas of={TagStories.RemovableList} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Tag } from 'zweihander/tag'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/tag.json
```

- Source: [src/components/atomic-elements/Tag.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/atomic-elements/Tag.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/tag](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/tag)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={TagStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={TagStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

## Measurements

One size, Atlassian's tag: 20px tall, control tier xs (Foundations /
Sizing), so it sits in a line of text. The border is always there,
transparent unless outlined, so appearances never shift the layout.

In a line of text the tag is centred on the line, whatever the text's
size or family (the tag's own text is always the kit's sans; a mono table
cell around it changes nothing): a 20px line of body text stays 20px with a tag in it (so a Table row
stays 28px), and a taller line, like a heading's, keeps its height. Only a
line shorter than the tag, 12/16 small text, grows to 20px.

<Canvas of={TagStories.InText} />

`size` is deprecated and the prop will be removed in the next release.
`size="sm"` renders the same tag as `md` and warns once in development;
`size="md"`, the default written out, is silent.

<SpecTable
  caption="Every tag"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Height', token: '--control-xs' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Inline padding, from the outer edge', token: '--space-1' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--control-xs-radius' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Gap', token: '--space-1' },
    { part: 'Icon, avatar and remove button', property: 'Size', token: '--icon-xs' },
    { part: 'Text', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body-sm' },
    { part: 'Text', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body-sm' },
    { part: 'Remove button', property: 'Focus ring width', token: '--focus-width' },
    { part: 'Remove button', property: 'Hit area on touch screens', token: '--target-coarse' },
  ]}
/>

| Part | Property | Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Container | Maximum width | 180px |

The maximum width is Atlassian's and has no token: no size step is that
wide. Past it, and past the width of its parent, the text ends in an
ellipsis.

The corner is 4px and follows the Theme's radius preset like every
control: a pill under `radius="full-rounded"`.

## Color

Each variant has a solid, a colour on that solid, a subtle tint and a text
colour that subtle and outlined use. Subtle and outlined text is measured at
4.5:1 by the token build.

<SpecTable
  caption="neutral"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container, subtle', property: 'Background', token: '--color-background-neutral' },

/>

Every hue follows the same four tokens under its own name. Red, as an

<SpecTable

    { part: 'Container, subtle', property: 'Background', token: '--color-background-accent-red-subtler' },
    { part: 'Text, subtle and outlined', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-accent-red' },

<SpecTable caption="Every variant" rows={[{ part: 'Remove button focus ring', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-border-focused' }]} />

## States

The tag itself is not interactive. Its remove button is:

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
  ]}
>
  <Tag text="Design" hasRemoveButton />
</States>

- **Hover** tints the button with the tag's own text colour at 15%, so it
  reads on every variant and appearance without a token for each.
- **Focus** is the `--color-border-focused` outline every control uses, drawn inset so it
  stays inside a 20px tag.
- Pressing removes nothing by itself: `onRemove` reports it, and the
  parent drops the tag from its list.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={TagStories} />
</div>

Every other `<span>` attribute passes through to the container, including
`ref`.

### Differences from the spec

- **The spec's four variants needed new tokens.** `info`, `success`,
  `warning` and `danger` were added to the token layer for Tag and are
  shared with Alert and Toast.
- **One size.** The spec's sizes are gone: the tag takes Atlassian's box,
  20px tall with 12/16 text and a 180px maximum width. `size` stays one
  release as a deprecated prop that changes nothing.
- **No `isRounded`.** The corner reads the control tier's radius, so it
  follows the Theme's radius preset with every other control, and turns
  into a pill under `radius="full-rounded"`.
- **The 17 hue variants are additions.** Solid is step 600 with a white
  label on every hue, in both appearances, so a row of solid tags reads as
  one set; on the warm hues (orange, amber, yellow, lime and others) that
  label falls below 4.5:1. That is accepted on purpose.
- **`startAvatar` wins over `startIcon`** if both are passed; the spec
  does not say.
- **Digits are tabular.** Every digit takes the same width, so a tag
  holding a count or a countdown does not change width as it ticks.
- **The tag does not remove itself.** `onRemove` reports the click and
  the parent drops the tag from its list, so the list stays the one
  source of truth.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Tag to label or categorise: a status on a row, the categories of an
item, the filters applied to a list, the people picked in a field. Where a
tag has to pass AA, use `subtle` or `outlined`: solid hue tags keep one
white label across hues, which the warm ones carry under 4.5:1.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={TagStories.DoSubtleHues} />}
  doCaption="Warm hues in subtle: every label clears 4.5:1."
  dont={<Story of={TagStories.DontSolidWarmHues} />}
  dontCaption="The same hues solid: the white label falls under 4.5:1."
/>

Colour carries meaning here, so it is never the only signal: the text says
what the status is.

In a wrapped list of removable tags on touch, keep at least `--space-6`
between rows. The remove button's touch area reaches 12px above and below
a 20px tag, and neighbouring targets would overlap.

## When not to use

- **For an action.** A tag is a label; its only control is remove. Use a
  [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs).
- **For a choice the user toggles on and off.** Use a
  [Toggle Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-togglebutton--docs) or a
  Checkbox.
- **For a count.** Use a
  [Badge](?path=/docs/components-atomic-elements-badge--docs).

## Accessibility

- The remove button is named **"Remove `text`"** (e.g. "Remove Design"),
  so a list of tags does not read as a row of identical "Remove" buttons.
- It is a native `<button>`: Tab to reach, Enter or Space to press.
- On touch screens (`pointer: coarse`) its hit area grows to 44×44px
  without changing how the tag looks. That area reaches 12px above and
  below a 20px tag.
- After a tag is removed, focus has nowhere to stay and drops to the page.
  If that matters, move it to the next tag's remove button, or to the
  field the tags belong to, in your `onRemove`.
- The icon and the avatar are decorative.
- Every label clears 4.5:1 in both themes, measured by the `Contrast`
  story, except solid hue tags (see Differences from the spec).

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

'use client'

import {
  useCallback,
  useLayoutEffect,
  useRef,
  type ComponentProps,
  type CSSProperties,
  type ReactNode,
} from 'react'
import { Field } from '@base-ui/react/field'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import {
  assignRef,
  InputField,
  boxClass,
  focusControl,
  inputStyles,
  type InputSize,
  type ValidationState,
} from './InputField'
import styles from './Textarea.module.css'

export interface TextareaProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'textarea'>, 'size'> {
  label?: ReactNode
  helperText?: ReactNode
  validationState?: ValidationState
  size?: InputSize
  isFullWidth?: boolean
  /** Which way the user can drag to resize. Ignored with `hasAutoSize`. */
  resize?: 'none' | 'both' | 'vertical' | 'horizontal'
  /** Grow and shrink with the content, between `minRows` and `maxRows`. */
  hasAutoSize?: boolean
  /** The starting height, in lines. */
  minRows?: number
  /** The most it grows to before scrolling, in lines. */
  maxRows?: number
}

export function Textarea({
  label,
  helperText,
  validationState,
  size = 'md',
  isFullWidth,
  resize = 'vertical',
  hasAutoSize = false,
  minRows = 3,
  maxRows,
  required,
  disabled,
  name,
  className,
  onInput,
  ref,
  style,
  ...props
}: TextareaProps) {
  const inner = useRef<HTMLTextAreaElement | null>(null)
  const fit = useCallback(() => {
    const el = inner.current
    if (!el || !hasAutoSize) return
    // Collapse first so a shrinking value can shrink the box; max-block-size
    // (from maxRows) caps the result and the rest scrolls.
    el.style.blockSize = 'auto'
    el.style.blockSize = `${el.scrollHeight}px`
  }, [hasAutoSize])
  // Controlled values change without an input event; fit to those too.
  useLayoutEffect(fit, [fit, props.value])

  return (
    <InputField
      label={label}
      helperText={helperText}
      validationState={validationState}
      required={required}
      disabled={disabled}
      name={name}
      isFullWidth={isFullWidth}
      className={className}
    >
      <span className={cn(boxClass(size), styles.multiline, styles[`pad-${size}`])} onMouseDown={focusControl}>
        <Field.Control
          render={
            <textarea
              rows={minRows}
              ref={(node) => {
                inner.current = node
                assignRef(ref, node)
              }}
            />
          }
          {...(props as ComponentProps<typeof Field.Control>)}
          required={required}
          onInput={(event) => {
            fit()
            onInput?.(event as unknown as Parameters<NonNullable<TextareaProps["onInput"]>>[0])
          }}
          className={cn(inputStyles.control, styles.textarea)}
          style={
            {
              ...style,
              resize: hasAutoSize ? 'none' : resize,
              ...(maxRows && { maxBlockSize: `calc(${maxRows} * 1lh + 2 * var(--pad-block))` }),
            } as CSSProperties
          }
        />
      </span>
    </InputField>
  )
}

# Textarea Several lines of text: a message, a description, a note. The same field as [Tex...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import { Textarea } from './Textarea'
import * as TextareaStories from './Textarea.stories'

<Meta of={TextareaStories} />

# Textarea

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

Several lines of text: a message, a description, a note. The same field as
[Text Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textinput--docs): label, helper,
validation and sizes are shared.

<Status of={TextareaStories} />

<Canvas of={TextareaStories.Default} />

## Variants

One appearance, the white outlined box. What changes is the size and how
the height is set.

<Canvas of={TextareaStories.Sizes} />

| Size | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `md` | Forms and dialogs: the default. |
| `sm` | Dense places: a comment box in a table row, a side panel. |

<Canvas of={TextareaStories.AutoSize} />

| Height | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `resize="vertical"` (default) | People may want to see more at once and drag the corner to get it. |
| `hasAutoSize` with `maxRows` | Text whose length varies a lot, such as a chat message: the field grows as they write, up to `maxRows`, then scrolls. |
| `resize="none"` | A fixed height the layout depends on. |

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Textarea } from 'zweihander/textarea'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/textarea.json
```

<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={TextareaStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={TextareaStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The resize handle is the browser's own, in the input's bottom corner, on
the axes `resize` allows; `hasAutoSize` hides it. The placeholder is the
textarea's, in `--color-text-subtlest`.

## Measurements

A textarea grows, so it has no height token: it takes block padding
instead, after Atlassian's textarea: 2px in `sm` and 6px in `md`. Both
sizes take body type and 10px of inline padding, as every field's box,
so the text starts 11px from the outer edge. The starting height is `minRows` lines (3 by default)
plus that padding. The padding sits on the textarea, not the box, so the
resize handle lands in the field's corner.

<SpecTable
  caption="sm"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Input', property: 'Block padding', token: '--space-0-5' },
    { part: 'Input', property: 'Inline padding', token: '--space-2-5' },
    { part: 'Input', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body' },
    { part: 'Input', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--control-md-radius-field' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="md"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Input', property: 'Block padding', token: '--space-1-5' },
    { part: 'Input', property: 'Inline padding', token: '--space-2-5' },
    { part: 'Input', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body' },
    { part: 'Input', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--control-md-radius-field' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Every size"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Label and helper text', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body-sm' },

    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Width', token: '--focus-width' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Offset', token: '--focus-offset' },
  ]}
/>

20rem wide, capped at its container, or the container's width with
`isFullWidth`. With `maxRows`, the input stops at that many lines plus its
padding, whether it grew by itself or was dragged.

## Color

The same colours as Text Input: no colour variants, and the validation
state changes the edge and the helper text together.

/>

/>

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus' },
    { label: 'Error', content: <Textarea label="Note" minRows={2} validationState="error" helperText="Add a note." required /> },
    { label: 'Read-only', content: <Textarea label="Note" minRows={2} defaultValue="Ships Monday." readOnly /> },
    { label: 'Disabled', content: <Textarea label="Note" minRows={2} defaultValue="Ships Monday." disabled /> },
  ]}
>
  <Textarea label="Note" minRows={2} placeholder="Add a note" />
</States>

- **Hover** changes nothing; the cursor turns to a text cursor.
- **Focus** is a 2px `--color-border-focused` outline around the whole box, 2px outside
  it, on click as well as keyboard. In the error state it is
  `--color-text-danger`.
- **Read-only** fills the box with `--color-background-input`.
- **Disabled** is the enabled look at 50% opacity.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={TextareaStories} />
</div>

Every other `<textarea>` attribute passes through, including `ref`,
`name` and `autoComplete`.

### Differences from the spec

- **No `filled` appearance**, as on Text Input: every field is the white
  outlined box.
- Native `disabled`, `required`, `readOnly` names, and native `onChange`,
  as on Text Input.
- **`minRows` defaults to 3.** The spec gives none; the browser's own
  default of 2 is too short to read as a multi-line field.
- **`hasAutoSize`, `minRows` and `maxRows` are added**: the spec has a
  fixed `rows` only.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Textarea when the answer may run past one line: a message, a
description, feedback, an address. Set `minRows` to the length you expect,
so the field shows how much to write before anyone starts.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={TextareaStories.DoFitTheAnswer} />}
  doCaption="A starting height that fits the answer expected tells people how much to write."
  dont={<Story of={TextareaStories.DontOneRow} />}
  dontCaption="One row looks like a single-line field and hides what has been written."
/>

Use auto-size for text whose length varies a lot, always with a `maxRows`,
so a long entry never pushes the rest of the form off the screen.

## When not to use

- **For one line**, such as a name or a title. Use a
  [Text Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textinput--docs): Enter can
  submit the form there.
- **For formatted text** (bold, lists, links). A Textarea is plain text;
  use a rich-text editor.
- **For a search query.** Use [Search](?path=/docs/components-inputs-search--docs).

## Accessibility

- A real `<textarea>` with its `<label>`: clicking the label focuses it,
  and the label is its accessible name. Without a visible label, pass
  `aria-label`: it goes to the `<textarea>` itself.
- `helperText` is its description (`aria-describedby`);
  `validationState="error"` sets `aria-invalid="true"`. The helper text
  carries the message, not only the colour.
- `required` sets the native `required`; the label's asterisk is
  `aria-hidden`.
- Enter inserts a line break; it does not submit the form.
- Auto-size caps at `maxRows` and scrolls beyond it, so the page does not
  grow without limit and the text stays reachable by keyboard.
- The edge is the light `--color-border-input`, about 1.5:1, the same approved
  exception to WCAG 1.4.11 as Text Input; set
  `--color-border-input: var(--color-border-bold)` where 3:1 is needed.
- Focus ring: 2px, 2px offset, around the whole field.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

'use client'

import { createContext, useContext, type ComponentProps, type ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Field } from '@base-ui/react/field'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import {
  InputField,
  boxClass,
  focusControl,
  inputStyles,
  type InputSize,
  type ValidationState,
} from './InputField'

export interface TextInputProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'input'>, 'size' | 'prefix'> {
  label?: ReactNode
  /** Under the field; the error message when `validationState` is error. */
  helperText?: ReactNode
  validationState?: ValidationState
  size?: InputSize
  /** Text or an icon before the value, e.g. `<Icon name="search" />` or "https://". */
  prefix?: ReactNode
  /** Text or an icon after the value, e.g. "kg". */
  suffix?: ReactNode
  /** A filled segment joined to the start of the box: text that belongs to the value ("https://", "USD") or a `TextInputButton`. */
  startAddon?: ReactNode
  /** A filled segment joined to the end of the box: text (".com") or an attached `TextInputButton` ("Apply"). */
  endAddon?: ReactNode
  isFullWidth?: boolean
}

/** Lets a TextInputButton follow the field's `disabled` without being told twice. */
const FieldDisabledContext = createContext(false)

export function TextInput({
  label,
  helperText,
  validationState,
  size = 'md',
  prefix,
  suffix,
  startAddon,
  endAddon,
  isFullWidth,
  required,
  disabled,
  name,
  className,
  ...props
}: TextInputProps) {
  return (
    <InputField
      label={label}
      helperText={helperText}
      validationState={validationState}
      required={required}
      disabled={disabled}
      name={name}
      isFullWidth={isFullWidth}
      className={className}
    >
      <FieldDisabledContext value={Boolean(disabled)}>
        <span className={boxClass(size)} onMouseDown={focusControl}>
          {startAddon && <span className={cn(inputStyles.addon, inputStyles.addonStart)}>{startAddon}</span>}
          {prefix && <span className={inputStyles.affix}>{prefix}</span>}
          <Field.Control {...props} required={required} className={cn(inputStyles.control)} />
          {suffix && <span className={inputStyles.affix}>{suffix}</span>}
          {endAddon && <span className={cn(inputStyles.addon, inputStyles.addonEnd)}>{endAddon}</span>}
        </span>
      </FieldDisabledContext>
    </InputField>
  )
}

export type TextInputButtonProps = ComponentProps<'button'>

/**
 * A button inside a Text Input: an icon in `prefix` or `suffix` (give it an
 * `aria-label`), or a word in an add-on, where it fills the segment. Disabled
 * with the field; a read-only field keeps it, since copying or opening a
 * fixed value is what it is for.
 */
export function TextInputButton({ type = 'button', disabled, className, ...props }: TextInputButtonProps) {
  const fieldDisabled = useContext(FieldDisabledContext)
  return (
    <button
      type={type}
      disabled={disabled || fieldDisabled}
      className={cn(inputStyles.iconButton, className)}
      {...props}
    />
  )
}

# Text Input A single line of text: a name, an email, a URL. ## Variants There is one appe...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import { TextInput } from './TextInput'
import * as TextInputStories from './TextInput.stories'

<Meta of={TextInputStories} />

# Text Input

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A single line of text: a name, an email, a URL.

<Status of={TextInputStories} />

<Canvas of={TextInputStories.Default} />

## Variants

There is one appearance, the white outlined box. What changes is the
size, what sits beside the value, and the validation state.

<Canvas of={TextInputStories.Sizes} />

| Size | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `md` | Forms and dialogs: the default. |
| `sm` | Dense places: toolbars, table filters, inline edits. As tall as a default Button. |

<Canvas of={TextInputStories.PrefixSuffix} />

| Affix | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `prefix` | A fixed start the value continues: "https://", a currency sign, an icon that says what the field holds. |
| `suffix` | A unit the value is measured in: "kg", "%", "days". |

**Add-ons** are filled segments joined to the edge of the box, divided
from the value by a hairline. Use them when the fixed part is long enough,
or important enough, to need its own place: a protocol and a domain, a
currency code, or an action attached to the field.

<Canvas of={TextInputStories.Addons} />

| Add-on | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `startAddon` | A fixed start that is part of the value people see: "https://", "USD". |
| `endAddon` | A fixed ending (".com"), or an attached `TextInputButton` that acts on the value: "Apply", "Check". |

**Buttons in the field** act on the value without leaving it: open a link,
reveal, clear. `TextInputButton` is an icon button sized to the field; put
it in `suffix` (or `prefix`), or in an add-on, where it fills the segment.

<Canvas of={TextInputStories.WithButton} />

<Canvas of={TextInputStories.Validation} />

| Validation state | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `default` | Before anything is checked. |
| `error` | The value cannot be accepted. `helperText` says what to change. |
| `success` | A value checked against the server and accepted, such as a free username. Not for every field that passes. |

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { TextInput, TextInputButton } from 'zweihander/text-input'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/text-input.json
```

- Behaviour: [Base UI Field](https://base-ui.com/react/components/field)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={TextInputStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={TextInputStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The placeholder has no element of its own: it is the input's, shown in
`--color-text-subtlest` while the input is empty. With `required`, an
asterisk follows the label.

## Measurements

A field is one step taller than a Button, after Atlassian Design: `sm` is
32px and `md` is 40px (Foundations / Sizing). The sizes share the rest:
10px of inline padding, the 16px icon, the field radius, which never
becomes a pill, and body type.

The label and helper are 12px in both sizes, the label in bold
(`--font-weight-label`, 653, as Atlassian's form Label): only the box
changes height. A button in `prefix` or `suffix` is a 24px target
round its icon. The field is 20rem wide, capped at its container; with
`isFullWidth` it fills the container. The edge is 1px. An add-on runs
the full height of the box, and its 1px divider takes the edge's colour,
so a field in the error state is red all round, divider included.

## Color

The field has no colour variants. Its validation state changes the edge
and the helper text together. Switch the theme in the toolbar: the values
follow.

  ]}
/>

<SpecTable caption="Read-only" rows={[{ part: 'Container', property: 'Background', token: '--color-background-input' }]} />

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus' },
    { label: 'Filled', content: <TextInput label="Name" defaultValue="Okami" /> },
    { label: 'Error', content: <TextInput label="Name" validationState="error" helperText="Enter a name." required /> },
    { label: 'Read-only', content: <TextInput label="Name" defaultValue="Okami" readOnly /> },
    { label: 'Disabled', content: <TextInput label="Name" defaultValue="Okami" disabled /> },
  ]}
>
  <TextInput label="Name" placeholder="Your name" />
</States>

- **Hover** changes nothing: the field is already plainly a field, and the
  cursor turns to a text cursor.
- **Focus** is a 2px `--color-border-focused` outline, 2px outside the box, drawn on click
  as well as from the keyboard, since that is where typing will go. In the
  error state the ring is `--color-text-danger`.
- **Read-only** fills the box with `--color-background-input`: it can be focused
  and copied, not changed.
- **Disabled** is the enabled look at 50% opacity.
- **A button in an add-on** fills the segment: hover gives it `--color-background-neutral`,
  and its focus ring sits inside the segment, so the box's edge does not
  cut it. An icon button in `prefix` or `suffix` turns `--color-text` on
  hover. In a read-only field the box takes the add-on's fill, so only the
  divider sets the add-on apart.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={TextInputStories} />
</div>

`TextInputButton` takes every `<button>` attribute; it is `type="button"`
by default and follows the field's `disabled`.

Every other `<input>` attribute passes through to the input, including
`ref`, `type`, `name`, `pattern`, `maxLength`, `inputMode` and
`autoComplete`.

### Differences from the spec

- **No `filled` appearance.** The spec's filled field (a tinted box with a bottom rule) was dropped to match the Claude apps, where every field is the white outlined box.
- **Two sizes, not three.** `sm` (32px) and `md` (40px), after Atlassian Design: a field is one step taller than a button, so `sm` lines up with a Button in a toolbar. The spec's largest step was dropped; a big call to action is `md` with more room around it, not a taller box.
- **Native names** for native attributes: `disabled`, `required`,
  `readOnly` rather than `isDisabled`, `isRequired`, `isReadOnly`.
- **`onChange` is the native event**, not a value: the kit's rule for
  components that wrap a real input, so it works with every form library
  as-is.
- **Changed in 0.8:** `error` became `validationState="error"` plus
  `helperText`; `forwardRef` is gone (`ref` is a prop in React 19).

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Text Input for short free text on one line: a name, an email
address, a URL, a title. Give every field a visible label, and use the
placeholder only for a hint of the format.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={TextInputStories.DoVisibleLabel} />}
  doCaption="A visible label names the field; the placeholder only hints at the format."
  dont={<Story of={TextInputStories.DontPlaceholderAsLabel} />}
  dontCaption="A placeholder as the label disappears on the first keystroke, and with it what the field was for."
/>

**Errors** say what to change, in the helper text, next to the field. The
red edge only points at the message.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={TextInputStories.DoSayWhatToFix} />}
  doCaption="The error says what is wrong and how to fix it."
  dont={<Story of={TextInputStories.DontColourOnly} />}
  dontCaption="A red edge and 'Invalid' leave people guessing what to change."
/>

**Prefix or add-on.** A prefix is a hint inside the box, read past
without stopping: an icon, a currency sign. An add-on is a segment of its
own, for a fixed part long enough to label the value ("https://", ".com")
or for an action attached to it. Use one start and one end at most; a
field with an add-on and a prefix on the same side has two things before
the value to read.

## When not to use

- **For several lines.** Use a
  [Textarea](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textarea--docs): Enter adds a
  line instead of submitting.
- **For a quantity.** Use a
  [Number Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-numberinput--docs), which
  steps and parses. For numbers that are identifiers (postcodes, card
  numbers, phone numbers) keep the Text Input with `inputMode="numeric"`.
- **For a search query.** Use [Search](?path=/docs/components-inputs-search--docs),
  which clears and is exposed as a searchbox.
- **To pick from a known list.** Use a
  [Select](?path=/docs/components-inputs-select--docs) or a
  [Combobox](?path=/docs/components-inputs-combobox--docs).
- **For a unit people choose** (a currency, a country code). Add-ons take
  text or a `TextInputButton`, not a Select: put a
  [Select](?path=/docs/components-inputs-select--docs) beside the field.
- **For a date.** Use a [Date Picker](?path=/docs/components-inputs-datepicker--docs).

## Accessibility

- The label is a real `<label>` for the input: clicking it focuses the
  input, and it is the input's accessible name.
- `helperText` is the input's description (`aria-describedby`), so a
  screen reader reads it after the name.
- `validationState="error"` sets `aria-invalid="true"` on the input.
  Colour is never the only signal: the helper text carries the message.
- `required` sets the native `required`; the asterisk is `aria-hidden`, so
  it is not read as "star".
- Do not rely on the placeholder as a label: it is not reliably announced
  and disappears as soon as anyone types. Without a visible label, pass
  `aria-label`.
- Pressing the field's padding, a prefix or a text add-on focuses the
  input, as a click anywhere on a native field does.
- A `TextInputButton` is a native `<button>` after the input in the tab
  order, pressed with Enter or Space. An icon-only one needs `aria-label`.
  Pressing it does not move focus to the input.
- `TextInputButton` is disabled with the field. In a read-only field it
  stays enabled, since opening or copying a fixed value is what it is for.
- **The edge is `--color-border-input`, about 1.5:1, a deliberate exception to
  WCAG 1.4.11** (approved 2026-10-08), for the light hairline of the
  Claude apps. The field is a white `--color-surface-raised` box on the off-white page, and the label, placeholder and focus ring mark it too.
  If your audience needs 3:1, set `--color-border-input: var(--color-border-bold)`.
- Focus ring: 2px, 2px offset, on click and keyboard alike.
- Heights are 32 and 40px, above WCAG 2.5.8's 24px minimum; a button in
  the field is a 24px target. The
  label is part of the target, since clicking it focuses the input.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-vite'
import { expect } from 'storybook/test'
import { Button } from '@/components/buttons/Button'
import { TextInput } from '@/components/inputs/TextInput'
import { ACCENT_COLORS, GRAY_COLORS, Theme } from '@/theme/Theme'
import docs from './docs.module.css'

function Panel({ label }: { label: string }) {
  return (
    <div
      className={docs.card}
      style={{ display: 'flex', flexDirection: 'column', gap: 'var(--space-3)', background: 'var(--color-surface-raised)', color: 'var(--color-text)' }}
    >
      <span style={{ fontSize: 'var(--text-body)', fontWeight: 500 }}>{label}</span>
      <TextInput label="Email" placeholder="you@example.com" />
      <div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 'var(--space-2)' }}>
        <Button>Primary</Button>
        <Button variant="secondary">Secondary</Button>
      </div>
    </div>
  )
}

// Narrative and prose live in Overview.mdx.
const meta = {
  title: 'Foundations/Overview',
  component: Theme,
  parameters: { layout: 'padded' },
} satisfies Meta<typeof Theme>

export default meta
type Story = StoryObj<typeof meta>

export const AccentColor: Story = {
  name: 'Accent color',
  render: () => (
    <div className={docs.stackWide} style={{ gap: 'var(--space-4)' }}>
      <div style={{ display: 'flex', flexWrap: 'wrap', gap: 'var(--space-2)' }}>
        {ACCENT_COLORS.map((accent) => (
          <Theme key={accent} accentColor={accent} render={<Button size="sm" />}>
            {accent}
          </Theme>
        ))}
      </div>
      <p className={docs.note}>
        Every label above clears 4.5:1 on its own fill — the warm hues take dark
        labels rather than white.
      </p>
    </div>
  ),
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    const solid = (name: string) =>
      getComputedStyle(canvas.getByRole('button', { name })).backgroundColor
    // Changing the accent has to actually move --color-background-brand-bold.
    await expect(solid('blue')).not.toBe(solid('red'))
  },
}

export const GrayColor: Story = {
  name: 'Gray color',
  render: () => (
    <div className={docs.gridThirds}>
      {GRAY_COLORS.map((gray) => (
        <Theme key={gray} grayColor={gray} appearance="dark" style={{ borderRadius: 'var(--radius-panel)', padding: 'var(--space-3)' }}>
          <div
            style={{
              display: 'flex',
              alignItems: 'center',
              justifyContent: 'space-between',
              borderRadius: 'var(--radius-field)',
              background: 'var(--color-surface)',
              padding: 'var(--space-2) var(--space-3)',
            }}
          >
            <span style={{ fontSize: 'var(--text-body)', color: 'var(--color-text)' }}>{gray}</span>
            <span style={{ fontSize: 'var(--text-body)', color: 'var(--color-text-subtlest)' }}>muted</span>
          </div>
        </Theme>
      ))}
    </div>
  ),
}

export const Appearance: Story = {
  render: () => (
    <div className={docs.gridHalves} style={{ gap: 'var(--space-4)' }}>
      <Theme appearance="light" style={{ borderRadius: 'var(--radius-panel)', background: 'var(--color-surface)', padding: 'var(--space-4)' }}>
        <Panel label="appearance=&quot;light&quot;" />
      </Theme>
      <Theme appearance="dark" style={{ borderRadius: 'var(--radius-panel)', background: 'var(--color-surface)', padding: 'var(--space-4)' }}>
        <Panel label="appearance=&quot;dark&quot;" />
      </Theme>
    </div>
  ),
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    const [light, dark] = canvas.getAllByText(/appearance=/)
    const bg = (el: HTMLElement) =>
      getComputedStyle(el.closest('.light, .dark') as HTMLElement).getPropertyValue('--color-surface')
    await expect(bg(light)).not.toBe(bg(dark))
  },
}

export const TokenOverride: Story = {
  // Shows a consumer's own --color-background-brand-bold override; its contrast is the consumer's, not the kit's.
  parameters: { a11y: { test: 'off' } },
  name: 'Token override',
  render: () => (
    <div className={docs.gridHalves} style={{ gap: 'var(--space-4)' }}>
      <Theme style={{ borderRadius: 'var(--radius-panel)', padding: 'var(--space-4)' }}>
        <Panel label="default tokens" />
      </Theme>
      <Theme style={{ borderRadius: 'var(--radius-panel)', padding: 'var(--space-4)' }} tokens={{ radius: '1.5rem', 'color-background-brand-bold': 'oklch(0.55 0.2 150)' }}>
        <Panel label="radius + brand overridden" />
      </Theme>
    </div>
  ),
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    const scope = canvas.getByText('radius + brand overridden').closest('div[style]')
    await expect(scope).toHaveStyle({ '--radius': '1.5rem' })
  },
}

export const Nested: Story = {
  render: () => (
    <Theme appearance="dark" style={{ borderRadius: 'var(--radius-panel)', background: 'var(--color-surface)', padding: 'var(--space-4)' }}>
      <div className={docs.stackWide} style={{ gap: 'var(--space-4)' }}>
        <Panel label="dark page" />
        <Theme appearance="light" style={{ borderRadius: 'var(--radius-panel)', background: 'var(--color-surface)', padding: 'var(--space-4)' }}>
          <Panel label="light island inside it" />
        </Theme>
      </div>
    </Theme>
  ),
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    const island = canvas.getByText('light island inside it').closest('.light')
    await expect(island).toBeInTheDocument()
    const bg = (el: Element) => getComputedStyle(el as HTMLElement).getPropertyValue('--color-surface').trim()
    // Compared against :root rather than a literal, so the assertion is about
    // the nested scope resolving to the light default — not about how the
    // generator happens to spell oklch().
    await expect(bg(island!)).toBe(bg(document.documentElement))
    await expect(bg(island!)).not.toBe(bg(island!.parentElement!.closest('.dark')!))
  },
}

/**
 * An accent or gray set on a light island inside a dark page takes the
 * island's appearance, not the page's: the nearest scope wins at any depth.
 */
export const NestedPalettes: Story = {
  render: () => (
    <Theme appearance="dark" accentColor="orange" grayColor="slate" data-testid="dark" style={{ background: 'var(--color-surface)', padding: 'var(--space-4)' }}>
      <Theme appearance="light" style={{ background: 'var(--color-surface)', padding: 'var(--space-4)' }}>
        <Theme accentColor="orange" grayColor="slate" data-testid="island">
          <Panel label="orange on slate, light, inside dark" />
          <Theme appearance="dark" style={{ padding: 'var(--space-2)' }}>
            <Theme accentColor="orange" grayColor="slate" data-testid="deep">
              <Panel label="and dark again inside that" />
            </Theme>
          </Theme>
        </Theme>
        <Theme accentColor="orange" grayColor="slate" appearance="dark" data-testid="same-element">
          <Panel label="accent and appearance on one element" />
        </Theme>
      </Theme>
    </Theme>
  ),
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    const v = (el: Element, name: string) => getComputedStyle(el).getPropertyValue(name).trim()
    const dark = canvas.getByTestId('dark')
    const island = canvas.getByTestId('island')
    for (const name of ['--color-text-brand', '--color-background-brand-bold', '--color-border-focused', '--color-text', '--color-text-subtlest', '--color-border-bold']) {
      // Light inside dark: the light palette, not the page's dark one.
      await expect(v(island, name)).not.toBe(v(dark, name))
      // Dark again one level down, and on the same element: the dark palette.
      await expect(v(canvas.getByTestId('deep'), name)).toBe(v(dark, name))
      await expect(v(canvas.getByTestId('same-element'), name)).toBe(v(dark, name))
    }
  },
}
