# Foundations Foundations are the decisions every component inherits: color, type, spacing...
import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as OverviewStories from './Overview.stories'

<Meta of={OverviewStories} />

# Foundations

Foundations are the decisions every component inherits: color, type,
spacing, radius, elevation, cursors, and the breakpoints layouts respond
to. They live in **one file** — `src/tokens.css` — as CSS custom
properties.

There is no JavaScript theme object and no `ThemeProvider` that owns
values. A token is a CSS variable, which means the platform already knows
how to scope it, cascade it, inherit it and override it. Everything on
this page follows from that.

`tokens.css` is itself generated — see [Where the values come
from](#where-the-values-come-from) — but nothing downstream of it is.
**You** consume a plain stylesheet with no build step of your own.

## The three layers

| Layer | Where | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Raw value | `:root` / `.dark` in `tokens.css` | `--color-background-brand-bold: oklch(51.1% 0.262 276.966)` |
| Derived value | the `*` block in `tokens.css` | `--radius-control: max(…)` |
| Usage | a component's `.module.css` | `background: var(--color-background-brand-bold)` |

Components only ever read the variable. That is what makes a rebrand a
change to one file, and what keeps theme conditionals out of component CSS
entirely — the value behind `var(--color-background-brand-bold)` changes, the rule does not.

The derived layer is on `*` rather than `:root` on purpose: a custom
property that reads another one resolves where it is *declared*, so
putting these at the root would freeze them there and a `Theme` further
down the tree could not move them.

## Where the values come from

`tokens.css` is not written by hand. The source is a set of JSON files in
the [W3C design-token format](https://tr.designtokens.org/format/), and a
generator turns them into the stylesheet, the `Theme` component's list of
palettes, the swatches on the **Color** page, and an export for design
tools — four artefacts that used to be four chances to disagree with each
other.

Two things follow from that, and both are visible on other pages here.

**Nothing semantic holds a literal.** In the source,
`color-background-brand-bold` is `{accent.solid}` and `color-text` is
`{gray.950}` — references, not colours. Swapping a ramp moves everything downstream of it in one edit,
which is what makes the 17 accents and 9 grays on this page a
three-line change rather than a rewrite.

**The contrast numbers are measured, not claimed.** For each of the 17
accents the generator converts the ramp through OKLCH → sRGB → relative
luminance, computes the contrast of each candidate step against a white
and a black label, and takes the first that clears 4.5:1. The focus ring
is a separate measurement against the page at 3:1. The lowest passing
accent in the current set sits at **4.56:1** — close enough to the floor
that guessing would have missed it.

Edit a ramp so that no step can carry a readable label and the build
stops with the hue named. The accessibility claims on the
[Color](?path=/docs/foundations-colors--docs) page are therefore checks,
not documentation.

## The pages

- **[Color](?path=/docs/foundations-colors--docs)** — semantic tokens, the
  contrast measurements, and where every value comes from.
- **[Dark mode](?path=/docs/foundations-dark-mode--docs)** — how the two
  modes are declared and switched.
- **[Typography](?path=/docs/foundations-typography--docs)** — the
  role-based type scale, and the system font stack behind it.
- **[Spacing](?path=/docs/foundations-spacing--docs)** — six roles,
  one value each.
- **[Breakpoints](?path=/docs/foundations-breakpoints--docs)** — the
  responsive range, and the kit's lack of opinion about it.
- **[Radius](?path=/docs/foundations-radius--docs)** — four steps off one
  base, and what happens at the extremes.
- **[Shadows](?path=/docs/foundations-shadows--docs)** — elevation, and why
  dark mode needs its own alphas.
- **[Focus](?path=/docs/foundations-focus--docs)** — one ring, two
  offsets, and when to draw it inside.
- **[Motion](?path=/docs/foundations-motion--docs)** — three transition
  durations, one spinner speed, and reduced motion in one place.
- **[Layering](?path=/docs/foundations-layering--docs)** — four layers,
  and why every overlay shares one.
- **[Cursors](?path=/docs/foundations-cursors--docs)** — two tokens and one
  contested convention.

## Theming

Overriding tokens globally is just CSS — redeclare them after Zweihänder's
stylesheet loads:

```css
:root {
  --radius: 1rem;
  --color-background-brand-bold: oklch(0.55 0.2 264);
}
```

For anything narrower than the whole document, use `Theme`. It is a thin
wrapper that applies an appearance class and writes token overrides as
inline custom properties on one element, so everything inside it resolves
against those values.

```tsx
import { Theme } from 'zweihander/theme'

<Theme accentColor="violet" grayColor="slate" appearance="dark" radius="full-rounded">
  <Button>Inside a violet, slate, dark, rounder scope</Button>
</Theme>
```

Four settings, each independent:

| Prop | Values |
| --- | --- |
| `accentColor` | 17 hues — drives the brand tokens (`--color-background-brand-bold`, `--color-text-brand`, `--color-icon-brand`) and `--color-border-focused` |
| `grayColor` | 9 neutral ramps — drives backgrounds, text, borders |
| `appearance` | `light`, `dark`, `inherit` |
| `radius` | `sharp`, `rounded`, `full-rounded` |

### Accent color

The brand hue. Seventeen, all of them measured: the solid step and the
label colour are chosen per hue so every accent clears 4.5:1 for its own
label, which is why the warm hues below carry dark labels and the cool
ones carry white. The focus ring uses a step darker than the fill, because
the lighter solids miss the 3:1 a focus indicator needs.

<Canvas of={OverviewStories.AccentColor} />

### Gray color

The neutral ramp behind surfaces, text, borders and neutral fills. The
differences are subtle and cumulative; they read most clearly in dark
mode, which is how they are shown here.

<Canvas of={OverviewStories.GrayColor} />

### Radius

Covered on its own page, including why `full` pills a button but not a
text field: **[Radius](?path=/docs/foundations-radius--docs)**.

### Appearance

`appearance` takes `light`, `dark`, or `inherit` (the default, which
leaves the surrounding mode alone).

<Canvas of={OverviewStories.Appearance} />

### Token overrides

`tokens` takes any custom property, with or without the `--` prefix. It is
not limited to tokens Zweihänder defines — the component writes whatever
you pass onto the element, so a token your own components read works the
same way.

<Canvas of={OverviewStories.TokenOverride} />

Overrides cascade, so a nested `Theme` inherits what it does not restate.
Because they are inline styles they also beat any stylesheet rule, which
is what makes a scoped override reliable — and what makes `Theme` the
wrong tool for setting global defaults. Use CSS for those.

### Nesting

Scopes nest in either direction: a dark panel on a light page, or a light
island inside a dark one.

<Canvas of={OverviewStories.Nested} />

The light island works because `tokens.css` declares the light values on
`:root, .light`, not on `:root` alone. `.dark` is declared afterwards at
equal specificity, so the nearer scope's class is what an element inside
it resolves against.

An `accentColor` or `grayColor` inside a nested scope follows the same
rule. Each appearance sets two switches, `--use-light` and `--use-dark`,
and the palette scopes pick their light or dark values through them, so
the nearest appearance wins at any depth, on the same element too.

<Canvas of={OverviewStories.NestedPalettes} />

**One caveat.** If your own CSS branches on theme with a descendant
selector (`.dark .thing { … }`), that selector still matches inside a
light island nested in a dark ancestor, and will style it as dark.
Zweihänder's own CSS never branches on theme, so it is unaffected. Read
the tokens instead of matching on `.dark` and the problem does not arise.

## Installing

Both distribution paths carry the same tokens. Copy-source drops the
component's own source into your repo and merges these values into your
stylesheet; the npm package ships them as `zweihander/tokens.css`, which
you import after your base stylesheet.

The exact commands for either are in the
[repo README](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander).

'use client'

import { type ReactNode, type RefObject } from 'react'
import { Toast as BaseToast } from '@base-ui/react/toast'
import { Icon, type IconName } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Toast.module.css'

export type ToastVariant = 'neutral' | 'info' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger'

export interface ToastOptions {
  title?: ReactNode
  description?: ReactNode
  variant?: ToastVariant
  /** One button, e.g. "Undo". Keep the same action reachable elsewhere: the toast goes away. */
  action?: { label: ReactNode; onClick: () => void }
  /** Milliseconds before it closes; `0` keeps it until dismissed. */
  timeout?: number
  /** `high` interrupts the screen reader (danger defaults to it). */
  priority?: 'low' | 'high'
  onClose?: () => void
}

export interface ToastProviderProps {
  children: ReactNode
  placement?: 'top-left' | 'top-center' | 'top-right' | 'bottom-left' | 'bottom-center' | 'bottom-right'
  /** Default time on screen, in milliseconds. */
  timeout?: number
  /** Toasts shown at once; older ones wait. */
  limit?: number
  /**
   * Where the toasts render, `document.body` by default. In an element with
   * a `transform` they sit in its corner instead of the window's, and in a
   * size container (`container-type: inline-size`) they fit its width: a
   * preview, or a frame in the page.
   */
  container?: HTMLElement | RefObject<HTMLElement | null> | null
}

// Base UI's promise() sets these types itself.
const variantOf = (type: string | undefined): ToastVariant | 'loading' =>
  type === 'error' ? 'danger' : type === 'loading' ? 'loading' : ((type as ToastVariant) ?? 'neutral')

const icons: Partial<Record<ToastVariant, IconName>> = {
  info: 'info-filled',
  success: 'success-filled',
  warning: 'warning-filled',
  danger: 'danger-filled',
}

function ToastList({ swipe }: { swipe: 'left' | 'right' | 'up' | 'down' }) {
  const { toasts } = BaseToast.useToastManager()
  return toasts.map((toast) => {
    const variant = variantOf(toast.type)
    const icon = variant === 'loading' ? null : icons[variant]
    return (
      <BaseToast.Root
        key={toast.id}
        toast={toast}
        swipeDirection={swipe}
        // Each toast is a (non-modal) dialog and needs a name. promise()
        // passes its strings as the description, with no title: name it by
        // what it says rather than leave it unnamed.
        aria-label={toast.title ? undefined : typeof toast.description === 'string' ? toast.description : 'Notification'}
        className={cn(styles.toast, styles[variant])}
      >
        {variant === 'loading' && <span className={cn(styles.icon, styles.spinner)} aria-hidden="true" />}
        {icon && (
          <span className={styles.icon} aria-hidden="true">
            <Icon name={icon} />
          </span>
        )}
        <BaseToast.Content className={styles.content}>
          {toast.title && <BaseToast.Title className={styles.title} />}
          {toast.description && <BaseToast.Description className={styles.description} />}
          {toast.actionProps && <BaseToast.Action className={styles.action} />}
        </BaseToast.Content>
        <BaseToast.Close aria-label="Dismiss" className={styles.close}>
          <Icon name="close" />
        </BaseToast.Close>
      </BaseToast.Root>
    )
  })
}

/** Wrap the app once. Toasts render in a corner of the viewport, above everything. */
export function ToastProvider({ children, placement = 'bottom-right', timeout = 5000, limit = 3, container }: ToastProviderProps) {
  const [vertical, horizontal] = placement.split('-') as ['top' | 'bottom', 'left' | 'center' | 'right']
  const swipe = horizontal === 'center' ? (vertical === 'top' ? 'up' : 'down') : horizontal
  return (
    <BaseToast.Provider timeout={timeout} limit={limit}>
      {children}
      <BaseToast.Portal container={container}>
        <BaseToast.Viewport className={cn(styles.viewport, styles[vertical], styles[horizontal])}>
          <ToastList swipe={swipe} />
        </BaseToast.Viewport>
      </BaseToast.Portal>
    </BaseToast.Provider>
  )
}

/** Show, update and close toasts from anywhere inside a ToastProvider. */
export function useToast() {
  const manager = BaseToast.useToastManager()
  // Only the fields that were given: Base UI merges an update over the
  // toast, so an explicit undefined would wipe its variant or action.
  const toOptions = ({ variant, action, priority, ...rest }: ToastOptions) => {
    const options: Record<string, unknown> = { ...rest }
    if (variant !== undefined) options.type = variant
    const p = priority ?? (variant === 'danger' ? 'high' : undefined)
    if (p !== undefined) options.priority = p
    if (action !== undefined) options.actionProps = { children: action.label, onClick: action.onClick }
    return options
  }
  return {
    /** Returns the toast's id. */
    add: (options: ToastOptions) => manager.add(toOptions(options)),
    update: (id: string, options: ToastOptions) => manager.update(id, toOptions(options)),
    /** Closes one toast, or every toast without an id. */
    close: (id?: string) => manager.close(id),
    /** A loading toast that turns into success or danger when the promise settles. */
    promise: manager.promise,
  }
}

./src/components/notifications/Toast.mdx
# Toast A short message in a corner of the screen about something that just happened: save...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import * as ToastStories from './Toast.stories'

<Meta of={ToastStories} />

# Toast

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A short message in a corner of the screen about something that just
happened: saved, sent, moved, failed. It closes itself after a few seconds
and never blocks the page.

<Status of={ToastStories} />

<Canvas of={ToastStories.Static} />

Try it: the toast opens in the corner of this window.

<Canvas of={ToastStories.Default} />

## Variants

`variant` colours the icon only; the message stays in the surface's text
colour.

<Canvas of={ToastStories.VariantsStatic} />

| Variant | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `neutral` | Most toasts: something done, nothing to judge. "File moved to Trash." |
| `info` | A neutral fact about what just happened: "Sync paused while offline." |
| `success` | A result worth confirming because it was not obvious: "Invite sent to 12 people." |
| `warning` | Done, with a catch: "Saved, but 2 rows were skipped." |
| `danger` | Something failed. Interrupts the screen reader. Say what to do next, and keep the way to do it on the page too. |

`promise()` adds a loading toast that becomes `success` or `danger` when
the promise settles.

<Canvas of={ToastStories.PromiseToast} />

<Canvas of={ToastStories.TopCenter} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { ToastProvider, useToast } from 'zweihander/toast'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/toast.json
```

- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/toast](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/toast)
- Behaviour: [Base UI Toast](https://base-ui.com/react/components/toast)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={ToastStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={ToastStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

Only the title, or the description alone, is required. The icon box is one
line of body text tall, so it sits on the title's line.

## Measurements

One size. Toasts stack with a gap, the newest nearest the edge they grow
from.

At most 25rem (400px) wide, and never wider than the window less the edge
distance on both sides. The padding counts the 1px border: the content
sits 16px from the toast's edge. The close button is 24px, top-aligned with
the content and flush with the padding, 16px from the text. The action is a 24px row straight under the
description.

## Color

The toast takes the page's own appearance: the overlay surface, its
border and the overlay shadow lift it off what is under it.

`neutral` shows no icon.

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
    { label: 'Pending', content: <Story of={ToastStories.Pending} /> },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={ToastStories.StateExample} />
</States>

- **Hover** fills the close button with `--color-background-neutral`. Hovering the stack
  also pauses every toast's timer.
- **Focus** is a 2px `--color-border-focused` outline inside the action or the close
  button. Focus in the stack pauses the timers too.
- **Pending** is a `promise()` toast: a spinner in place of the icon, and
  no timer until it settles.
- **Entering** fades in and slides `--space-2` from the edge the stack grows
  from; **leaving** fades out. With reduced motion, only the fade.

## API

`ToastProvider` wraps the app once:

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={ToastStories} />
</div>

`useToast()`, anywhere inside it, shows and closes toasts:

```tsx
const toast = useToast()
toast.add({ title: 'File moved to Trash', action: { label: 'Undo', onClick: restore } })
```

{/* Markdown tables do not scroll by themselves on a phone either. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>

| `useToast()` | |
| --- | --- |
| `add(options)` | Shows a toast, returns its id. |
| `update(id, options)` | Changes one in place; only the options given change. |
| `close(id?)` | Closes one, or all. |
| `promise(promise, { loading, success, error })` | A loading toast that becomes success or danger when the promise settles. |

| Option | Values | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title`, `description` | node | |
| `variant` | `neutral`, `info`, `success`, `warning`, `danger` | `neutral` |
| `action` | `{ label, onClick }` | One button. |
| `timeout` | number (ms) | The provider's by default. `0` keeps it until dismissed. |
| `priority` | `low`, `high` | `high` by default for `danger`. |
| `onClose` | function | |

</div>

### Differences from the spec

- **Sized after Atlassian's flag**: 400px wide, 16px padding, 16px from
  the icon to the text, 8px from the title to the description, 8px
  corners, the overlay shadow, a 24px close button. The stack sits 16px
  from the window edge, where Atlassian's sits 48px up and 80px in: that
  offset clears its own navigation, and the kit's stack can sit on any
  edge.

- **Bottom right by default**, where the spec suggests top right.
  `placement` takes any corner or edge centre.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Toast to confirm something the reader just did, when the result is
not already visible: moved, sent, copied, saved in the background. Offer
"Undo" when it can be undone.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={ToastStories.DoUndo} />}
  doCaption="News about something just done, with a way to undo it. Undo is also reachable from the Trash."
  dont={<Story of={ToastStories.DontMustAct} />}
  dontCaption="A problem the reader has to fix goes away in a few seconds. Put it in an Alert on the page."
/>

Keep it to a few words. A toast is read in passing, often half-noticed.

## When not to use

- **For something the reader must act on, or might need to read twice.**
  Use an [Alert](?path=/docs/components-notifications-alert--docs) on the
  page, or a Modal for a decision.
- **For an error in a form.** Use the field's own error, or an
  [Inline Alert](?path=/docs/components-notifications-inlinealert--docs)
  under the form.
- **As the only way to an action.** The toast goes away; the same action
  ("Undo") must be reachable somewhere else.
- **To confirm what is already visible.** A row that appears in a table
  needs no "Row added" toast.

## Accessibility

- The stack is a polite live region: a new toast is announced without
  interrupting. `danger` toasts (and any with `priority: 'high'`) are
  `role="alertdialog"` and announced at once.
- Each toast is a non-modal dialog named by its title, or by its
  description when it has none (as `promise()` toasts do).
- A toast closes after 5 seconds by default (the provider's `timeout`);
  `timeout: 0` keeps it until it is dismissed. At most three show at once
  (`limit`).
- Timers pause while the pointer is over the stack or focus is in it, so
  there is time to reach the action. F6 moves focus to the stack.
- The close button is named `Dismiss`; Enter and Space press it. On touch
  screens its hit area grows to 44×44px, and a toast swipes away toward
  the nearest edge.
- A toast raised from inside a modal shows above it and is not hidden from
  assistive tech by it.

  <Canvas of={ToastStories.FromModal} />

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

'use client'

import type { ComponentProps, ReactNode, Ref } from 'react'
import { Toggle } from '@base-ui/react/toggle'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import { Button, type ButtonProps } from './Button'
import styles from './ToggleButton.module.css'

interface ToggleButtonBaseProps
  extends Omit<ComponentProps<'button'>, 'ref' | 'value' | 'defaultValue' | 'onChange'> {
  // Always a <button> (Button itself may be an <a>, hence its wider type).
  ref?: Ref<HTMLButtonElement>
  /** Colour of the pressed state. Unpressed is always neutral. */
  variant?: ButtonProps['variant']
  /** Style of the pressed state. */
  appearance?: ButtonProps['appearance']
  size?: ButtonProps['size']
  startIcon?: ReactNode
  endIcon?: ReactNode
  isLoading?: boolean
  isFullWidth?: boolean
  /** Controlled pressed state (the spec's `isSelected`). */
  pressed?: boolean
  defaultPressed?: boolean
  /** Base UI's second argument (event details) is dropped: nothing here needs it. */
  onPressedChange?: (pressed: boolean) => void
  /** Identifies the toggle inside a group. */
  value?: string
}

/** An icon-only toggle has no text to name it, so `aria-label` is required. */
export type ToggleButtonProps =
  | (ToggleButtonBaseProps & { isIconOnly?: false })
  | (ToggleButtonBaseProps & { isIconOnly: true; 'aria-label': string })

export function ToggleButton({
  variant = 'primary',
  appearance = 'contained',
  size,
  startIcon,
  endIcon,
  isLoading,
  isFullWidth,
  isIconOnly,
  pressed,
  defaultPressed,
  onPressedChange,
  disabled,
  className,
  children,
  ...props
}: ToggleButtonProps) {
  return (
    <Toggle
      {...props}
      pressed={pressed}
      defaultPressed={defaultPressed}
      onPressedChange={onPressedChange && ((next) => onPressedChange(next))}
      disabled={disabled}
      render={(toggleProps, state) => {
        const buttonProps = {
          ...toggleProps,
          // Off is the same neutral button whatever the pressed style is, so
          // "on" is always the one that stands out.
          variant: state.pressed ? variant : 'secondary',
          appearance: state.pressed ? appearance : appearance === 'ghost' ? 'ghost' : 'outlined',
          size,
          startIcon,
          endIcon,
          isLoading,
          isFullWidth,
          // Its aria-label reached Toggle with the other props and comes back
          // in toggleProps, which is what Button's icon-only type asks for.
          isIconOnly,
          // A disabled ButtonGroup disables its toggles through state.
          disabled: state.disabled,
          className: cn(state.pressed && appearance !== 'contained' && styles.tinted, className),
          children,
        } as ButtonProps
        return <Button {...buttonProps} />
      }}
    />
  )
}

# Toggle Button A button that stays pressed: bold on or off, following or not, a filter ap...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import { ToggleButton } from './ToggleButton'
import * as ToggleButtonStories from './ToggleButton.stories'

<Meta of={ToggleButtonStories} />

# Toggle Button

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A button that stays pressed: bold on or off, following or not, a filter
applied or not. It looks like a [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs).

<Status of={ToggleButtonStories} />

<Canvas of={ToggleButtonStories.Default} />

## Variants

Unpressed is always the same neutral button, so the pressed one is the one
that stands out. `variant` and `appearance` choose how it looks when
pressed. Each pair below: unpressed, then pressed.

<Canvas of={ToggleButtonStories.Matrix} />

| Appearance when pressed | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `contained` | A toggle that should read as clearly on from across the screen: a filter, Follow. |
| `outlined` | A toggle among other outlined controls. Pressed, it fills neutral and keeps the variant's border. |
| `ghost` | Toolbars and dense rows: Bold, Italic, a star. Usually `isIconOnly`. |

<Canvas of={ToggleButtonStories.IconOnly} />

<Canvas of={ToggleButtonStories.WithIcon} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { ToggleButton } from 'zweihander/toggle-button'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/toggle-button.json
```

- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/toggle-button](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/toggle-button)
- Behaviour: [Base UI Toggle](https://base-ui.com/react/components/toggle)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>

for tables and dense rows, with a 14/20 label at both.

## Color

Unpressed is the same in every variant. Pressed and `contained` takes the
variant's solid, as on Button. Pressed `outlined` and `ghost` fill with the
neutral secondary instead of a tint of the variant: a toggle stays pressed
indefinitely, so its label has to pass 4.5:1 on the fill, and red text on a
red tint measures 3.7:1.

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Unpressed' },
    { label: 'Pressed', content: <ToggleButton defaultPressed>Subscribe</ToggleButton> },
    { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
    { label: 'Disabled', content: <Story of={ToggleButtonStories.Disabled} /> },
    { label: 'Loading', content: <Story of={ToggleButtonStories.Loading} /> },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={ToggleButtonStories.Default} />
</States>

Hover, focus, disabled and loading behave as on Button, in both the
pressed and the unpressed look. A toggle has no press-and-hold state:
holding the pointer down shows hover until it flips.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={ToggleButtonStories} />
</div>

Every other `<button>` attribute passes through, including `ref`.

### Differences from the spec

- **Two sizes, not four.** The sizes follow Atlassian Design: 32px (`md`) by default, 24px (`sm`) for tables and dense rows. Both take 12px from the outer edge to the label (11px on ghost), a 6px gap and a 14/20 label; `sm` is a shorter box, not smaller type. The spec's larger steps were dropped; a big call to action is `md` with more room around it, not a taller box.
- **`pressed`, `defaultPressed`, `onPressedChange`** instead of
  `isSelected`: Base UI's names, per the kit's convention for components
  built on it. "Pressed" is also the ARIA word (`aria-pressed`).
- **`disabled`**, not `isDisabled`.
- **`variant` and `appearance` describe the pressed state.** The spec
  applies them to the button without saying what changes when it is
  selected. If unpressed also took them, a contained toggle would look
  pressed whether it was or not.
- **A pressed outlined or ghost toggle is filled neutral, not tinted with
  its variant.** It stays in that state indefinitely, so its label has to
  pass 4.5:1 on the fill.
- **`isIconOnly`**, as on Button.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a toggle for a setting that is on or off and applies immediately:
Bold, Follow, a filter. The label names the setting, and stays the same in
both states.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={ToggleButtonStories.DoSameLabel} />}
  doCaption="The label names the setting; pressed says it is on. A screen reader hears “Follow, toggle button, pressed”."
  dont={<Story of={ToggleButtonStories.DontSwitchLabel} />}
  dontCaption="A label that flips to the action reads as “Unfollow, pressed”, which contradicts itself."
/>

<Canvas of={ToggleButtonStories.Controlled} />

## When not to use

- **For a choice submitted with a form.** Use a Checkbox or a Switch: a
  toggle applies at once, a form field waits for Submit.
- **For one of many.** Put the toggles in a
  [Button Group](?path=/docs/components-buttons-buttongroup--docs), or use
  radios or Tabs. A lone toggle is independent: pressing one does not
  release another.
- **For an action.** Something that happens once (Save, Send) is a
  [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs).

## Accessibility

- A native `<button>` with `aria-pressed`, so a screen reader announces
  "Subscribe, toggle button, pressed".
- **Keep the label the same in both states.** `aria-pressed` carries the
  state; a label that switches from "Follow" to "Unfollow" as well reads
  as "Unfollow, pressed", which contradicts itself.
- Enter and Space both toggle it.
- `isIconOnly` needs `aria-label`, as on Button.
- `isLoading` keeps it focusable but inert, as on Button.
- 44×44px touch target at `sm` and `md`, from Button.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

'use client'

import { useId, useState, type ReactElement, type ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Tooltip as BaseTooltip } from '@base-ui/react/tooltip'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Tooltip.module.css'

export interface TooltipProps {
  /** What the tooltip says. Short: a label or a hint, never the only way to learn something essential. */
  content: ReactNode
  /** The trigger: one focusable element, such as a Button. Its props are merged, not wrapped. */
  children: ReactElement
  side?: 'top' | 'right' | 'bottom' | 'left'
  align?: 'start' | 'center' | 'end'
  /** Milliseconds of hover before it opens. Focus opens it at once. */
  delay?: number
  closeDelay?: number
  open?: boolean
  defaultOpen?: boolean
  onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void
  /** Never open, e.g. while the trigger's label is already visible. */
  disabled?: boolean
  /** Where the tooltip renders instead of `<body>`, e.g. an element in fullscreen. */
  container?: HTMLElement | null
  className?: string
}

export function Tooltip({
  content,
  children,
  side = 'top',
  align = 'center',
  delay = 300,
  closeDelay = 0,
  open: openProp,
  defaultOpen = false,
  onOpenChange,
  disabled = false,
  container,
  className,
}: TooltipProps) {
  const id = useId()
  const [openState, setOpenState] = useState(defaultOpen)
  const open = openProp ?? openState
  return (
    <BaseTooltip.Root
      open={open}
      onOpenChange={(next) => {
        setOpenState(next)
        onOpenChange?.(next)
      }}
      disabled={disabled}
    >
      <BaseTooltip.Trigger
        delay={delay}
        closeDelay={closeDelay}
        render={children}
        // Base UI leaves tooltips out of the accessibility tree; while one is
        // open, point the trigger at it so it is read as a description.
        aria-describedby={open ? id : undefined}
      />
      <BaseTooltip.Portal container={container}>
        <BaseTooltip.Positioner className={styles.positioner} side={side} align={align} sideOffset={6}>
          <BaseTooltip.Popup id={id} role="tooltip" className={cn(styles.popup, className)}>
            {content}
          </BaseTooltip.Popup>
        </BaseTooltip.Positioner>
      </BaseTooltip.Portal>
    </BaseTooltip.Root>
  )
}

/** Tooltips inside share one delay: once one has opened, moving to the next opens it at once. */
export const TooltipGroup = BaseTooltip.Provider

# Tooltip A short label that appears when you hover over or focus a control: the name of a...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import * as TooltipStories from './Tooltip.stories'

<Meta of={TooltipStories} />

# Tooltip

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A short label that appears when you hover over or focus a control: the
name of an icon-only button, a keyboard shortcut, a one-line hint.

<Status of={TooltipStories} />

<Canvas of={TooltipStories.LongContent} />

## Variants

| Variant | When to use |
|---|---|
| Tooltip | A label or a one-line hint on a control. |

The tooltip opens on hover after a short delay and on keyboard focus at
once. Wrap a row of tooltips in `TooltipGroup` so that
once one has opened, moving to the next opens it without the delay:

<Canvas of={TooltipStories.Group} />

Only one tooltip is open at a time: opening one closes any other. Hover or
focus the triggers above to see them.

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Tooltip, TooltipGroup } from 'zweihander/tooltip'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/tooltip.json
```

- Source: [src/components/overlays/Tooltip.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/overlays/Tooltip.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/tooltip](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/tooltip)
- Behaviour: [Base UI Tooltip](https://base-ui.com/react/components/tooltip)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={TooltipStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={TooltipStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The open tooltips on this tab and the next are pictures: real tooltips
held open and rendered in place with `container`, laid out above the
trigger where they open.

## Measurements

<SpecTable
  caption="Container"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Block padding', token: '--space-1' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Inline padding', token: '--space-1-5' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-sm' },
    { part: 'Text', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body-sm' },
    { part: 'Text', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body-sm' },
  ]}
/>

The container is as wide as its text, at most 240px (15rem) and never wider than
the room beside the trigger; longer text wraps. It opens 6px from the
trigger, on the `--layer-tooltip` layer, above popovers and modals, so a
tooltip on a control inside one still shows. It fades in over
`--duration-fast`.

## Color

<SpecTable
  caption="Every tooltip"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Background', token: '--color-text' },
    { part: 'Text', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-surface' },
  ]}
/>

The tooltip is inverted in both modes: a tooltip is not part of the page, and the
dark-on-light (light-on-dark in dark mode) box says so, at the same
contrast as body text.

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Closed', content: <Story of={TooltipStories.Closed} /> },
    { label: 'Open', content: <Story of={TooltipStories.OpenPicture} /> },
  ]}
/>

- **Closed** until the pointer rests on the trigger for `delay` (300ms), or
  the trigger takes keyboard focus, which opens it at once.
- **Open** until Escape, blur or the pointer leaves, after `closeDelay`.
  Opening fades it in and scales it up from 96%.
- The trigger keeps the states of its own component; the tooltip has none
  of its own.
## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={TooltipStories} />
</div>

`TooltipGroup` is Base UI's `Tooltip.Provider`: tooltips inside it share
one delay.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Tooltip for a label or a hint: the name of an icon-only button, a
keyboard shortcut, one line on what a control does. 300ms before it opens
is quick enough to feel responsive and long enough that tooltips do not
flash as the pointer crosses a toolbar.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={TooltipStories.DoShortLabel} />}
  doCaption="A short label that repeats the icon-only button's name for sighted users."
  dont={<Story of={TooltipStories.DontEssentialInfo} />}
  dontCaption="Rules the reader needs to fill the field. Touch cannot open a tooltip, and it hides as soon as focus moves on: put the rules under the field."
/>

It opens on the `side` given, top by default. When that side has no room,
it flips to the other one.

## When not to use

- **For anything a reader needs to finish a task.** Put it on the page: a
  tooltip cannot be reached by touch, and it disappears the moment you
  look away.
- **For links, buttons or other interactive content.** Hover and touch
  cannot reach the tooltip. Use a
  [Popover](?path=/docs/components-overlays-popover--docs).
- **For a rich preview.** A tooltip holds text only. Use a
  [Popover](?path=/docs/components-overlays-popover--docs) with
  `openOnHover`.
- **On a disabled button.** It is not focusable, so its tooltip never opens
  by keyboard. Put the reason it is disabled in text next to it.

## Accessibility

- It opens on hover after `delay` and on keyboard focus at once, and
  closes on Escape, blur or pointer leave.

  <Canvas of={TooltipStories.Default} />

- Base UI keeps tooltips out of the accessibility tree. This component
  gives the popup `role="tooltip"` and, while it is open, points the
  trigger's `aria-describedby` at it, so it is read as a description.
- It is a **description, not a name.** An icon-only button still needs its
  own `aria-label`; the tooltip then shows that label to sighted users too.
- The trigger must be focusable: a Button, a link, a field.
- `--color-surface` on `--color-text` reads at 16:1 or more in both modes.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

  { token: 'body-sm', px: '12 / 16' },
] as const

function Row({ token, px, weight }: { token: string; px: string; weight: number }) {
  return (
    <div
      className={docs.rowBaseline}
      style={{ borderBottom: '1px solid var(--color-border)', padding: 'var(--space-2) 0' }}
    >
      <span className={docs.caption} style={{ width: '10rem', flexShrink: 0 }}>
        --text-{token}
      </span>
      <span style={{ flex: 1, ...role(token, weight) }}>Zweihänder</span>
      <span className={docs.caption} style={{ width: '7rem', textAlign: 'right' }}>
        {px}
      </span>
    </div>
  )
}

const WEIGHTS = [
  { value: 400, name: 'regular' },
  { value: 500, name: 'medium' },
  { value: 600, name: 'semibold' },
  { value: 700, name: 'bold' },
] as const

// Narrative and prose live in Typography.mdx.
const meta = {
  title: 'Foundations/Typography',
  parameters: { layout: 'padded' },
} satisfies Meta

export default meta
type Story = StoryObj<typeof meta>

export const Headings: Story = {
  render: () => (
    <div style={{ display: 'flex', flexDirection: 'column' }}>
      {HEADINGS.map((h) => (
        <Row key={h.token} {...h} weight={600} />
      ))}
    </div>
  ),
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    const el = canvas.getAllByText('Zweihänder')[0]
    // A heading role carries its weight, not just its size.
    await expect(getComputedStyle(el).fontWeight).toBe('600')
    await expect(Number.parseFloat(getComputedStyle(el).fontSize)).toBe(32)
  },
}

export const Body: Story = {
  render: () => (
    <div style={{ display: 'flex', flexDirection: 'column' }}>
      {BODY.map((b) => (
        <Row key={b.token} {...b} weight={400} />
      ))}
    </div>
  ),
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    const el = canvas.getAllByText('Zweihänder')[1]
    // body is 14px, one step down from the 16px many interfaces start at.
    await expect(Number.parseFloat(getComputedStyle(el).fontSize)).toBe(14)
    // Every body line sits on the 4px grid.
    for (const sample of canvas.getAllByText('Zweihänder')) {
      await expect(Number.parseFloat(getComputedStyle(sample).lineHeight) % 4).toBeCloseTo(0, 5)
    }
  },
}

export const Weights: Story = {
  render: () => (
    <div className={docs.stack}>
      {WEIGHTS.map(({ value, name }) => (
        <div key={value} className={docs.rowBaseline}>
          <span className={docs.caption} style={{ width: '8rem', flexShrink: 0 }}>
            {value}
          </span>
          <span style={{ ...role('body-lg', value) }}>Zweihänder</span>
          <span className={docs.caption}>{name}</span>
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  ),
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    const bold = canvas.getAllByText('Zweihänder').at(-1)!
    await expect(getComputedStyle(bold).fontWeight).toBe('700')
  },
}

export const Families: Story = {
  render: () => (
    <div className={docs.stackWide}>
      <div className={docs.stack}>
        <span className={docs.caption}>--font-sans</span>
        <span style={{ ...role('heading-md', 700), fontFamily: 'var(--font-sans)' }}>
          Zweihänder — system-ui 0123
        </span>
      </div>
      <div className={docs.stack}>
        <span className={docs.caption}>--font-mono</span>
        <span style={{ ...role('heading-md', 700), fontFamily: 'var(--font-mono)' }}>
          Zweihänder — ui-monospace 0123
        </span>
      </div>
    </div>
  ),
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    const sans = canvas.getByText(/system-ui 0123/)
    await expect(getComputedStyle(sans).fontFamily).toMatch(/^system-ui/)
  },
}

# Typography Type is **role-based**: you reach for `--text-heading-lg` or `--text-body`, n...
import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as TypographyStories from './Typography.stories'

<Meta of={TypographyStories} />

# Typography

Type is **role-based**: you reach for `--text-heading-lg` or `--text-body`,
not a size. Each role carries its size, line height and weight together, so a
heading cannot end up at body weight or a body line height by omission.

The alternative — a purely dimensional scale, where a name says how big and
never what it is for — is what this replaces. Each role is three variables
that belong together:

```css
.heading {
  font-size: var(--text-heading-lg);
  line-height: var(--leading-heading-lg);
  font-weight: 600;
}
```

## The typeface

One face: the platform UI font. Nothing is downloaded, and text looks the
way the rest of the operating system does — San Francisco on Apple, Segoe UI
on Windows, Roboto on Android.

```css
--font-sans: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, …
--font-mono: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, 'SF Mono', Menlo, …
```

Components read two role tokens rather than the face directly, so a
product can give headings or prose their own face without touching a
component:

| Role | Default | Read by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--font-heading` | `var(--font-sans)` | Page titles, `Modal` and `EmptyState` titles |
| `--font-prose` | `var(--font-sans)` | long-form reading text; no component reads it yet |

<Canvas of={TypographyStories.Families} />

**There is nothing to load.** To use a brand face instead, load it yourself
and point the tokens at it (see **Customization**).

## Headings

Seven steps, all semibold (600). The line height tightens as the size grows, which
is the thing a single ratio applied across a whole scale gets wrong.

<Canvas of={TypographyStories.Headings} />

| Role | Size | Line height |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--text-heading-2xl` | 2rem / 32px | 36px |
| `--text-heading-xl` | 1.75rem / 28px | 32px |
| `--text-heading-lg` | 1.5rem / 24px | 28px |
| `--text-heading-md` | 1.25rem / 20px | 24px |
| `--text-heading-sm` | 1rem / 16px | 20px |
| `--text-heading-xs` | 0.875rem / 14px | 20px |
| `--text-heading-2xs` | 0.75rem / 12px | 16px |

Note that headings go *below* body size: `--text-heading-2xs` is 12px. Those
bottom steps are for labels and section eyebrows — a heading role is about
the semantic weight of the text, not about being large.

## Body

Three steps. `--text-body` is the default at 14px — one step down from the
16px a lot of interfaces start at, which is deliberate for dense product
UI and worth knowing before you reach for it in long-form content.

<Canvas of={TypographyStories.Body} />

| Role | Size | Line height |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--text-body-lg` | 1rem / 16px | 24px |
| `--text-body` | 0.875rem / 14px | 20px |
| `--text-body-sm` | 0.75rem / 12px | 16px |

**Every component uses these.** Button, the field label, the input itself,
and the helper and error text are all `--text-body`; only the large Button
steps up to `--text-body-lg`.

`--text-body-sm` is the label of every small control (the `sm` and `xs`
size tiers, see [Sizing](?path=/docs/foundations-sizing--docs)), and
secondary text: helper text in a menu, shortcuts, captions.

12px is the smallest text size in the kit. `--text-body-xs` used to be
11px; it is now the same as `--text-body-sm` and deprecated, kept so
existing styles keep working.

Every body line height is a multiple of 4px (24, 20, 16), so body text
of any size sits on the same 4px grid as the spacing and control heights.

## Weights

Four. Anything outside this set is not part of the system.

<Canvas of={TypographyStories.Weights} />

| Weight | Value |
| --- | --- |
| regular | 400 |
| medium | 500 |
| semibold | 600 |
| bold | 700 |

Headings are semibold (600). A label beside an icon, such as a button's
or a tab's, is medium (500).

{/* docs:check allow --font-weight-medium -- the paragraph explains why weights are not tokens */}

Weight is written directly rather than tokenised — there are four of them
and they are the same four everywhere, so a `--font-weight-medium`
indirection would buy nothing. The one exception is `--font-weight-label`
(653), a field's label, which a variable face draws between medium and
semibold. Button is `--text-body` at `font-weight:
500`; the role supplies the size and line height, the rule supplies the
weight.

With a system stack, the weight you ask for is not guaranteed to be a
drawn face: where one is missing the browser synthesises it, and
synthesised weights look noticeably worse. 400 and 500 are safe
everywhere; verify 600 on the platforms you support.

## What is not here

**A metric role for large figures.** Its sizes would be identical to three
of the heading steps; the real difference is tabular figures, which
`font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` already covers. There is no stat
component yet, so it would be a role nothing reads.

**A code role.** Same size as `--text-body-sm`, differing only by family.
`var(--font-mono)` covers it until a Code component exists.

## Customization

The family is a token like any other:

```css
:root {
  --font-sans: 'Geist Variable', system-ui, sans-serif;
  --font-heading: 'Newsreader Variable', Georgia, serif; /* serif headings */
}
```

Every rule that reads `var(--font-sans)` picks it up with no component
change — which is all of them, because components set the family
explicitly rather than inheriting it from the page. Re-check the weights when you do — a real typeface
usually ships fewer weights than the four above, or different ones.

To move the scale itself rather than the face, override the role tokens
directly — each is a `--text-<role>` and its `--leading-<role>` partner.

import type { ComponentProps, MouseEvent, ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Icon, type IconName } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Alert.module.css'

export interface AlertProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'div'>, 'title'> {
  variant?: 'info' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger'
  appearance?: 'subtle' | 'outlined' | 'solid'
  title?: ReactNode
  /** Replaces the variant's icon; `false` shows none. */
  icon?: ReactNode | false
  /** Buttons or links under the message, e.g. "Retry". */
  action?: ReactNode
  /** Shows a close button that calls this. The alert does not hide itself: remove it when this fires. */
  onClose?: (event: MouseEvent<HTMLButtonElement>) => void
  /** Accessible name of the close button. */
  closeLabel?: string
  /**
   * Announce the alert when it appears. `danger` and `warning` interrupt
   * (`role="alert"`), the others wait their turn (`role="status"`). Leave it
   * off for an alert that is on the page from the start.
   */
  isLive?: boolean
}

const icons: Record<NonNullable<AlertProps['variant']>, IconName> = {
  info: 'info-filled',
  success: 'success-filled',
  warning: 'warning-filled',
  danger: 'danger-filled',
}

export function Alert({
  variant = 'info',
  appearance = 'subtle',
  title,
  icon,
  action,
  onClose,
  closeLabel = 'Dismiss',
  isLive = false,
  className,
  children,
  ...props
}: AlertProps) {
  const urgent = variant === 'danger' || variant === 'warning'
  return (
    <div
      role={isLive ? (urgent ? 'alert' : 'status') : undefined}
      className={cn(styles.alert, styles[variant], styles[appearance], className)}
      {...props}
    >
      {icon !== false && (
        <span className={styles.icon} aria-hidden="true">
          {icon ?? <Icon name={icons[variant]} />}
        </span>
      )}
      <div className={styles.body}>
        {title && <div className={styles.title}>{title}</div>}
        {children && <div className={styles.description}>{children}</div>}
        {action && <div className={styles.action}>{action}</div>}
      </div>
      {onClose && (
        <button type="button" aria-label={closeLabel} className={styles.close} onClick={onClose}>
          <Icon name="close" />
        </button>
      )}
    </div>
  )
}

# Alert A message about a page or a section that stays until the situation changes or the ...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import * as AlertStories from './Alert.stories'

<Meta of={AlertStories} />

# Alert

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A message about a page or a section that stays until the situation changes
or the reader dismisses it: something went wrong, needs attention, or worked.

<Status of={AlertStories} />

<Canvas of={AlertStories.WithAction} />

## Variants

`variant` is the colour, by meaning; `appearance` is the emphasis. Any
variant takes any appearance.

<Canvas of={AlertStories.Variants} />

| Variant | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `info` | Something worth knowing that changes nothing: a plan change, scheduled maintenance. |
| `success` | Something finished and stays true: a domain verified, an import done. |
| `warning` | Something that will go wrong if nobody acts: a card expiring, a quota nearly used. |
| `danger` | Something that went wrong and needs a next step: a failed upload, a lost connection. |

<Canvas of={AlertStories.Appearances} />

| Appearance | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `subtle` | The default. Sits on the page without shouting. |
| `outlined` | On a tinted or busy background, where a tint would disappear. |
| `solid` | The one message nobody should miss, such as an outage banner. Rarely more than one per page. |

<Canvas of={AlertStories.Dismissible} />

<Canvas of={AlertStories.WithoutIcon} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Alert } from 'zweihander/alert'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/alert.json
```

- Source: [src/components/notifications/Alert.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/notifications/Alert.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/alert](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/alert)
- Behaviour: a plain element, no Base UI part
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={AlertStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={AlertStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

Only the description is required. The icon is one line of body text tall,
so it sits on the title's line.

## Measurements

One size. The text is body text, so an alert sits in running content
without a jump in size.

<SpecTable
  caption="Every alert"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Padding, from the outer edge', token: '--space-group' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-lg' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Gap, icon to text', token: '--space-group' },
    { part: 'Title and description', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body' },
    { part: 'Title and description', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body' },
    { part: 'Title and description', property: 'Gap', token: '--space-inline' },
    { part: 'Action', property: 'Space above, and between actions', token: '--space-inline' },
    { part: 'Close button', property: 'Size', token: '--box-sm' },
    { part: 'Close button', property: 'Icon size', token: '--icon-md' },
    { part: 'Close button', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-sm' },
    { part: 'Close button', property: 'Minimum hit area on touch screens', token: '--target-coarse' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Width', token: '--focus-width' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Offset (inside)', token: '--focus-offset-inset' },
  ]}
/>

The border is always there, 1px and transparent unless `outlined`, so
switching appearance never moves the content. The padding counts that
pixel: the content sits 16px from the alert's edge. The close button is 24px,
flush with the padding and top-aligned with the icon. No shadow: an alert is
part of the page.

## Color

Each variant reads four tokens, the same four as a Tag of that variant, so
the two always agree. Subtle and outlined keep the description in
`--color-text`: a paragraph in the variant's colour is tiring to read, so
the colour goes on the icon, the title and the close button.

<SpecTable
  caption="info"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container, subtle', property: 'Background', token: '--color-background-info' },
    { part: 'Container, outlined', property: 'Border', token: '--color-text-info' },
    { part: 'Icon and title, subtle and outlined', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-info' },
    { part: 'Close button, subtle and outlined', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-info' },
    { part: 'Container, solid', property: 'Background', token: '--color-background-info-bold' },
    { part: 'Content, solid', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-info-inverse' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="success"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container, subtle', property: 'Background', token: '--color-background-success' },
    { part: 'Container, outlined', property: 'Border', token: '--color-text-success' },
    { part: 'Icon and title, subtle and outlined', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-success' },
    { part: 'Close button, subtle and outlined', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-success' },
    { part: 'Container, solid', property: 'Background', token: '--color-background-success-bold' },
    { part: 'Content, solid', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-success-inverse' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="warning"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container, subtle', property: 'Background', token: '--color-background-warning' },
    { part: 'Container, outlined', property: 'Border', token: '--color-text-warning' },
    { part: 'Icon and title, subtle and outlined', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-warning' },
    { part: 'Close button, subtle and outlined', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-warning' },
    { part: 'Container, solid', property: 'Background', token: '--color-background-warning-bold' },
    { part: 'Content, solid', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-warning-inverse' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="danger"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container, subtle', property: 'Background', token: '--color-background-danger' },
    { part: 'Container, outlined', property: 'Border', token: '--color-text-danger' },
    { part: 'Icon and title, subtle and outlined', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-danger' },
    { part: 'Close button, subtle and outlined', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-danger' },
    { part: 'Container, solid', property: 'Background', token: '--color-background-danger-bold' },
    { part: 'Content, solid', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-danger-inverse' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Every variant"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Description, subtle and outlined', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text' },
    { part: 'Container, outlined', property: 'Background', token: '--color-surface' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-border-focused' },
  ]}
/>

## States

The alert itself has no states. Its close button does.

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Close hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Close focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={AlertStories.Dismissible} />
</States>

- **Hover** tints the close button with 15% of the alert's own text
  colour, so it reads on every variant and appearance.
- **Focus** is a 2px `--color-border-focused` outline, inside the button's edge.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={AlertStories} />
</div>

Every other `<div>` attribute passes through, including `ref`.

### Differences from the spec

- **Sized after Atlassian's section message**: 16px padding, 16px from
  the icon to the text, 8px between title, description and actions, 8px
  corners, no shadow, a semibold 14/20 title, a 24px close button.

- **Placed in the content, not at the top of the screen.** The spec
  describes a prominent message at the top; here an alert goes where the
  thing it is about is. An outage banner is a `solid` alert placed at the
  top by the page.
- **Closing is the parent's job.** `onClose` reports the click and the
  alert stays until whoever rendered it removes it, so "dismissed" lives in
  your state and can be remembered across visits.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use an Alert for a message about a page or a section that should stay put
until it is dealt with: a failed save, a card about to expire, an import
that finished. The title says what happened; the description says what it
means and what to do.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={AlertStories.DoSayWhatHappened} />}
  doCaption="Say what happened and offer the next step."
  dont={<Story of={AlertStories.DontVague} />}
  dontCaption="“Something went wrong” leaves the red box to do the talking, and the reader with nothing to do."
/>

The icon is decorative, so the variant has to be clear from the words too:
"Upload failed", not just a red box.

## When not to use

- **For news about something that just happened and needs nothing more.**
  Use a [Toast](?path=/docs/components-notifications-toast--docs): it goes
  away by itself.
- **For a one-line message under a form or a group of fields.** Use an
  [Inline Alert](?path=/docs/components-notifications-inlinealert--docs).
- **For an error on one field.** Use the field's own `validationState` and
  `helperText`, tied to it with `aria-describedby`.
- **For a decision the reader must make before going on.** Use a Modal.

## Accessibility

- A plain `<div>` by default: an alert on the page when it loads is read in
  order, like the text around it, and does not interrupt.
- An alert that **appears** in response to something (a failed save) needs
  `isLive`. `danger` and `warning` become `role="alert"` and are read at
  once; `info` and `success` become `role="status"` and wait for the screen
  reader to finish.

  <Canvas of={AlertStories.Live} />

- The icon is `aria-hidden`: the words carry the meaning.
- The close button is a native `<button>` named `Dismiss` (change it with
  `closeLabel`). Tab reaches it, Enter and Space press it.
- Focus ring: 2px `--color-border-focused` on the close button. On touch screens its hit
  area grows to 44×44px without the button growing.
- Every variant and appearance passes the story tests' contrast check
  (light mode).

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

'use client'

import { useState, type ComponentProps } from 'react'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import type { AccentColor } from '@/theme/palettes'
import { Tooltip, TooltipGroup } from '../overlays/Tooltip'
import { Badge, type BadgeProps } from './Badge'
import styles from './Avatar.module.css'

type AvatarStatus = 'online' | 'away' | 'busy' | 'offline'

// Badge's presence colours, so a dot on an avatar and a dot beside a name match.
const STATUS: Record<AvatarStatus, { variant: BadgeProps['variant']; label: string }> = {
  online: { variant: 'success', label: 'Online' },
  away: { variant: 'warning', label: 'Away' },
  busy: { variant: 'destructive', label: 'Busy' },
  offline: { variant: 'secondary', label: 'Offline' },
}

export interface AvatarProps extends ComponentProps<'span'> {
  /** 16, 24, 32, 40, 96 or 128px across: Atlassian's avatar sizes. */
  size?: 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl' | '2xl'
  imageSrc?: string
  /** Who this is. Without it the avatar is decorative and hidden from assistive tech. */
  imageAlt?: string
  /** Shown when there is no image, or it fails to load. One or two letters; `xs` has room for the first only. */
  initials?: string
  /** Any accent hue. Unset is the neutral gray. */
  color?: AccentColor
  /** `subtle` is a tint of the hue; `solid` is its 600 step (400 in dark). */
  variant?: 'subtle' | 'solid'
  /** A presence dot at the bottom-end corner. Joins the name as ", Online" when there is `imageAlt`. */
  status?: AvatarStatus
  /** The status word in the name, for another language. Defaults to Online, Away, Busy or Offline. */
  statusLabel?: string
}

export function Avatar({
  size = 'md',
  imageSrc,
  imageAlt,
  initials,
  color,
  variant = 'subtle',
  status,
  statusLabel = status && STATUS[status].label,
  className,
  ...props
}: AvatarProps) {
  // Keyed by src, so a new imageSrc gets a fresh attempt instead of staying
  // on the fallback from the last one that failed.
  const [failedSrc, setFailedSrc] = useState<string>()
  // An empty string is no image, not a request for the page's own URL.
  const showImage = !!imageSrc && failedSrc !== imageSrc
  // 16px holds one letter at the smallest type size. A count ("+3", "9+")
  // stays whole: half of it would be a different number.
  const letters = size === 'xs' && initials && !initials.includes('+') ? Array.from(initials)[0] : initials

  return (
    <span
      // The label lives on the container so the image, the initials and the silhouette
      // all announce the same thing: the person, not "S R" or nothing.
      role={imageAlt ? 'img' : undefined}
      // Children of role="img" are not read, so the status joins the name.
      aria-label={imageAlt && status ? `${imageAlt}, ${statusLabel}` : imageAlt}
      aria-hidden={imageAlt ? undefined : true}
      // The Theme's own palette switch: on the avatar it remaps --color-background-brand-bold and
      // its tints to this hue, already measured for contrast.
      data-accent={color}
      // A CSS class cannot start with a digit.
      className={cn(styles.avatar, styles[size === '2xl' ? 'xxl' : size], styles[variant], status && styles.hasStatus, className)}
      {...props}
    >
      {showImage ? (
        <img
          src={imageSrc}
          alt=""
          className={styles.image}
          onError={() => setFailedSrc(imageSrc)}
        />
      ) : letters ? (
        <span className={styles.initials}>{letters}</span>
      ) : (
        <Icon name="user" className={styles.silhouette} />
      )}
      {status && (
        <Badge
          isDot
          variant={STATUS[status].variant}
          // 8px from sm to lg, as Figma; xl and 2xl size it in CSS, xs hides it.
          size="md"
          className={styles.status}
        />
      )}
    </span>
  )
}

export interface AvatarGroupProps extends ComponentProps<'span'> {
  /** The people, in order. Each takes Avatar's props; the group's `size` wins. */
  avatars: AvatarProps[]
  /** The most circles in the row, the "+n" included. Unset shows everyone. */
  max?: number
  size?: AvatarProps['size']
  /** The name of the "+n" avatar, for another language. Used only when the avatars are named. */
  moreLabel?: (count: number) => string
  /** Each named avatar shows its name on hover, and the "+n" lists the people it stands for, on hover or focus. */
  hasTooltips?: boolean
}

/** Avatars overlapping in a row, with a "+n" for the ones past `max`. */
export function AvatarGroup({
  avatars,
  max,
  size = 'md',
  moreLabel = (count) => `${count} more`,
  hasTooltips = false,
  className,
  ...props
}: AvatarGroupProps) {
  // The "+n" takes the last slot, so it always stands for two or more: never "+1"
  // where the person would have fitted.
  const shown = max !== undefined && avatars.length > max ? avatars.slice(0, Math.max(max - 1, 0)) : avatars
  const hidden = avatars.length - shown.length
  // Named avatars get a named "+n"; decorative ones (the names are printed) a decorative one.
  const isNamed = avatars.some((a) => a.imageAlt)

  // With tooltips, the "+n" lists who it stands for, and takes focus so
  // that list can be read by keyboard too.
  const hiddenNames = hasTooltips
    ? avatars
        .slice(shown.length)
        .map((a) => a.imageAlt)
        .filter(Boolean)
        .join(', ')
    : ''
  const more = hidden > 0 && (
    // A 16px circle holds two characters, so past nine the xs count reads "9+".
    // ponytail: larger sizes are not capped; an sm circle outgrows +99.
    <Avatar
      size={size}
      initials={size === 'xs' && hidden > 9 ? '9+' : `+${hidden}`}
      imageAlt={isNamed ? moreLabel(hidden) : undefined}
      tabIndex={hiddenNames ? 0 : undefined}
    />
  )

  const group = (
    <span className={cn(styles.group, className)} {...props}>
      {shown.map((avatar, i) => {
        const el = <Avatar {...avatar} size={size} style={{ zIndex: shown.length - i, ...avatar.style }} />
        return hasTooltips && avatar.imageAlt ? (
          <Tooltip key={i} content={avatar.imageAlt}>
            {el}
          </Tooltip>
        ) : (
          <Avatar key={i} {...avatar} size={size} style={{ zIndex: shown.length - i, ...avatar.style }} />
        )
      })}
      {more && hiddenNames ? <Tooltip content={hiddenNames}>{more}</Tooltip> : more}
    </span>
  )
  // One shared delay: once a name shows, the next shows as the pointer moves on.
  return hasTooltips ? <TooltipGroup>{group}</TooltipGroup> : group
}

# Avatar A picture of a person or account, with initials or a silhouette when there is no ...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import { Avatar, AvatarGroup } from './Avatar'
import * as AvatarStories from './Avatar.stories'

<Meta of={AvatarStories} />

# Avatar

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A picture of a person or account, with initials or a silhouette when there
is no picture, an optional presence dot, and a group that overlaps several.

<Status of={AvatarStories} />

<Canvas of={AvatarStories.Fallbacks} />

## Variants

Neutral by default. `color` picks any accent hue, and `variant` how strong
it is. Behind a photo the colour only shows while it loads or where the
image is transparent.

<Canvas of={AvatarStories.Colors} />

| Variant | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| <Avatar initials="SR" /> `subtle` | Most places: lists, comments, a byline. A tint that sits quietly next to text. |
| <Avatar initials="SR" variant="solid" /> `solid` | Where the avatar has to stand out on its own: a header, an account menu trigger. |

Colour tells people apart in a list; it carries no meaning. Pick it from the
person (a hash of their id), never from a status.

### Sizes

Atlassian's six. `md` is the default.

<Canvas of={AvatarStories.Sizes} />

| `size` | Across | Use for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `xs` | 16px | Inline with a line of small text: a mention, a dense table cell. One initial. |
| `sm` | 24px | Beside a name in a row, a field or a table cell. |
| `md` | 32px | The default: a comment, a feed event, the account button in a top bar. |
| `lg` | 40px | The leading visual of a list row or a card. |
| `xl` | 96px | A profile header. |
| `2xl` | 128px | A profile page, or the picture being edited. |

With initials, `xs` shows the first letter only: two do not fit in 16px.

<Canvas of={AvatarStories.InitialsSizes} />

### Status

`status` puts a presence dot on the bottom-end corner, in Badge's presence
colours: online, away, busy, offline.

<Canvas of={AvatarStories.Status} />

The dot grows with the avatar, and at `xl` and `2xl` it sits on the curve:

<Canvas of={AvatarStories.StatusSizes} />

### Group

`AvatarGroup` overlaps a row of avatars, for the people on a record or a
thread. `max` is the most circles in the row, the "+n" included.

<Canvas of={AvatarStories.Group} />

With `hasTooltips`, each named avatar shows its name on hover, and the
"+n" lists the people it stands for, on hover or keyboard focus:

<Canvas of={AvatarStories.GroupTooltips} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Avatar, AvatarGroup } from 'zweihander/avatar'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/avatar.json
```

- Source: [src/components/atomic-elements/Avatar.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/atomic-elements/Avatar.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/avatar](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/avatar)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={AvatarStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={AvatarStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

One avatar shows one of image, initials or silhouette, in that order of
preference. A broken image falls back to the next. The status dot and the
group are optional.

## Measurements

The circle ignores the Theme's radius preset: a circle is the shape, not a
corner setting.

<SpecTable
  caption="xs"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Size', token: '--avatar-xs' },
    { part: 'Initials', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body-sm' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="sm"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Size', token: '--avatar-sm' },
    { part: 'Initials', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body-sm' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="md"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Size', token: '--avatar-md' },
    { part: 'Initials', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body-sm' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="lg"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Size', token: '--avatar-lg' },
    { part: 'Initials', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="xl"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Size', token: '--avatar-xl' },
    { part: 'Initials', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-heading-xl' },
    { part: 'Status dot', property: 'Size', token: '--box-2xs' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="2xl"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Size', token: '--avatar-2xl' },
    { part: 'Initials', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-heading-2xl' },
    { part: 'Status dot', property: 'Size', token: '--box-xs' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable caption="Every size" rows={[{ part: 'Container', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-pill' }]} />

The image fills the circle edge to edge. The silhouette is the kit's
`user` icon at 60% of the circle, centred.

Initials are 12px up to `md`, where `xs` keeps only the first letter, 14px
on `lg`, then 28px and 32px: the type scale stops at 32px, so on `xl` and
`2xl` the letters are a smaller share of the circle. They are medium (500)
up to `lg` and semibold (600) on `xl` and `2xl`, Figma's Heading/xl and
Heading/2xl.

An `xs` avatar draws no status dot, as in Atlassian: at 16px the dot would
cover most of the picture, so the status is in the accessible name only.
The status dot is an 8px Badge dot (`md`) on the sm, md and lg avatars,
flush on the corner of the avatar's box, outside the curve. On `xl` and `2xl` that corner is far off the circle and a Badge dot
is a speck, so the dot is 16px and 20px, and its centre sits on the circle
at 45°.

<SpecTable
  caption="Status dot and group"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Status dot', property: 'Ring', token: '--color-surface' },
    { part: 'Group', property: 'Ring around each avatar', token: '--color-surface' },
    { part: 'Group', property: 'Overlap, every size but sm', token: '--space-1' },
  ]}
/>

The ring is 2px at every size, as on a floating Badge. The overlap is
Atlassian's: 4px, and none at `sm`, where the 24px circles only touch.

## Color

`color` sets the Theme's own `data-accent` on the avatar, so a hue avatar
reads the accent tokens of that hue: switch the accent in the toolbar to see
the values for another one.

The status dot takes Badge's presence colours: online `success`, away
`warning`, busy `destructive`, offline `secondary`. The "+n" in a group is a
neutral subtle avatar.

## States

An avatar is not interactive: no hover, focus or pressed. Its states are
which part it can show.

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Image', content: <Avatar size="lg" imageSrc={AvatarStories.default.args.imageSrc} imageAlt="Mary Thompson" /> },
    { label: 'Initials', content: <Avatar size="lg" initials="SR" imageAlt="Sam Rivera" /> },
    { label: 'Silhouette', content: <Avatar size="lg" imageAlt="Unknown user" /> },
    { label: 'Broken image', content: <Story of={AvatarStories.BrokenImage} /> },
    { label: 'Online', content: <Avatar size="lg" initials="SR" imageAlt="Sam Rivera" status="online" /> },
    { label: 'Offline', content: <Avatar size="lg" initials="SR" imageAlt="Sam Rivera" status="offline" /> },
  ]}
/>

- **Image** shows while `imageSrc` loads and after.
- **Broken image** drops the `<img>` and shows the initials, or the
  silhouette when there are none, instead of the browser's broken-image
  icon. A new `imageSrc` is tried again. An empty `imageSrc` is no image.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={AvatarStories} />
</div>

Every other `<span>` attribute passes through to the container, including
`ref`.

### AvatarGroup

<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={AvatarGroup} />
</div>

Every other `<span>` attribute passes through to the row.

### Differences from the spec

- **`initials` is added.** The spec's Anatomy has an Initials part but
  its prop list has no way to set them. Pass the letters, not a name:
  how to abbreviate a name depends on the language, and the kit should
  not guess.
- **A broken image falls back** to initials or the silhouette instead
  of showing the browser's broken-image icon.
- **Sizes follow Atlassian Design**: 16, 24, 32, 40, 96 and
  128px, with `md` (32px) the default, so an avatar lines up with the
  kit's 32px controls. There is no 48px.
- **`xs` shows one initial.** Two letters do not fit in 16px at the
  smallest type size.
- **No square, no `appearance`.** Always a circle, so a person never
  reads as a product or workspace logo.
- **The placeholder is the kit's `user` icon** at 60% of the circle,
  centred, as in Figma. It takes `color` and `variant` like initials do.
- **`color` and `variant` are added**, to tell people apart in a list.
- **The circle ignores the radius preset.**
- **`status` and `AvatarGroup` are added.** The status words and the
  "+n" name are English by default; `statusLabel` and `moreLabel` translate
  them.
- **`max` counts the "+n".** The row never grows past `max` circles, and
  the "+n" always stands for two or more: never "+1" where the person
  would have fitted.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use an Avatar to show who: the author of a comment, the people on a
project, the account that is signed in. Give it `imageAlt` when the avatar
is the only thing that says who it is. When the name is printed next to
it, leave `imageAlt` out: the avatar is decorative, and the name is read
once.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={AvatarStories.DoDecorativeBesideName} />}
  doCaption="The name is printed, so the avatar has no imageAlt. A screen reader hears “Mary Thompson” once."
  dont={<Story of={AvatarStories.DontRepeatName} />}
  dontCaption="imageAlt repeats the printed name: “Mary Thompson, image, Mary Thompson”."
/>

## When not to use

- **For a product, team or workspace logo.** An Avatar is always round, so
  it reads as a person. Use an image with its own shape.
- **For status through colour.** The avatar's `color` means nothing. Use
  `status` for presence, and print the status where people act on it (an
  assignee picker): a dot is a glance, not the only cue.
- **For a long list of people.** A group shows who at a glance; past a
  handful, show the count or a list of names instead.
- **For an icon in a circle.** Use the icon itself, or an icon-only
  [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs) when it acts.

## Accessibility

- `imageAlt` names the **whole avatar** (`role="img"`), not just the
  image, so the image, the initials and the silhouette all announce the
  same person. The inner `<img>` has `alt=""`.
- Without `imageAlt` the avatar is **decorative** and hidden
  (`aria-hidden`), its status dot with it.
- With `status`, the status **joins the name**: "Mary Thompson, Online".
  The dot itself is not read.
- In a group, the "+n" is named "3 more" when the avatars are named, and
  decorative when they are not.
- With `hasTooltips`, the "+n" is the one avatar that takes focus, with
  the focus ring, and its tooltip of hidden names is its description. The
  other avatars' tooltips open on hover only: their names are already
  their accessible names.
- Initials are never read out: with `imageAlt` the avatar's name replaces
  them, without it the avatar is hidden. They are uppercased with CSS, so
  the text keeps the letters as passed.
- Initials meet 4.5:1 in every colour and variant, on every gray ramp in
  both modes, measured by the `Contrast` story. Neutral solid is gray 600
  under gray 50, 6.5:1 or more.
- The silhouette uses the initials colour (neutral subtle uses
  `--color-text-subtlest`), past the 3:1 a graphic needs in every colour
  and variant, measured by the `Contrast` story.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>
