# Badge A small count or dot that flags something new on another element: unread messages ...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import { Badge } from './Badge'
import * as BadgeStories from './Badge.stories'

<Meta of={BadgeStories} />

# Badge

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A small count or dot that flags something new on another element: unread
messages on an inbox, a status on an avatar.

<Status of={BadgeStories} />

<Canvas of={BadgeStories.Variants} />

## Variants

Each variant comes as a count or, with `isDot`, a dot.

| Variant | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| <Badge count={8} /> `primary` | The default: new items in the brand colour. |
| <Badge count={8} variant="accent" /> `accent` | Strong and neutral, where the brand colour would clash. |
| <Badge count={8} variant="secondary" /> `secondary` | Low emphasis: a total, not news. As a dot, Offline. |
| <Badge count={8} variant="destructive" /> `destructive` | Something needs attention: failures, overdue items. As a dot, Busy. |
| <Badge count={8} variant="success" /> `success` | As a dot, Online. |
| <Badge count={8} variant="warning" /> `warning` | As a dot, Away or Pending. |

<Canvas of={BadgeStories.Status} />

<Canvas of={BadgeStories.Sizes} />

`maxCount` keeps a large number from stretching the badge past its anchor.

<Canvas of={BadgeStories.MaxCount} />

`isFloating` pins the badge to a corner of the element it wraps.

<Canvas of={BadgeStories.Floating} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Badge } from 'zweihander/badge'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/badge.json
```

- Source: [src/components/atomic-elements/Badge.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/atomic-elements/Badge.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/badge](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/badge)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={BadgeStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={BadgeStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The anchor only exists when the badge has `children`. A badge on its own
is just the container.

## Measurements

One count badge, Atlassian's: 16px tall and at least 24px wide, so a
column of one- and two-digit counts lines up. `size` picks the dot: 8px
(`md`) or 6px (`sm`).

`size="sm"` on a count is deprecated. It renders the same badge as `md`
and warns once in development; in the next release `sm` is for dots only.
`size="md"` on a count, the default written out, and `sm` on a dot are
silent.

A floating badge is centred on its corner of the anchor, half in and half
out, with a 2px ring.

A dot has no text to carry it, so it must reach 3:1 against the page on its
own. That is why the `secondary` and `warning` dots step to a darker colour
than their count badge.

## States

A badge is not interactive: no hover, focus or pressed. Its states are what
it shows.

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Count', content: <Badge count={8} /> },
    { label: 'Over maxCount', content: <Badge count={120} maxCount={99} /> },
    { label: 'Zero', content: <Badge count={0} /> },
    { label: 'Dot', content: <Badge isDot /> },
  ]}
/>

`count={0}` shows "0". Hide the badge yourself if nothing new should mean
no badge.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={BadgeStories} />
</div>

Every other `<span>` attribute passes through to the badge, not to the
anchor.

### Differences from the spec

- **Atlassian's box, not a pill.** A count is 16px tall, at least 24px
  wide, with a 2px corner, in one size. Only the dot is round.
- **`children` is added.** A floating badge needs something to float on.
  The badge wraps it in a `position: relative` span rather than asking
  every consumer to position the anchor themselves.
- **`accent` is the inverted neutral.** The token set has one brand hue,
  which `primary` already uses, so `accent` is foreground-on-background:
  the strongest contrast available without inventing a colour.
- **`success` and `warning` are added** from the status tokens, for
  presence and state dots.
- **`floatingPlacement` defaults to `top-end`**, the usual notification
  corner; the spec gives no default.
- **Start and end are physical** (left and right). RTL pages would get
  mirrored placement.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Badge to say something is new, or how many, on the element it
belongs to: unread messages on an inbox button, a status dot on an avatar.
A floating badge is hidden from assistive tech, so the element it sits on
carries the meaning in its own name.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={BadgeStories.DoNameTheAnchor} />}
  doCaption="The button is named “Notifications, 4 unread”: the count reaches a screen reader too."
  dont={<Story of={BadgeStories.DontCountOnlyInBadge} />}
  dontCaption="The count lives only in the badge, which is hidden: a screen reader hears “Notifications”."
/>

Colour is never the only signal. A destructive badge still needs words
somewhere that say what is wrong, and a status dot needs `aria-label` or
a name beside it.

## When not to use

- **For a label or category.** Use a
  [Tag](?path=/docs/components-atomic-elements-tag--docs): it holds words,
  a badge holds a number.
- **For a message that needs reading.** Use an Alert or a Toast.
- **On every item of a list.** A badge flags what is new; if everything
  is, nothing stands out.

## Accessibility

- An **inline count** is plain text and is read where it sits. Inside a
  button it becomes part of the name ("Inbox 12").
- A **floating** badge is hidden from assistive tech: it sits *outside*
  the element it decorates, so it would be read as a stray number after
  it. Put the meaning in that element's name instead:
  `aria-label="Notifications, 4 unread"`.
- A **dot** has no text and is hidden too.
- Pass `aria-label` to any badge to expose it as an image with that name
  instead, e.g. a status dot on an avatar: `aria-label="Online"`.
- Contrast is checked by addon-a11y in error mode for every story.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

  render?: ReactElement
}

export interface BreadcrumbsProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'nav'>, 'children'> {
  /** From the top level down. The last one is the current page. */
  items: BreadcrumbItem[]
  /**
   * Collapse the middle when there are more than this many: the first item,
   * "…", and the last `maxItems - 1`. The "…" expands them in place.

  maxItems?: number

}

function Crumb({ item }: { item: BreadcrumbItem }) {

    render: item.render,
    defaultTagName: 'a',
    props: { href: item.href, className: styles.link, children: item.label },
  })
}

export function Breadcrumbs({
  items,
  maxItems,
  separator,
  size = 'md',
  'aria-label': ariaLabel = 'Breadcrumb',
  className,
  ...props
}: BreadcrumbsProps) {
  const [expanded, setExpanded] = useState(false)
  const listRef = useRef<HTMLOListElement>(null)
  // The "…" button is gone once pressed: move focus to the first item it
  // revealed, rather than dropping it on <body>.
  const justExpanded = useRef(false)

    if (!justExpanded.current) return
    justExpanded.current = false
    listRef.current?.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('li')[1]?.querySelector<HTMLElement>('a, [href], button')?.focus()
  }, [expanded])
  const collapse = !expanded && maxItems !== undefined && maxItems >= 2 && items.length > maxItems
  const shown: (BreadcrumbItem | 'ellipsis')[] = collapse
    ? [items[0], 'ellipsis', ...items.slice(items.length - (maxItems - 1))]
    : items
  const sep = (
    <span className={styles.separator} aria-hidden="true">
      {separator ?? <Icon name="chevron-right" />}
    </span>
  )

  return (
    <nav aria-label={ariaLabel} className={cn(styles.breadcrumbs, styles[size], className)} {...props}>
      <ol ref={listRef} className={styles.list}>
        {shown.map((item, i) => {
          const last = i === shown.length - 1
          return (
            <li key={i} className={styles.item}>
              {item === 'ellipsis' ? (
                <button
                  type="button"
                  className={styles.ellipsis}
                  aria-label={`Show ${items.length - maxItems!} more`}
                  onClick={() => {
                    justExpanded.current = true
                    setExpanded(true)
                  }}
                >
                  <Icon name="more" />
                </button>
              ) : last ? (
                // The current page: text, not a link to itself.
                <span className={styles.current} aria-current="page">
                  {item.label}
                </span>
              ) : (
                <Crumb item={item} />
              )}
              {!last && sep}
            </li>
          )
        })}
      </ol>
    </nav>
  )
}

# Breadcrumbs The trail from the top of a hierarchy down to the current page, each step a ...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import * as BreadcrumbsStories from './Breadcrumbs.stories'

<Meta of={BreadcrumbsStories} />

# Breadcrumbs

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

The trail from the top of a hierarchy down to the current page, each step a
link back up.

<Status of={BreadcrumbsStories} />

<Canvas of={BreadcrumbsStories.Default} />

## Variants

Breadcrumbs has one look. What changes is the size, how a long trail
collapses, and what sits between the steps.

| Form | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `md` | Under a page title, at body size. The default. |
| `sm` | Dense headers, panels and side sheets, at `body-sm`. |
| `maxItems` | Deep hierarchies, or a trail in a narrow place: the middle collapses to "…", which expands in place. |
| `separator` | A slash or other glyph, where a chevron would clash with nearby icons. |

<Canvas of={BreadcrumbsStories.Small} />

<Canvas of={BreadcrumbsStories.Collapsed} />

<Canvas of={BreadcrumbsStories.CustomSeparator} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Breadcrumbs } from 'zweihander/breadcrumbs'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/breadcrumbs.json
```

- Source: [src/components/navigation/Breadcrumbs.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/navigation/Breadcrumbs.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/breadcrumbs](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/breadcrumbs)
- Behaviour: a plain `<nav>` and `<ol>`, after the [APG breadcrumb pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/breadcrumb/)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={BreadcrumbsStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={BreadcrumbsStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

Each step is a list item: its link (or the ellipsis), then a separator.
The last item has no separator after it.

## Measurements

Breadcrumbs is text, not a row of controls. At `md` each item sits in a
24px box around its 14/20 text, with 8px either side of the separator, as
Atlassian Design's breadcrumb items.
Atlassian Design has no small breadcrumb; `sm` is the kit's own, and its
height is its line height.

<SpecTable
  caption="sm"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Text', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body-sm' },
    { part: 'Text', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body-sm' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="md"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Item', property: 'Minimum height', token: '--control-sm' },
    { part: 'Text', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body' },
    { part: 'Text', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Every size"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Item', property: 'Gap between items, and around the separator', token: '--space-inline' },
    { part: 'Ellipsis', property: 'Inline padding', token: '--space-1' },
    { part: 'Ellipsis', property: 'Icon size, md', token: '--icon-md' },
    { part: 'Ellipsis', property: 'Icon size, sm', token: '--icon-sm' },
    { part: 'Link and ellipsis', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-sm' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Width', token: '--focus-width' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Offset', token: '--focus-offset' },
    { part: 'Ellipsis', property: 'Hit area on touch screens', token: '--target-coarse' },
  ]}
/>

The separator icon is 1em: it follows the text size.

## Color

One colour set. Switch the theme in the toolbar: the values follow.

<SpecTable
  caption="Every size"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Link', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-subtlest' },
    { part: 'Link, hover', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text' },
    { part: 'Current page', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text' },
    { part: 'Separator', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-subtlest' },
    { part: 'Ellipsis', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-subtlest' },
    { part: 'Ellipsis, hover', property: 'Background', token: '--color-background-neutral' },
    { part: 'Ellipsis, hover', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-border-focused' },
  ]}
/>

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={BreadcrumbsStories.StatesExample} />
</States>

- **Hover** turns a link to `--color-text` and underlines it; on the
  ellipsis it fills an `--color-background-neutral` chip.
- **Focus** is a 2px `--color-border-focused` outline, 2px outside the link or the
  ellipsis.
- There is no disabled state: a level the reader cannot open is left out
  of the trail.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={BreadcrumbsStories} />
</div>

Every other `<nav>` attribute passes through.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use Breadcrumbs on pages three or more levels deep, under the page title,
so a reader can see where they are and jump back up any number of levels.
It is a secondary aid: the main navigation still has to get people
everywhere.

Keep the trail on one line. When it would wrap, collapse the middle with
`maxItems`; the first level and the nearest ones stay in view.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={BreadcrumbsStories.DoCollapseLongTrail} />}
  doCaption="Collapse a long trail with maxItems: one line, and the levels that matter most stay visible."
  dont={<Story of={BreadcrumbsStories.DontWrapLongTrail} />}
  dontCaption="A trail that wraps reads as two rows and pushes the page down."
/>

Write each label as the title of the page it opens, short enough to scan.
The last item is the current page, as text: a link to the page you are on
does nothing useful.

## When not to use

- **For history.** Breadcrumbs shows where a page sits, not how the reader
  got there. For "go back", use a Back link or
  [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs).
- **On a flat site.** One or two levels need no trail; the main
  navigation already says where you are.
- **For the steps of a task.** Use a Stepper: it shows the steps ahead
  too, and which are done.
- **As the main navigation.** Use a side navigation of links, or Tabs.

## Accessibility

- A `<nav>` landmark named "Breadcrumb" (change it with `aria-label`),
  around an ordered list: screen readers announce the number of items and
  the position of each.
- Each level above the current page is a real `<a href>`, in the tab
  order.
- The last item is text with `aria-current="page"`, not a link.
- Separators are `aria-hidden`, so they are not read between items.
- The ellipsis is a button named "Show 3 more". Enter or Space expands the
  trail and moves focus to the first item it revealed, rather than
  dropping it on the page.
- The ellipsis is under 44px; on touch screens (`pointer: coarse`) its hit
  area grows to 44×44px without it growing.
- Focus ring: 2px `--color-border-focused`, 2px offset.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

'use client'

import type { ComponentProps, ReactNode, Ref } from 'react'
import { Button as BaseButton } from '@base-ui/react/button'
import { mergeProps } from '@base-ui/react/merge-props'
import { useRender } from '@base-ui/react/use-render'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Button.module.css'

interface ButtonBaseProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'button'>, 'ref'> {
  ref?: Ref<HTMLElement>
  variant?: 'primary' | 'accent' | 'secondary' | 'destructive'
  appearance?: 'contained' | 'outlined' | 'ghost'
  size?: 'sm' | 'md'
  startIcon?: ReactNode
  endIcon?: ReactNode
  /** Shows a spinner, blocks clicks and keeps focus, so a keyboard user is not dropped. On a link it behaves as disabled. */
  isLoading?: boolean
  isFullWidth?: boolean
  /** Renders an `<a>` instead of a `<button>`: it navigates, it does not act. */
  href?: string
  target?: string
  rel?: string
  /** Replaces the rendered element, e.g. a router's `<Link />`. */
  render?: useRender.RenderProp
}

/** An icon-only button has no text to name it, so `aria-label` is required. */
export type ButtonProps =
  | (ButtonBaseProps & { isIconOnly?: false })
  | (ButtonBaseProps & { isIconOnly: true; 'aria-label': string })

export function Button({
  variant = 'primary',
  appearance = 'contained',
  size = 'md',
  startIcon,
  endIcon,
  isLoading = false,
  isFullWidth = false,
  isIconOnly = false,
  href,
  target,
  rel,
  render,
  disabled,
  type = 'button',
  className,
  children,
  ...props
}: ButtonProps) {
  const content = (
    <>
      {isLoading && <span className={styles.spinner} aria-hidden="true" />}
      {startIcon && (
        <span className={styles.icon} aria-hidden="true">
          {startIcon}
        </span>
      )}
      {children}
      {endIcon && (
        <span className={styles.icon} aria-hidden="true">
          {endIcon}
        </span>
      )}
    </>
  )
  const own = {
    className: cn(
      styles.button,
      styles[variant],
      styles[appearance],
      styles[size],
      isIconOnly && styles.iconOnly,
      isFullWidth && styles.fullWidth,
      isLoading && styles.loading,
      className,
    ),
    'aria-busy': isLoading || undefined,
    children: content,
  }

  // `href` or `render` means someone else's element — an <a>, a router's
  // Link — whose semantics must survive: Base UI's Button would stamp
  // role="button" on it. Props are merged onto it instead.
  //
  // Disabled (or loading, which a link cannot show) drops the render
  // element too and leaves a bare <a> with no href: removing the href is
  // the only thing that stops an <a> navigating, and a router's Link keeps
  // its own. aria-disabled says why it is inert.
  const inert = disabled || isLoading
  const custom = useRender({
    enabled: href !== undefined || render !== undefined,
    render: inert ? undefined : render,
    defaultTagName: 'a',
    props: mergeProps<'a'>(own, props as ComponentProps<'a'>, {
      ...(!inert && href !== undefined && { href }),
      target,
      rel,
      'aria-disabled': inert || undefined,
    }),
  })
  if (custom) return custom

  return (
    <BaseButton
      {...props}
      {...own}
      type={type}
      disabled={disabled || isLoading}
      focusableWhenDisabled={isLoading}
    />
  )
}

# Button Triggers an action on the current page, or, with `href`, navigates. ## Variants `...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import { Button } from './Button'
import * as ButtonStories from './Button.stories'

<Meta of={ButtonStories} />

# Button

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

Triggers an action on the current page, or, with `href`, navigates.

<Status of={ButtonStories} />

<Canvas of={ButtonStories.Default} />

## Variants

`variant` is the colour, by meaning; `appearance` is the emphasis. Any
variant takes any appearance.

<Canvas of={ButtonStories.Matrix} />

| Variant | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| <Button>Primary</Button> | The next step: Save, Continue, Create. One per view. |
| <Button variant="accent">Accent</Button> | A strong action in neutral black or white, where the brand colour would clash or already means something else. |
| <Button variant="secondary">Secondary</Button> | Everything else: Cancel, Back, Export. |
| <Button variant="destructive">Destructive</Button> | Deleting, or anything that cannot be undone. |

| Appearance | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| <Button>Contained</Button> | The action to take, filled so it is found first. |
| <Button appearance="outlined">Outlined</Button> | Actions that matter but are not the next step. |
| <Button appearance="ghost">Ghost</Button> | Low emphasis and dense places: toolbars, table rows, a card's corner. |

<Canvas of={ButtonStories.Sizes} />

<Canvas of={ButtonStories.WithIcons} />

<Canvas of={ButtonStories.IconOnly} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Button } from 'zweihander/button'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/button.json
```

- Source: [src/components/buttons/Button.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/buttons/Button.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/button](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/button)
- Behaviour: [Base UI Button](https://base-ui.com/react/components/button)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={ButtonStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={ButtonStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

While `isLoading`, a spinner takes the content's place; the content stays,
invisible, so the button keeps its width and its name.

## Measurements

Each size is a control tier (Foundations / Sizing), with Atlassian
Design's numbers: 32px by default, 24px for tables and dense rows. Buttons
take the spacious inline padding, 12px at both sizes: a centred label
needs more room either side than a field's left-aligned text. The 12px is
measured from the button's outer edge to its label or icon, border
included, as in Atlassian Design, and is the same with or without an icon
on that side; icon and label sit 6px apart. Ghost has no border, so it is
11px from edge to label, as Figma binds it. The label is 14/20 at both
sizes.

  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Height', token: '--control-sm' },

    { part: 'Container', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--control-sm-radius' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Gap', token: '--control-sm-gap' },

## Color

Each variant has a solid (the contained fill), a colour on that solid, and
a tone that outlined and ghost use for their label. Switch the theme and the
accent in the toolbar: the values follow.

Ghost and outlined have no fill at rest. Contained is lit from above: a
lighter top, a highlight on the top edge, a bottom-edge inner shadow
(black at 18%, 1px up, 1.2px blur, 0.35px spread) and a hairline border a
step darker than the solid. The hairline is the variant's solid moved in
lightness, so it has no token of its own and follows the accent and the
mode; the highlight and the shadow are light, the same on every fill.

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
    { label: 'Pressed', pseudo: 'active' },
    { label: 'Disabled', content: <Story of={ButtonStories.Disabled} /> },
    { label: 'Loading', content: <Story of={ButtonStories.Loading} /> },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={ButtonStories.Default} />
</States>

- **Hover and pressed** are mixed from the variant's own colours, not a
  token each. A coloured solid (primary, destructive) moves away from its
  label and gains contrast; accent and secondary move toward it. Outlined
  and ghost tint the background with their tone, 8% on hover and 14% when
  pressed, and their label moves 25% and 40% toward `--color-text`. Every state keeps the label at 4.5:1, measured by the
  `StateContrast` story under all seventeen accents in both modes.
- **Pressed**, on contained, turns the light over: shade on the top edge,
  no drop shadow, no gradient, as if pushed in.
- **Focus** is a 2px `--color-border-focused` outline, 2px outside the button.
- **Disabled** is the enabled look at 50% opacity.
- **Loading** keeps the full colour: the button is busy, not unavailable.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={ButtonStories} />
</div>

Every other `<button>` attribute passes through, including `ref`.

### Differences from the spec

- **Two sizes, not four.** The sizes follow Atlassian Design: 32px (`md`) by default, 24px (`sm`) for tables and dense rows. Both take 12px from the outer edge to the label (11px on ghost, which has no border), a 6px gap and a 14/20 label; `sm` is a shorter box, not smaller type. The spec's larger steps were dropped; a big call to action is `md` with more room around it, not a taller box.
- **`disabled`, not `isDisabled`**: the native attribute keeps its name.
- **`isIconOnly` is added.** The spec has no icon-only button, and a
  square button that still requires a name is common enough to need one.
- **`render` is added** for composition with routers and other elements,
  matching Base UI and shadcn. It replaced `asChild` in 0.8.
- **`accent` is the inverted neutral** (foreground on background), as on
  Badge: the token set has one brand hue and `primary` uses it.
- Outlined and ghost `primary` use `--color-text-brand`, a step of the accent
  measured to read at 4.5:1 on the page. The solid step would not, for
  warm accents.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Button for an action on the current page: save, submit, open a
dialog, delete. Use one `primary contained` button per view, for the thing
to do next. Everything else steps down to `outlined` or `ghost`, or to
`secondary`.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={ButtonStories.DoOnePrimary} />}
  doCaption="One primary button: the thing to do next. The rest step down."
  dont={<Story of={ButtonStories.DontTwoPrimaries} />}
  dontCaption="Two primary buttons compete for the same click."
/>

**Loading** keeps the button's width and focus and blocks it from acting
again, so a double-submit is impossible and a keyboard user is not dropped
back to the top of the page.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={ButtonStories.Loading} />}
  doCaption="Show progress with isLoading: the button stays where focus is, and cannot fire twice."
  dont={<Story of={ButtonStories.DontDisableWhileSaving} />}
  dontCaption="Disabling it to show progress drops keyboard focus and reads as unavailable."
/>

## When not to use

- **To navigate.** A link is not a button. Pass `href` and Button renders a
  real `<a>`: it keeps link semantics, opens in a new tab on middle-click,
  and gets the link cursor. A plain Button with an `onClick` that changes
  the page does none of that.
- **For a setting that stays on or off.** Use a
  [Toggle Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-togglebutton--docs), a
  Switch or a Checkbox.
- **For a link inside running text.** Use Link.

<Canvas of={ButtonStories.Href} />

## Accessibility

- A native `<button>`, `type="button"` by default so it never submits a
  form by accident. Enter and Space both activate it.
- `isIconOnly` needs `aria-label`; TypeScript refuses it without one.
  Icons are `aria-hidden` everywhere else, so they never double the name.
- `isLoading` sets `aria-busy` and `aria-disabled` but keeps the button
  focusable. `disabled` removes it from the tab order, as native buttons
  do.
- A disabled or loading link renders a bare `<a>` with no `href` (the
  only thing that stops an `<a>` navigating) and `aria-disabled`. With
  `render`, the render element is dropped too, since a router's Link would
  keep its own `href`.
- `render` is for elements that are already interactive: a link or a
  router's Link. It merges props onto the element and adds no role or
  keyboard handling, so do not render a `<div>` through it.
- Hover and pressed keep the label at 4.5:1 too. The `StateContrast`
  story measures every variant × appearance × state under all seventeen
  accents in both modes, from the CSS that ships.
- `sm` and `md` are under 44px; on touch screens (`pointer: coarse`) the
  hit area grows to 44×44px without the button growing.
- Focus ring: 2px `--color-border-focused`, 2px offset, at 3:1 or better on the page.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

import type { ComponentProps } from 'react'
import { ToggleGroup } from '@base-ui/react/toggle-group'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './ButtonGroup.module.css'

export interface ButtonGroupProps
  extends Omit<ComponentProps<'div'>, 'defaultValue' | 'onChange' | 'dir'> {
  /** `separate`: ToggleButtons 4px apart. `joined`: one bar, inner corners square, borders shared. */
  type?: 'separate' | 'joined'
  /** Controlled: the `value` of the ToggleButton that is on. Pair with `onValueChange`. */
  value?: string
  /** Uncontrolled: the value on at first. */
  defaultValue?: string
  /** Called with the value of the ToggleButton just turned on. */
  onValueChange?: (value: string) => void
  /** Disables every toggle in the group. */
  disabled?: boolean
}

/** ToggleButtons that share one selection, exactly one on at a time, like Tabs. */
export function ButtonGroup({
  type = 'separate',
  value,
  defaultValue,
  onValueChange,
  className,
  ...props
}: ButtonGroupProps) {
  return (
    <ToggleGroup
      {...props}
      value={value === undefined ? undefined : [value]}
      defaultValue={defaultValue === undefined ? undefined : [defaultValue]}
      onValueChange={(next, details) => {
        // Once one is on, pressing it again does not leave none on.
        if (next.length === 0) return details.cancel()
        onValueChange?.(next[0])
      }}
      className={cn(styles[type], className)}
    />
  )
}

# Button Group

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A selection control, like Tabs without the panel:
[Toggle Buttons](?path=/docs/components-buttons-togglebutton--docs) that
share one selection, exactly one on at a time. `type="separate"` sets them
4px apart; `type="joined"` makes them one bar.

<Status of={ButtonGroupStories} />

Button Group is outside the 1.0 component list; it is beta from 0.9.0.

<Canvas of={ButtonGroupStories.Default} />

## Variants

| `type` | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `separate` | The default. Outlined toggles 4px apart: one view, one mode, one period at a time. |
| `joined` | A segmented control: one bar, where the options read as one control. |

<Canvas of={ButtonGroupStories.Joined} />

<Canvas of={ButtonGroupStories.IconToggles} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { ButtonGroup } from 'zweihander/button-group'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/button-group.json
```

- Source: [src/components/buttons/ButtonGroup.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/buttons/ButtonGroup.tsx)
- Spec: none on uiguideline.com; after [shadcn/ui Button Group](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/button-group) and [Toggle Group](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/toggle-group)
- Behaviour: [Base UI Toggle Group](https://base-ui.com/react/components/toggle-group)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={ButtonGroupStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={ButtonGroupStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The toggles keep their own anatomy; the container only spaces them
(`separate`) or joins them (`joined`).

## Measurements

The group adds no size of its own. Each button keeps its tier, so a group
of `sm` buttons is `--control-sm` tall.

`joined`: the inner corners are square and each toggle after the first
overlaps the one before by its 1px border, so two outlined toggles share
one line. The outer corners keep the toggles' radius.

`separate` leaves its toggles whole: every toggle keeps its four corners
and its border, and they stand `--space-1` (4px) apart in one row that does
not wrap. In a group wider than its content the toggles share the extra
width.

  caption="separate"
  rows={[

/>

<SpecTable

## Color

The group paints nothing: off and on colours are the Toggle Button's. In
a joined group the toggle that is on is raised over its neighbours so its
own border wins where they overlap.

<SpecTable

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
    { label: 'Disabled', content: <Story of={ButtonGroupStories.Disabled} /> },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={ButtonGroupStories.Default} />
</States>

Hover and focus are each toggle's own; a toggle has no press-and-hold
state. In a joined group the focused toggle is raised over its neighbours
so the ring is never cut; in a separate group the ring fits in the gap.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={ButtonGroupStories} />
</div>

Every other `<div>` attribute passes through.

### Differences from the spec

- **A selection control, not a row of actions.** As in the Figma library,
  ButtonGroup holds ToggleButtons with exactly one on, in a `separate` or
  `joined` `type`. In 0.9 it replaced both the old action-row
  `ButtonGroup` and `ToggleGroup`. There is no `multiple`: for settings
  that combine, use separate ToggleButtons. For related actions, lay out
  Buttons yourself.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a ButtonGroup when the toggles answer one question with one answer:
which view, which mode, which period. Give every toggle in a group the
same variant and appearance, so the one that is on is the only one that
stands out.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={ButtonGroupStories.DoSameLook} />}
  doCaption="One look across the group: only the toggle that is on stands out."
  dont={<Story of={ButtonGroupStories.DontMixLooks} />}
  dontCaption="A different variant per button reads as several states at once."
/>

<Canvas of={ButtonGroupStories.Controlled} />

## When not to use

- **To switch between panels of content.** Use Tabs: they own the panel
  and its `tabpanel` role.
- **For a choice submitted with a form.** Use a Radio group or Checkboxes:
  a toggle applies at once, a form field waits for Submit.
- **For actions.** A ButtonGroup keeps one option on; for previous and
  next, or zoom in and out, lay out Buttons side by side.
- **For settings that combine** (status filters, Bold and Italic). Use
  separate ToggleButtons: a ButtonGroup keeps exactly one on.
- **For more than a handful of options.** Use a Select.

## Accessibility

- The container has `role="group"`; name it with `aria-label`.
- Each toggle is a native `<button>` with `aria-pressed`, so a screen reader
  announces "Board, toggle button, pressed".
- The group is one tab stop. Arrow keys move between its toggles and
  wrap, Home and End jump to the first and last; Space or Enter turns one
  on. This is the APG toolbar pattern Base UI's Toggle Group follows.
- Exactly one stays on: pressing the one that is on again does not
  release it.
- A disabled group disables every toggle in it.
- An icon-only toggle needs its own `aria-label`, as on Button. A
  [Tooltip](?path=/docs/components-overlays-tooltip--docs) can show that
  label to sighted users: it merges onto the toggle instead of wrapping
  it, so the group still holds only its toggles.

  <Canvas of={ButtonGroupStories.WithTooltips} />

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

/* ------------------------------------------------------------ plain dates
   Calendar dates carry no time: every Date here is local midnight. */

export const startOfDay = (d: Date) => new Date(d.getFullYear(), d.getMonth(), d.getDate())
export const isSameDay = (a: Date | null | undefined, b: Date | null | undefined) =>
  !!a && !!b && a.getFullYear() === b.getFullYear() && a.getMonth() === b.getMonth() && a.getDate() === b.getDate()
export const addDays = (d: Date, n: number) => new Date(d.getFullYear(), d.getMonth(), d.getDate() + n)
/** Adds months, keeping the day where it exists: 31 Jan + 1 month is 28/29 Feb. */
export const addMonths = (d: Date, n: number) => {
  const first = new Date(d.getFullYear(), d.getMonth() + n, 1)
  const last = new Date(first.getFullYear(), first.getMonth() + 1, 0).getDate()
  return new Date(first.getFullYear(), first.getMonth(), Math.min(d.getDate(), last))
}
const startOfMonth = (d: Date) => new Date(d.getFullYear(), d.getMonth(), 1)
const clamp = (d: Date, min?: Date | null, max?: Date | null) =>
  min && d < startOfDay(min) ? startOfDay(min) : max && d > startOfDay(max) ? startOfDay(max) : d

/** The locale's first day of the week (0 = Sunday), where the browser knows it. */
export function firstDayOfWeek(locale?: string) {
  try {
    const l = new Intl.Locale(locale ?? navigator.language) as Intl.Locale & {
      getWeekInfo?: () => { firstDay: number }
      weekInfo?: { firstDay: number }
    }
    const info = l.getWeekInfo?.() ?? l.weekInfo
    if (info) return info.firstDay % 7
  } catch {
    /* fall through */
  }
  return 1
}

  defaultValue = null,
  onValueChange,
  month: monthProp,
  defaultMonth,
  onMonthChange,
  min,
  max,
  isDateDisabled,
  range,
  locale,
  weekStartsOn,
  autoFocus = false,
  className,
}: CalendarProps) {
  const today = startOfDay(new Date())
  const [valueState, setValueState] = useState(defaultValue)
  const selected = range ? range.start : value !== undefined ? value : valueState
  const rangeEnd = range?.end ?? null
  const [monthState, setMonthState] = useState(() => startOfMonth(defaultMonth ?? selected ?? today))
  const month = monthProp ? startOfMonth(monthProp) : monthState
  // The day with the roving tab stop, and where the keyboard moves from.
  const [focused, setFocused] = useState(() => clamp(selected ?? (isSameMonth(today, month) ? today : month), min, max))
  const gridRef = useRef<HTMLTableElement>(null)
  const moveFocus = useRef(autoFocus)

  const first = weekStartsOn ?? firstDayOfWeek(locale)
  const fmt = useMemo(() => {
    return {
      title: new Intl.DateTimeFormat(locale, { month: 'long', year: 'numeric', calendar: 'gregory' }),
      weekday: new Intl.DateTimeFormat(locale, { weekday: 'short', calendar: 'gregory' }),
      weekdayNarrow: new Intl.DateTimeFormat(locale, { weekday: 'narrow', calendar: 'gregory' }),
      weekdayLong: new Intl.DateTimeFormat(locale, { weekday: 'long', calendar: 'gregory' }),
      day: new Intl.DateTimeFormat(locale, { day: 'numeric', calendar: 'gregory' }),
      full: new Intl.DateTimeFormat(locale, { dateStyle: 'full', calendar: 'gregory' }),
    }
  }, [locale])

  const disabled = (d: Date) =>
    (!!min && d < startOfDay(min)) || (!!max && d > startOfDay(max)) || (isDateDisabled?.(d) ?? false)

  const setMonth = (m: Date) => {
    const next = startOfMonth(m)
    setMonthState(next)
    onMonthChange?.(next)
  }
  const focusDay = (d: Date) => {
    const next = clamp(d, min, max)
    setFocused(next)
    if (!isSameMonth(next, month)) setMonth(next)
    moveFocus.current = true
  }
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!moveFocus.current) return
    moveFocus.current = false
    gridRef.current?.querySelector<HTMLElement>('[tabindex="0"]')?.focus()
  })
  // Keep the tab stop inside the month when it changes from outside.
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!isSameMonth(focused, month)) setFocused(clamp(selected && isSameMonth(selected, month) ? selected : month, min, max))
  }, [month.getTime()]) // eslint-disable-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps

  const select = (d: Date) => {
    if (disabled(d)) return
    setValueState(d)
    onValueChange?.(d)
    setFocused(d)
  }

  const onKeyDown = (e: KeyboardEvent<HTMLElement>) => {
    const dow = (focused.getDay() - first + 7) % 7
    // Right to left mirrors the grid, so the arrows follow what is on screen.
    const ahead = getComputedStyle(e.currentTarget).direction === 'rtl' ? -1 : 1
    const moves: Record<string, () => Date> = {
      ArrowLeft: () => addDays(focused, -ahead),
      ArrowRight: () => addDays(focused, ahead),
      ArrowUp: () => addDays(focused, -7),
      ArrowDown: () => addDays(focused, 7),
      Home: () => addDays(focused, -dow),
      End: () => addDays(focused, 6 - dow),
      PageUp: () => addMonths(focused, e.shiftKey ? -12 : -1),
      PageDown: () => addMonths(focused, e.shiftKey ? 12 : 1),
    }
    if (moves[e.key]) {
      e.preventDefault()
      focusDay(moves[e.key]())
    } else if (e.key === 'Enter' || e.key === ' ') {
      e.preventDefault()
      select(focused)
    }
  }

  // Six rows of seven days, starting on the week's first day.
  const lead = (month.getDay() - first + 7) % 7
  const start = addDays(month, -lead)
  const weeks = Array.from({ length: 6 }, (_, w) => Array.from({ length: 7 }, (_, d) => addDays(start, w * 7 + d)))
  const weekdays = weeks[0]
  // Two letters where the short names are short ("Mon" → "Mo", "lun." →
  // "lu"); the narrow ones where they are not ("Thứ 2" → "T2").
  const weekdayName = (d: Date) => {
    const short = fmt.weekday.format(d)
    return weekdays.every((w) => fmt.weekday.format(w).length <= 4) ? short.slice(0, 2) : fmt.weekdayNarrow.format(d)
  }
  const minMonth = min ? startOfMonth(min) : null
  const maxMonth = max ? startOfMonth(max) : null
  const nav = (label: string, months: number) => {
    const back = months < 0
    return (
      <button
        type="button"
        className={styles.nav}
        aria-label={label}
        disabled={back ? !!minMonth && minMonth >= month : !!maxMonth && maxMonth <= month}
        onClick={() => setMonth(clamp(addMonths(month, months), minMonth, maxMonth))}
      >
        <Icon name={back ? 'chevron-left' : 'chevron-right'} className={styles.dirIcon} />
      </button>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className={cn(styles.calendar, className)}>
      {/* Month back at the start, the month centred, month on at the end.
          Years are Shift+Page Up and Shift+Page Down. */}
      <div className={styles.header}>
        {nav('Previous month', -1)}
        {/* Not a heading: a calendar can sit anywhere in a page's outline.
            It announces the month as it changes. */}
        <div className={styles.title} aria-live="polite">
          {fmt.title.format(month)}
        </div>
        {nav('Next month', 1)}
      </div>
      <table ref={gridRef} role="grid" aria-label={fmt.title.format(month)} className={styles.grid} onKeyDown={onKeyDown}>
        <thead>
          <tr>
            {weekdays.map((d) => (
              <th key={d.getDay()} scope="col" abbr={fmt.weekdayLong.format(d)} className={styles.weekday}>
                {weekdayName(d)}
              </th>
            ))}
          </tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
          {weeks.map((week, w) => (
            <tr key={w}>
              {week.map((d, col) => {
                const outside = !isSameMonth(d, month)
                // Selection and the band stay inside the month: a day of the month
                // either side is only there for shape, and two months side by
                // side would otherwise both draw the days where they overlap.
                const isSelected = !outside && (isSameDay(d, selected) || isSameDay(d, rangeEnd))
                const between = !outside && !!selected && !!rangeEnd && d > selected && d < rangeEnd
                const banded = !!rangeEnd && !isSameDay(selected, rangeEnd) && (isSelected || between)
                const isDisabled = disabled(d)
                return (
                  <td
                    key={d.getTime()}
                    role="gridcell"
                    aria-selected={isSelected || between || undefined}
                    className={cn(
                      styles.cell,
                      banded && styles.inRange,
                      banded && isSameDay(d, selected) && styles.rangeStart,
                      banded && isSameDay(d, rangeEnd) && styles.rangeEnd,
                      // Rounded off where a week or the month starts or ends.
                      banded && (col === 0 || d.getDate() === 1) && styles.bandStart,
                      banded && (col === 6 || addDays(d, 1).getDate() === 1) && styles.bandEnd,
                    )}
                  >
                    {outside ? (
                      // The months either side are shape, not content: hidden from
                      // assistive tech, not pickable, and faded past muted. Arrow
                      // keys still cross into them, by moving the month.
                      <span aria-hidden="true" data-outside="" className={cn(styles.day, styles.outside)}>
                        {fmt.day.format(d)}
                      </span>
                    ) : (
                      <button
                        type="button"
                        tabIndex={isSameDay(d, focused) ? 0 : -1}
                        aria-label={fmt.full.format(d)}
                        aria-current={isSameDay(d, today) ? 'date' : undefined}
                        aria-disabled={isDisabled || undefined}
                        className={cn(
                          styles.day,
                          isSelected && styles.selected,
                          between && styles.between,
                          isSameDay(d, today) && styles.today,
                        )}
                        onClick={() => select(d)}
                        onFocus={() => setFocused(d)}
                      >
                        {fmt.day.format(d)}
                      </button>
                    )}
                  </td>
                )
              })}
            </tr>
          ))}
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </div>
  )
}

function isSameMonth(a: Date, b: Date) {
  return a.getFullYear() === b.getFullYear() && a.getMonth() === b.getMonth()
}

const Today = (args) => {
  const now = new Date()
  const range = { start: new Date(now.getFullYear(), now.getMonth(), now.getDate() - 1), end: new Date(now.getFullYear(), now.getMonth(), now.getDate() + 1) }
  return (
    <div style={{ display: 'flex', flexWrap: 'wrap', gap: 16 }}>
      {(['light', 'dark'] as const).flatMap((mode) =>
        [undefined, range].map((r) => (
          <Theme key={mode + !!r} appearance={mode} style={{ background: 'var(--color-surface)', padding: 8 }} data-audit={`${mode}${r ? ' range' : ''}`}>
            {/* Today's month, not the range's: on the 1st the range starts last month. */}
            <Calendar {...args} range={r} defaultMonth={now} />
          </Theme>
        )),
      )}
    </div>
  )
};

# Calendar A month grid to pick one day from, or to show one: a booking page, the inside o...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import { Calendar } from './Calendar'
import * as CalendarStories from './Calendar.stories'

<Meta of={CalendarStories} />

# Calendar

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A month grid to pick one day from, or to show one: a booking page, the
inside of a [Date Picker](?path=/docs/components-inputs-datepicker--docs).

<Status of={CalendarStories} />

<Canvas of={CalendarStories.Default} />

## Variants

Calendar has one look and one size. What changes is what it shows.

| Variant | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| One day (`value`) | Picking or showing a single day: a delivery date, a booking. |
| A span (`range`) | Showing a stay or a report period. Clicks still report one day; Date Range Picker decides the span. |
| Limits (`min`, `max`) | Booking windows: nothing before tomorrow, nothing after the season ends. |
| Ruled-out days (`isDateDisabled`) | Weekends, holidays, days already booked. |
| Locale (`locale`, `weekStartsOn`) | Month and weekday names in the reader's language, and their first day of the week. |

<Canvas of={CalendarStories.Range} />

<Canvas of={CalendarStories.MinMax} />

<Canvas of={CalendarStories.NoWeekends} />

The locale decides the week: `vi-VN` and `en-GB` start on Monday, `en-US`
on Sunday, read from `Intl.Locale` where the browser knows it (Monday
otherwise). The grid is always Gregorian, so a locale whose own calendar is
not (Persian) still gets Gregorian days, in its own digits.

<Canvas of={CalendarStories.Vietnamese} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Calendar } from 'zweihander/calendar'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/calendar.json
```

- Source: [src/components/data-display/Calendar.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/data-display/Calendar.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/calendar](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/calendar)
- Behaviour: a plain element, using `Intl` for names and the week's first day: no date library
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={CalendarStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={CalendarStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The grid always has six rows. Months span four to six weeks; a fixed height
keeps a popover or a page from jumping as you page through them.

Two more looks sit on the days: **today**, an orange fill with the
control's corners, as a selected day has; and with `range`, the **band**, as tall as a day,
one unbroken strip behind the days from one end to the other. Under the
two ends it covers only the half that faces the range, so each end keeps
its own corners on the outside. The band rounds off where a week or
the month starts or ends. Days of the months either side are never banded,
so two months side by side never draw the same day twice.

## Measurements

Calendar has one size, after `@atlaskit/calendar`. Days are 40px wide and
32px tall and touch: the whole cell is the day's target, and a range's
band runs unbroken from cell to cell. The weekday row is 32px tall, 8px
round a 16px line of bold 12px. The header keeps 8px at each end and sits
12px above the grid; its arrows are 24px round a 12px chevron. In a Date
Picker the panel adds 16px round all of it.

The header is one row: previous month at the start, the month and year
centred, in the 14px heading size, and next month at the end. There are
no year buttons; Shift+Page Up and Shift+Page Down page by year. The kit
keeps its own looks for today and the selected day.

<SpecTable
  caption="Header"

Figures are tabular, so the columns of dates line up. On touch screens
(`pointer: coarse`) days grow to 44px square, the touch target: they
touch, so a larger invisible area would lie over the next day. The
previous and next buttons stay 24px and grow an invisible 44px area
instead. The header makes room for them: it pads 10px (half of 44px less
24px) and the month keeps 10px clear at each side, so the areas lie over
neither the month nor the calendar's edge.

## Color

One table per kind of day. Switch the theme and the accent in the toolbar:
the values follow.

  caption="Header and weekdays"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Month', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text' },

    { part: 'Weekdays', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-subtlest' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable

  rows={[
    { part: 'Day', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Selected"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Day', property: 'Background', token: '--color-background-brand-bold' },
    { part: 'Day', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-brand-inverse' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Today"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Day', property: 'Background', token: '--color-background-accent-orange-bolder' },
    { part: 'Day', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-accent-orange-contrast' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Range"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Band', property: 'Background', token: '--color-background-neutral' },
    { part: 'Days between', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text' },
    { part: 'Today, between', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-accent-orange-contrast' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Outside the month and unavailable"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Outside day', property: 'Colour, at 50%', token: '--color-text-subtlest' },
    { part: 'Unavailable day', property: 'Colour, at 60% opacity', token: '--color-text-subtlest' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable caption="Every part" rows={[{ part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-border-focused' }]} />

- **Day** has no fill at rest.
- **Today's figure** is `--color-text-accent-orange-contrast`, semibold:
  near-black on `--color-background-accent-orange-bolder`, 4.9:1 in both
  modes. White would be 3.4:1 in light, under the 4.5:1 a 14px figure
  needs. A selected today shows as selected.
- **Days between** the ends of a range are `--color-text`, regular weight.
- **Outside days** are `--color-text-subtlest` mixed 50% with transparent,
  about 2:1. No token is lighter, and WCAG allows it for decoration: they
  are hidden from assistive tech and cannot be picked.
- **Unavailable days** are struck through as well as faded, so they do not
  rely on colour.

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={CalendarStories.Default} />
</States>

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
    { label: 'Pressed', pseudo: 'active' },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={CalendarStories.Default} />
</States>

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Disabled', content: <Story of={CalendarStories.MinMax} /> },
    { label: 'Today', content: <Calendar locale="en-GB" weekStartsOn={1} /> },
  ]}
/>

<States states={[{ label: 'Selected range', content: <Story of={CalendarStories.Range} /> }]} />

Each example forces the state on every day at once; on screen it is the
one under the pointer or the keyboard.

- **Hover** fills a day, or the previous and next buttons, with `--color-background-neutral`
  behind `--color-text`. The selected day and today keep their own
  colours; unavailable and outside days do not react.
- **Focus** is a 2px `--color-border-focused` outline, 2px outside the day. The days
  touch, so the focused day is lifted above its neighbours and the ring
  is drawn whole over their edges.
- **Pressed** has no look of its own: the click selects the day, and the
  selected look follows.
- **Disabled** is per day: before `min`, after `max`, or ruled out by
  `isDateDisabled`. The previous and next buttons
  disable in the month of `min` or `max`, at 50% opacity.
- **Selected** is the brand fill, with the control's corners; **today** is
  the orange fill, with the same corners. With `range`, both ends are selected and the days between are
  banded.

## API

</div>

Also exported, for working with the same plain dates: `isSameDay`,
`addDays`, `addMonths`, `startOfDay`, `firstDayOfWeek` and the `DateRange`
type. Every date is local midnight; times are ignored.

### Differences from the spec

The header follows `@atlaskit/calendar` in the size of its buttons and
the centred month and year, without its year buttons: Shift+Page Up and
Shift+Page Down page by year.

- **The buttons disable at `min` and `max`.** Atlassian's stay enabled and
  page into months with nothing to pick.
- **Fixed button names.** "Previous month" and "Next month", in English
  like the kit's other built-in labels. Atlassian takes them as props and
  adds the month they lead to ("Previous month, August 2026").
- **The month is not a heading.** Atlassian's is one, with a level prop; a
  calendar can sit anywhere in a page's outline, so here it is a plain
  live region, and the grid is named with the same text.
- **Always a live region.** Atlassian turns `aria-live` on after the first
  press of a header button; here it is there from the start, which
  announces nothing until the month changes.
- **Semibold is 600**, as the kit's other headings; Atlassian's heading
  weight is 653.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Calendar where the day is picked by looking at the month: a booking
page, a delivery slot, a few weeks either side of today. Rule out the days
that cannot be picked with `min`, `max` and `isDateDisabled`, rather than
refusing the choice after it is made.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={CalendarStories.DoNearDate} />}
  doCaption="A date close to now, where seeing the week matters: unavailable days are struck through before anyone picks them."
  dont={<Story of={CalendarStories.DontFarDate} />}
  dontCaption="A date of birth is decades away: paging back a month, or even a year, at a time is slow. Type it in a Date Picker."
/>

Month steps keep the day where they can: 31 January plus a month is 28
February, not 3 March.

<Canvas of={CalendarStories.MonthEnds} />

## When not to use

- **For a date far from today**, or one people know by heart, like a date
  of birth. Use a [Date Picker](?path=/docs/components-inputs-datepicker--docs):
  it takes the date typed, and opens this calendar when wanted.
- **For a span inside a form.** Use a
  [Date Range Picker](?path=/docs/components-inputs-daterangepicker--docs):
  it owns the two clicks that make a span and shows it here.
- **For a schedule of events.** A day here holds a number, not content.
  List the events in a [Table](?path=/docs/components-data-display-table--docs).

## Accessibility

- A `role="grid"` named by the month and year ("September 2026"), with
  column headers that carry the full weekday name in `abbr`.
- Each day is a button named by its full date ("Friday 18 September
  2026"). The selected cell has `aria-selected`, and with `range` every
  cell from one end to the other does. Today has `aria-current="date"`.
- One tab stop: the selected day, or today when nothing is selected.
- Arrow keys move a day or a week, Home and End go to the week's ends,
  Page Up and Page Down move a month, and Shift+Page Up and Shift+Page
  Down a year. Enter or Space selects. Moving past the month shows the
  next one.
- Right to left, the arrows follow the screen (ArrowLeft is the next day)
  and the previous and next chevrons are mirrored.

  <Canvas of={CalendarStories.Keyboard} />

- The month and year are a polite live region, so paging is announced,
  by a month or by a year.
- The header's buttons are ordinary buttons in the tab order, before the
  grid: "Previous month", then after the month "Next month".
- Both are disabled at the limits: previous in the month of `min`, next
  in the month of `max`.
- Unavailable days stay focusable with `aria-disabled`, so they are found
  and announced as unavailable rather than skipped. Enter on one does
  nothing.
- Days of the months either side are not buttons and are hidden from
  assistive tech.
- Today's figure should measure at least 4.5:1 on its fill, in both modes,
  on its own and inside a range. The `Today` story measures it.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

import type { CSSProperties } from 'react'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Chart.module.css'

export interface ChartLegendItem {
  key: string
  label: string
  /** A CSS colour, usually from `colorVar`. */
  color: string
  /** Shown after the label, e.g. the series total "2.56K". */
  value?: string
}

export interface ChartLegendProps {
  items: ChartLegendItem[]
  /** Keys of series that are switched off. */
  hiddenKeys?: string[]
  /** Makes each item a toggle button. Without it the legend is a plain list. */
  onToggle?: (key: string) => void
  /** Called with the key under the pointer or focus, null when it leaves. Charts use it to fade the other series. */
  onFocusChange?: (key: string | null) => void
  /** `dot` for bars and slices, `line` for line and area series. */
  marker?: 'dot' | 'line'
  className?: string
}

/** Swatch, label and value per series, centred in a wrapping row. As toggles, it shows and hides series in the chart above it. */
export function ChartLegend({ items, hiddenKeys = [], onToggle, onFocusChange, marker = 'dot', className }: ChartLegendProps) {
  const visibleCount = items.length - hiddenKeys.length
  return (
    <ul
      className={cn(styles.legend, className)}
      aria-label="Legend"
      onPointerLeave={() => onFocusChange?.(null)}
    >
      {items.map((item) => {
        const isHidden = hiddenKeys.includes(item.key)
        const content = (
          <>
            <span className={cn(styles.swatch, marker === 'line' && styles.swatchLine)} style={{ '--swatch': item.color } as CSSProperties} aria-hidden="true" />
            <span className={styles.legendLabel}>{item.label}</span>
            {item.value !== undefined && <span className={styles.legendValue}>{item.value}</span>}
          </>
        )
        const focus = () => onFocusChange?.(isHidden ? null : item.key)
        const blur = () => onFocusChange?.(null)
        return (
          <li key={item.key} onPointerEnter={focus}>
            {onToggle ? (
              <button
                type="button"
                className={styles.legendItem}
                aria-pressed={!isHidden}
                // The last visible series cannot be hidden: an empty chart reads as "no data".
                aria-disabled={!isHidden && visibleCount === 1 ? true : undefined}
                onClick={() => (!isHidden && visibleCount === 1 ? undefined : onToggle(item.key))}
                onFocus={focus}
                onBlur={blur}
              >
                {content}
              </button>
            ) : (
              <span className={styles.legendItem}>{content}</span>
            )}
          </li>
        )
      })}
    </ul>
  )
}

'use client'

import { useCallback, useRef, type ReactNode, type Ref } from 'react'
import { Checkbox as BaseCheckbox } from '@base-ui/react/checkbox'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import { ChoiceField, choiceStyles, type ValidationState } from './ChoiceField'
import styles from './Checkbox.module.css'

export interface CheckboxProps {
  ref?: Ref<HTMLElement>
  checked?: boolean
  defaultChecked?: boolean
  /** The spec's `onChange`. Base UI's event details are dropped. */
  onCheckedChange?: (checked: boolean) => void
  /** Neither checked nor unchecked: a "select all" with some selected. */
  isIndeterminate?: boolean
  label?: ReactNode
  helperText?: ReactNode
  name?: string
  /** Submitted when checked; "on" by default. */
  value?: string
  /** Colour of the checked box. */
  variant?: 'primary' | 'neutral'
  disabled?: boolean
  required?: boolean
  readOnly?: boolean
  autoFocus?: boolean
  validationState?: ValidationState
  id?: string
  className?: string
  'aria-label'?: string
}

export function Checkbox({
  ref,
  autoFocus,
  label,
  helperText,
  name,
  variant = 'neutral',
  isIndeterminate,
  disabled,
  required,
  validationState,
  className,
  onCheckedChange,
  ...props
}: CheckboxProps) {
  // The root is a focusable <span>, and React only honours autoFocus on form
  // elements, so it is done by hand — once, on mount, not on every render.
  const focused = useRef(false)
  const setRef = useCallback(
    (node: HTMLElement | null) => {
      if (node && autoFocus && !focused.current) {
        focused.current = true
        node.focus()
      }
      if (typeof ref === 'function') ref(node)
      else if (ref) ref.current = node
    },
    [autoFocus, ref],
  )
  return (
    <ChoiceField
      label={label}
      helperText={helperText}
      validationState={validationState}
      required={required}
      disabled={disabled}
      name={name}
      className={cn(styles.field, className)}
    >
      <BaseCheckbox.Root
        {...props}
        ref={setRef}
        indeterminate={isIndeterminate}
        required={required}
        onCheckedChange={onCheckedChange && ((next) => onCheckedChange(next))}
        className={cn(choiceStyles.control, styles.box, styles[variant])}
      >
        <BaseCheckbox.Indicator
          className={styles.indicator}
          render={(indicatorProps, state) => (
            <span {...indicatorProps}>
              <Icon name={state.indeterminate ? 'minus' : 'check'} />
            </span>
          )}
        />
      </BaseCheckbox.Root>
    </ChoiceField>
  )
}

# Checkbox Selects an option, or several from a list, to apply when a form is submitted. #...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import { Checkbox } from './Checkbox'
import * as CheckboxStories from './Checkbox.stories'

<Meta of={CheckboxStories} />

# Checkbox

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

Selects an option, or several from a list, to apply when a form is
submitted.

<Status of={CheckboxStories} />

<Canvas of={CheckboxStories.Default} />

## Variants

`variant` is the colour of the checked box. Each row: unchecked, checked,
indeterminate.

<Canvas of={CheckboxStories.Variants} />

| Variant | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| <Checkbox defaultChecked label="Neutral" /> | The default: lists, forms, tables. The checked box is the foreground colour, so a column of them stays calm. |
| <Checkbox variant="primary" defaultChecked label="Primary" /> | One checkbox that carries the brand: an opt-in, a terms box beside a primary button. |

**Indeterminate** is for a parent whose children are partly selected. It
is a display state: clicking the parent chooses all or none, never
"mixed".

<Canvas of={CheckboxStories.SelectAll} />

<Canvas of={CheckboxStories.Validation} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Checkbox } from 'zweihander/checkbox'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/checkbox.json
```

- Source: [src/components/controls/Checkbox.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/controls/Checkbox.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/checkbox](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/checkbox)
- Behaviour: [Base UI Checkbox](https://base-ui.com/react/components/checkbox) and [Field](https://base-ui.com/react/components/field)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={CheckboxStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={CheckboxStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The label wraps the box, so the whole label is part of the click target.

## Measurements

One size. The box is 16px, Atlassian's, inside a 24px hit area, and
sits centred on the first line of its label, however many lines the
label wraps to. The label starts 8px from the box: Atlassian's 4px gap
after the 24px area.

<SpecTable
  caption="Every checkbox"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Size', token: '--choice-box' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-xs' },
    { part: 'Check mark', property: 'Size', token: '--icon-xs' },
    { part: 'Label', property: 'Gap from the box', token: '--space-inline' },
    { part: 'Label', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body' },
    { part: 'Label', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body' },
    { part: 'Helper text', property: 'Gap from the label', token: '--space-1' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Width', token: '--focus-width' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Offset', token: '--focus-offset' },
    { part: 'Hit area', property: 'Minimum', token: '--box-sm' },
    { part: 'Hit area', property: 'Minimum on touch screens', token: '--target-coarse' },
  ]}
/>

The box's corner is the radius step, not the control tier's radius: a box
that turned round under `radius="full-rounded"` would read as a radio.
The label is regular weight, as Atlassian's checkbox label is; the form
label weight is for a field's or a group's label, not an option's.

## Color

  caption="Unchecked, every variant"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Background', token: '--color-surface' },

/>

/>

    { part: 'Helper text, error', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-danger' },
    { part: 'Helper text, success', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-success' },
    { part: 'Required asterisk', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-danger' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-border-focused' },
  ]}
/>

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Unchecked' },
    { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
    { label: 'Checked', content: <Checkbox defaultChecked label="Remember me" /> },
    { label: 'Indeterminate', content: <Story of={CheckboxStories.Indeterminate} /> },
    { label: 'Disabled', content: <Checkbox disabled defaultChecked label="Remember me" /> },
    { label: 'Error', content: <Checkbox validationState="error" label="Remember me" /> },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={CheckboxStories.Default} />
</States>

- **Hover** anywhere on the label darkens an unchecked outline to
  `--color-text`. A checked box mixes 12% of the mark's colour into its
  fill, as Button does. An error outline stays red.
- **Focus** is a 2px `--color-border-focused` outline, 2px outside the box.
- **Disabled** dims the box and the label to 50%.
- **Read-only** looks enabled but has no hover and an arrow cursor.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={CheckboxStories} />
</div>

`id`, `className`, `aria-label` and `ref` pass through to the box.

### Differences from the spec

- **Atlassian's box.** 16px with a 2px corner inside a 24px hit area, and
  a 12px mark: the kit's own step, since Atlassian draws the mark as part
  of the box.
- **Base UI's and HTML's names:** `defaultChecked` and `onCheckedChange`
  for the spec's `defaultValue` (a string there, which reads as the
  submitted value: that is `value`) and `onChange`; native `disabled`,
  `required`, `readOnly` for the `is…` forms.
- **`isIndeterminate` keeps its prefix.** Indeterminate is a DOM property,
  not an HTML attribute, so by the kit's naming rule it takes `is`; Base UI
  calls it `indeterminate`.
- **`autoFocus` is applied on mount by the component.** The box is a
  focusable `<span>`, which React's own `autoFocus` ignores.
- **No `secondary`.** A light fill barely reads as checked, so only
  `neutral` (the foreground colour) and `primary` ship.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a checkbox for a choice that is submitted with a form: accepting
terms, opting in, picking several items from a list. Nothing happens
until the form is sent.

Write the label so that checked means yes.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={CheckboxStories.DoPositiveLabel} />}
  doCaption="The label says what checking does: checked means yes."
  dont={<Story of={CheckboxStories.DontNegativeLabel} />}
  dontCaption="A negative label makes unchecked a double negative, and readers stop to work it out."
/>

## When not to use

- **For a setting that applies at once.** Use a
  [Switch](?path=/docs/components-controls-switch--docs): it acts like a
  light switch, a checkbox waits for Submit.
- **For one choice out of several.** Use a
  [Radio](?path=/docs/components-controls-radio--docs) group; checkboxes
  are independent.
- **For a toggle in a toolbar.** Use a
  [Toggle Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-togglebutton--docs).

## Accessibility

- `role="checkbox"` with `aria-checked`, `mixed` when indeterminate.
  Space toggles it.
- The label wraps the box, so it names it and clicking it toggles the box.
  Without a visible label, pass `aria-label`: it goes to the box itself.
- `helperText` is the box's description; the error state sets
  `aria-invalid`.
- The unchecked outline is `--color-border-bold`, 3:1 on the page on every
  gray ramp.
- A hidden native input carries `name`, `value` and `required` into form
  submission and validation.
- The hit area is 24×24px, 44×44px on coarse pointers, without the box
  growing.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

  disabled = false,
  hiddenUntilFound = true,
  className,
}: CollapseProps) {
  return (
    <Collapsible.Root
      open={open}
      defaultOpen={defaultOpen}
      onOpenChange={onOpenChange && ((next) => onOpenChange(next))}
      disabled={disabled}
      className={cn(styles.collapse, styles[size], className)}
    >
      <Collapsible.Trigger className={styles.trigger}>
        <span className={styles.chevron} aria-hidden="true">
          <Icon name="chevron-right" />
        </span>
        {openLabel === undefined ? (
          label
        ) : (
          <>
            <span className={styles.closedLabel}>{label}</span>
            <span className={styles.openLabel}>{openLabel}</span>
          </>
        )}
      </Collapsible.Trigger>
      <Collapsible.Panel className={styles.panel} hiddenUntilFound={hiddenUntilFound}>
        <div className={styles.content}>{children}</div>
      </Collapsible.Panel>
    </Collapsible.Root>
  )
}

# Collapse One show/hide section, such as "Show details" or "Advanced settings": a text bu...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import * as CollapseStories from './Collapse.stories'

<Meta of={CollapseStories} />

# Collapse

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

One show/hide section, such as "Show details" or "Advanced settings": a
text button with a chevron, and the content it reveals under it.

<Status of={CollapseStories} />

<Canvas of={CollapseStories.Open} />

## Variants

Collapse has one look. `size` matches it to the text around it, and
`openLabel` decides whether the label changes when it opens.

| Size | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `md` | Body text, 14px. The default. |
| `sm` | Small text, 12px: captions, dense panels, notes under a field. |

<Canvas of={CollapseStories.Default} />

<Canvas of={CollapseStories.Small} />

| Label | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| With `openLabel` | A label that names the action: "Show details" becomes "Hide details". |
| Without `openLabel` | A label that names the section: "Advanced settings" stays the same, and the chevron shows the state. |

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Collapse } from 'zweihander/collapse'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/collapse.json
```

- Spec: the kit's own. uiguideline.com has no page for it.
- Behaviour: [Base UI Collapsible](https://base-ui.com/react/components/collapsible)
- Figma: not in the library yet

## Measurements

The trigger has no padding: it is as tall as a line of its text, 20px at
`md` and 16px at `sm`.

## Color

The trigger has no fill and no border in any state.

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
    { label: 'Pressed', pseudo: 'active' },
    { label: 'Open', content: <Story of={CollapseStories.Open} /> },
    { label: 'Disabled', content: <Story of={CollapseStories.Disabled} /> },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={CollapseStories.Default} />
</States>

- **Hover** underlines the label, like a link.
- **Focus** is a 2px `--color-border-focused` outline, 2px outside the trigger.
- **Pressed** has no look of its own: the label stays underlined while the
  pointer is down.
- **Open** turns the chevron from right to down, shows `openLabel` if
  there is one, and animates the panel's height over `--duration-base`.
- **Disabled** dims the trigger to 50% opacity, with no underline on hover.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={CollapseStories} />
</div>

The props are the kit's own, since there is no spec to follow. Closed
content is kept as `hidden="until-found"` by default: the browser's
find-in-page still matches it and opens the section.

<Canvas of={CollapseStories.Searchable} />

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Collapse for one aside in running content: billing details under a
plan, advanced settings under a form. It is a text button, not a bar,
because it belongs to the content around it, and its trigger reads like a
link in a sentence.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={CollapseStories.DoAsideInText} />}
  doCaption="One aside, under the text it belongs to. The label says what opening it does."
  dont={<Story of={CollapseStories.DontStackAsList} />}
  dontCaption="Bare Collapses stacked with nothing around them read as a menu, not as asides. Give each section a heading, and a Collapse under it only for what can wait."
/>

## When not to use

- **As the structure of a page.** A list of sections needs real
  headings. Give each one a heading, in a
  [Card](?path=/docs/components-data-display-card--docs) section where it
  needs a frame, and put a Collapse under a heading only for the part
  that can wait.
- **For a short hint about a control.** Use a
  [Tooltip](?path=/docs/components-overlays-tooltip--docs) or a
  [Popover](?path=/docs/components-overlays-popover--docs), which do not
  push the page down.
- **For content most readers need.** Hiding it costs everyone a click.
  Show it.

## Accessibility

- The trigger is a `<button>` with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`
  pointing at the panel.
- Enter or Space toggles it. With `openLabel`, the button's name changes
  with its state ("Show details" / "Hide details"), and `aria-expanded`
  says it either way. Without it, the name stays the same.
- The chevron is decorative (`aria-hidden`), so it adds nothing to the
  name.
- Closed content is `hidden="until-found"` by default, so find-in-page
  reaches it.
- The trigger grows to a 44px target on coarse pointers.
- Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the panel and chevron change without
  animating.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

import { Field } from '@base-ui/react/field'
import { Popover } from '@base-ui/react/popover'
import { Slider } from '@base-ui/react/slider'

import { Select } from '../inputs/Select'
import {
  InputField,
  boxClass,
  focusControl,
  inputStyles,
  type InputSize,
  type ValidationState,
