    { part: 'Preset', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-control' },

Presets are 2px apart and at least 7rem wide in the column. The field is
20rem wide unless `isFullWidth`; a range is longer than one date, so give
it room or `isFullWidth`.

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Empty', content: <DateRangePicker label="Period" locale="en-GB" /> },
    { label: 'Filled' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus' },
    {
      label: 'Error',
      content: <DateRangePicker label="Period" locale="en-GB" validationState="error" helperText="Choose both ends." />,
    },
    {
      label: 'Read-only',
      content: <DateRangePicker label="Period" locale="en-GB" defaultValue={{ start: new Date(2026, 8, 7), end: new Date(2026, 8, 13) }} readOnly />,
    },
    {
      label: 'Disabled',
      content: <DateRangePicker label="Period" locale="en-GB" defaultValue={{ start: new Date(2026, 8, 7), end: new Date(2026, 8, 13) }} disabled />,
    },
  ]}
>
  <DateRangePicker label="Period" locale="en-GB" defaultValue={{ start: new Date(2026, 8, 7), end: new Date(2026, 8, 13) }} />
</States>

The field's states are Date Picker's: a `--color-border-focused` outline while the input
has focus, `--color-text-danger` in error (also while the typed text is not a
range), `--color-background-input` and no calendar button when read-only, 50%
opacity when disabled. A preset matching the picked range
stays in its pressed look.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={DateRangePickerStories} />
</div>

### Design notes

- **Either way round.** The first click starts the range, the second
  ends it; a second click before the first swaps them. So does typing
  the later date first.
- **Presets are whole periods.** "This month" is the 1st to the last
  day, not the 1st to today, so a preset reads the same all month.
- **No Cancel or Apply.** A range applies, and the popover closes, once
  both ends are in; Escape before the second click leaves the value as
  it was.
- **No hover preview.** The band shows once both ends are in; add a
  preview if testing shows people lose track of the first click.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Date Range Picker when the two dates are one thing: a period to
report on, a stay, a sprint. Both ends are set together, start never after
end, and the value is complete or `null`.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={DateRangePickerStories.DoOneField} />}
  doCaption="One field for one period: it cannot be half filled or set back to front."
  dont={<Story of={DateRangePickerStories.DontTwoFields} />}
  dontCaption="Two Date Pickers for one period: here the end is before the start, and nothing stops it."
/>

## When not to use

- **For one date.** Use a
  [Date Picker](?path=/docs/components-inputs-datepicker--docs).
- **When one end is optional**, such as a contract with no end date. The
  range needs both ends; use two Date Pickers and check their order
  yourself.

## Accessibility

- As Date Picker: a labelled text box, an error state with the expected
  pattern, and the calendars in a dialog named "Choose dates". Without a
  visible label, pass `aria-label` to name the input.
- The calendar button is named "Choose dates", with the current range
  when there is one.
- `readOnly` works as on Date Picker: `readonly` on the input, no
  calendar button, and a click or Alt+Down opens nothing.
- Every day in the range has `aria-selected`, so the span is announced,
  not only its ends.
- A day of the month either side is decoration: hidden from assistive
  tech and not pickable, so each day is one button.
- Presets are toggle buttons in a group named "Presets"; the one that
  matches the picked range is `aria-pressed`.
- After both ends are in, the field goes back to rest, as Date Picker's
  does after a pick.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A thin line that separates content into groups: sections of a card, items
in a toolbar, blocks of a page.

<Status of={DividerStories} />

<Canvas of={DividerStories.Default} />

## Variants

| Appearance | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `solid` | Almost everywhere: the quiet default. |
| `dashed` | A boundary that is softer or provisional: a drop zone, a "more below" break, a draft section. |

<Canvas of={DividerStories.Dashed} />

A **vertical** divider separates items in a row: toolbar groups, links in
a footer. It has no fixed height and stretches to its flex row.

<Canvas of={DividerStories.Vertical} />

**Inset** stops the line short of the container's edges, so it aligns with
the text in a padded list rather than running edge to edge.

<Canvas of={DividerStories.Inset} />

<Canvas of={DividerStories.Sizes} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Divider } from 'zweihander/divider'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/divider.json
```

- Source: [src/components/atomic-elements/Divider.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/atomic-elements/Divider.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/divider](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/divider)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={DividerStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={DividerStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

One part. The line is a border, top for horizontal and start for
vertical, and the box shrinks to it: a vertical divider is exactly as
wide as its line.

## Measurements

Thickness is whole pixels, not a token: `--border-width` covers 1px and
`--border-width-selected` 2px, and a divider's three weights stay its own.

| Size | Thickness |
| --- | --- |
| `sm` | 1px |
| `md` | 2px |
| `lg` | 4px |

<SpecTable
  caption="inset, every size"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Horizontal line', property: 'Inline margin', token: '--space-4' },
    { part: 'Vertical line', property: 'Block margin', token: '--space-2' },
  ]}
/>

## Color

Every size and appearance uses the same colour.

<SpecTable caption="Every appearance" rows={[{ part: 'Line', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-border' }]} />

## States

A divider is not interactive: no hover, focus or pressed. It looks the same
whether it is announced or decorative; only a screen reader tells them
apart.

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Solid', content: <Stack><Divider /></Stack> },
    { label: 'Dashed', content: <Stack><Divider appearance="dashed" size="md" /></Stack> },
    { label: 'Inset', content: <Stack><Divider inset /></Stack> },
    { label: 'Decorative', content: <Stack><Divider aria-hidden /></Stack> },
  ]}
/>

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={DividerStories} />
</div>

Every other `<hr>` attribute passes through, including `ref` and
`aria-hidden`.

### Differences from the spec

- **`appearance`, not `variant`.** In this kit `variant` always means a
  colour by intent (primary, destructive…) and `appearance` means a style.
  Solid versus dashed is a style.
- **Thickness is raw px.** `--border-width` and `--border-width-selected`
  cover 1px and 2px strokes; a divider is the only component that needs a
  third, so its three weights stay its own.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Divider between groups that spacing alone does not separate: the
sections of a menu, the blocks of a settings page, groups in a toolbar.
Divide groups, not every item: a line after each row turns a list into
stripes and makes the real breaks harder to see.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={DividerStories.DoDivideGroups} />}
  doCaption="One line between two groups: the break carries meaning."
  dont={<Story of={DividerStories.DontDivideEveryItem} />}
  dontCaption="A line after every item: nothing stands out as a group."
/>

## When not to use

- **Where space already separates.** Cards, list items with padding and
  headed sections are grouped by their own whitespace; a line adds noise.
- **As the only thing that tells groups apart.** The line is faint on
  purpose (see Accessibility). Pair it with a heading or space.
- **For a border of a component.** Draw that with the component's own
  border, not a Divider beside it.

## Accessibility

- `<hr>` is announced as a separator. Vertical dividers add
  `aria-orientation="vertical"`; horizontal ones don't, because that is
  already the default.
- If the line is purely decorative, e.g. between two icons that are
  already grouped, pass `aria-hidden` so it isn't announced at all.
- The `--color-border` colour is below 3:1 against the background on purpose: a
  divider is decoration and is not required to meet the non-text contrast
  ratio. Never let a divider be the only thing that tells groups apart.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

# Empty State What a list, a table or a page shows when there is nothing in it yet: why it...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import * as EmptyStateStories from './EmptyState.stories'

<Meta of={EmptyStateStories} />

# Empty State

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

What a list, a table or a page shows when there is nothing in it yet: why
it is empty, and what to do about it.

<Status of={EmptyStateStories} />

<Canvas of={EmptyStateStories.FirstUse} />

## Variants

There are three kinds of empty, and they need three kinds of copy. The
component is the same; the words and the action are not.

| Kind | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| First use | Nothing has been made yet. Say what will live here, and offer the way in: "No projects yet", New project. |
| No results | A search or a filter matched nothing. Say what was searched, and offer to clear it: "No projects match", Clear search. |
| Cleared out | Everything is done. Often no action at all: "All caught up". |

<Canvas of={EmptyStateStories.Default} />

<Canvas of={EmptyStateStories.TitleOnly} />

`size="sm"` fits a panel or a table body; `md` fills a page or a section.

<Canvas of={EmptyStateStories.Small} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { EmptyState } from 'zweihander/empty-state'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/empty-state.json
```

- Source: [src/components/states/EmptyState.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/states/EmptyState.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/empty-state](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/empty-state)
- Behaviour: a plain element, no Base UI part
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={EmptyStateStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={EmptyStateStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

Only the title is required. [Error State](?path=/docs/components-states-errorstate--docs)
and [Success State](?path=/docs/components-states-successstate--docs) are
this layout with the disc in their own tone.

## Measurements

The icon is half the disc's size. Title and description are at most
464px wide at `md` and 304px at `sm` (29rem and 19rem, Atlassian's wide
and narrow empty state), so they stay a short paragraph on a wide page.
`md` keeps Atlassian's rhythm: 48px above and below, 24px under the
image, 16px under the heading, 24px above the buttons, 8px between them.
`sm` keeps the 16px and 24px and is 16px under a smaller image.

## States

Empty State itself is static: it has no hover, focus or pressed look. Its
action does, and those are the action's own (here, an outlined Button).

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Action hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Action focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
    { label: 'Action pressed', pseudo: 'active' },
  ]}
>

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={EmptyStateStories} />
</div>

Every other `<div>` attribute passes through, including `ref`.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use an Empty State wherever a list, a table or a page can have nothing in
it: before the first item is made, after a search matches nothing, when
everything is done. Write the title for the reader's situation, and give
them the next step.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={EmptyStateStories.FirstUse} />}
  doCaption="Say what is empty and what will live here, and offer the way in."
  dont={<Story of={EmptyStateStories.DontNoData} />}
  dontCaption="“No data” says neither why nor what to do next."
/>

## When not to use

- **When loading failed.** Use an
  [Error State](?path=/docs/components-states-errorstate--docs): "No
  projects" when the request failed tells the reader their work is gone.
- **When a flow has finished.** Use a
  [Success State](?path=/docs/components-states-successstate--docs).
- **While content is loading.** Use a Skeleton or a Spinner: an empty
  state shown before the data arrives flashes the wrong message.

## Accessibility

- The title is a real heading, so a screen reader user jumping by
  headings finds out the area is empty. Set `headingLevel` to fit the
  outline: `3` inside a section headed by an `h2`.
- The icon is `aria-hidden`; the title has to say it all.
- It is not a live region, so it is not announced when it replaces
  results. If a search updates as you type, announce the count elsewhere,
  in a `role="status"` line such as "0 results".

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

import type { ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import { EmptyState, type EmptyStateProps } from './EmptyState'
import styles from './ErrorState.module.css'

export interface ErrorStateProps extends Omit<EmptyStateProps, 'title'> {
  /** What failed, in the reader's words. */
  title?: ReactNode
  /** A reference for support, e.g. an error code or request id. Shown small, selectable. */
  details?: ReactNode
  /** Announce it when it replaces content that was loading (`role="alert"`). */
  isLive?: boolean
}

/**
 * What a list, panel or page shows when loading it failed: why, and a way
 * forward, usually a retry. Empty State's layout in the danger tone.
 */
export function ErrorState({
  title = 'Something went wrong',
  icon = <Icon name="danger" />,
  description,
  details,
  isLive = false,
  className,
  ...props
}: ErrorStateProps) {
  return (
    <EmptyState
      role={isLive ? 'alert' : undefined}
      title={title}
      icon={icon}
      description={
        (description || details) && (
          <>
            {description}
            {details && <span className={styles.details}>{details}</span>}
          </>
        )
      }
      className={cn(styles.error, className)}
      {...props}
    />
  )
}

What a list, a panel or a page shows when loading it failed: what went
wrong, and a way forward, usually "Try again".

<Canvas of={ErrorStateStories.Default} />

## Variants

| Variant | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| With details | A failure support may need to trace: an error code or request id under the description, selected in one click. |
| Default title | The last resort, for a failure you cannot describe: "Something went wrong". |
| `sm` | A panel, a card or a table body that failed on its own while the rest of the page loaded. |

## States

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use an Error State in place of content that failed to load: a list, a
panel, a whole page. Say what failed in the reader's words, say that
nothing is lost when that is true, and offer a way forward.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={ErrorStateStories.Default} />}
  doCaption="Say what failed, that nothing is lost, and offer to try again."
  dont={<Story of={ErrorStateStories.DontRawError} />}
  dontCaption="A raw error is for developers, and with no action the reader is stuck."
/>

Details are for support, not for the reader: keep them small and
selectable so they can be pasted into a message.

## When not to use

- **When there is simply nothing there.** Use an
  [Empty State](?path=/docs/components-states-emptystate--docs).
- **When an action failed but the screen is fine**, such as a save. Use an
  Alert or a Toast and keep the reader's work on screen.
- **For a field's error.** Show it on the field, through its own error
  message.

## Accessibility

- The title is a real heading, as on Empty State. Set `headingLevel` to
  fit the outline.
- The icon is `aria-hidden`; the title says what failed.
- `isLive` makes it a `role="alert"`: use it when the error replaces
  content that was loading, so a screen reader hears that it failed.
  Without it, nothing is announced.

'use client'

import { useEffect, useId, useRef, useState, type DragEvent, type ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import { Button } from '../buttons/Button'
import { Spinner } from '../loaders/Spinner'
import styles from './FileUploader.module.css'

export interface FileRejection {
  file: File
  reason: 'type' | 'size' | 'count'
  /** Ready to show, e.g. "photo.gif is not an accepted type." */
  message: string
}

export interface FileStatus {
  /** 0–100 while uploading: a ring beside the remove button, hidden at 100. */
  progress?: number
  /** Short, beside the remove button in the danger colour, e.g. "Upload failed". */
  error?: string
}

export interface FileUploaderProps {
  files?: File[]
  defaultFiles?: File[]
  /** The list after an add or a remove. Rejected files are never in it. */
  onFilesChange?: (files: File[]) => void
  /** Files that were dropped or chosen but did not pass `accept`, `maxSize` or `maxFiles`. */
  onReject?: (rejections: FileRejection[]) => void
  /** As the native attribute: extensions and MIME types, e.g. `".pdf,image/*"`. Also checked on drop. */
  accept?: string
  multiple?: boolean
  /** In bytes. */
  maxSize?: number
  maxFiles?: number
  label?: ReactNode
  /** Inside the drop zone, under the button, e.g. "PNG or JPG, up to 5 MB." */
  helperText?: ReactNode
  /** Upload progress or a server error per file. The uploader does not upload: you do. */
  getFileStatus?: (file: File) => FileStatus | undefined
  /** Submitted with the form, as a native file input. */
  name?: string
  disabled?: boolean
  required?: boolean
  isFullWidth?: boolean
  className?: string
}

const sizeFormat = (bytes: number) => {
  const [value, unit] =
    bytes >= 1e6 ? [bytes / 1e6, 'megabyte'] : bytes >= 1e3 ? [bytes / 1e3, 'kilobyte'] : [bytes, 'byte']
  return new Intl.NumberFormat(undefined, { style: 'unit', unit, unitDisplay: 'short', maximumFractionDigits: 1 }).format(value)
}

/** Does the file match the `accept` list? Extensions, exact MIME types and `type/*`. */
function accepts(file: File, accept?: string) {
  if (!accept) return true
  const name = file.name.toLowerCase()
  const type = file.type.toLowerCase()
  return accept
    .split(',')
    .map((t) => t.trim().toLowerCase())
    .filter(Boolean)
    .some((t) => (t.startsWith('.') ? name.endsWith(t) : t.endsWith('/*') ? type.startsWith(t.slice(0, -1)) : type === t))
}

function syncInput(input: HTMLInputElement | null, files: File[]) {
  if (!input || typeof DataTransfer === 'undefined') return
  const transfer = new DataTransfer()
  files.forEach((f) => transfer.items.add(f))
  input.files = transfer.files
}

type FileKind = 'word' | 'excel' | 'powerpoint' | 'pdf' | 'image' | 'audio'

function fileKind(file: File): FileKind | undefined {
  const ext = file.name.split('.').pop()?.toLowerCase() ?? ''
  const type = file.type.toLowerCase()
  if (ext === 'pdf' || type === 'application/pdf') return 'pdf'
  if (['doc', 'docx', 'odt', 'rtf'].includes(ext)) return 'word'
  if (['xls', 'xlsx', 'csv', 'ods'].includes(ext)) return 'excel'
  if (['ppt', 'pptx', 'odp'].includes(ext)) return 'powerpoint'
  if (type.startsWith('image/')) return 'image'
  if (type.startsWith('audio/') || ['mp3', 'wav', 'm4a', 'ogg', 'flac'].includes(ext)) return 'audio'
}

const badgeText: Record<FileKind, string> = {
  word: 'DOC',
  excel: 'XLS',
  powerpoint: 'PPT',
  pdf: 'PDF',
  image: 'IMG',
  audio: 'MP3',
}

/**
 * A page with a coloured type badge, after Microsoft 365's file icons, on
 * the Figma library's 20px grid. Unknown types get the bare page. DOC and
 * MP3 are wider letters, so their badge is 16px, the rest 14px.
 */
function FileTypeIcon({ file }: { file: File }) {
  const kind = fileKind(file)
  const badgeWidth = kind === 'word' || kind === 'audio' ? 16 : 14
  return (
    <svg className={styles.fileIcon} data-kind={kind} viewBox="0 0 20 20" aria-hidden="true">
      <path className={styles.page} d="M4 1h8l5 5v13H4Z" />
      <path className={styles.fold} d="M12 1l5 5h-5Z" />
      {kind && (
        <g>
          <rect className={styles.badge} x="1" y="10" width={badgeWidth} height="8" rx="1.5" />
          <text className={styles.badgeText} x={1 + badgeWidth / 2} y="14" textAnchor="middle" dominantBaseline="central">
            {badgeText[kind]}
          </text>
        </g>
      )}
    </svg>
  )
}

const sameFile = (a: File, b: File) => a.name === b.name && a.size === b.size && a.lastModified === b.lastModified

export function FileUploader({
  files: filesProp,
  defaultFiles = [],
  onFilesChange,
  onReject,
  accept,
  multiple = false,
  maxSize,
  maxFiles,
  label,
  helperText,
  getFileStatus,
  name,
  disabled = false,
  required,
  isFullWidth,
  className,
}: FileUploaderProps) {
  const id = useId()
  const inputRef = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null)
  const chooseRef = useRef<HTMLElement>(null)
  const listRef = useRef<HTMLUListElement>(null)
  const [filesState, setFilesState] = useState(defaultFiles)
  const files = filesProp ?? filesState
  const [rejections, setRejections] = useState<FileRejection[]>([])
  const [dragging, setDragging] = useState(false)
  const [announcement, setAnnouncement] = useState('')
  const limit = multiple ? (maxFiles ?? Infinity) : 1

  const [missing, setMissing] = useState(false)

  // The native input carries the list, so a plain form post sends it. Also
  // after a controlled `files` changes from outside, e.g. cleared after upload.
  useEffect(() => syncInput(inputRef.current, files), [files])

  const update = (next: File[]) => {
    setFilesState(next)
    syncInput(inputRef.current, next)
    onFilesChange?.(next)
  }

  const add = (incoming: File[]) => {
    const rejected: FileRejection[] = []
    const accepted: File[] = []
    for (const file of incoming) {
      if (!accepts(file, accept)) rejected.push({ file, reason: 'type', message: `${file.name} is not an accepted type.` })
      else if (maxSize !== undefined && file.size > maxSize)
        rejected.push({ file, reason: 'size', message: `${file.name} is larger than ${sizeFormat(maxSize)}.` })
      else accepted.push(file)
    }
    // A single-file uploader replaces its file, but only with one that passed:
    // a rejected drop leaves the chosen file where it is. A multiple one appends.
    let next = multiple ? [...files] : []
    for (const file of accepted) {
      if (next.some((f) => sameFile(f, file))) continue
      if (next.length >= limit)
        rejected.push({
          file,
          reason: 'count',
          message: multiple ? `${file.name} was not added: the limit is ${limit} files.` : `${file.name} was not added: only one file can be added.`,
        })
      else next.push(file)
    }
    if (!multiple && next.length === 0) next = files
    const added = next.filter((f) => !files.some((g) => sameFile(f, g))).length
    setRejections(rejected)
    if (rejected.length) onReject?.(rejected)
    if (next.length) setMissing(false)
    if (added || next.length !== files.length) update(next)
    else syncInput(inputRef.current, files)
    setAnnouncement(
      [added ? `${added} ${added === 1 ? 'file' : 'files'} added.` : '', rejected.length ? `${rejected.length} not added.` : '']
        .filter(Boolean)
        .join(' '),
    )
  }

  const remove = (index: number) => {
    const removed = files[index]
    const next = files.filter((_, i) => i !== index)
    update(next)
    setAnnouncement(`${removed.name} removed.`)
    // Focus goes to the next remove button, else the previous, else Choose.
    requestAnimationFrame(() => {
      const buttons = listRef.current?.querySelectorAll<HTMLButtonElement>('button[data-remove]')
      const target = buttons?.[Math.min(index, buttons.length - 1)] ?? chooseRef.current
      target?.focus()
    })
  }

  const onDrop = (e: DragEvent) => {
    e.preventDefault()
    setDragging(false)
    if (!disabled) add([...e.dataTransfer.files])
  }

  const helperId = `${id}-helper`
  const errorId = `${id}-errors`

  return (
    // A group named by the label: the control inside is a button with its own
    // name ("Choose files"), so a <label> would have nothing to label.
    <div
      role="group"
      aria-labelledby={label ? `${id}-label` : undefined}
      className={cn(styles.uploader, isFullWidth && styles.fullWidth, disabled && styles.disabled, className)}
    >
      {label && (
        <div id={`${id}-label`} className={styles.label}>
          {label}
          {required && (
            <>
              <span className={styles.required} aria-hidden="true">
                *
              </span>
              {/* A group cannot be aria-required; the name says it instead. */}
              <span className={styles.srOnly}> (required)</span>
            </>
          )}
        </div>
      )}
      <div
        className={cn(styles.dropzone, dragging && styles.dragging, (rejections.length > 0 || missing) && styles.invalid)}
        data-disabled={disabled || undefined}
        onDragEnter={(e) => {
          e.preventDefault()
          if (!disabled) setDragging(true)
        }}
        onDragOver={(e) => {
          e.preventDefault()
          e.dataTransfer.dropEffect = disabled ? 'none' : 'copy'
        }}
        onDragLeave={(e) => {
          if (!e.currentTarget.contains(e.relatedTarget as Node)) setDragging(false)
        }}
        onDrop={onDrop}
      >
        <span className={styles.icon} aria-hidden="true">
          <Icon name="upload" />
        </span>
        <p className={styles.prompt}>
          {/* Dragging is a shortcut; the button is the way in for everyone. */}
          Drag {multiple ? 'files' : 'a file'} here or
        </p>
        <Button
          ref={chooseRef}
          variant="accent"
          size="sm"
          disabled={disabled}
          aria-describedby={[helperText ? helperId : '', rejections.length || missing ? errorId : ''].filter(Boolean).join(' ') || undefined}
          onClick={() => inputRef.current?.click()}
        >
          {multiple ? 'Choose files' : 'Choose a file'}
        </Button>
        {helperText && (
          <p id={helperId} className={styles.helper}>
            {helperText}
          </p>
        )}
        <input
          ref={inputRef}
          type="file"
          className={styles.srOnly}
          tabIndex={-1}
          name={name}
          accept={accept}
          multiple={multiple}
          disabled={disabled}
          required={required && files.length === 0}
          aria-hidden="true"
          onChange={(e) => add([...(e.target.files ?? [])])}
          // The browser would focus this hidden input and pin its bubble to
          // it. Show the message ourselves and send focus to Choose instead.
          onInvalid={(e) => {
            e.preventDefault()
            setMissing(true)
            chooseRef.current?.focus()
          }}
        />
      </div>
      {(rejections.length > 0 || missing) && (
        <ul id={errorId} className={styles.errors}>
          {missing && <li>{multiple ? 'Choose at least one file.' : 'Choose a file.'}</li>}
          {rejections.map((r, i) => (
            <li key={i}>{r.message}</li>
          ))}
        </ul>
      )}
      {files.length > 0 && (
        <ul ref={listRef} className={styles.list} aria-label={multiple ? 'Chosen files' : 'Chosen file'}>
          {files.map((file, i) => {
            const status = getFileStatus?.(file)
            const uploading = status?.progress !== undefined && status.progress < 100 && !status.error
            return (
              <li key={`${file.name}-${file.size}-${file.lastModified}`} className={styles.item}>
                <FileTypeIcon file={file} />
                {/* The name truncates; the size always shows in full. */}
                <span className={styles.nameRow}>
                  <span className={styles.name}>{file.name}</span>
                  <span className={styles.size}>{sizeFormat(file.size)}</span>
                </span>
                {uploading && (
                  <Spinner value={status?.progress} variant="primary" size="sm" aria-label={`Uploading ${file.name}`} />
                )}
                {status?.error && (
                  <span className={styles.fileError} title={status.error}>
                    {status.error}
                  </span>
                )}
                <Button
                  isIconOnly
                  data-remove=""
                  className={styles.remove}
                  aria-label={`Remove ${file.name}`}
                  variant="secondary"
                  appearance="ghost"
                  size="sm"
                  disabled={disabled}
                  onClick={() => remove(i)}
                >
                  <Icon name="close" />
                </Button>
              </li>
            )
          })}
        </ul>
      )}
      <p role="status" className={styles.srOnly}>
        {announcement}
      </p>
    </div>
  )
}

# File Uploader

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

Choose files to send: drag them onto the drop zone or pick them with the
button. It checks type, size and count, lists what was chosen, and shows
progress or an error per file. It does not upload: your code does, and
tells it how that is going.

<Status of={FileUploaderStories} />

<Canvas of={FileUploaderStories.WithStatus} />

## Variants

| Mode | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `multiple` | Attachments, a batch of photos: files are appended, up to `maxFiles`. |
| Single | One document: an invoice, a CV. A new file replaces the chosen one, if it passes the checks. |

<Canvas of={FileUploaderStories.Single} />

Each file gets a type icon: a page with a coloured badge for Word, Excel,
PowerPoint, PDF, image and audio, after Microsoft 365, from the extension
or MIME type. Anything else is the bare page.

<Canvas of={FileUploaderStories.FileTypes} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { FileUploader } from 'zweihander/file-uploader'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/file-uploader.json
```

- Source: [src/components/inputs/FileUploader.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/inputs/FileUploader.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/file-uploader](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/file-uploader)
- Behaviour: a native `<input type="file">` behind a kit [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={FileUploaderStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={FileUploaderStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

Two more parts show only when needed:

- **Errors**: one line per file that was not added, under the drop zone,
  e.g. "raw-scan.png is larger than 5 MB."
- **File error**: in place of the progress ring, a short message from
  `getFileStatus`, e.g. "Upload failed". A long one truncates.

<Canvas of={FileUploaderStories.Rejected} />

## Measurements

One size. The buttons inside are `sm` Buttons, 24px tall.

<SpecTable
  caption="Drop zone"
  rows={[

/>

    { part: 'File row', property: 'Block padding', token: '--space-stack' },
    { part: 'File row', property: 'Gap', token: '--space-inline' },
    { part: 'File row', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-field' },
    { part: 'Name', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body' },
    { part: 'Size, file error', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body-sm' },
    { part: 'Remove button', property: 'Size', token: '--control-sm' },
    { part: 'Remove button', property: 'Minimum on touch screens', token: '--target-coarse' },
  ]}
/>

The uploader is 24rem wide unless `isFullWidth`. A file row has no
inline padding, so its icon and remove button line up with the drop
zone's edges. The type icon is 20px: a 13 × 18 page with a folded corner,
and a badge 8px tall (14px wide, 16px for DOC and MP3) naming the type
in 6px bold: DOC, XLS, PPT, PDF, IMG or MP3.

    { part: 'Required asterisk, errors', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-danger' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="File list"
  rows={[
    { part: 'File row, hover', property: 'Background', token: '--color-interaction-hovered' },
    { part: 'Type icon', property: 'Line round the page and fold', token: '--color-surface-raised' },
    { part: 'Name', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text' },
    { part: 'Size', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-subtlest' },
    { part: 'Progress ring', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-brand' },
    { part: 'File error', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-danger' },
  ]}
/>

The type badges keep fixed colours in both modes: they are each file
type's identity, not the theme's, and white on each is above 4.5:1. The
page is an 18% tint of the badge colour and the fold a 40% one; an
unknown type gets a fixed light gray page (#e3e5e8, fold #c2c5cc). The
Choose button is an `accent contained` Button and the remove buttons
`secondary ghost`; their states are Button's.

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
    { label: 'Uploading', content: <Fit><Story of={FileUploaderStories.Anatomy} /></Fit> },
    { label: 'Disabled', content: <Fit><Story of={FileUploaderStories.Disabled} /></Fit> },
  ]}
>
  <Fit><Story of={FileUploaderStories.DoStateTheRules} /></Fit>
</States>

- **Dragging**: while a file is over the drop zone its edge turns solid
  `--color-border-focused` and it fills with `--color-background-neutral`, so the change is not colour
  alone.
- **Rejected or required and empty**: the drop zone's edge turns
  `--color-text-danger` and the errors list why, one line per file.
- **Focus** is the Choose button's and the remove buttons' own ring.
- **Uploading**: a progress ring beside the remove button while
  `progress` is under 100; it goes at 100. An `error` takes its place.
- **Disabled** fades the icon and the buttons, not the text: none of it
  is a native label, so faded text would fail contrast rather than be
  exempt.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={FileUploaderStories} />
</div>

### Design notes

- **Checks on every path in.** The system picker filters by `accept`, but
  a drop, or "All files" in the picker, does not. The uploader checks the
  type, size and count of everything and says why a file was left out.
- **A rejected file never replaces a good one.** In single-file mode a
  new file replaces the chosen one only if it passes the checks.
- **The same file twice is one file.** Name, size and modified time
  match, so it is skipped rather than listed again.
- **Uploading is yours.** Start it in `onFilesChange` and report through
  `getFileStatus`.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a File Uploader to attach files to a form: receipts to a claim,
documents to an application. Say what is allowed in `helperText`, and set
`accept`, `maxSize` and `maxFiles` to match, so the rules are read before
a file is turned away.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={FileUploaderStories.DoStateTheRules} />}
  doCaption="The rules up front: types and size in the helper text, checked by accept and maxSize."
  dont={<Story of={FileUploaderStories.DontHideTheRules} />}
  dontCaption="No rules shown: people learn them one rejection at a time."
/>

Report upload progress per file with `getFileStatus`, and keep errors
short ("Upload failed"): the row has room for a few words.

## When not to use

- **For text people could paste.** Use a
  [Textarea](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textarea--docs).
- **For a link to a file.** Use a
  [Text Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textinput--docs) with
  `type="url"`.

## Accessibility

- Dragging is a shortcut, never the only way: the Choose button is a
  real button, reached by Tab, and opens the system picker. The file
  input itself is hidden from assistive tech so there is one control, not
  two.
- The uploader is a `group` named by its label; `required` adds
  "(required)" to that name, since a group cannot be `aria-required`.
  Submitting it empty shows "Choose at least one file." (or "Choose a
  file.") in the errors and moves focus to the Choose button, instead of
  the browser's bubble on the hidden input.
- The helper text and any errors describe the Choose button, so they
  are read when focus lands on it.
- The chosen files are a list named "Chosen files" ("Chosen file" when
  `multiple` is off), one item per file.
- A polite status line announces "2 files added. 1 not added." and
  "report.pdf removed."
- Remove buttons are named "Remove report.pdf". After a remove, focus
  moves to the next file's button, or back to Choose when the list is
  empty, so it is never lost.
- The progress ring is a `progressbar` named "Uploading report.pdf",
  with its value.
- While dragging, the drop zone's edge turns solid as well as changing
  colour.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

import type { ComponentProps, ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Icon, type IconName } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './InlineAlert.module.css'

export interface InlineAlertProps extends ComponentProps<'div'> {
  variant?: 'info' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger'
  size?: 'sm' | 'md'
  /** Replaces the variant's icon; `false` shows none. */
  icon?: ReactNode | false
  /** A short link or button after the message, e.g. "Retry". */
  action?: ReactNode
  /**
   * Announce it when it appears: `danger` and `warning` interrupt
   * (`role="alert"`), the others wait (`role="status"`).
   */
  isLive?: boolean
}

const icons: Record<NonNullable<InlineAlertProps['variant']>, IconName> = {
  info: 'info-filled',
  success: 'success-filled',
  warning: 'warning-filled',
  danger: 'danger-filled',
}

/**
 * A one-line message in the flow of a form or a section: no box, no title,
 * no close button. For a message about a whole page or region, use Alert.
 */
export function InlineAlert({
  variant = 'info',
  size = 'md',
  icon,
  action,
  isLive = false,
  className,
  children,
  ...props
}: InlineAlertProps) {
  const urgent = variant === 'danger' || variant === 'warning'
  return (
    <div
      role={isLive ? (urgent ? 'alert' : 'status') : undefined}
      className={cn(styles.inlineAlert, styles[variant], styles[size], className)}
      {...props}
    >
      {icon !== false && (
        <span className={styles.icon} aria-hidden="true">
          {icon ?? <Icon name={icons[variant]} />}
        </span>
      )}
      <span className={styles.message}>{children}</span>
      {action && <span className={styles.action}>{action}</span>}
    </div>
  )
}

# Inline Alert A one-line message in the flow of a form or a section, with no box, no titl...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import * as InlineAlertStories from './InlineAlert.stories'

<Meta of={InlineAlertStories} />

# Inline Alert

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A one-line message in the flow of a form or a section, with no box, no
title and no close button: "Changes are saved automatically", "Couldn't
reach the server".

<Status of={InlineAlertStories} />

<Canvas of={InlineAlertStories.Variants} />

## Variants

`variant` is the colour, by meaning, and the whole line takes it.

| Variant | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `info` | A fact about what is above it: "Changes are saved automatically." |
| `success` | A check that passed: "Domain verified." |
| `warning` | A consequence to know before going on: "This link expires in 24 hours." |
| `danger` | Something that failed: "Couldn't reach the server." |

<Canvas of={InlineAlertStories.Small} />

<Canvas of={InlineAlertStories.WithAction} />

<Canvas of={InlineAlertStories.LongMessage} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { InlineAlert } from 'zweihander/inline-alert'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/inline-alert.json
```

- Source: [src/components/notifications/InlineAlert.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/notifications/InlineAlert.tsx)
- Spec: our own; uiguideline.com has no page for it
- Behaviour: a plain element, no Base UI part
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={InlineAlertStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={InlineAlertStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The icon box is one line tall, so on a message that wraps it stays on the
first line.

## Measurements

<SpecTable
  caption="sm"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Message', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body-sm' },
    { part: 'Message', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body-sm' },
    { part: 'Icon', property: 'Size', token: '--icon-xs' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Gap, icon to message', token: '--control-sm-gap' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="md"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Message', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body' },
    { part: 'Message', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body' },
    { part: 'Icon', property: 'Size', token: '--icon-md' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Gap, icon to message', token: '--space-inline' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable caption="Every size" rows={[{ part: 'Action', property: 'Space before', token: '--space-1' }]} />

No padding, border or background: it lines up with the text and fields
around it.

## Color

The whole line, icon and message, takes the variant's text colour. An Alert
can keep its message in `--color-text` because its box carries the colour;
an inline alert has no box, so the text does. Every `--*-text` token is
4.5:1 on the page in both modes, so a message of any length stays readable.

<SpecTable
  caption="Icon and message, by variant"
  rows={[
    { part: 'info', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-info' },
    { part: 'success', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-success' },
    { part: 'warning', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-warning' },
    { part: 'danger', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-danger' },
  ]}
/>

The action keeps its own colours: a Link or a Button, as passed.

## States

The message has no states. An action in it has its own.

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Action hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Action focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={InlineAlertStories.WithAction} />
</States>

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={InlineAlertStories} />
</div>

Every other `<div>` attribute passes through, including `ref`.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use an Inline Alert for a short message about the thing right above it: a
group of fields, a whole form, a section. A failed submit is the common
case.

<Canvas of={InlineAlertStories.InAForm} />

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={InlineAlertStories.DoFieldError} />}
  doCaption="An error about one field goes on the field, as its helper text: it is read when the field is focused."
  dont={<Story of={InlineAlertStories.DontForOneField} />}
  dontCaption="An inline alert under a field is not tied to it: a screen reader in the field never hears it."
/>

## When not to use

- **For an error on one field.** Use the field's own `validationState` and
  `helperText`, tied to it with `aria-describedby`.
- **For a message about a whole page or region**, or one that needs a
  title, an action row or a close button. Use an
  [Alert](?path=/docs/components-notifications-alert--docs).
- **For news about something that just happened.** Use a
  [Toast](?path=/docs/components-notifications-toast--docs).

## Accessibility

- A plain `<div>` by default, read in order with the page.
- `isLive` for a message that appears in response to something (a failed
  submit): `danger` and `warning` become `role="alert"` and are read at
  once, `info` and `success` become `role="status"` and wait.
- The icon is `aria-hidden`: the words carry the meaning.
- The action is whatever you pass (a Link, a Button) and keeps its own
  keyboard behaviour and focus ring.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

# Kbd A key cap that shows which key to press: a glyph like ⌘ or ⇧, a letter, or a short w...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import { Kbd } from './Kbd'
import * as KbdStories from './Kbd.stories'

<Meta of={KbdStories} />

# Kbd

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A key cap that shows which key to press: a glyph like ⌘ or ⇧, a letter,
or a short word like Esc.

<Status of={KbdStories} />

Kbd is outside the 1.0 component list; it is beta from 0.9.0.

<Canvas of={KbdStories.Sizes} />

## Variants

| Form | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| <Kbd>Esc</Kbd> one key | A single key: `children`. |
| <Kbd keys={['⌘', 'K']} /> combination | Keys pressed together: `keys`, one cap per key. |

<Canvas of={KbdStories.Combination} />

`size="sm"` (16px) fits inside a small control or a dense row; `md`
(20px) is the default, for running text, tooltips and menus.

<Canvas of={KbdStories.InText} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Kbd } from 'zweihander/kbd'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/kbd.json
```

- Source: [src/components/atomic-elements/Kbd.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/atomic-elements/Kbd.tsx)
- Spec: none on uiguideline.com; after [shadcn/ui Kbd](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/kbd)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={KbdStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={KbdStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

A combination is HTML's own markup for one: an outer `<kbd>` holding a
`<kbd>` per key. A single key is just the cap.

## Measurements

<SpecTable
  caption="md"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Key', property: 'Height and minimum width', token: '--box-xs' },
    { part: 'Key', property: 'Inline padding', token: '--space-1' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="sm"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Key', property: 'Height and minimum width', token: '--box-2xs' },
    { part: 'Key', property: 'Inline padding', token: '--space-0-5' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Every size"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Key', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-xs' },
    { part: 'Key', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body-sm' },
    { part: 'Key', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body-sm' },
    { part: 'Group', property: 'Gap between keys', token: '--space-0-5' },
  ]}
/>

The border is 1px, 2px along the bottom so the cap reads as raised.

## Color

<SpecTable
  caption="Key"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Key', property: 'Background', token: '--color-background-neutral' },
    { part: 'Key', property: 'Border', token: '--color-border' },
    { part: 'Key', property: 'Glyph', token: '--color-text-subtlest' },
  ]}
/>

## States

A key cap is not interactive: no hover, focus or pressed. Its states are
what it shows.

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Glyph', content: <Kbd>⌘</Kbd> },
    { label: 'Word', content: <Kbd>Esc</Kbd> },
    { label: 'Combination', content: <Kbd keys={['⌘', '⇧', 'P']} /> },
    { label: 'sm', content: <Kbd size="sm" keys={['⌘', 'K']} /> },
  ]}
/>

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={KbdStories} />
</div>

Every other `<kbd>` attribute passes through to the outer element.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use Kbd wherever the page tells someone which key to press: a hint in a
tooltip, a command palette row, a line of help text, a shortcuts sheet.
These are places where people come to learn a shortcut, so the key gets a
cap. A Menu is not: see below.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={KbdStories.DoHideInControl} />}
  doCaption="Inside a control the caps are hidden and the button says Meta+K through aria-keyshortcuts: its name stays “Search”."
  dont={<Story of={KbdStories.DontLeaveInName} />}
  dontCaption="Left in, the glyphs join the name: a screen reader hears “Search ⌘ K”, and ⌘ is read as “place of interest”."
/>

Match the platform: ⌘ and ⌥ on a Mac, Ctrl and Alt elsewhere. Kbd shows
what it is given and does not detect the platform.

## When not to use

- **For a Menu item's shortcut.** Use Menu's `shortcut` string: menus
  show shortcuts as quiet text at the end of the row, the way desktop
  menus do. The menu is for acting, and a cap on every row would pull the
  eye from the labels. A command palette is the exception: it is where
  shortcuts are discovered, so its rows use Kbd.
- **For code or a value someone types.** Use `<code>`: Kbd is a key, not
  text to copy.
- **To bind the key.** Kbd is display only; the page binds the shortcut.

## Accessibility

- Kbd is a native `<kbd>`; a combination is a `<kbd>` of `<kbd>`s, one
  per key.
- It is not focusable and has no role: it is never in the tab order.
- In running text it is read where it sits, as text: "Press Esc to close".
  A combination's keys are read one after the other with no "plus" (⌘S);
  write the combination out in the sentence when that matters.
- Inside a control, hide it with `aria-hidden` and put the shortcut on the
  control with `aria-keyshortcuts` (for example `Meta+K`), so the
  control's name stays its label.
- Contrast is checked by addon-a11y in error mode for every story.

</DocTab>

'use client'

import type { ReactElement, ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Menu as BaseMenu } from '@base-ui/react/menu'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Menu.module.css'

interface ItemBase {
  label: ReactNode
  /** Used for typeahead when `label` is not plain text. */
  textValue?: string
  icon?: ReactNode
  disabled?: boolean
}

/** An action, a link (`href`), or a submenu (`items`). */
export interface MenuActionItem extends ItemBase {
  type?: 'item'
  onSelect?: () => void
  href?: string
  /** Shown right-aligned, e.g. "⌘ D". Display only: it does not bind the key. */
  shortcut?: string
  /** Deletes or removes something: drawn in the danger colour. */
  isDestructive?: boolean
  /** Opens a submenu instead of acting. */
  items?: MenuEntry[]
}
export interface MenuCheckboxItem extends ItemBase {
  type: 'checkbox'
  checked?: boolean
  defaultChecked?: boolean
  onCheckedChange?: (checked: boolean) => void
}
export interface MenuRadioGroupItem {
  type: 'radio'
  label?: ReactNode
  value?: string
  defaultValue?: string
  onValueChange?: (value: string) => void
  options: { value: string; label: ReactNode; disabled?: boolean }[]
}
export interface MenuGroupItem {
  type: 'group'
  label: ReactNode
  items: MenuEntry[]
}
export interface MenuSeparator {
  type: 'separator'
}
export type MenuEntry = MenuActionItem | MenuCheckboxItem | MenuRadioGroupItem | MenuGroupItem | MenuSeparator

export interface MenuProps {
  /** The button that opens it. Its props are merged, not wrapped. */
  trigger: ReactElement
  items: MenuEntry[]
  side?: 'top' | 'right' | 'bottom' | 'left'
  align?: 'start' | 'center' | 'end'
  open?: boolean
  defaultOpen?: boolean
  onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void
  /**
   * While open, lock page scroll and make the rest of the page inert, so the
   * menu is the only thing to interact with. `false` leaves the page as is.
   */
  isModal?: boolean
  /** Where the popup renders instead of `<body>`, e.g. an element in fullscreen. */
  container?: HTMLElement | null
  className?: string
}

const text = (label: ReactNode, textValue?: string) => textValue ?? (typeof label === 'string' ? label : undefined)

/** Renders `MenuEntry[]` as Base UI menu parts, inside a `MenuSurface`. A building block for menus that share Menu's look. */
export function MenuEntries({ items }: { items: MenuEntry[] }) {
  return items.map((entry, i) => {
    switch (entry.type) {
      case 'separator':
        return <BaseMenu.Separator key={i} className={styles.separator} />
      case 'group':
        return (
          <BaseMenu.Group key={i} className={styles.group}>
            <BaseMenu.GroupLabel className={styles.groupLabel}>{entry.label}</BaseMenu.GroupLabel>
            <MenuEntries items={entry.items} />
          </BaseMenu.Group>
        )
      case 'checkbox':
        return (
          <BaseMenu.CheckboxItem
            key={i}
            label={text(entry.label, entry.textValue)}
            checked={entry.checked}
            defaultChecked={entry.defaultChecked}
            onCheckedChange={entry.onCheckedChange && ((c) => entry.onCheckedChange!(c))}
            disabled={entry.disabled}
            closeOnClick={false}
            className={styles.item}
          >
            <span className={styles.indicator}>
              <BaseMenu.CheckboxItemIndicator>
                <Icon name="check" />
              </BaseMenu.CheckboxItemIndicator>
            </span>
            <span className={styles.label}>{entry.label}</span>
          </BaseMenu.CheckboxItem>
        )
      case 'radio':
        return (
          <BaseMenu.Group key={i} className={styles.group}>
            {entry.label && <BaseMenu.GroupLabel className={styles.groupLabel}>{entry.label}</BaseMenu.GroupLabel>}
            <BaseMenu.RadioGroup
              value={entry.value}
              defaultValue={entry.defaultValue}
              onValueChange={entry.onValueChange && ((v) => entry.onValueChange!(v as string))}
            >
              {entry.options.map((o) => (
                <BaseMenu.RadioItem
                  key={o.value}
                  value={o.value}
                  label={text(o.label)}
                  disabled={o.disabled}
                  closeOnClick={false}
                  className={styles.item}
                >
                  <span className={styles.indicator}>
                    <BaseMenu.RadioItemIndicator>
                      <Icon name="check" />
                    </BaseMenu.RadioItemIndicator>
                  </span>
                  <span className={styles.label}>{o.label}</span>
                </BaseMenu.RadioItem>
              ))}
            </BaseMenu.RadioGroup>
          </BaseMenu.Group>
        )
      default: {
        const content = (
          <>
            {entry.icon && (
              <span className={styles.icon} aria-hidden="true">
                {entry.icon}
              </span>
            )}
            <span className={styles.label}>{entry.label}</span>
            {entry.shortcut && (
              <kbd className={styles.shortcut} aria-hidden="true">
                {entry.shortcut}
              </kbd>
            )}
          </>
        )
        const className = cn(styles.item, entry.isDestructive && styles.destructive)
        if (entry.items) {
          return (
            <BaseMenu.SubmenuRoot key={i}>
              <BaseMenu.SubmenuTrigger label={text(entry.label, entry.textValue)} disabled={entry.disabled} className={className}>
                {content}
                <span className={styles.chevron} aria-hidden="true">
                  <Icon name="chevron-right" />
                </span>
              </BaseMenu.SubmenuTrigger>
              <MenuSurface side="right" align="start">
                <MenuEntries items={entry.items} />
              </MenuSurface>
            </BaseMenu.SubmenuRoot>
          )
        }
        // A disabled link is an inert item: Base UI's LinkItem has no disabled state.
        if (entry.href !== undefined && !entry.disabled) {
          return (
            <BaseMenu.LinkItem key={i} href={entry.href} label={text(entry.label, entry.textValue)} className={className}>
              {content}
            </BaseMenu.LinkItem>
          )
        }
        return (
          <BaseMenu.Item
            key={i}
            label={text(entry.label, entry.textValue)}
            disabled={entry.disabled}
            onClick={entry.onSelect && (() => entry.onSelect!())}
            className={className}
          >
            {content}
          </BaseMenu.Item>
        )
      }
    }
  })
}

/** Menu's popup surface, rendered through a portal, 4px from its trigger by default. */
export function MenuSurface({
  side,
  align,
  sideOffset = 4,
  container,
  className,
  children,
}: {
  side: MenuProps['side']
  align: MenuProps['align']
  sideOffset?: number
  container?: HTMLElement | null
  className?: string
  children: ReactNode
}) {
  return (
    <BaseMenu.Portal container={container}>
      <BaseMenu.Positioner className={styles.positioner} side={side} align={align} sideOffset={sideOffset}>
        <BaseMenu.Popup className={cn(styles.popup, className)}>{children}</BaseMenu.Popup>
      </BaseMenu.Positioner>
    </BaseMenu.Portal>
  )
}

export function Menu({
  trigger,
  items,
  side = 'bottom',
  align = 'start',
  open,
  defaultOpen,
  onOpenChange,
  isModal = true,
  container,
  className,
}: MenuProps) {
  return (
    <BaseMenu.Root
      open={open}
      defaultOpen={defaultOpen}
      onOpenChange={onOpenChange && ((next) => onOpenChange(next))}
      modal={isModal}
    >
      <BaseMenu.Trigger render={trigger} />
      <MenuSurface side={side} align={align} container={container} className={className}>
        <MenuEntries items={items} />
      </MenuSurface>
    </BaseMenu.Root>
  )
}

# Menu A list of actions that opens from a button: the "…" on a row, an "Actions" dropdown...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import * as MenuStories from './Menu.stories'

<Meta of={MenuStories} />

# Menu

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A list of actions that opens from a button: the "…" on a row, an
"Actions" dropdown, a "View" menu of toggles. It acts or toggles; to pick a
value for a form, use a [Select](?path=/docs/components-inputs-select--docs).

<Status of={MenuStories} />

<Canvas of={MenuStories.Default} />

## Variants

Menu has one look. What changes is the kind of entry in `items`, and a
menu can mix them:

| Entry | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| Action (the default) | Something to do now: Edit, Duplicate, Delete. Closes the menu. `isDestructive` draws it in the danger colour. |
| Link (`href`) | Going somewhere: Documentation, Settings. A real `<a>`. |
| Submenu (`items`) | A set of choices that belongs under one item: Move to, Share with. |
| Checkbox (`type: 'checkbox'`) | Settings that are on or off, several at a time: Show hidden files. Keeps the menu open. |
| Radio (`type: 'radio'`) | One of a few settings: Sort by name, date or size. Keeps the menu open. |
| Group (`type: 'group'`) and separator | Structure for a longer menu: a label over related items, a rule between sets. |

<Canvas of={MenuStories.Groups} />

<Canvas of={MenuStories.Submenu} />

<Canvas of={MenuStories.Links} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Menu } from 'zweihander/menu'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/menu.json
```

- Source: [src/components/navigation/Menu.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/navigation/Menu.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/menu](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/menu)
- Behaviour: [Base UI Menu](https://base-ui.com/react/components/menu)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={MenuStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={MenuStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

A link item has the same parts as an action. Checkbox and radio items show
a check where an action shows its icon, so their labels line up.

## Measurements

The item follows Atlassian Design's dropdown item: 8px block and 12px
inline padding around a 20px line, so a one-line item is 36px tall. The
box ramp has no 36px step, so the md control tier (32px) is the floor and
the padding makes the rest. Items sit 4px inside the
popup's border and 2px apart, with a 6px corner and 12px between icon and
label; a shortcut or a chevron sits 24px after the label; a separator is
as wide as the items, with 4px above and below; a group label has 8px
block padding, 12px before and 24px after.

  caption="Popup"
  rows={[

    { part: 'Popup', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-lg' },

/>

The popup is at least 12rem wide, or the trigger's width if that is wider,
and no taller than the space on screen: past that it scrolls. It opens
4px from the trigger.

The destructive item uses the danger text colour, not the solid: it reads
at 4.5:1 on the popup and on its highlight.

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Closed', content: <Story of={MenuStories.Default} /> },
    { label: 'Open', content: <Story of={MenuStories.Open} /> },
  ]}
/>

- **Highlighted** is where the arrow keys or the pointer are: a `--color-background-neutral`
  fill; the icon keeps `--color-text-subtlest`. A submenu's item stays highlighted
  while its submenu is open. Focus moves with the highlight, so there is no
  separate focus ring inside the popup.
- **Disabled** items are muted at 60% opacity and skipped by the arrow
  keys (Archive, above).
- **Checked** checkbox and radio items show the check; unchecked ones keep
  the empty column.
- The trigger's own hover, focus and pressed states are the
  [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs)'s.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={MenuStories} />
</div>

`items` is data, like Select's `options`, not child components.
`shortcut` is display only: binding the key is left to the page, which
knows what else is bound.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Menu for actions that belong to one thing but would crowd the
screen as buttons: the actions on a table row, a card's overflow, a
toolbar's "More". Keep it short, put the most used item first, and give
destructive actions the last place, after a separator.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={MenuStories.DoDestructiveLast} />}
  doCaption="Delete last, after a separator, in the danger colour."
  dont={<Story of={MenuStories.DontDestructiveAmongOthers} />}
  dontCaption="Delete between two everyday actions: one arrow key too far and it is chosen."
/>

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={MenuStories.DoActions} />}
  doCaption="A menu of actions. Each item does something now."
  dont={<Story of={MenuStories.DontMenuAsField} />}
  dontCaption="A menu standing in for a form field. Use a Select: it has a label, a value and a form name."
/>

The popup opens below the trigger, lined up with its start edge; `side`
and `align` place it elsewhere.

## When not to use

- **To pick a value for a form.** Use a
  [Select](?path=/docs/components-inputs-select--docs), or a
  [Combobox](?path=/docs/components-inputs-combobox--docs) when the list
  is long enough to search.
- **For one or two actions.** Show them as
  [Buttons](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs): a hidden action
  is one fewer person finds.
- **For the app's main navigation.** Use a side navigation of
  [Links](?path=/docs/components-navigation-link--docs) or
  [Tabs](?path=/docs/components-navigation-tabs--docs), which show where
  the reader is.
- **For content: a form, a preview.** Use a
  [Popover](?path=/docs/components-overlays-popover--docs). A menu holds
  only menu items.

## Accessibility

- The trigger has `aria-haspopup="menu"` and `aria-expanded`; the popup
  is a `role="menu"` of `menuitem`, `menuitemcheckbox` and
  `menuitemradio`, with `aria-checked` on the toggles and
  `aria-disabled` on disabled items.
- Keyboard: Enter, Space or Arrow Down on the trigger opens it; arrows
  move (disabled items are skipped), typing a few letters jumps to the
  matching item, Enter selects, Arrow Right opens a submenu and Arrow
  Left closes it, Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger.
- Toggles keep the menu open, so several can be changed in one go;
  actions close it and focus returns to the trigger.
- The icon and shortcut are hidden from assistive tech; the label names
  the item. Give `textValue` when a label is not plain text, or typeahead
  cannot find it.
- A disabled link has no `href`, so it cannot be followed.
- Items are 36px tall, 44px on touch screens (`pointer: coarse`).
- `isModal` (the default) makes the rest of the page inert while the menu
  is open, so a screen reader stays in the menu.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

export interface MenubarMenu {
  /** The top-level item: File, Edit, View. */
  label: string
  /** The flyout's entries, the same data as Menu's `items`. */
  items: MenuEntry[]
  disabled?: boolean
  /** Open this menu on first render, uncontrolled. */
  defaultOpen?: boolean
}

export interface MenubarProps {
  menus: MenubarMenu[]
  /** Names the bar. Needed when a page has more than one menubar. */
  'aria-label'?: string
  /**
   * While a flyout is open, lock page scroll and make the rest of the page
   * inert. `false` leaves the page as is.
   */
  isModal?: boolean
  /** Where the flyouts render instead of `<body>`, e.g. an element in fullscreen. */
  container?: HTMLElement | null
  className?: string
}

/** A row of menus, as in a desktop app: File, Edit, View, each opening a flyout. */
export function Menubar({ menus, 'aria-label': ariaLabel, isModal = true, container, className }: MenubarProps) {
  return (
    <BaseMenubar aria-label={ariaLabel} modal={isModal} className={cn(styles.bar, className)}>
      {menus.map((menu, i) => (
        <BaseMenu.Root key={i} disabled={menu.disabled} defaultOpen={menu.defaultOpen}>
          <BaseMenu.Trigger className={styles.trigger}>{menu.label}</BaseMenu.Trigger>
          <MenuSurface side="bottom" align="start" container={container}>
            <MenuEntries items={menu.items} />
          </MenuSurface>
        </BaseMenu.Root>
      ))}
    </BaseMenubar>
  )
}

# Menubar A row of menus across the top of a tool, as in a desktop app: File, Edit, View, ...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import * as MenubarStories from './Menubar.stories'

<Meta of={MenubarStories} />

# Menubar

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A row of menus across the top of a tool, as in a desktop app: File, Edit,
View, each opening a flyout of commands. Use it in an editor-like screen
with more commands than a toolbar can show.

<Status of={MenubarStories} />

<Canvas of={MenubarStories.Default} />

## Variants

Menubar has one look. Each flyout is a
[Menu](?path=/docs/components-navigation-menu--docs) popup and takes the
same entries: actions with shortcuts, links, submenus, checkbox and radio
items, groups and separators.

| Menu | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| Enabled (the default) | Commands that apply now. |
| Disabled (`disabled`) | A menu that does not apply in the current state. It stays in place, muted, so the bar does not shift. |

<Canvas of={MenubarStories.DisabledMenu} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Menubar } from 'zweihander/menubar'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/menubar.json
```

- Source: [src/components/navigation/Menubar.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/navigation/Menubar.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/menu](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/menu)
- Behaviour: [Base UI Menubar](https://base-ui.com/react/components/menubar)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={MenubarStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={MenubarStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The flyout on this tab is a picture: it is drawn open in place, not
positioned over the page. Its parts are Menu's; see
[Menu](?path=/docs/components-navigation-menu--docs) for the item's own
anatomy.

## Measurements

The bar is a strip: its triggers are rows of the sm control tier (24px),
shorter than the 36px items in the flyout. Atlassian Design has no
menubar, so the bar follows the Figma library; the flyouts are Menu's. The
bar has no fill, border or padding: it is its triggers side by side,
touching, each with the sm control's corner. Labels are regular weight.

<SpecTable
  caption="Bar"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Trigger', property: 'Height', token: '--control-sm' },
    { part: 'Trigger', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--control-sm-radius' },
    { part: 'Trigger', property: 'Inline padding', token: '--control-sm-pad' },
    { part: 'Trigger', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body' },
    { part: 'Trigger', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body' },
    { part: 'Trigger', property: 'Focus ring width', token: '--focus-width' },
    { part: 'Hit area', property: 'Minimum on touch screens', token: '--target-coarse' },
  ]}
/>

A flyout opens 4px below its trigger, lined up with the trigger's start
edge. When the bar is wider than its container, it scrolls sideways.

## Color

<SpecTable
  caption="Bar"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Bar', property: 'Text', token: '--color-text' },
    { part: 'Trigger, hover, highlighted or open', property: 'Background', token: '--color-background-neutral' },
    { part: 'Trigger, hover, highlighted or open', property: 'Text', token: '--color-text' },
    { part: 'Trigger, disabled', property: 'Text', token: '--color-text-subtlest' },
    { part: 'Trigger, focus', property: 'Ring', token: '--color-border-focused' },
  ]}
/>

The flyout's colours are Menu's.

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Closed', content: <Story of={MenubarStories.Default} /> },
    { label: 'Open', content: <Story of={MenubarStories.Open} /> },
    { label: 'Disabled menu', content: <Story of={MenubarStories.DisabledMenu} /> },
  ]}
/>

- **Hover and highlighted**: the trigger takes the same `--color-background-neutral` fill as
  a highlighted item in the flyout.
- **Open**: the trigger keeps that fill while its flyout is open, so the
  reader sees which menu they are in.
- **Focus**: a keyboard focus ring inside the trigger, so it does not
  collide with its neighbours.
- **Disabled**: muted at 60% opacity, no fill on hover, skipped by the
  arrow keys.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={MenubarStories} />
</div>

`menus` is data, and each menu's `items` is Menu's `items`. Shortcuts are
plain trailing text, as in Menu: display only, binding the key is left to
the page.

### Differences from the spec

- **No navigation menu.** The source pairs a menubar with a navigation
  menu: links in flyouts, each with a description. Zweihänder leaves that
  out: app navigation is a side or top navigation of links, which shows
  the current page; a flyout of described links is a marketing-site
  pattern.
- **No item description.** Flyout items are Menu's entries, one line
  each. A second line of text is what a navigation menu needs, and it is
  not built.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Menubar in a screen that works like a desktop tool, an invoice or
report editor, a spreadsheet, where people look for commands by category
and learn their shortcuts. Name each menu for what it holds and keep the
order people know from desktop apps: File, Edit, View, then your own,
then Help.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={MenubarStories.DoConventionalOrder} />}
  doCaption="Commands, grouped by the familiar File, Edit, View, with their shortcuts."
  dont={<Story of={MenubarStories.DontNavigation} />}
  dontCaption="Pages behind flyouts. Navigation belongs in a side or top navigation of links, where the current page shows."
/>

## When not to use

- **For the app's navigation.** Use a side or top navigation of
  [Links](?path=/docs/components-navigation-link--docs): it shows where
  the reader is, a menubar does not.
- **For a few actions on one thing.** Use a
  [Menu](?path=/docs/components-navigation-menu--docs) from a button, or
  Buttons.

## Accessibility

- The bar is a `role="menubar"`, named by `aria-label`. Each trigger is a
  `menuitem` with `aria-haspopup="menu"` and `aria-expanded`; a disabled
  menu's trigger has `aria-disabled`.
- The bar is one tab stop. Arrow Left and Right move along the triggers,
  skipping disabled menus.
- Arrow Down, Enter or Space on a trigger opens its flyout on the first
  item. Inside a flyout the keys are Menu's.
- With a flyout open, Arrow Right and Left move to the next and previous
  menu and open it, and moving the pointer onto another trigger opens that
  menu instead.
- Escape closes the flyout and returns focus to its trigger; choosing an
  action closes it too.
- Shortcuts and icons are hidden from assistive tech; the label names the
  item.
- Triggers are 24px tall; on touch screens (`pointer: coarse`) their hit
  area grows to 44px.
- `isModal` (the default) makes the rest of the page inert while a flyout
  is open, so a screen reader stays in the menu.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

'use client'

import type { ReactElement, ReactNode, RefObject } from 'react'
import { AlertDialog } from '@base-ui/react/alert-dialog'
import { Dialog } from '@base-ui/react/dialog'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Modal.module.css'

export interface ModalProps {
  /** The button that opens it. Omit when `open` is controlled from elsewhere. */
  trigger?: ReactElement
  /** Required: it names the dialog. */
  title: ReactNode
  description?: ReactNode
  children?: ReactNode
  /** Actions, right-aligned under the content: the main one last. */
  footer?: ReactNode
  /** Max width: 400px, 600px, 800px. Never wider than the screen. */
  size?: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'
  /** Defaults to `true`, or `false` when `isAlert`. */
  hasCloseButton?: boolean
  closeLabel?: string
  /**
   * A decision that must be made: `role="alertdialog"`, and a click on the
   * backdrop does not close it. Pair it with explicit buttons in `footer`.
   */
  isAlert?: boolean
  /** Close on a click on the backdrop. Ignored when `isAlert`. */
  closeOnBackdropClick?: boolean
  /**
   * While open, trap focus, lock page scroll and make the rest of the page
   * inert. `false` drops those three; the backdrop still covers the page.
   * Ignored when `isAlert`: an alert
   * is always modal.
   */
  isModal?: boolean
  /** Where the modal renders instead of `<body>`, e.g. an element in fullscreen. */
  container?: HTMLElement | null
  open?: boolean
  defaultOpen?: boolean
  onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void
  /** Where focus goes on open. By default, the first focusable element. */
  initialFocus?: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>
  className?: string
}

const widths = { sm: styles.sm, md: styles.md, lg: styles.lg }

export function Modal({
  trigger,
  title,
  description,
  children,
  footer,
  size = 'md',
  hasCloseButton,
  closeLabel = 'Close',
  isAlert = false,
  closeOnBackdropClick = true,
  isModal = true,
  container,
  open,
  defaultOpen,
  onOpenChange,
  initialFocus,
  className,
}: ModalProps) {
  const showClose = hasCloseButton ?? !isAlert
  const content = (
    <>
      {trigger && (isAlert ? <AlertDialog.Trigger render={trigger} /> : <Dialog.Trigger render={trigger} />)}
      <Dialog.Portal container={container}>
        <Dialog.Backdrop className={styles.backdrop} />
        <Dialog.Viewport className={styles.viewport}>
          <Dialog.Popup initialFocus={initialFocus} className={cn(styles.popup, widths[size], className)}>
            <div className={styles.header}>
              <div className={styles.heading}>
                <Dialog.Title className={styles.title}>{title}</Dialog.Title>
                {description && <Dialog.Description className={styles.description}>{description}</Dialog.Description>}
              </div>
              {showClose && (
                <Dialog.Close aria-label={closeLabel} className={styles.close}>
                  <Icon name="close" />
                </Dialog.Close>
              )}
            </div>
            {children && <div className={styles.body}>{children}</div>}
            {footer && <div className={styles.footer}>{footer}</div>}
          </Dialog.Popup>
        </Dialog.Viewport>
      </Dialog.Portal>
    </>
  )
  const change = onOpenChange && ((next: boolean) => onOpenChange(next))
  return isAlert ? (
    <AlertDialog.Root open={open} defaultOpen={defaultOpen} onOpenChange={change}>
      {content}
    </AlertDialog.Root>
  ) : (
    <Dialog.Root
      open={open}
      defaultOpen={defaultOpen}
      onOpenChange={change}
      disablePointerDismissal={!closeOnBackdropClick}
      modal={isModal}
    >
      {content}
    </Dialog.Root>
  )
}

/** A button inside the modal that closes it, e.g. "Cancel": `<ModalClose render={<Button />}>Cancel</ModalClose>`. */
export const ModalClose = Dialog.Close
