# Modal A dialog over the page that has to be dealt with before going back: a short form, ...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import * as ModalStories from './Modal.stories'

<Meta of={ModalStories} />

# Modal

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A dialog over the page that has to be dealt with before going back: a
short form, a confirmation, a decision. Everything behind it is dimmed and
out of reach until it closes.

<Status of={ModalStories} />

<Canvas of={ModalStories.Default} />

## Variants

| Variant | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| Dialog (default) | A short task on its own: edit a profile, invite people. A close button, Escape and a press on the backdrop all close it. |
| Alert (`isAlert`) | A decision with consequences: delete, discard, leave. No close button and a press on the backdrop does nothing, so it ends only through its own buttons or Escape. |

<Canvas of={ModalStories.Alert} />

`size` sets the maximum width: `sm` (400px) for an alert, `md` (600px) for
a short form, `lg` (800px) for long content. Taller than the screen, the
body scrolls and the title and footer stay in view. On a screen under
480px wide the modal is the whole screen.

<Canvas of={ModalStories.ScreenGutter} />

<Canvas of={ModalStories.Long} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Modal, ModalClose } from 'zweihander/modal'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/modal.json
```

- Source: [src/components/overlays/Modal.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/overlays/Modal.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/modal](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/modal)
- Behaviour: [Base UI Dialog](https://base-ui.com/react/components/dialog) and [Alert Dialog](https://base-ui.com/react/components/alert-dialog)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={ModalStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={ModalStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The open modals on this tab and the next are pictures: real modals
rendered in a frame with `container`, not modal (`isModal={false}`) and
inert, so they do not lock this page or take its focus.

## Measurements

<SpecTable
  caption="Container"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Padding, from the outer edge', token: '--space-container' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-panel' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Shadow', token: '--shadow-overlay' },
    { part: 'Title', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-heading-md' },
    { part: 'Title', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-heading-md' },
    { part: 'Title to close button', property: 'Gap', token: '--space-group' },
    { part: 'Title to description', property: 'Gap', token: '--space-inline' },
    { part: 'Body, footer', property: 'Gap above', token: '--space-group' },
    { part: 'Footer', property: 'Gap between actions', token: '--space-inline' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Close button"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Close button', property: 'Padding', token: '--control-xs-gap' },
    { part: 'Close button', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-sm' },
    { part: 'Icon', property: 'Size', token: '--icon-md' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Width', token: '--focus-width' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Offset', token: '--focus-offset-inset' },
    { part: 'Hit area', property: 'Minimum on touch screens', token: '--target-coarse' },
  ]}
/>

The gutter to the screen has no token: the spacing scale has no 60px
step, so the CSS adds two (`--space-12` and `--space-3`).

| Screen width | Gutter, each side | From the top | Width | Height |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 480px and up | 60px | 60px | `size`, at most the screen less 120px | Its content, at most the screen less 120px; then the body scrolls |
| Under 480px | 0 | 0 | The screen | The screen; the body scrolls, the footer sits at the bottom |

"Screen" is the box the modal opens in: the window, or the `container`
when that contains layout. Under 480px the modal has no corner radius and
no shadow.

Width is `size`: at most 400px (`sm`), 600px (`md`) or 800px (`lg`), set
in rem (25, 37.5, 50), and never wider than the screen less its gutter.
These are Atlassian's small, medium and large modals, with its 24px
padding, 12px corner and 20/24 semibold title, 16px from the title to the
body and from the body to the footer, and 8px between the footer's
buttons. The 8px from the title to the description is the kit's own:
Atlassian's header has no description. The 60px gutter, the 60px from
the top (the modal is not centred, so a body that grows does not move the
title) and the full screen under 480px are Atlassian's too. The header stacks the title and the description in one
column, with the close button beside both. The close button is a 24px box, as
tall as the title's line, flush with the padding. The border is 1px, and the padding counts it:
the content sits 24px from the modal's edge. Backdrop
and modal sit on the `--layer-overlay` layer and fade in over
`--duration-base`.

## Color

<SpecTable
  caption="Every modal"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Backdrop', property: 'Background', token: '--color-blanket' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Background', token: '--color-surface-overlay' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Border', token: '--color-border' },
    { part: 'Title, body', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text' },
    { part: 'Description', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-subtlest' },
    { part: 'Close button', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-subtlest' },
    { part: 'Close button, hover', property: 'Background', token: '--color-background-neutral' },
    { part: 'Close button, hover', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-border-focused' },
  ]}
/>

Buttons in the footer keep their own colours: see Button.

## States

The modal is open or closed. Opening fades the backdrop in and scales the
container up from 97%; closing reverses it. The close button is the only
part with states of its own:

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={ModalStories.CloseButton} />
</States>

- **Hover** fills the button with `--color-background-neutral`.
- **Focus** is a 2px `--color-border-focused` outline drawn inside the button, so it is not
  clipped at the container's corner.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={ModalStories} />
</div>

`ModalClose` closes the modal it is in. Give it your own button with
`render`: `<ModalClose render={<Button variant="secondary" />}>Cancel</ModalClose>`.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Reach for a modal last: it stops everything else. Use one when the task
must be finished or abandoned before going on, or for a decision with
consequences. For a decision, use `isAlert`, say exactly what will happen in
the description, and name the buttons after what they do. Before a delete
or anything else that cannot be undone, use a
[Confirm Dialog](?path=/docs/components-overlays-confirm-dialog--docs): it
is this alert with the warning, the focus on Cancel and type to confirm
built in.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={ModalStories.DoNameTheActions} />}
  doCaption="Name the buttons after what they do: Delete, Keep project. The choice reads without the question."
  dont={<Story of={ModalStories.DontOkCancel} />}
  dontCaption="OK and Cancel make the reader go back to the question to know which one deletes."
/>

Put the main action last in the footer, and dismiss actions (Cancel, Keep)
in the `secondary` variant.

## When not to use

- **For a small form tied to one button**, such as Share or a filter. Use a
  [Popover](?path=/docs/components-overlays-popover--docs): it opens beside
  the button and leaves the page usable.
- **For information**: a success, a warning, a tip. Use an
  [Inline Alert](?path=/docs/components-notifications-inlinealert--docs) or a
  [Toast](?path=/docs/components-notifications-toast--docs); neither stops
  the reader.
- **For a long or many-step task.** Give it a page of its own.
- **Over another modal.** Close the first, or move the second step into it.

## Accessibility

- `role="dialog"` (or `alertdialog`), named by the title and described by
  the description.
- Opening moves focus to the first focusable element, or `initialFocus`,
  and traps it inside. The page behind is `aria-hidden`, its pointer
  events are blocked by the backdrop, and its scroll is locked. Closing
  returns focus to the trigger.
- `isModal={false}` drops the focus trap, the scroll lock and the hidden
  page, but the backdrop still covers the page. It is for pictures of a
  modal, such as the ones on these tabs: a real modal stays modal.
- Escape closes it, as does a press outside unless `isAlert` or
  `closeOnBackdropClick={false}`. An alert dialog closes only through its
  own buttons (and Escape).

  <Canvas of={ModalStories.Dismissing} />

- **One layer with the popups.** Modal, Popover, Select and Combobox all
  sit at `--layer-overlay`. Each portals to the end of `<body>` when it
  opens, so the most recent is on top: a Select opened inside a modal
  lists its options above the modal, which a higher modal layer would
  hide.

  <Canvas of={ModalStories.WithSelect} />

- The close button is named `Close` (`closeLabel`), has the 2px focus ring
  and a 44px hit area on touch screens.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

# Number Input A number, typed or stepped: a quantity, a price, a count. The field is [Tex...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import { NumberInput } from './NumberInput'
import * as NumberInputStories from './NumberInput.stories'

<Meta of={NumberInputStories} />

# Number Input

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A number, typed or stepped: a quantity, a price, a count. The field is
[Text Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textinput--docs)'s, with a
decrease and an increase button inside it.

<Status of={NumberInputStories} />

<Canvas of={NumberInputStories.Default} />

## Variants

One appearance, the white outlined box. What changes is the size and how
the number steps and is shown.

<Canvas of={NumberInputStories.Sizes} />

| Size | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `md` | Forms and dialogs: the default. |
| `sm` | Dense places: a quantity in a cart row or a table cell. |

<Canvas of={NumberInputStories.Precision} />

| Setting | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `min`, `max` | A range the value must stay in. The button at a limit is disabled. |
| `step` | Values that move in fixed amounts: 5 minutes, 0.25 of a unit. |
| `precision` | A fixed number of decimals, such as 2 for a price: `9.5` shows as `9.50`. |

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { NumberInput } from 'zweihander/number-input'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/number-input.json
```

- Source: [src/components/inputs/NumberInput.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/inputs/NumberInput.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/number-input](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/number-input)
- Behaviour: [Base UI Number Field](https://base-ui.com/react/components/number-field)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={NumberInputStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={NumberInputStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The steppers float inside the box: no divider, a small inset from its end,
and a fill only on hover.

## Measurements

The box is Text Input's: `sm` is 32px and `md` is 40px, one step taller
than a Button. A stepper is a 24px square in both, centred in the box.
The value sits 10px from the start edge and 8px before the steppers; the
steppers are 2px apart and 6px from the end edge, so each icon sits 10px
in.

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus' },
    { label: 'Stepper hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'At max', content: <NumberInput label="Guests" defaultValue={12} min={1} max={12} /> },
    { label: 'Error', content: <NumberInput label="Guests" defaultValue={0} validationState="error" helperText="At least 1." /> },
    { label: 'Disabled', content: <NumberInput label="Guests" defaultValue={4} disabled /> },
  ]}
>
  <NumberInput label="Guests" defaultValue={4} min={1} max={12} />
</States>

- **Hover** on a stepper fills it with `--color-background-neutral` and darkens its icon; the
  field itself does not change.
- **Focus** is the field's 2px ring around the whole box, in
  `--color-text-danger` when invalid.
- **At a limit** the stepper that would go past it is disabled, at 50%
  opacity, and ignores hover, so it looks as unavailable as it is.
- **Read-only** fills the box with `--color-background-input`; the steppers do
  nothing.
- **Disabled** dims the whole field to 50%.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={NumberInputStories} />
</div>

`ref` goes to the input. `id` and `className` are passed through too; no
other attributes are.

### Differences from the spec

- **No `filled` appearance.** The spec's filled field (a tinted box with a bottom rule) was dropped to match the Claude apps, where every field is the white outlined box.
- **Two sizes, not three.** `sm` (32px) and `md` (40px), after Atlassian Design: a field is one step taller than a button, so `sm` lines up with a Button in a toolbar. The spec's largest step was dropped; a big call to action is `md` with more room around it, not a taller box.
- **`onValueChange` with a number**, not `onChange`: built on Base UI, it
  takes Base UI's name, and the value arrives parsed rather than as text.
- **`max` is optional with no default.** The spec marks it required with a
  default of 100, which contradicts itself; a quantity with no upper
  bound is common.
- **`label`, `helperText`, `validationState`** are added
  from the shared field.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Number Input for a quantity people adjust by a little, or type
outright: guests, items in a cart, minutes, a price. Set `min` and `max`
whenever the range is known, so the steppers stop at its ends.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={NumberInputStories.DoQuantity} />}
  doCaption="A quantity, nudged up and down within a known range."
  dont={<Story of={NumberInputStories.DontIdentifier} />}
  dontCaption="A postcode is not a quantity: stepping it is meaningless, and formatting may change it."
/>

## When not to use

- **For numbers that are identifiers**: postcodes, card numbers, phone
  numbers, IDs. Use a
  [Text Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textinput--docs) with
  `inputMode="numeric"`, which brings up the number keyboard without
  steppers or formatting.
- **For a value picked on a scale**, such as volume or a percentage
  people judge by eye. Use a Slider.
- **For a small fixed set of numbers** (1, 2 or 4 seats). Use radios or a
  [Select](?path=/docs/components-inputs-select--docs).

## Accessibility

- The input is a text field with `inputmode="numeric"` and the role
  description "Number field", named by the label. Without a visible label,
  pass `aria-label`: a placeholder is a hint, not a name.
- **Keyboard:** Up and Down step the value by `step` from the input; with
  Shift they step by 10, with Alt by 0.1. The steppers are out of the tab order
  (`tabindex="-1"`): the arrow keys do the same from the field.
- The steppers are named "Increase" and "Decrease" and are disabled at
  the limits, so a screen reader hears why nothing happened.
- The value is parsed and formatted in the user's locale; the form
  receives the plain number.
- `helperText` is the input's description and
  `validationState="error"` sets `aria-invalid`, as on Text Input.
- Steppers widen to 44px on touch screens, the one direction they can
  grow without covering the input or each other.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

'use client'

import { Fragment, useRef, type ReactNode, type Ref } from 'react'
import { OTPField } from '@base-ui/react/otp-field'
import { ResendButton } from '../buttons/ResendButton'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import { InputField, assignRef, type InputSize, type ValidationState } from './InputField'
import styles from './OTPInput.module.css'

export interface OTPInputProps {
  /** Points at the first cell. */
  ref?: Ref<HTMLInputElement>
  /** Number of characters. */
  length?: number
  /** Splits the cells into groups of this many, with a dash between groups. */
  groupSize?: number
  value?: string
  defaultValue?: string
  onValueChange?: (value: string) => void
  /** Called once every cell is filled, typed or pasted. */
  onValueComplete?: (value: string) => void
  /** Which characters a cell accepts; others are dropped. */
  validationType?: 'numeric' | 'alpha' | 'alphanumeric'
  /** Shows dots instead of the characters. */
  mask?: boolean
  /** Submits the surrounding form once every cell is filled. */
  autoSubmit?: boolean
  /**
   * Shows a resend button under the cells, disabled while the cooldown counts
   * down. Return a promise to show the button busy until it settles: the
   * cooldown restarts only if it resolves, so a failed send can be retried.
   */
  onResend?: () => void | Promise<unknown>
  /** Seconds before resend is allowed, from mount and after each resend. */
  resendCooldown?: number
  resendLabel?: string
  /** The accessible name of each cell after the first, which the label names. */
  slotLabel?: (position: number, length: number) => string
  /** Names the group and the first cell. Required: Base UI names the first cell only through a label. */
  label: ReactNode
  helperText?: ReactNode
  validationState?: ValidationState
  size?: InputSize
  name?: string
  disabled?: boolean
  readOnly?: boolean
  required?: boolean
  id?: string
  className?: string
}

const defaultSlotLabel = (position: number, length: number) => `Character ${position} of ${length}`

export function OTPInput({
  ref,
  length = 6,
  groupSize,
  onValueChange,
  onValueComplete,
  onResend,
  resendCooldown = 30,
  resendLabel = 'Resend code',
  slotLabel = defaultSlotLabel,
  label,
  helperText,
  validationState,
  size = 'md',
  name,
  disabled,
  required,
  className,
  ...props
}: OTPInputProps) {
  const firstCell = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null)

  async function resend() {
    await onResend?.()
    // The button is about to be disabled: move focus to where the new code goes.
    firstCell.current?.focus()
  }

  return (
    <InputField
      label={label}
      helperText={helperText}
      validationState={validationState}
      required={required}
      disabled={disabled}
      name={name}
      className={className}
      footer={
        onResend && (
          <ResendButton
            className={styles.resend}
            cooldown={resendCooldown}
            label={resendLabel}
            disabled={disabled}
            onResend={resend}
          />
        )
      }
    >
      <OTPField.Root
        {...props}
        length={length}
        required={required}
        // Only the value: Base UI's event details are not part of this API.
        onValueChange={onValueChange && ((next) => onValueChange(next))}
        onValueComplete={onValueComplete && ((next) => onValueComplete(next))}
        className={cn(styles.root, styles[size])}
      >
        {Array.from({ length }, (_, i) => (
          <Fragment key={i}>
            {groupSize && i > 0 && i % groupSize === 0 && (
              <OTPField.Separator className={styles.separator}>–</OTPField.Separator>
            )}
            <OTPField.Input
              ref={
                i === 0
                  ? (node: HTMLInputElement | null) => {
                      firstCell.current = node
                      assignRef(ref, node)
                    }
                  : undefined
              }
              aria-label={i === 0 ? undefined : slotLabel(i + 1, length)}
              className={styles.cell}
            />
          </Fragment>
        ))}
      </OTPField.Root>
    </InputField>
  )
}

# OTP Input A short one-time code, typed or pasted into a row of single-character cells: t...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import { OTPInput } from './OTPInput'
import * as OTPInputStories from './OTPInput.stories'

<Meta of={OTPInputStories} />

# OTP Input

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A short one-time code, typed or pasted into a row of single-character
cells: the code from a text message, an email or an authenticator app.

<Status of={OTPInputStories} />

<Canvas of={OTPInputStories.Default} />

## Variants

One appearance, a row of small outlined boxes. What changes is the size,
whether the cells are grouped, and whether there is a resend button.

<Canvas of={OTPInputStories.Sizes} />

| Size | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `md` | Sign-in, verification and confirmation screens: the default. |
| `sm` | A code asked for inside a dense panel or a table row. |

<Canvas of={OTPInputStories.Resend} />

| Setting | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `groupSize` | A code people read in chunks: `3` shows six digits as 3 – 3, `4` an eight-character backup code as 4 – 4. |
| `onResend` | A code that was sent and may not arrive. The button waits `resendCooldown` seconds, showing the time left. Return a promise: a failed send starts no cooldown. |
| `validationType` | `numeric` for codes from texts and apps; `alphanumeric` for backup and recovery codes. |
| `mask` | A code that should not be read over someone's shoulder. |

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { OTPInput } from 'zweihander/otp-input'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/otp-input.json
```

- Source: [src/components/inputs/OTPInput.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/inputs/OTPInput.tsx)
- Spec: none on uiguideline.com; the reference is [shadcn/ui Input OTP](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/input-otp)
- Behaviour: [Base UI OTP Field](https://base-ui.com/react/components/otp-field)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={OTPInputStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={OTPInputStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

Each cell is its own box with the field's edge, fill and radius, so the
row reads as several small fields that belong together. The label and
helper text are Text Input's.

## Measurements

A cell is a square as tall as a Text Input of the same size: 32px in
`sm`, 40px in `md`. The digit is Heading lg (24/28, semibold) in both;
the separator between groups is body type.

<SpecTable
  caption="sm"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Cell', property: 'Width and height', token: '--control-md' },
    { part: 'Cell', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--control-md-radius-field' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="md"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Cell', property: 'Width and height', token: '--control-lg' },
    { part: 'Cell', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--control-md-radius-field' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Every size"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Cells and separator', property: 'Gap', token: '--space-2' },
    { part: 'Cell', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-heading-lg' },
    { part: 'Cell', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-heading-lg' },
    { part: 'Separator', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body' },
    { part: 'Resend button', property: 'Pulled back to line up with the cells', token: '--control-sm-pad' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Width', token: '--focus-width' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Offset', token: '--focus-offset' },
    { part: 'Cell', property: 'Height on touch screens', token: '--target-coarse' },
  ]}
/>

The characters use tabular figures, centred in the cell. The resend
button is a small ghost [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs).

## Color

<SpecTable
  caption="default"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Cell', property: 'Background', token: '--color-surface-raised' },
    { part: 'Cell', property: 'Border', token: '--field-edge' },
    { part: 'Character', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text' },
    { part: 'Caret', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-border-focused' },
    { part: 'Group separator', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-subtlest' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-border-focused' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="error"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-danger' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable caption="Read-only" rows={[{ part: 'Cell', property: 'Background', token: '--color-background-input' }]} />

`--field-edge` is the shared field's edge colour: `--color-border-input` by
default, `--color-text-danger` on error and `--color-text-success` on success, so every
cell and the helper text change together.

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus' },
    { label: 'Filled', content: <OTPInput label="Code" length={4} defaultValue="4821" /> },
    { label: 'Error', content: <OTPInput label="Code" length={4} defaultValue="4821" validationState="error" helperText="That code is wrong." /> },
    { label: 'Disabled', content: <OTPInput label="Code" length={4} defaultValue="48" disabled /> },
  ]}
>
  <OTPInput label="Code" length={4} />
</States>

- **Hover** changes nothing: a cell is a text field, and the caret shows
  where typing goes.
- **Focus** rings only the cell being typed into, in `--color-text-danger` when
  invalid.
- **Error** turns every cell's edge and the helper text `--color-text-danger`.
- **Read-only** fills the cells with `--color-background-input`; typing does
  nothing.
- **Disabled** dims the cells to 50% and disables the resend button.
- **Cooling down**, the resend button is disabled and shows the time left
  as `m:ss`.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={OTPInputStories} />
</div>

`ref` goes to the first cell. `id` and `className` are passed through too;
no other attributes are.

### Differences from the spec

There is no uiguideline.com spec for this component; the reference is shadcn/ui Input OTP.

- **One component, flat props.** shadcn composes `InputOTP`, `InputOTPGroup`,
  `InputOTPSlot` and `InputOTPSeparator`; Zweihänder takes `length` and
  `groupSize`, as the API conventions ask for flat props before 1.0.
- **Resend is built in.** shadcn leaves it to the page. Every screen that
  sends a code needs the same button and countdown, so it lives here.
- **Real inputs, one per cell**, from Base UI, not one hidden input under
  drawn slots: each cell is focusable and named.
- **`label`, `helperText`, `validationState`** are added from the shared field.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use an OTP Input for a short code someone copies from another place: a
text message, an email, an authenticator app. Say where the code was sent
in `helperText`, and give a way to send another.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={OTPInputStories.DoOneField} />}
  doCaption="Six digits, labelled, with where the code went and a way to resend it."
  dont={<Story of={OTPInputStories.DontLongCode} />}
  dontCaption="Sixteen cells are too many to scan or correct. A long key is one Text Input."
/>

## When not to use

- **For codes longer than about 8 characters**, licence keys or recovery
  phrases. Use a [Text Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textinput--docs).
- **For a PIN or password people make up themselves.** Use a
  [Text Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textinput--docs) with
  `type="password"`: cells suggest a code that was sent.
- **For a number people adjust.** Use a
  [Number Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-numberinput--docs).

## Accessibility

- The cells sit in a `group` named by the label; the label also names the
  first cell, and each later cell is named by `slotLabel`, "Character 2 of 6"
  by default.
- **Keyboard:** the group is one tab stop: only the cell to type into is in
  the tab order. Typing a character fills the cell and moves to the next;
  Backspace clears the cell before and moves back; Left and Right move
  between cells.
- Characters `validationType` does not allow are dropped, so letters cannot
  enter a numeric code.
- Pasting the whole code into any cell fills every cell; spaces are ignored.
- The first cell has `autocomplete="one-time-code"`, so phones offer the code
  from a text message.
- `helperText` is the group's description and `validationState="error"` sets
  `aria-invalid` on every cell.
- The resend button is disabled during the cooldown and its name carries the
  time left. After a send, focus moves to the first cell, so it is not lost
  with the disabled button; while a send is pending the button stays
  focusable and is marked `aria-busy`. The countdown is not a live region, so it does not interrupt
  every second.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

'use client'

import { useState, type ComponentProps, type ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import { Select } from '../inputs/Select'
import styles from './Pagination.module.css'

export interface PaginationProps extends Omit<ComponentProps<'nav'>, 'children' | 'onChange'> {
  /** Ignored when `totalItems` is set: the count is then worked out from `pageSize`, so the two cannot disagree. */
  totalPages?: number
  /** Rows in all. Shows the "21–40 of 340" summary. */
  totalItems?: number
  pageSize?: number
  defaultPageSize?: number
  onPageSizeChange?: (pageSize: number) => void
  /** Choices for the "Rows per page" select; without them there is no select. */
  pageSizeOptions?: number[]
  /** 1-based. */
  page?: number
  defaultPage?: number
  onPageChange?: (page: number) => void
  /** Pages shown either side of the current one. */
  siblingCount?: number
  /** Pages always shown at each end. */
  boundaryCount?: number
  /** @deprecated Pagination has one size, 32px controls: `sm` renders the same as `md`. Drop the prop; removed in the next release. */
  size?: 'sm' | 'md'
  /** Render links instead of buttons, for pages with their own URL. */
  getHref?: (page: number) => string
  /** The nav landmark's name. */
  'aria-label'?: string
}

const range = (from: number, to: number) => Array.from({ length: Math.max(0, to - from + 1) }, (_, i) => from + i)

/** The page numbers to show, with 'start-ellipsis' / 'end-ellipsis' where a run is skipped. */
export function paginationItems(page: number, total: number, siblings = 1, boundary = 1) {
  const start = range(1, Math.min(boundary, total))
  const end = range(Math.max(total - boundary + 1, boundary + 1), total)
  const siblingsStart = Math.max(Math.min(page - siblings, total - boundary - siblings * 2 - 1), boundary + 2)
  const siblingsEnd = Math.min(Math.max(page + siblings, boundary + siblings * 2 + 2), end.length > 0 ? end[0] - 2 : total - 1)
  return [
    ...start,
    ...(siblingsStart > boundary + 2 ? ['start-ellipsis' as const] : boundary + 1 < total - boundary ? [boundary + 1] : []),
    ...range(siblingsStart, siblingsEnd),
    ...(siblingsEnd < total - boundary - 1 ? ['end-ellipsis' as const] : total - boundary > boundary ? [total - boundary] : []),
    ...end,
  ]
}

let hasWarned = false

export function Pagination({
  totalPages,
  totalItems,
  pageSize: pageSizeProp,
  defaultPageSize = 20,
  onPageSizeChange,
  pageSizeOptions,
  page: pageProp,
  defaultPage = 1,
  onPageChange,
  siblingCount = 1,
  boundaryCount = 1,
  size = 'md',
  getHref,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel = 'Pagination',
  className,
  ...props
}: PaginationProps) {
  // The kit's deprecation rule: warn on a value that is not the documented
  // default. `size="md"` is what you get anyway, so it stays silent.
  if (import.meta.env.DEV && !hasWarned && size !== 'md') {
    hasWarned = true
    console.warn('Pagination: `size="sm"` is deprecated and renders as `md`: Pagination has one size. `size` will be removed in the next release.')
  }
  const [pageState, setPageState] = useState(defaultPage)
  const [pageSizeState, setPageSizeState] = useState(defaultPageSize)
  const pageSize = Math.max(1, pageSizeProp ?? pageSizeState)
  const pagesFor = (size: number) => Math.max(1, totalItems === undefined ? (totalPages ?? 1) : Math.ceil(totalItems / size))
  const total = pagesFor(pageSize)
  const page = Math.min(Math.max(1, pageProp ?? pageState), total)
  const go = (p: number) => {
    setPageState(p)
    onPageChange?.(p)
  }
  const first = (page - 1) * pageSize + 1
  const changePageSize = (size: number) => {
    setPageSizeState(size)
    onPageSizeChange?.(size)
    // Keep the first row the reader was looking at on screen.
    const next = Math.min(Math.floor((first - 1) / size) + 1, pagesFor(size))
    if (next !== page) go(next)
  }
  // Grouped in the reader's locale; the words around it are English, like the rest of the labels.
  const formatCount = (n: number) => n.toLocaleString()

  const control = (target: number, label: string, content: ReactNode, extra?: string, current?: boolean) => {
    const disabled = target < 1 || target > total
    const common = {
      className: cn(styles.control, extra, current && styles.current),
      'aria-label': label,
      'aria-current': current ? ('page' as const) : undefined,
    }
    if (getHref) {
      // A link at the ends has nowhere to go: no href, aria-disabled. Without
      // href an <a> has no role, and aria-label is not allowed on it, so the
      // role is set back explicitly.
      return disabled ? (
        <a {...common} role="link" aria-disabled="true">
          {content}
        </a>
      ) : (
        <a {...common} href={getHref(target)} onClick={() => !current && go(target)}>
          {content}
        </a>
      )
    }
    return (
      <button type="button" {...common} disabled={disabled} onClick={() => !current && go(target)}>
        {content}
      </button>
    )
  }

  return (
    <nav aria-label={ariaLabel} className={cn(styles.pagination, className)} {...props}>
      {totalItems !== undefined && (
        <p role="status" className={styles.summary}>
          {totalItems > 0
            ? `${formatCount(first)}–${formatCount(Math.min(page * pageSize, totalItems))} of ${formatCount(totalItems)}`
            : '0 of 0'}
        </p>
      )}
      <ul className={styles.list}>
        <li>{control(page - 1, 'Previous page', <Icon name="chevron-left" />, styles.step)}</li>
        {paginationItems(page, total, siblingCount, boundaryCount).map((item) => (
          <li key={item}>

              <span className={styles.ellipsis} aria-hidden="true">

              </span>
            ) : (
              control(item, `Page ${item}`, item, undefined, item === page)

          </li>
        ))}
        <li>{control(page + 1, 'Next page', <Icon name="chevron-right" />, styles.step)}</li>
      </ul>
      {pageSizeOptions && (
        <div className={styles.pageSize}>
          {/* The select carries the same name; this text is only what sighted readers see. */}
          <span aria-hidden="true">Rows per page</span>
          <Select
            aria-label="Rows per page"
            // A field's sm is the 32px that lines up with the page buttons.
            size="sm"
            className={styles.pageSizeSelect}
            options={pageSizeOptions.map(String)}
            value={String(pageSize)}
            onValueChange={(v) => v && changePageSize(Number(v))}
          />
        </div>
      )}
    </nav>
  )
}

./src/components/navigation/Pagination.mdx
# Pagination Moves through a long list one page at a time: previous, next, and the page nu...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import * as PaginationStories from './Pagination.stories'

<Meta of={PaginationStories} />

# Pagination

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

Moves through a long list one page at a time: previous, next, and the page
numbers around the current one. Under a table it can also say which rows
are shown ("21–40 of 340") and let the reader pick how many rows a page
holds.

<Status of={PaginationStories} />

<Canvas of={PaginationStories.Middle} />

## Variants

Pagination has one look and one size. What changes is how many numbers
show, whether the pages are buttons or links, and the two optional ends.

| Form | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `getHref` | Pages with their own URL: each page is a link that can be opened in a new tab and shared. |
| Buttons | Pages that only exist in this view's state, such as a filtered list in a dialog. The default. |
| `totalItems` | A table footer, where the reader needs to know how many rows there are: adds the summary at the start. |
| `pageSizeOptions` | Long tables where readers scan in bulk: adds a "Rows per page" select at the end. |

<Canvas of={PaginationStories.WithSummary} />

<Canvas of={PaginationStories.FewPages} />

<Canvas of={PaginationStories.Links} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Pagination } from 'zweihander/pagination'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/pagination.json
```

- Source: [src/components/navigation/Pagination.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/navigation/Pagination.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/pagination](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/pagination)
- Behaviour: a plain `<nav>` around a list of buttons or links
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={PaginationStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={PaginationStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The first and last page always show, the current page keeps a sibling
each side, and "…" appears only where it hides two or more pages. A single
hidden page is shown instead, since "…" would take the same room. So the
number of controls stays the same as you move through the middle, and
Next does not jump.

The summary and the select only appear when `totalItems` and
`pageSizeOptions` are passed. The summary sits at the start and pushes the
pages and the select to the end; on a narrow screen the row wraps.

## Measurements

One size, Atlassian Design's: the `md` control tier (Foundations /
Sizing), 32px. A control is square at its minimum; the inline padding only
shows on a page number of three digits or more. Previous and next have no
padding, so they stay square. The controls sit 4px apart, and the
ellipsis has 8px either side.

<SpecTable
  caption="Every pagination"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Control', property: 'Height and minimum width', token: '--control-md' },
    { part: 'Control', property: 'Inline padding', token: '--control-md-pad' },
    { part: 'Control', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--control-md-radius' },
    { part: 'Previous, Next', property: 'Icon size', token: '--icon-md' },
    { part: 'Label', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body' },
    { part: 'Label', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body' },
    { part: 'Summary, List, Rows per page', property: 'Gap between them', token: '--space-inline' },
    { part: 'Control', property: 'Gap between controls', token: '--space-1' },
    { part: 'Ellipsis', property: 'Inline padding', token: '--space-2' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Width', token: '--focus-width' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Offset', token: '--focus-offset' },
    { part: 'Control', property: 'Height and minimum width on touch screens', token: '--target-coarse' },
  ]}
/>

## Color

One colour set: the current page is the only fill. Switch the theme and
the accent in the toolbar: the values follow.

<SpecTable
  caption="Every pagination"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Page, Previous, Next', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text' },
    { part: 'Page, Previous, Next, hover', property: 'Background', token: '--color-background-neutral' },
    { part: 'Page, Previous, Next, hover', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text' },
    { part: 'Current page', property: 'Background', token: '--color-background-brand-bold' },
    { part: 'Current page', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-brand-inverse' },
    { part: 'Ellipsis, Summary, Rows per page label', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-subtlest' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-border-focused' },
  ]}
/>

At rest a control has no fill.

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={PaginationStories.StatesExample} />
</States>

- **Selected**: the current page is filled with `--color-background-brand-bold`, medium
  weight. It does not change on hover, and pressing it does nothing.
- **Hover** fills a page, Previous or Next with an `--color-background-neutral` chip.
- **Focus** is a 2px `--color-border-focused` outline, 2px outside the control.
- **Disabled**: Previous on the first page (above) and Next on the last, at 50%
  opacity. As buttons they are `disabled`; as links they lose their
  `href`.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={PaginationStories} />
</div>

The rows-per-page select is a [Select](?path=/docs/components-inputs-select--docs)
at `size="sm"`, 32px: level with the page controls. Changing it moves to the page that holds the first row
shown before, so the reader does not lose their place; it calls
`onPageSizeChange`, then `onPageChange` if the page moved.

`size` is deprecated. Pagination has one size, as Atlassian's does:
`size="sm"` renders the same 32px controls as `md`. It is still accepted
for one release; drop it. The kit's rule for a deprecated prop: it warns
in the development console, once, when it is passed a value that is not
its documented default (or when a renamed prop is used under its old
name). So `size="sm"` warns, and `size="md"`, the default, is silent.

Every other `<nav>` attribute passes through. `paginationItems(page,
total, siblings, boundary)` is exported too, for building your own.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use Pagination under a long list or table when the reader needs to know
where they are in it and jump to a page: search results, an audit log, an
order history. Put it below the content it pages, and keep the list's
position stable as pages change.

Leave `siblingCount` and `boundaryCount` at 1. The control stays short and
keeps the same width as the reader moves, so Next stays under the pointer.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={PaginationStories.DoKeepItShort} />}
  doCaption="The default range: first, last, and the current page with a neighbour each side, on one line."
  dont={<Story of={PaginationStories.DontShowEveryPage} />}
  dontCaption="Every page number at once wraps over several lines and buries the current page."
/>

Under a table, pass `totalItems` so the reader knows how much there is.
Offer `pageSizeOptions` only when readers really scan in bulk; three or
four choices (10, 20, 50, 100) are enough.

When the pages have URLs, pass `getHref`, so a page can be opened in a new
tab, bookmarked and shared.

## When not to use

- **For a feed read top to bottom.** Load more as the reader scrolls, or
  with a "Load more" [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs):
  page numbers mean nothing in a stream.
- **For a few items.** If everything fits on one page, show it all.
- **For the steps of a task.** Use a Stepper.
- **For switching between views of one thing.** Use Tabs.

## Accessibility

- A `<nav>` landmark named "Pagination", around a list.
- Each page control is named "Page 3"; the current one has
  `aria-current="page"`. Previous and next are named "Previous page" and
  "Next page".
- At either end, Previous or Next is disabled. As links they lose their
  `href` (the only thing that stops an `<a>` navigating) and keep
  `role="link"` with `aria-disabled`, so they are still announced as a
  disabled link.
- With `getHref`, each control is a real `<a href>`; without it, a native
  `<button>`. Both are in the tab order and activate with Enter (buttons
  with Space too).
- The summary has `role="status"`, a polite live region, so "21–40 of 340"
  is read out after a page or size change.
- The rows-per-page select is a combobox named "Rows per page"; its
  visible label is `aria-hidden` so the name is not read twice.
- The ellipsis is `aria-hidden`: the page names already say which numbers
  are there.
- Controls are 32px and grow to 44px on touch screens (`pointer:
  coarse`).
- Focus ring: 2px `--color-border-focused`, 2px offset.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

'use client'

import { useId, useState } from 'react'
import { arc, pie } from 'd3-shape'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import { Table } from '../data-display/Table'
import { Skeleton } from '../loaders/Skeleton'
import { ChartFrame, useEnterOnce } from './ChartFrame'
import { ChartLegend } from './ChartLegend'
import { colorVar, formatCompact, formatShare, groupSlices, type Slice } from './chart-utils'
import styles from './Chart.module.css'

export interface PieChartProps {
  /** Shown above the chart, and its accessible name. */
  title: string
  data: Slice[]
  /** `donut` leaves a hole with the total in it. */
  appearance?: 'pie' | 'donut'
  /** Under the total in a donut, e.g. "requests". */
  centerLabel?: string
  /** Diameter in pixels. */
  size?: number
  format?: (value: number) => string
  isLoading?: boolean
  className?: string
}

/**
 * Parts of one whole. No labels on the slices: the legend below it carries
 * each share, the table the values. Past six slices, or under 3%, slices
 * merge into "Other".
 */
export function PieChart({
  title,
  data,
  appearance = 'pie',
  centerLabel = 'Total',
  size = 160,
  format = formatCompact,
  isLoading = false,
  className,
}: PieChartProps) {
  const id = useId()
  const [focusKey, setFocusKey] = useState<string | null>(null)
  const total = data.reduce((sum, d) => sum + d.value, 0)
  // All zeros is no data: a pie of nothing has no parts to show.
  const hasData = total > 0
  const isEntering = useEnterOnce(!isLoading && hasData)
  const shareOf = (value: number) => formatShare(value / total)

  const slices = groupSlices(data)
  const isDonut = appearance === 'donut'
  const radius = size / 2 - 2
  const arcs = pie<(typeof slices)[number]>()
    .sort(null)
    .value((d) => d.value)(slices)
  const path = arc<(typeof arcs)[number]>()
    .innerRadius(isDonut ? radius * 0.64 : 0)
    .outerRadius(radius)
    .padAngle(isDonut ? 0.015 : 0)
    .cornerRadius(isDonut ? 2 : 0)

  return (
    <ChartFrame
      title={title}
      isLoading={isLoading}
      loading={<Skeleton appearance="circle" width={size} height={size} />}
      hasData={hasData}
      emptyHeight={size}
      className={className}
      table={() => (
        <Table
          caption={title}
          rows={data}
          getRowId={(_, i) => String(i)}
          columns={[
            { key: 'label', header: 'Label', isRowHeader: true },
            { key: 'value', header: 'Value', align: 'end', cell: (d) => format(d.value) },
            { key: 'share', header: 'Share', align: 'end', cell: (d) => shareOf(d.value) },
          ]}
        />
      )}
    >
      {(titleId) => (
        <div className={styles.pieBody}>
          <svg
            role="img"
            aria-labelledby={`${titleId} ${id}-desc`}
            className={cn(isEntering && styles.entering)}
            width={size}
            height={size}
            viewBox={`${-size / 2} ${-size / 2} ${size} ${size}`}
          >
            {/* The sweep-in: a ring stroke drawn round the mask, once. */}
            <mask id={`${id}-sweep`}>
              <circle className={styles.sweep} r={radius / 2} fill="none" stroke="white" strokeWidth={radius + 4} pathLength={1} transform="rotate(-90)" />
            </mask>
            <g mask={isEntering ? `url(#${id}-sweep)` : undefined}>
              {arcs.map((a, i) => (
                <path
                  key={i}
                  className={cn(styles.slice, focusKey && focusKey !== String(i) && styles.dim)}
                  d={path(a) ?? ''}
                  fill={colorVar(a.data.color)}
                  onPointerEnter={() => setFocusKey(String(i))}
                  onPointerLeave={() => setFocusKey(null)}
                />
              ))}
            </g>
            {isDonut && (
              <>
                <text className={styles.centerTotal} textAnchor="middle" dy="-0.05em">
                  {format(total)}
                </text>
                <text className={styles.centerLabel} textAnchor="middle" dy="1.5em">
                  {centerLabel}
                </text>
              </>
            )}
          </svg>
          <span id={`${id}-desc`} className={styles.srOnly}>
            {slices.map((s) => `${s.label} ${shareOf(s.value)}`).join(', ')}
          </span>
          <ChartLegend
            items={slices.map((s, i) => ({ key: String(i), label: s.label, color: colorVar(s.color), value: shareOf(s.value) }))}
            onFocusChange={setFocusKey}
          />
        </div>
      )}
    </ChartFrame>
  )
}

'use client'

import type { ReactElement, ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Popover as BasePopover } from '@base-ui/react/popover'
import { Icon } from '@/lib/icon'
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils'
import styles from './Popover.module.css'

export interface PopoverProps {
  /** The element that opens it: one button. Its props are merged, not wrapped. */
  trigger: ReactElement
  /** Names the popover (it is a dialog). Without one, pass `aria-label`. */
  title?: ReactNode
  description?: ReactNode
  children?: ReactNode
  side?: 'top' | 'right' | 'bottom' | 'left'
  align?: 'start' | 'center' | 'end'
  /** A close button in the corner. Escape and a click outside close it either way. */
  hasCloseButton?: boolean
  closeLabel?: string
  /** Open on hover as well as click, for previews. Content must still be reachable by click and keyboard. */
  openOnHover?: boolean
  open?: boolean
  defaultOpen?: boolean
  onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void
  /** Trap focus inside while open, lock page scroll and block clicks outside (Base UI's modal mode). */
  isModal?: boolean
  /** Where the popup renders instead of `<body>`, e.g. an element in fullscreen. */
  container?: HTMLElement | null
  'aria-label'?: string
  className?: string
}

export function Popover({
  trigger,
  title,
  description,
  children,
  side = 'bottom',
  align = 'center',
  hasCloseButton = false,
  closeLabel = 'Close',
  openOnHover = false,
  open,
  defaultOpen,
  onOpenChange,
  isModal = false,
  container,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel,
  className,
}: PopoverProps) {
  return (
    <BasePopover.Root
      open={open}
      defaultOpen={defaultOpen}
      onOpenChange={onOpenChange && ((next) => onOpenChange(next))}
      modal={isModal}
    >
      <BasePopover.Trigger render={trigger} openOnHover={openOnHover} />
      <BasePopover.Portal container={container}>
        <BasePopover.Positioner className={styles.positioner} side={side} align={align} sideOffset={6}>
          <BasePopover.Popup aria-label={title ? undefined : ariaLabel} className={cn(styles.popup, className)}>
            {(title || description || hasCloseButton) && (
              <div className={styles.header}>
                {(title || description) && (
                  <div className={styles.heading}>
                    {title && <BasePopover.Title className={styles.title}>{title}</BasePopover.Title>}
                    {description && <BasePopover.Description className={styles.description}>{description}</BasePopover.Description>}
                  </div>
                )}
                {hasCloseButton && (
                  <BasePopover.Close aria-label={closeLabel} className={styles.close}>
                    <Icon name="close" />
                  </BasePopover.Close>
                )}
              </div>
            )}
            {/* Base UI only traps focus in a modal popover that contains a
                Close, and a touch screen reader needs one to get out. */}
            {isModal && !hasCloseButton && (
              <BasePopover.Close aria-label={closeLabel} className={cn(styles.close, styles.hiddenClose)}>
                <Icon name="close" />
              </BasePopover.Close>
            )}
            {children && <div className={styles.body}>{children}</div>}
          </BasePopover.Popup>
        </BasePopover.Positioner>
      </BasePopover.Portal>
    </BasePopover.Root>
  )
}

# Popover A small panel anchored to a button, for content you interact with: a share form,...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import * as PopoverStories from './Popover.stories'

<Meta of={PopoverStories} />

# Popover

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

A small panel anchored to a button, for content you interact with: a share
form, a filter, a set of options. It opens on click and stays until you
close it.

<Status of={PopoverStories} />

<Canvas of={PopoverStories.Open} />

## Variants

| Variant | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| Non-modal (default) | Most popovers. Tab can leave it and the page stays usable while it is open. |
| Modal (`isModal`) | A popover that must be finished or closed first: focus stays inside, the page does not scroll and presses outside are blocked. |
| `openOnHover` | A preview that also opens on hover, when what it holds must be reachable by click, keyboard and touch. A person or record preview on a link fits here too. |

A title is optional. Without one, name the popover with `aria-label`:

<Canvas of={PopoverStories.ContentOnly} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Popover } from 'zweihander/popover'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/popover.json
```

- Source: [src/components/overlays/Popover.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/overlays/Popover.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/popover](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/popover)
- Behaviour: [Base UI Popover](https://base-ui.com/react/components/popover)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={PopoverStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={PopoverStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The open popovers on this tab and the next are pictures: real popovers
rendered in place with `container` and inert, the popup laid out under the
trigger where it opens.

## Measurements

<SpecTable
  caption="Container"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Padding', token: '--space-group' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-lg' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Shadow', token: '--shadow-overlay' },
    { part: 'Title', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body' },
    { part: 'Title', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body' },
    { part: 'Title to close button', property: 'Gap', token: '--space-cluster' },
    { part: 'Body', property: 'Gap above', token: '--space-3' },
  ]}
/>

<SpecTable
  caption="Close button"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Close button', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-sm' },
    { part: 'Icon', property: 'Size', token: '--icon-md' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Width', token: '--focus-width' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Offset', token: '--focus-offset-inset' },
    { part: 'Hit area', property: 'Minimum on touch screens', token: '--target-coarse' },
  ]}
/>

The container is as wide as its content, at most 22rem and never wider
than the room beside the trigger. It has no arrow: it opens 6px from the
trigger and lines up with it, which already ties the two. It has a 1px
border and a semibold title. The header stacks the title and the
description with no gap between them, and the close button sits beside
both, flush in the top-right corner of the padding. The 8px corner and the overlay shadow are
Atlassian's popup; the 16px padding and the 22rem cap are the kit's own. The close button is 20px: 2px around its icon,
one line of text tall. Popovers sit on the `--layer-overlay` layer and fade
in over `--duration-fast`.

## Color

<SpecTable
  caption="Every popover"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Background', token: '--color-surface-overlay' },
    { part: 'Container', property: 'Border', token: '--color-border' },
    { part: 'Title, body', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text' },
    { part: 'Description', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-subtlest' },
    { part: 'Close button', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-subtlest' },
    { part: 'Close button, hover', property: 'Background', token: '--color-background-neutral' },
    { part: 'Close button, hover', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text' },
    { part: 'Focus ring', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-border-focused' },
  ]}
/>

Select and Combobox lists use the same surface: `--color-surface-overlay`, its border
and shadow.

## States

The popover is open or closed. Opening fades it in and scales it up from
97%, from the trigger's side. The trigger keeps the states of its own
component (see Button); the close button is the only part with states of
its own:

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={PopoverStories.CloseButton} />
</States>

- **Hover** fills the close button with `--color-background-neutral`.
- **Focus** is a 2px `--color-border-focused` outline drawn inside the button.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={PopoverStories} />
</div>

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Popover for a short task that belongs to the button that opens it:
share a file, set a filter, pick from a few options. It holds links,
inputs and buttons, which a Tooltip must not.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={PopoverStories.DoShortTask} />}
  doCaption="A short task tied to its button: one field and one action."
  dont={<Story of={PopoverStories.DontLongForm} />}
  dontCaption="A whole form in a popover. It closes on a stray press outside and loses the work: use a Modal."
/>

It opens below the trigger by default; `side` and `align` move it. When
that side has no room, it flips to the other one.

## When not to use

- **For a label or a hint** on hover or focus. Use a
  [Tooltip](?path=/docs/components-overlays-tooltip--docs).
- **For a list of actions or commands.** Use a
  [Menu](?path=/docs/components-navigation-menu--docs): it has the
  arrow-key navigation a list of commands needs.
- **For a long form or a decision with consequences.** Use a
  [Modal](?path=/docs/components-overlays-modal--docs).

## Accessibility

- The popup is a `role="dialog"` named by `title` (or `aria-label`) and
  described by `description`. The trigger carries `aria-expanded` and
  `aria-haspopup`.
- Opening moves focus into the popup; Escape or a press outside closes it
  and returns focus to the trigger.
- **Non-modal by default:** Tab can leave the popup, and the page stays
  usable. `isModal` switches to Base UI's modal mode: focus is trapped,
  page scroll is locked and presses outside are blocked.
- Base UI only traps focus when the popup contains a close button, and a
  touch screen reader needs one to get out. So a modal popover without
  `hasCloseButton` still renders one: hidden until it has keyboard focus,
  then shown in the corner, so focus is never invisible.

  <Canvas of={PopoverStories.Modal} />

- `openOnHover` adds hover to click, it does not replace it: the content
  stays reachable by keyboard and touch.
- The close button has the 2px focus ring and a 44px hit area on touch
  screens.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

import styles from './ProgressBar.module.css'

export interface ProgressBarProps extends Omit<Progress.Root.Props, 'value' | 'children' | 'className' | 'render'> {
  value?: number
  /** The spec's `maxValue`. */
  max?: number
  size?: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'
  isRounded?: boolean
  variant?: 'primary' | 'accent' | 'secondary' | 'destructive'
  /** Progress is happening but how much is unknown: a sliding bar. */
  isIndeterminate?: boolean
  /** Show the value ("70%") after the bar. */
  showValueLabel?: boolean
  /** A visible label above the bar; also its accessible name. */
  label?: ReactNode
  /** The accessible name when there is no visible `label`. */
  'aria-label'?: string
  className?: string
}

export function ProgressBar({
  value = 0,
  max = 100,
  size = 'md',
  isRounded = false,
  variant = 'primary',
  isIndeterminate = false,
  showValueLabel = false,
  label,
  className,
  'aria-label': ariaLabel,
  ...props
}: ProgressBarProps) {

    <Progress.Root
      {...props}
      value={isIndeterminate ? null : value}
      max={max}
      aria-label={label ? undefined : ariaLabel}

        </Progress.Track>
        {showValueLabel && !isIndeterminate && <Progress.Value className={styles.value} />}

}

# Progress Bar Shows how far a task with a known size has got: an upload, an install, the ...
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks'
import { ProgressBar } from './ProgressBar'
import * as ProgressBarStories from './ProgressBar.stories'

<Meta of={ProgressBarStories} />

# Progress Bar

<DocTabs>
<DocTab value="overview">

Shows how far a task with a known size has got: an upload, an install,
the steps of a setup.

<Status of={ProgressBarStories} />

<Canvas of={ProgressBarStories.ValueLabel} />

## Variants

`variant` is the colour of the fill, by meaning. The track is the same in
all four.

<Canvas of={ProgressBarStories.Variants} />

| Variant | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `primary` | The default: a task the user started and is waiting on. |
| `accent` | A strong fill in neutral black or white, where the brand colour would clash or already means something else. |
| `secondary` | Low emphasis: progress in the background, or one of many bars in a list. |
| `destructive` | A task that is failing, or a quota about to run out. |

`size` is the track's thickness, and `isRounded` gives it pill ends.

<Canvas of={ProgressBarStories.Sizes} />

When a task has started but its size is not known yet, go indeterminate,
and switch to a value as soon as there is one.

<Canvas of={ProgressBarStories.Indeterminate} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { ProgressBar } from 'zweihander/progress-bar'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/progress-bar.json
```

- Source: [src/components/loaders/ProgressBar.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/loaders/ProgressBar.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/progress-bar](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/progress-bar)
- Behaviour: [Base UI Progress](https://base-ui.com/react/components/progress)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={ProgressBarStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={ProgressBarStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

## Measurements

The bar fills the width of its container. Each size sets only the track's
height.

<SpecTable caption="sm" rows={[{ part: 'Track', property: 'Height', token: '--progress-sm' }]} />

<SpecTable caption="md" rows={[{ part: 'Track', property: 'Height', token: '--progress-md' }]} />

<SpecTable caption="lg" rows={[{ part: 'Track', property: 'Height', token: '--progress-lg' }]} />

<SpecTable
  caption="Every size"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Label to track', property: 'Gap', token: '--control-sm-gap' },
    { part: 'Track to value label', property: 'Gap', token: '--space-cluster' },
    { part: 'Track and indicator, rounded', property: 'Corner radius', token: '--radius-pill' },
    { part: 'Label and value label', property: 'Font size', token: '--text-body' },
    { part: 'Label and value label', property: 'Line height', token: '--leading-body' },
    { part: 'Indicator', property: 'Transition between values', token: '--duration-slow' },
  ]}
/>

The value label is at least 4 characters wide, so the bar does not jump as
the number grows from 9% to 100%.

## Color

The fill is what carries the value, so it must clear 3:1 against the
track. Not every accent's solid does (amber's is about 2.9:1 on white), so
each variant fills with a colour meant to be read as text on the page,
which keeps it at 3:1 or better on the track. Switch the theme and the
accent in the toolbar: the values follow.

<SpecTable caption="primary" rows={[{ part: 'Indicator', property: 'Background', token: '--color-text-brand' }]} />

<SpecTable caption="accent" rows={[{ part: 'Indicator', property: 'Background', token: '--color-text' }]} />

<SpecTable caption="secondary" rows={[{ part: 'Indicator', property: 'Background', token: '--color-text-subtlest' }]} />

<SpecTable caption="destructive" rows={[{ part: 'Indicator', property: 'Background', token: '--color-text-danger' }]} />

<SpecTable
  caption="Every variant"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Track', property: 'Background', token: '--color-background-neutral' },
    { part: 'Label', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text' },
    { part: 'Value label', property: 'Colour', token: '--color-text-subtlest' },
  ]}
/>

## States

A progress bar is not interactive: it has no hover, focus or pressed
state.

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Progress' },
    { label: 'Indeterminate', content: <ProgressBar isIndeterminate label="Connecting" /> },
    { label: 'Complete', content: <ProgressBar value={100} label="Uploaded" showValueLabel /> },
  ]}
>
  <ProgressBar value={70} label="Uploading" showValueLabel />
</States>

- **Progress** fills from the start edge, easing between values over
  `--duration-slow`.
- **Indeterminate** slides 40% of the track across, once every 1.4s.
  The value label is hidden: there is no value to show.
- **Complete** is a full bar. It does not change on its own; replace or
  remove it when the task ends.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={ProgressBarStories} />
</div>

Every other prop goes to Base UI's `Progress.Root`: `id`,
`aria-labelledby`, `min`, `format`, `locale`, `getAriaValueText`.

### Differences from the spec

- **`max`, not `maxValue`**, the name Base UI and the native `<progress>`
  use.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Progress Bar for a task that takes long enough to wait on and whose
size is known, or will be: an upload, an import, the steps of a setup.
Name the task in the `label`.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={ProgressBarStories.DoNameTheTask} />}
  doCaption="The label names the task, so the reader knows what they are waiting for."
  dont={<Story of={ProgressBarStories.DontBareBar} />}
  dontCaption="A bare bar leaves sighted readers guessing what it measures, even with an aria-label."
/>

`value` is out of `max`, and the value label shows the percentage:

<Canvas of={ProgressBarStories.Max} />

Without a visible label, `aria-label` names the bar for screen readers.
Use it only where the context already says what the bar measures.

<Canvas of={ProgressBarStories.WithoutVisibleLabel} />

## When not to use

- **For a short wait with no known size.** Use a
  [Spinner](?path=/docs/components-loaders-spinner--docs).
- **For content whose shape you know.** A
  [Skeleton](?path=/docs/components-loaders-skeleton--docs) keeps the
  layout.
- **For steps the user moves through themselves.** Use a
  [Stepper](?path=/docs/components-navigation-stepper--docs): it names the
  steps, and the user can go back.

## Accessibility

- `role="progressbar"` with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin` and
  `aria-valuemax`, and `aria-valuetext` from Base UI. Indeterminate drops
  `aria-valuenow` rather than reporting 0.
- Every bar needs a name: a visible `label` (linked by Base UI) or
  `aria-label`.
- The fill clears 3:1 on the track for every variant and accent, in both
  modes. The value label is `--color-text-subtlest`.
- Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the fill stops easing between values and
  the indeterminate slide slows from 1.4s to 4s a pass.
- A progressbar is not a live region. If completion matters, announce it
  (a Toast, or a status message) when the task ends.

</DocTab>
</DocTabs>

  value?: string
  defaultValue?: string
  /** The spec's `onChange`. Base UI's event details are dropped. */
  onValueChange?: (value: string) => void
  name?: string
  /** Colour of the selected radio. */
  variant?: 'primary' | 'neutral'
  orientation?: 'vertical' | 'horizontal'
  disabled?: boolean
  required?: boolean
  readOnly?: boolean
  validationState?: ValidationState
  className?: string
  'aria-label'?: string
}

/**
 * A set of radios, one of which is selected. A radio is meaningless alone —
 * arrow keys move within its group — so the component is the group, with
 * the radios as flat `options`.
 */
export function RadioGroup({
  ref,
  options,
  label,
  helperText,
  name,
  variant = 'neutral',
  orientation = 'vertical',
  disabled,
  required,
  validationState = 'default',
  className,
  onValueChange,
  ...props
}: RadioGroupProps) {
  // Plain help describes the group once. An error message goes through Field,
  // which puts it on every radio: whichever one has focus, the reader hears
  // what is wrong.
  const helperId = useId()
  const isError = validationState === 'error'
  return (
    <Field.Root
      name={name}
      disabled={disabled}
      invalid={isError}
      className={cn(choiceStyles.field, choiceStyles[validationState], styles.field, className)}
    >
      <Fieldset.Root
        render={
          <BaseRadioGroup
            {...props}
            ref={ref}
            aria-describedby={helperText && !isError ? helperId : undefined}
            required={required}
            onValueChange={onValueChange && ((next) => onValueChange(next as string))}
          />
        }
        className={cn(styles.group, styles[orientation])}
      >
        {label && (
          <Fieldset.Legend className={styles.legend}>
            {label}
            {required && (
              <span aria-hidden="true" className={choiceStyles.required}>
                *
              </span>
            )}
          </Fieldset.Legend>
        )}
        {options.map((option) => (
          <Field.Item key={option.value} disabled={option.disabled} className={styles.item}>
            <Field.Label className={choiceStyles.label}>
              <Radio.Root
                value={option.value}
                className={cn(choiceStyles.control, styles.radio, styles[variant])}
              >
                <Radio.Indicator className={styles.dot} />
              </Radio.Root>
              {option.label}
            </Field.Label>
            {option.helperText && (
              <Field.Description className={cn(choiceStyles.helper, styles.optionHelper)}>
                {option.helperText}
              </Field.Description>
            )}
          </Field.Item>
        ))}
      </Fieldset.Root>
      {helperText &&
        (isError ? (
          <Field.Description className={cn(choiceStyles.helper, styles.groupHelper)}>
            {helperText}
          </Field.Description>
        ) : (
          <p id={helperId} className={cn(choiceStyles.helper, styles.groupHelper)}>
            {helperText}
          </p>
        ))}
    </Field.Root>
  )
}
