      table: { type: { summary: 'string[]' }, defaultValue: { summary: '[]' } },
    },
    onSelectionChange: {
      description: "Called with every selected id. Ids selected on other pages are kept when the header checkbox changes this page's rows.",
      control: false,
      table: { type: { summary: '(ids: string[]) => void' } },
    },
    expandedContent: {
      description:
        'Content shown under a row when it is open, across the full width. Adds an expand button to each row that returns content; a row that returns `null`, `undefined` or `false` gets none. Runs for every row on each render, so keep it cheap.',
      control: false,
      table: { type: { summary: '(row: Row) => ReactNode' } },
    },
    expandedIds: {
      description: 'Controlled expansion: ids from `getRowId`, so sorting keeps the right rows open.',
      control: false,
      table: { type: { summary: 'string[]' } },
    },
    defaultExpandedIds: {
      description: 'The rows open at first when uncontrolled.',
      control: false,
      table: { type: { summary: 'string[]' }, defaultValue: { summary: '[]' } },
    },
    onExpandedChange: {
      description: 'Called with every open id when an expand button is pressed.',
      control: false,
      table: { type: { summary: '(ids: string[]) => void' } },
    },
    rowActions: {
      description:
        'The items of a menu at the end of each row, opened by a "more" button named after the row ("Actions for Atlas"). A row that returns no items gets no button.',
      control: false,
      table: { type: { summary: '(row: Row) => MenuEntry[] | null | undefined' } },
    },
    size: {
      description: 'Deprecated: Table has one size, and `sm` renders the same table as `md`. Drop the prop; it will be removed in the next release. Warns in development for any value but `md`.',
      control: false,
      table: { type: { summary: "'sm' | 'md'" } },
    },
    density: {
      description: 'Deprecated: does nothing, like `size`. Will be removed in the next release.',
      control: false,
      table: { type: { summary: "'sm' | 'md'" } },
    },
    hasStickyHeader: {
      description: 'Keeps the header row in view while the table scrolls inside its container, when something limits the container\'s height.',
      control: 'boolean',
      table: { type: { summary: 'boolean' }, defaultValue: { summary: 'false' } },
    },
    emptyState: {
      description: 'Shown in place of the rows when there are none, e.g. an Empty State.',
      control: false,
      table: { type: { summary: 'ReactNode' } },
    },
    isResizable: {
      description:
        'A handle at the end of each column header that drags, or arrow-keys, the column wider or narrower (48 to 1200px). The table is then laid out by its header widths (`table-layout: fixed`): columns without a `width` share what is left, and what no longer fits is clipped.',
      control: 'boolean',
      table: { type: { summary: 'boolean' }, defaultValue: { summary: 'false' } },
    },
    columnWidths: {
      description: 'Column widths in px, by key, for controlled resizing. Pair with `onColumnWidthsChange`; without it the table keeps its own.',
      control: false,
      table: { type: { summary: 'Record<string, number>' } },
    },
    onColumnWidthsChange: {
      description: 'Called with every resized column\'s width in px while a handle moves. Store it to keep the widths across visits.',
      control: false,
      table: { type: { summary: '(widths: Record<string, number>) => void' } },
    },
    className: {
      description: 'Added to the scroll container around the table.',
      control: false,
      table: { type: { summary: 'string' } },
    },
  },
  excludeStories: ['anatomyParts'],
} satisfies Meta<typeof Table<Project>>

export default meta
type Story = StoryObj<typeof meta>

/** Heights of a row's cell and its header cell, without the header's rule. */
const cellHeights = (canvas: ReturnType<typeof within>) =>
  [canvas.getAllByRole('rowheader')[0], canvas.getAllByRole('columnheader')[0]].map((c: HTMLElement) => c.clientHeight)

/** Text only: a row of these is one 20px line tall. */
const textColumns = columns.filter((c) => c.key !== 'status')

/** Where an element's content is drawn, without its own padding. */
const contentBox = (el: Element) => {
  const range = document.createRange()
  range.selectNodeContents(el)
  return range.getBoundingClientRect()
}

const names = (canvas: ReturnType<typeof within>) => canvas.getAllByRole('rowheader').map((c: HTMLElement) => c.textContent)

export const Default: Story = {
  play: async ({ args, canvas }) => {
    const table = canvas.getByRole('table', { name: 'Projects' })
    await expect(within(table).getAllByRole('row')).toHaveLength(5)
    // 8px above and below the header's 16px line: the sort button adds nothing.
    await expect(cellHeights(canvas)[1]).toBe(32)
    // The header ends on a 1px rule; the rows have no divider.
    await expect(getComputedStyle(canvas.getAllByRole('columnheader')[0]).borderBottomWidth).toBe('1px')
    await expect(getComputedStyle(canvas.getAllByRole('rowheader')[0]).borderBottomWidth).toBe('0px')
    // A table with rows closes on the same rule: 1px, the header's colour, right under the last row.
    const closing = getComputedStyle(table)
    await expect(closing.borderBottomWidth).toBe('1px')
    await expect(closing.borderBottomColor).toBe(getComputedStyle(canvas.getAllByRole('columnheader')[0]).borderBottomColor)
    await expect(table.getBoundingClientRect().bottom - within(table).getAllByRole('row').at(-1)!.getBoundingClientRect().bottom).toBe(1)
    // So a one-line row is 36px all told, and the Tag in it adds nothing.
    const atlas = canvas.getByRole('rowheader', { name: 'Atlas' }).closest('tr')!
    await expect(within(atlas).getByText('Active')).toBeVisible()
    await expect(atlas.getBoundingClientRect().height).toBe(36)
    await expect(names(canvas)).toEqual(['Atlas', 'Billing revamp', 'Onboarding', 'Design tokens'])
    // Sort: ascending, descending, then back to unsorted. aria-sort follows.
    const files = canvas.getByRole('columnheader', { name: /Files/ })
    await expect(files).toHaveAttribute('aria-sort', 'none')
    await userEvent.click(within(files).getByRole('button'))
    await expect(files).toHaveAttribute('aria-sort', 'ascending')
    await expect(args.onSortChange).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith({ key: 'files', direction: 'ascending' })
    await expect(names(canvas)).toEqual(['Design tokens', 'Billing revamp', 'Atlas', 'Onboarding'])
    await userEvent.click(within(files).getByRole('button'))
    await expect(files).toHaveAttribute('aria-sort', 'descending')
    await expect(names(canvas)).toEqual(['Onboarding', 'Atlas', 'Billing revamp', 'Design tokens'])
    await userEvent.click(within(files).getByRole('button'))
    await expect(files).toHaveAttribute('aria-sort', 'none')
    await expect(names(canvas)).toEqual(['Atlas', 'Billing revamp', 'Onboarding', 'Design tokens'])
    // Dates sort as dates, text by locale with numbers in order.
    await userEvent.click(within(canvas.getByRole('columnheader', { name: /Updated/ })).getByRole('button'))
    await expect(names(canvas)[0]).toBe('Design tokens')
  },
}

export const Selectable: Story = {
  args: { isSelectable: true, defaultSelectedIds: ['p2'] },
  play: async ({ args, canvas }) => {
    const all = canvas.getByRole('checkbox', { name: 'Select all rows' })
    // Some selected: the header box is mixed.
    await expect(all).toHaveAttribute('aria-checked', 'mixed')
    // Each row's box is named by the row header.
    // The row itself reports it, too.
    await expect(canvas.getByRole('checkbox', { name: 'Select Billing revamp' }).closest('tr')).toHaveAttribute('aria-selected', 'true')
    await userEvent.click(canvas.getByRole('checkbox', { name: 'Select Atlas' }))
    await expect(args.onSelectionChange).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith(['p2', 'p1'])
    await userEvent.click(all)
    await expect(args.onSelectionChange).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith(['p2', 'p1', 'p3', 'p4'])
    await expect(all).toHaveAttribute('aria-checked', 'true')
    await userEvent.click(all)
    await expect(args.onSelectionChange).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith([])
  },
}

function PagedTable(props: { onSelectionChange: (ids: string[]) => void }) {
  const [page, setPage] = useState(0)
  return (
    <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 'var(--space-3)', justifyItems: 'start' }}>
      <Table
        columns={columns}
        rows={projects.slice(page * 2, page * 2 + 2)}
        getRowId={(p) => p.id}
        caption={`Projects, page ${page + 1} of 2`}
        isSelectable
        onSelectionChange={props.onSelectionChange}
      />
      <Button variant="secondary" appearance="outlined" size="sm" onClick={() => setPage(1 - page)}>
        {page === 0 ? 'Next page' : 'Previous page'}
      </Button>
    </div>
  )
}

/** Selection with getRowId survives paging: "Select all" adds or removes this page's rows only. */
export const Paged: Story = {
  render: (args) => <PagedTable onSelectionChange={args.onSelectionChange!} />,
  play: async ({ args, canvas }) => {
    await userEvent.click(canvas.getByRole('checkbox', { name: 'Select Atlas' }))
    await userEvent.click(canvas.getByRole('button', { name: 'Next page' }))
    const all = canvas.getByRole('checkbox', { name: 'Select all rows' })
    await userEvent.click(all)
    await expect(args.onSelectionChange).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith(['p1', 'p3', 'p4'])
    await userEvent.click(all)
    await expect(args.onSelectionChange).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith(['p1'])
  },
}

/** Rows with no value sort last in both directions. */
export const EmptyValuesSortLast: Story = {
  args: {
    rows: [...projects, { id: 'p5', name: 'Scratch', owner: '', status: 'Paused', files: null as unknown as number, updated: new Date('2026-01-01') }],
    columns: columns.map((c) => (c.key === 'files' ? { ...c, cell: (p: Project) => (p.files == null ? '–' : p.files.toLocaleString('en')) } : c)),
  },
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    const files = within(canvas.getByRole('columnheader', { name: /Files/ })).getByRole('button')
    await userEvent.click(files)
    await expect(names(canvas).at(-1)).toBe('Scratch')
    await userEvent.click(files)
    await expect(names(canvas)).toEqual(['Onboarding', 'Atlas', 'Billing revamp', 'Design tokens', 'Scratch'])
  },
}

/**
 * Every cell, the first and last included, is padded 8px all round. The
 * header has no fill.
 */
export const EdgeCells: Story = {
  tags: ['!dev'],
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    const table = canvas.getByRole('table', { name: 'Projects' }).getBoundingClientRect()
    const row = canvas.getByRole('rowheader', { name: 'Atlas' }).closest('tr')!
    const head = canvas.getAllByRole('columnheader')
    // The first cell's text, and its header's label, start 8px in from the table's left edge.
    await expect(contentBox(row.firstElementChild!).left).toBeCloseTo(table.left + 8, 0)
    await expect(contentBox(within(head[0]).getByRole('button')).left).toBeCloseTo(table.left + 8, 0)
    // The last column is end-aligned: its figures and its label end 8px in from the right edge.
    await expect(contentBox(row.lastElementChild!).right).toBeCloseTo(table.right - 8, 0)
    await expect(contentBox(within(head.at(-1)!).getByRole('button')).right).toBeCloseTo(table.right - 8, 0)
    // Every cell: 8px each side, the edge cells too.
    for (const cell of [row.firstElementChild!, row.children[1], row.lastElementChild!, head[0], head[1], head.at(-1)!]) {
      const { paddingLeft, paddingRight } = getComputedStyle(cell)
      await expect([paddingLeft, paddingRight]).toEqual(['8px', '8px'])
    }
    // No header fill: the container's colour shows through.
    await expect(getComputedStyle(head[0]).backgroundColor).toBe('rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)')
  },
}

/** Passing the documented default of a deprecated prop is silent: only another value warns. */
export const ExplicitDefaultSize: Story = {
  tags: ['!dev'],
  args: { size: 'md' },
  beforeEach: () => {
    spyOn(console, 'warn').mockImplementation(() => {})
  },
  play: async () => {
    await expect(console.warn).not.toHaveBeenCalledWith(expect.stringContaining('Table: `size`'))
  },
}

/** `size` and `density` are deprecated: for one release they are accepted, and `sm` renders as `md`. */
export const DeprecatedSize: Story = {
  tags: ['!dev'],
  args: { size: 'sm', density: 'sm', columns: textColumns },
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    // 8px above and below one 20px line of text, and the header's 16px line.
    await expect(cellHeights(canvas)).toEqual([36, 32])
  },
}

export const Empty: Story = {
  args: {
    rows: [],
    // A total of nothing is noise next to an empty state: no footer row.
    columns: [{ ...columns[0], footer: 'Total' }, ...columns.slice(1)],
    emptyState: (
      <EmptyState
        size="sm"
        headingLevel={3}
        icon={<Icon name="search" />}
        title="No projects match “zeta”"
        action={<Button size="sm" appearance="outlined" variant="accent">Clear search</Button>}
      />
    ),
  },
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    await expect(canvas.getByRole('heading', { name: 'No projects match “zeta”' })).toBeVisible()
    await expect(canvas.getAllByRole('rowgroup')).toHaveLength(2)
    // No rows, no closing rule: only the header's.
    await expect(getComputedStyle(canvas.getByRole('table')).borderBottomWidth).toBe('0px')
  },
}

/** Sorted by the caller (e.g. a server): the table reports the sort and shows the rows as given. */
export const ControlledSort: Story = {
  render: function Render(args) {
    const [sort, setSort] = useState<{ key: string; direction: 'ascending' | 'descending' } | null>(null)
    const rows = sort ? [...projects].sort((a, b) => a.owner.localeCompare(b.owner) * (sort.direction === 'ascending' ? 1 : -1)) : projects
    return <Table {...args} rows={rows} sort={sort} onSortChange={setSort} />
  },
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    await userEvent.click(within(canvas.getByRole('columnheader', { name: /Owner/ })).getByRole('button'))
    await expect(canvas.getAllByRole('row')[1]).toHaveTextContent('Ava Stone')
  },
}

export const StickyHeader: Story = {
  args: {
    hasStickyHeader: true,
    rows: Array.from({ length: 20 }, (_, i) => ({ ...projects[i % 4], id: `r${i}`, name: `${projects[i % 4].name} ${i + 1}` })),
  },
  decorators: [(Story) => <div style={{ blockSize: '20rem', display: 'grid' }}>{Story()}</div>],
}

/** Plain columns: no sort buttons, so nothing in the cells takes focus. */
const plainColumns = columns.map((c) => ({ ...c, sortable: false }))

/**
 * Too narrow for its columns, with nothing focusable in the cells: the scroll
 * box becomes the tab stop, a region named by the caption, so keyboard users
 * can scroll it with the arrow keys.
 */
export const NarrowScroll: Story = {
  args: { columns: plainColumns },
  decorators: [(Story) => <div style={{ inlineSize: '16rem' }}>{Story()}</div>],
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    const region = await canvas.findByRole('region', { name: 'Projects' })
    await expect(region).toHaveAttribute('tabindex', '0')
    // Tab reaches it, with the focus ring; the browser scrolls a focused box with the arrow keys.
    await userEvent.tab()
    await expect(region).toHaveFocus()
    await expect(getComputedStyle(region).outlineStyle).toBe('solid')
  },
}

/** Narrow too, but the sort buttons already reach the scroll box: no extra tab stop. */
export const NarrowWithControls: Story = {
  tags: ['!dev'],
  decorators: NarrowScroll.decorators,
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    const box = canvas.getByRole('table', { name: 'Projects' }).parentElement!
    await waitFor(() => expect(box.scrollWidth).toBeGreaterThan(box.clientWidth))
    await expect(canvas.queryByRole('region')).toBeNull()
    await expect(box).not.toHaveAttribute('tabindex')
  },
}

/** Plain columns that fit: nothing to scroll, so no tab stop. */
export const FitsWithoutControls: Story = {
  tags: ['!dev'],
  args: { columns: plainColumns },
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    const box = canvas.getByRole('table', { name: 'Projects' }).parentElement!
    await waitFor(() => expect(box.scrollWidth).toBeLessThanOrEqual(box.clientWidth))
    await expect(canvas.queryByRole('region')).toBeNull()
    await expect(box).not.toHaveAttribute('tabindex')
  },
}

/** What an open row shows; archived projects have nothing to add, so no button. */
const details = (p: Project) =>
  p.status === 'Archived' ? null : (
    <p style={{ margin: 0 }}>
      {p.owner} owns {p.name}: {p.files.toLocaleString('en')} files, last updated {date.format(p.updated)}.
    </p>
  )

/** The text of each body row in order, open rows' content included. */
const rowTexts = (canvas: ReturnType<typeof within>): string[] =>
  canvas
    .getAllByRole('row')
    .slice(1)
    .map((r: HTMLElement) => r.textContent ?? '')

export const ExpandableRows: Story = {
  args: { expandedContent: details, isSelectable: true },
  play: async ({ args, canvas, step }) => {
    const atlas = canvas.getByRole('button', { name: 'Expand Atlas' })
    await step('A row with no content has no button', async () => {
      await expect(canvas.queryByRole('button', { name: 'Expand Design tokens' })).toBeNull()
    })
    await step('Click opens and closes, aria-expanded follows', async () => {
      await expect(atlas).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false')
      await userEvent.click(atlas)
      await expect(atlas).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true')
      await expect(args.onExpandedChange).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith(['p1'])
      const content = canvas.getByText(/Sam Rivera owns Atlas/)
      await expect(atlas).toHaveAttribute('aria-controls', content.closest('td')!.id)
      // The content spans the whole row, checkbox and button columns included.
      await expect(content.closest('td')).toHaveAttribute('colspan', String(columns.length + 2))
      await userEvent.click(atlas)
      await expect(atlas).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false')
      await expect(canvas.queryByText(/Sam Rivera owns Atlas/)).toBeNull()
    })
    await step('Enter and Space toggle from the keyboard', async () => {
      const billing = canvas.getByRole('button', { name: 'Expand Billing revamp' })
      billing.focus()
      await userEvent.keyboard('{Enter}')
      await expect(billing).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true')
      await userEvent.keyboard(' ')
      await expect(billing).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false')
      await userEvent.keyboard('{Enter}')
    })
    await step('Sorting keeps the same row open, its content right under it', async () => {
      await userEvent.click(within(canvas.getByRole('columnheader', { name: /Files/ })).getByRole('button'))
      await expect(names(canvas)).toEqual(['Design tokens', 'Billing revamp', 'Atlas', 'Onboarding'])
      const texts = rowTexts(canvas)
      const at = texts.findIndex((t) => t.includes('Billing revamp') && !t.includes('owns'))
      await expect(texts[at + 1]).toMatch(/Mia Chen owns Billing revamp/)
      await expect(canvas.getByRole('button', { name: 'Expand Billing revamp' })).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true')
      await expect(canvas.getByRole('button', { name: 'Expand Atlas' })).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false')
    })
    await step('Selecting a row leaves expansion alone', async () => {
      await userEvent.click(canvas.getByRole('checkbox', { name: 'Select Billing revamp' }))
      await userEvent.click(canvas.getByRole('checkbox', { name: 'Select all rows' }))
      await expect(args.onSelectionChange).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith(['p2', 'p4', 'p1', 'p3'])
      await expect(canvas.getByRole('button', { name: 'Expand Billing revamp' })).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true')
      await expect(args.onExpandedChange).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith(['p2'])
    })
  },
}

/** Opened from outside the table: `expandedIds` is the source of truth. */
export const ControlledExpansion: Story = {
  args: { expandedContent: details },
  render: function Render(args) {
    const [open, setOpen] = useState<string[]>([])
    return (
      <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 'var(--space-3)', justifyItems: 'start' }}>
        <Button variant="secondary" appearance="outlined" size="sm" onClick={() => setOpen(open.includes('p3') ? [] : ['p3'])}>
          {open.includes('p3') ? 'Close Onboarding' : 'Open Onboarding'}
        </Button>
        <Table
          {...args}
          expandedIds={open}
          onExpandedChange={(ids) => {
            setOpen(ids)
            args.onExpandedChange?.(ids)
          }}
        />
      </div>
    )
  },
  play: async ({ args, canvas }) => {
    const onboarding = canvas.getByRole('button', { name: 'Expand Onboarding' })
    await userEvent.click(canvas.getByRole('button', { name: 'Open Onboarding' }))
    await expect(onboarding).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true')
    await expect(canvas.getByText(/Leo Park owns Onboarding/)).toBeVisible()
    // The row's own button reports back; the caller decides.
    await userEvent.click(onboarding)
    await expect(args.onExpandedChange).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith([])
    await expect(onboarding).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false')
    await expect(canvas.getByRole('button', { name: 'Open Onboarding' })).toBeVisible()
  },
}

/** What each row's menu does; archived projects have no actions, so no button. */
const onAction = fn()
const actions = (p: Project): MenuEntry[] =>
  p.status === 'Archived'
    ? []
    : [
        { label: 'Edit', onSelect: () => onAction('edit', p.id) },
        { label: 'Duplicate', onSelect: () => onAction('duplicate', p.id) },
        { type: 'separator' },
        { label: 'Archive', isDestructive: true, onSelect: () => onAction('archive', p.id) },
      ]

/**
 * A row is as tall as what it holds. One line of text is 36px, and the
 * checkbox, the expand button and the actions button all fit in that; a
 * 32px button in a cell makes its row 48px.
 */
export const RowWithControl: Story = {
  tags: ['!dev'],
  args: {
    isSelectable: true,
    expandedContent: details,
    rowActions: actions,
    columns: [...textColumns, { key: 'open', header: 'Open', cell: (p) => (p.id === 'p1' ? <Button appearance="outlined">Open</Button> : null) }],
  },
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    const [atlas, billing] = canvas.getAllByRole('rowheader')
    await expect([atlas.clientHeight, billing.clientHeight]).toEqual([48, 36])
    await expect(cellHeights(canvas)[1]).toBe(32)
    // No divider: the row is exactly as tall as its cells.
    await expect(billing.closest('tr')!.getBoundingClientRect().height).toBe(36)
  },
}

/** The control columns at the edges: the expand button first, the actions button last, each 8px in from the edge. */
export const EdgeControls: Story = {
  tags: ['!dev'],
  args: { expandedContent: details, defaultExpandedIds: ['p1'], rowActions: actions },
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    const table = canvas.getByRole('table', { name: 'Projects' }).getBoundingClientRect()
    const expand = canvas.getByRole('button', { name: 'Expand Atlas' })
    const more = canvas.getByRole('button', { name: 'Actions for Atlas' })
    await expect(expand.getBoundingClientRect().left).toBeCloseTo(table.left + 8, 0)
    await expect(more.getBoundingClientRect().right).toBeCloseTo(table.right - 8, 0)
    // The open row's content lines up with the cells' text.
    await expect(contentBox(canvas.getByText(/Sam Rivera owns Atlas/)).left).toBeCloseTo(table.left + 8, 0)
    // The cell has no room for an outset ring: the rings are drawn inside the buttons.
    // Tab first, so the focus that follows counts as keyboard focus.
    await userEvent.tab()
    for (const button of [expand, more]) {
      button.focus()
      await expect(getComputedStyle(button).outlineStyle).toBe('solid')
      await expect(getComputedStyle(button).outlineOffset).toBe('-2px')
    }
  },
}

/** The menu renders into <body>, outside the story's canvas. */
const page = (el: HTMLElement) => within(el.ownerDocument.body)

/** A menu at the end of each row, for actions on that one record. */
export const RowActions: Story = {
  args: { rowActions: actions, isSelectable: true },
  play: async ({ canvas, step }) => {
    await step('The column has a hidden header, and a row with no items has no button', async () => {
      await expect(canvas.getByRole('columnheader', { name: 'Actions' })).toBeInTheDocument()
      await expect(canvas.queryByRole('button', { name: 'Actions for Design tokens' })).toBeNull()
    })
    await step('The button is named after the row and opens its menu', async () => {
      const atlas = canvas.getByRole('button', { name: 'Actions for Atlas' })
      await expect(atlas).toHaveAttribute('aria-haspopup', 'menu')
      await userEvent.click(atlas)
      await userEvent.click(await page(atlas).findByRole('menuitem', { name: 'Archive' }))
      await expect(onAction).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith('archive', 'p1')
      await waitFor(() => expect(atlas).toHaveFocus())
    })
    await step('Enter opens it from the keyboard; Escape closes it', async () => {
      const billing = canvas.getByRole('button', { name: 'Actions for Billing revamp' })
      billing.focus()
      await userEvent.keyboard('{Enter}')
      const menu = await page(billing).findByRole('menu')
      await waitFor(() => expect(menu).toBeVisible())
      await userEvent.keyboard('{Escape}')
      await waitFor(() => expect(billing).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false'))
      await waitFor(() => expect(billing).toHaveFocus())
    })
  },
}

/** Files summed in a footer row that sorting leaves at the bottom. */
const totalled: TableColumn<Project>[] = columns.map((c) =>
  c.key === 'name'
    ? { ...c, footer: 'Total' }
    : c.key === 'files'
      ? { ...c, footer: projects.reduce((n, p) => n + p.files, 0).toLocaleString('en') }
      : c,
)

export const TotalRow: Story = {
  args: { columns: totalled, isSelectable: true, expandedContent: details },
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    const [, body, foot] = canvas.getAllByRole('rowgroup')
    await expect(within(body).getAllByRole('row')).toHaveLength(4)
    // The label is the total row's header, so its cells read "Total, Files".
    await expect(within(foot).getByRole('rowheader', { name: 'Total' })).toBeInTheDocument()
    await expect(within(foot).getAllByRole('cell').map((c) => c.textContent)).toContain('1,464')
    // One cell per column, the checkbox and expand columns included, so it lines up.
    await expect(within(foot).getByRole('row').children).toHaveLength(canvas.getAllByRole('columnheader').length)
    // The header's 1px rule, over the total: 36px of row under it.
    const total = within(foot).getByRole('rowheader', { name: 'Total' })
    await expect(getComputedStyle(total).borderTopWidth).toBe('1px')
    // The table's closing rule sits under the total row.
    const table = canvas.getByRole('table')
    await expect(getComputedStyle(table).borderBottomWidth).toBe('1px')
    await expect(table.getBoundingClientRect().bottom - total.getBoundingClientRect().bottom).toBe(1)
    await expect(total.clientHeight).toBe(36)
    // Sorting moves the rows, never the total.
    await userEvent.click(within(canvas.getByRole('columnheader', { name: /Files/ })).getByRole('button'))
    await expect(canvas.getAllByRole('row').at(-1)).toHaveTextContent('Total')
  },
}

/** Drag or arrow-key a header's end edge to resize its column. */
export const Resizable: Story = {
  args: { isResizable: true, onColumnWidthsChange: fn() },
  play: async ({ args, canvas, step }) => {
    const owner = canvas.getByRole('columnheader', { name: /Owner/ })
    const handle = canvas.getByRole('separator', { name: 'Resize Owner' })
    await step('Every column header has a focusable vertical separator with its width as the value', async () => {
      await expect(canvas.getAllByRole('separator')).toHaveLength(columns.length)
      await expect(handle).toHaveAttribute('aria-orientation', 'vertical')
      await expect(handle).toHaveAttribute('aria-valuemin', '48')
      await expect(handle).toHaveAttribute('aria-valuemax', '1200')
      await waitFor(() => expect(Number(handle.getAttribute('aria-valuenow'))).toBe(Math.round(owner.getBoundingClientRect().width)))
    })
    await step('Arrow Right widens the column by 16px, Arrow Left narrows it', async () => {
      handle.focus()
      const before = Number(handle.getAttribute('aria-valuenow'))
      await userEvent.keyboard('{ArrowRight}')
      await expect(handle).toHaveAttribute('aria-valuenow', String(before + 16))
      await expect(args.onColumnWidthsChange).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith({ owner: before + 16 })
      await waitFor(() => expect(Math.round(owner.getBoundingClientRect().width)).toBe(before + 16))
      await userEvent.keyboard('{ArrowLeft}{ArrowLeft}')
      await expect(handle).toHaveAttribute('aria-valuenow', String(before - 16))
    })
    await step('End sets the widest width, Home the narrowest', async () => {
      await userEvent.keyboard('{End}')
      await expect(handle).toHaveAttribute('aria-valuenow', '1200')
      await userEvent.keyboard('{Home}')
      await expect(handle).toHaveAttribute('aria-valuenow', '48')
      await waitFor(() => expect(Math.round(owner.getBoundingClientRect().width)).toBe(48))
    })
    await step('Dragging the handle resizes by the distance moved', async () => {
      const files = canvas.getByRole('separator', { name: 'Resize Files' })
      const th = canvas.getByRole('columnheader', { name: /Files/ })
      const from = Math.round(th.getBoundingClientRect().width)
      const { x, y } = files.getBoundingClientRect()
      await userEvent.pointer([
        { keys: '[MouseLeft>]', target: files, coords: { clientX: x, clientY: y } },
        { target: files, coords: { clientX: x + 40, clientY: y } },
        { keys: '[/MouseLeft]', target: files, coords: { clientX: x + 40, clientY: y } },
      ])
      await expect(files).toHaveAttribute('aria-valuenow', String(from + 40))
      await waitFor(() => expect(Math.round(th.getBoundingClientRect().width)).toBe(from + 40))
    })
  },
}

/** Right to left: the handle is on the header's left edge, so Arrow Left widens. */
export const ResizableRtl: Story = {
  args: { isResizable: true },
  render: (args) => (
    <div dir="rtl">
      <Table {...args} />
    </div>
  ),
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    const handle = canvas.getByRole('separator', { name: 'Resize Owner' })
    await waitFor(() => expect(Number(handle.getAttribute('aria-valuenow'))).toBeGreaterThan(48))
    const before = Number(handle.getAttribute('aria-valuenow'))
    handle.focus()
    await userEvent.keyboard('{ArrowLeft}')
    await expect(handle).toHaveAttribute('aria-valuenow', String(before + 16))
    await userEvent.keyboard('{ArrowRight}{ArrowRight}')
    await expect(handle).toHaveAttribute('aria-valuenow', String(before - 16))
  },
}

/** Widths owned by the caller: the handle reports, the caller decides. */
export const ControlledWidths: Story = {
  args: { isResizable: true, columnWidths: { name: 200 }, onColumnWidthsChange: fn() },
  play: async ({ args, canvas }) => {
    const handle = canvas.getByRole('separator', { name: 'Resize Project' })
    await expect(handle).toHaveAttribute('aria-valuenow', '200')
    handle.focus()
    await userEvent.keyboard('{ArrowRight}')
    await expect(args.onColumnWidthsChange).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith({ name: 216 })
    // Not stored by the caller, so it stays where it was.
    await expect(handle).toHaveAttribute('aria-valuenow', '200')
  },
}

/** The parts the Specs tab numbers, each found by a selector inside the `Anatomy` story. */
export const anatomyParts = [
  { name: 'Caption', selector: 'caption', description: 'Names the table. Visually hidden unless showCaption.' },
  { name: 'Header row', selector: 'thead tr', description: 'Small semibold labels over a 1px rule, with no fill. Stays in view with hasStickyHeader.' },
  { name: 'Sort button', selector: 'th[aria-sort] button', description: 'The whole header label, with an icon for the sort. Only on sortable columns.' },
  { name: 'Select all', selector: 'thead [role="checkbox"]', description: 'With isSelectable. Selects or clears every row shown, and shows mixed when some are selected.' },
  { name: 'Row', selector: 'tbody tr', description: 'As tall as what it holds: 36px for one line of text. No divider: tinted when hovered or selected.' },
  { name: 'Row checkbox', selector: 'tbody [role="checkbox"]', description: 'Named after the row header: "Select Atlas".' },
  { name: 'Expand button', selector: 'tbody [aria-expanded]', description: 'With expandedContent: a ghost icon button. The chevron turns down when open.' },
  { name: 'Row header', selector: 'tbody th[scope="row"]', description: 'The column marked isRowHeader, medium weight: the name a row is known by.' },
  { name: 'Row actions', selector: 'tbody [aria-haspopup="menu"]', description: 'With rowActions: a ghost "more" button at the end of the row that opens a Menu.' },
  {
    name: 'Expanded row',
    selector: 'tbody td[colspan]',
    description: 'One cell spanning every column, under its row. Holds any layout.',
  },
  { name: 'Total row', selector: 'tfoot tr', description: 'With a footer on any column: a semibold row under a 1px rule, outside the sort.' },
]

/** Every part present: caption shown, a sortable column, selection, one row open, row actions, a total. */
export const Anatomy: Story = {
  tags: ['!dev'],
  args: {
    showCaption: true,
    isSelectable: true,
    expandedContent: details,
    defaultExpandedIds: ['p1'],
    rowActions: actions,
    // Every project, so the total matches the rows on screen.
    columns: totalled,
  },
  play: async ({ canvasElement, canvas }) => {
    const found = await expectAnatomy(canvasElement, anatomyParts)
    await expect(found[7]).toHaveTextContent('Atlas')
    await expect(found[9]).toHaveTextContent(/Sam Rivera owns Atlas/)
    await expect(found[10]).toHaveTextContent('Total')
    // Cells padded 8px all round, the caption 24px from the top and 8px from the table.
    const cell = getComputedStyle(found[7])
    await expect([cell.paddingTop, cell.paddingRight, cell.paddingBottom, cell.paddingLeft]).toEqual(['8px', '8px', '8px', '8px'])
    const caption = getComputedStyle(found[0])
    await expect([caption.paddingTop, caption.paddingBottom]).toEqual(['24px', '8px'])
    // 8px in from the table's edges, as the cells' text: the caption and the checkbox at the start, the actions button at the end.
    const table = canvas.getByRole('table').getBoundingClientRect()
    await expect(contentBox(found[0]).left).toBeCloseTo(table.left + 8, 0)
    await expect(found[5].getBoundingClientRect().left).toBeCloseTo(table.left + 8, 0)
    await expect(found[8].getBoundingClientRect().right).toBeCloseTo(table.right - 8, 0)
    // The checkbox column is the 16px box with 8px either side; the expand column, its 24px button with 8px either side.
    await expect([found[5].closest('td')!.clientWidth, found[6].closest('td')!.clientWidth]).toEqual([32, 40])
    await expect(canvas.getByRole('columnheader', { name: 'Actions' })).toBeInTheDocument()
    // The expand column is announced like the others, by a hidden header.
    await expect(canvas.getByRole('columnheader', { name: 'Details' })).toBeInTheDocument()
  },
}

/** Two columns and two rows, small enough for the Specs tab's States to sit side by side. */
const brief = { columns: columns.filter((c) => c.key === 'name' || c.key === 'files'), rows: projects.slice(0, 2) }

/** Specs, States: the plain table. */
export const StateEnabled: Story = { tags: ['!dev'], args: brief }

/** Specs, States: sorted by Files, ascending. */
export const StateSorted: Story = { tags: ['!dev'], args: { ...brief, defaultSort: { key: 'files', direction: 'ascending' } } }

/** Specs, States: Atlas selected. */
export const StateSelected: Story = { tags: ['!dev'], args: { ...brief, isSelectable: true, defaultSelectedIds: ['p1'] } }

/** Specs, States: Atlas open. */
export const StateExpanded: Story = { tags: ['!dev'], args: { ...brief, expandedContent: details, defaultExpandedIds: ['p1'] } }

/** Guidelines, Don't: numbers at the start, so the digits do not line up. */
export const DontNumbersAtStart: Story = {
  tags: ['!dev'],
  args: { columns: columns.map(({ align: _align, ...c }) => c) },
}

/** Guidelines, Don't: no row header, so a row's checkbox can only say which number it is. */
export const DontNoRowHeader: Story = {
  tags: ['!dev'],
  args: { isSelectable: true, columns: columns.map(({ isRowHeader: _isRowHeader, ...c }) => c) },
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    // Counted from `rows`, so a sort does not rename it; but "row 1" says nothing.
    await expect(canvas.getByRole('checkbox', { name: 'Select row 1' })).toBeInTheDocument()
    await expect(canvas.queryByRole('rowheader')).toBeNull()
    // Sorted by Files, Atlas moves to the third row and keeps its name.
    await userEvent.click(within(canvas.getByRole('columnheader', { name: /Files/ })).getByRole('button'))
    await expect(canvas.getByRole('checkbox', { name: 'Select row 1' }).closest('tr')).toHaveTextContent('Atlas')
    await expect(canvas.getAllByRole('row')[3]).toHaveTextContent('Atlas')
  },
}

<DocTab value="overview">

Rows of records with the same fields, to scan and compare: projects,
invoices, members. Columns can sort, rows can be selected, expanded and
acted on, and a total row can sum them up.

<Status of={TableStories} />

<Canvas of={TableStories.Selectable} />

## Variants

Table has one size: 8px round each cell, so a row of text is
36px, and a row that holds a button or a field grows to fit it. Any table
takes any of these together: a selectable table can also expand its rows
and keep its header in view.

| Variant | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `isSelectable` | Acting on several rows at once: archive, export, assign. |
| `expandedContent` | Details that belong to one row but do not fit in a column: a description, a timeline, line items. |
| `hasStickyHeader` | Long tables that scroll inside a fixed height, so the column names stay in view. |
| `rowActions` | Actions on one record (edit, duplicate, archive) that do not earn a column: a menu at the row's end. |
| `footer` on a column | A total row under the rows: sums, counts, averages. |
| `isResizable` | Tables whose columns hold text of unknown length (names, notes, emails), so people can widen what they read. |
| `emptyState` | Saying why there are no rows, and what to do: clear a search, add the first one. |

<Canvas of={TableStories.Default} />

Rows with details open under themselves. Expansion is independent of
selection and survives sorting:

<Canvas of={TableStories.ExpandableRows} />

A menu at the end of each row. A row with nothing to do gets no button:

<Canvas of={TableStories.RowActions} />

A total row under the rows, which sorting leaves at the bottom. The table
does not add anything up: you pass each column's `footer`, so you decide
whether it totals this page or every row.

<Canvas of={TableStories.TotalRow} />

A handle on each header's end edge resizes its column, by dragging or by
the arrow keys. The table is then laid out by its header widths: give the
columns a starting `width`, and keep `columnWidths` if they should last.
Pair it with a [Column Chooser](?path=/docs/components-data-display-column-chooser--docs)
to hide columns as well.

<Canvas of={TableStories.Resizable} />

<Canvas of={TableStories.StickyHeader} />

<Canvas of={TableStories.Empty} />

## Resources

From npm, or copied into your project through the registry:

```js
import { Table, type TableColumn } from 'zweihander/table'
```

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/table.json
```

- Source: [src/components/data-display/Table.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/data-display/Table.tsx)
- Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/table](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/table)
- Behaviour: a native `<table>`; selection uses the kit's [Checkbox](?path=/docs/components-controls-checkbox--docs), expansion its [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs), row actions its [Menu](?path=/docs/components-navigation-menu--docs)
- Figma: not in the library yet

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="specs">

## Anatomy

<Anatomy parts={TableStories.anatomyParts}>
  <Story of={TableStories.Anatomy} />
</Anatomy>

The table sits in a container that scrolls sideways on a narrow screen
rather than squeezing the columns. The selection column comes first, then
the expand column; the actions column comes last. A row whose
`expandedContent` or `rowActions` returns nothing leaves that cell empty.
The total row is a `<tfoot>`, so it stays at the bottom whatever the sort.

## Measurements

A row has no height of its own: it is as tall as what its cells hold.

| What the row holds | Row height |
| --- | --- |
| One line of text (20px), or a Tag | 36px |
| A checkbox, an expand button or an actions button (24px) | 36px |
| A 24px button | 40px |
| A 32px button or field | 48px |
| Header (one 16px line) | 32px |

A body row is exactly that tall: there is no divider under it. The header
and the total row add their 1px rule, and a table that has rows adds one
more under its last row. The checkbox, expand and actions
columns take 2px less block padding than the other cells, so their 24px
buttons do not make a row of text taller.

<SpecTable
  caption="Resize handle (isResizable)"
  rows={[
    { part: 'Handle', property: 'Width', token: '--box-2xs' },

The handle line is 1px at rest; no token covers a hairline. Its strip is 16px wide (44px on touch screens), at the
header's end, over the header's own padding. The last column's handle sits on the table's edge and shows its line
only on hover and drag. A column is 48px to 1200px wide; the arrow
keys move it 16px at a time.

Rows have no divider between them: the hover tint and the selection fill
tell them apart. The header ends on a 1px rule and its labels are
semibold; the total row sits under the same rule, so the sum reads as a
sum. A table that has rows closes on that rule too, as Atlassian's dynamic
table: under the last row, an open row's content or the total row,
whichever comes last. It is the table's own border, so under a sticky
header it scrolls with the rows, and whatever a page puts under the table
(a Pagination, a footer) keeps its own gap below the rule. An empty table
has no closing rule: the header's is the only one over the empty state.
The sort button pulls itself out
by its own padding, so its label lines up with the cells below and its
hover fill adds nothing to the header's height.

**Every cell is padded 8px all round**, the first and last of a row
included: the first column's text, the caption and an open row's content
all start 8px in from the table's left edge, and an end-aligned last
column ends 8px short of its right edge. The control columns are their
control with 8px either side: 32px for the 16px checkbox, 40px for the
24px expand and actions buttons. Focus rings in the control columns are
drawn inside the control, because the cell has no room for an outset
ring. Figures are tabular, so numbers line up column-wide.

- The header has no fill. With `hasStickyHeader` it takes the container's
  own `--color-surface-raised`, only so the rows scroll under it.
- Rows are not striped, and have no divider: hover and selection tint
  the row under the pointer or the checkbox, from edge to edge.
- The sort icon of a column that is not sorted is `--color-text-subtlest`;
  the sorted column's is the brand colour.
- **Two selected rows next to each other** read as one filled block;
  each row's checkbox says which are in it.
- **An open row and its content read as one block**: the content row
  shares its row's hover and selected tint, and its 16px block-end padding
  sets the pair apart from the next row.

## States

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={TableStories.StateEnabled} />
</States>

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
    { label: 'Pressed', pseudo: 'active' },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={TableStories.StateEnabled} />
</States>

<States
  states={[
    { label: 'Sorted', content: <Story of={TableStories.StateSorted} /> },
    { label: 'Selected', content: <Story of={TableStories.StateSelected} /> },
  ]}
/>

<States states={[{ label: 'Expanded', content: <Story of={TableStories.StateExpanded} /> }]} />

Each example forces the state on every row and button at once; on screen
it is the one under the pointer or the keyboard.

- **Hover** tints the row with `--color-background-neutral`, and the sort button too. The
  content row of an open row takes no hover of its own, only its row's.
- **Focus** is a 2px `--color-border-focused` outline, drawn 2px inside the sort button.
  The checkboxes and the expand button keep
  their own focus rings.
- **Pressed** has no look of its own: the click sorts, selects or opens,
  and that state's look follows.
- **Resize handle**: hover and drag thicken its line to 2px `--color-background-brand-bold`;
  focus draws the `--color-border-focused` outline inside the handle.
- **Disabled**: Table has none. A row that cannot be acted on is a row
  without the control.
- **Sorted** shows the column's icon at full colour, pointing up or down.
- **Selected** tints the row with `--color-background-brand-subtlest`.
- **Expanded** turns the chevron to point down and opens the content row
  under it.

## API

{/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
<div style={{ overflowX: 'auto' }}>
  <ArgTypes of={TableStories} />
</div>

`TableColumn<Row>` describes one column:

- `key`: unique; also the row field shown when there is no `cell`.
- `header`: the column's label.
- `cell`: renders the cell; defaults to `row[key]`.
- `sortable`: adds a sort button to the header. It sorts by `sortValue`,
  or by `row[key]`.
- `align`: `start`, `center` or `end`. `end` for numbers and dates, so the
  digits line up.
- `width`: any CSS width, e.g. `8rem` or `20%`.
- `isRowHeader`: makes the column's cells `<th scope="row">`, the name a
  row is known by. Usually the first column.
- `footer`: this column's cell in the total row, e.g. a sum. Any column
  with one adds the row; put the label ("Total") on the row header column.
  Hidden while there are no rows.

`TableSort` is `{ key, direction }`, with direction `ascending` or
`descending`.

`size` and `density` are deprecated. Table has one size, as Atlassian's
does: `size="sm"` (and `density="sm"`) renders the same table as `md`.
Both are still accepted for one release; drop them. The kit's rule for a
deprecated prop: it warns in the development console when it is passed a
value that is not its documented default, and a renamed prop warns
whenever it is used. So `size="sm"` and any `density` warn, and
`size="md"`, the default written out, is silent.

With `sort` controlled, the table leaves the order to you. `sortRows(rows,
columns, sort)` returns the rows in the order the table would sort them,
so you can sort every row before slicing out a page.

### Differences from the spec

Cell sizing follows the Figma library: Atlassian's dynamic table with 8px
round every cell.

- **No row height, and one size.** A cell has 8px padding all round
  and the row is as tall as its content; rows were a fixed 48px
  and 40px before, picked by `density` and then `size`, which are
  deprecated.
- **No row dividers.** Only the 1px rule under the header and the one
  that closes a table with rows, as Atlassian draws them; rows are told
  apart by the hover tint and the selection fill.
- **The total row has a 1px rule above it.** Atlassian's table has no
  total row; the rule is the header's, turned over. The table's closing
  rule then sits under the total row.
- **No header fill, and padded edges.** The header is its labels over the
  rule, as Atlassian's dynamic table. Unlike Atlassian's, the first and
  last cells keep their 8px at the table's edge. The hover and selection
  tints run edge to edge.
- **The caption** sits 24px from the top and 8px above the table, 8px in
  from the edge where the cells' text starts. Its type stays the cells' size,
  semibold; Atlassian's is a 20px heading.

</DocTab>
<DocTab value="guidelines">

## When to use

Use a Table for records that share their fields, when people compare them
or look one up: projects, invoices, members. Align numbers and dates to the
end, and mark the column a row is known by with `isRowHeader`.

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={TableStories.Default} />}
  doCaption="Numbers and dates aligned to the end, in tabular figures: the digits line up column-wide."
  dont={<Story of={TableStories.DontNumbersAtStart} />}
  dontCaption="Aligned to the start, 9 sits under the 1 of 1,203, and the column cannot be compared at a glance."
/>

<DoDont
  do={<Story of={TableStories.Selectable} />}
  doCaption="A row header names each row, so its checkbox reads “Select Atlas”."
  dont={<Story of={TableStories.DontNoRowHeader} />}
  dontCaption="Without one, every checkbox is “Select row 1”, “Select row 2”: a screen reader user cannot tell what they select."
/>

**Sort cycles ascending, descending, off.** The third click returns to the
original order, which is often the one that meant something. Uncontrolled,
the table sorts a copy: dates as dates, numbers as numbers, text by locale
with "file 2" before "file 10". Empty values sort last both ways.

<Canvas of={TableStories.EmptyValuesSortLast} />

With server-side sorting, pass `sort` and `onSortChange` and hand back the
rows already sorted:

<Canvas of={TableStories.ControlledSort} />

**Paging is not built in.** Put a
[Pagination](?path=/docs/components-navigation-pagination--docs) under the
table and pass it one page of `rows`. With `getRowId`, selection keeps
working across pages: "Select all" adds or removes this page's rows only.

<Canvas of={TableStories.Paged} />

Pass `expandedIds` to open rows from outside the table:

<Canvas of={TableStories.ControlledExpansion} />

## When not to use

- **For records that do not share fields**, or that are read one at a
  time, like products in a shop. Use [Cards](?path=/docs/components-data-display-card--docs).
- **For layout.** A table announces rows and columns to a screen reader;
  use CSS grid to place things side by side.
- **For a spreadsheet**, where arrow keys move between cells and cells
  are edited in place. Table is a plain table, not an ARIA grid; the kit
  has no data grid yet.

## Accessibility

- A real `<table>` named by its `<caption>`, with `<th scope="col">`
  headers and a `<th scope="row">` for the row header column: screen
  readers announce the column and the row for every cell.
- Sortable headers carry `aria-sort` (`ascending`, `descending` or
  `none`); the sort control is a button inside the header.
- Row checkboxes are named after the row header ("Select Atlas"), or
  "Select row 1" without one, counted from `rows` so a sort does not
  rename them. The header checkbox is "Select all rows" and reports
  `mixed` when some are selected. A selected row has `aria-selected`.
- Each expand button is named after the row header ("Expand Atlas"),
  reports `aria-expanded`, and while open points at the content cell with
  `aria-controls`. Enter and Space toggle it. The name stays the same open
  or closed; `aria-expanded` carries the state.
- A row with nothing to expand has no button.
- The expand column's header is "Details", visually hidden, so the column
  is announced like the others.
- The content cell spans every column, so it is read as one cell under its
  row.
- Each row actions button is named after the row header ("Actions for
  Atlas") and reports `aria-haspopup="menu"`. Enter opens the menu,
  Escape closes it, and focus returns to the button. A row with no items
  has no button.
- The actions column's header is "Actions", visually hidden.
- When the table is wider than its box and nothing in it takes focus, the
  scroll box becomes a tab stop with a focus ring: `role="region"` named by
  the caption, which the browser scrolls with the arrow keys. A table that
  fits, or whose cells hold a control (a sort button, a checkbox), gets no
  extra tab stop.
- With `isResizable`, each column header holds a focusable
  `role="separator"` with `aria-orientation="vertical"`, named "Resize"
  and the header ("Resize Owner"), or the column's `key` when the header
  is not plain text. Its `aria-valuenow` is the column's
  width in px, between `aria-valuemin` 48 and `aria-valuemax` 1200.
- Arrow Right widens the column 16px and Arrow Left narrows it (mirrored
  in right-to-left); Home sets the narrowest width and End the widest.
  Dragging the handle does the same with a pointer.
- The total row is in a `<tfoot>` with one cell per column, so each total
  is announced under its column; the label column is its row header.

import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-vite'
import { expect } from 'storybook/test'
import { Button } from '@/components/buttons/Button'
import { TextInput } from '@/components/inputs/TextInput'
import { ACCENT_COLORS, GRAY_COLORS, Theme } from '@/theme/Theme'
import docs from './docs.module.css'

function Panel({ label }: { label: string }) {
  return (
    <div
      className={docs.card}
      style={{ display: 'flex', flexDirection: 'column', gap: 'var(--space-3)', background: 'var(--color-surface-raised)', color: 'var(--color-text)' }}
    >
      <span style={{ fontSize: 'var(--text-body)', fontWeight: 500 }}>{label}</span>
      <TextInput label="Email" placeholder="you@example.com" />
      <div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 'var(--space-2)' }}>
        <Button>Primary</Button>
        <Button variant="secondary">Secondary</Button>
      </div>
    </div>
  )
}

// Narrative and prose live in Overview.mdx.
const meta = {
  title: 'Foundations/Overview',
  component: Theme,
  parameters: { layout: 'padded' },
} satisfies Meta<typeof Theme>

export default meta
type Story = StoryObj<typeof meta>

export const AccentColor: Story = {
  name: 'Accent color',
  render: () => (
    <div className={docs.stackWide} style={{ gap: 'var(--space-4)' }}>
      <div style={{ display: 'flex', flexWrap: 'wrap', gap: 'var(--space-2)' }}>
        {ACCENT_COLORS.map((accent) => (
          <Theme key={accent} accentColor={accent} render={<Button size="sm" />}>
            {accent}
          </Theme>
        ))}
      </div>
      <p className={docs.note}>
        Every label above clears 4.5:1 on its own fill — the warm hues take dark
        labels rather than white.
      </p>
    </div>
  ),
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    const solid = (name: string) =>
      getComputedStyle(canvas.getByRole('button', { name })).backgroundColor
    // Changing the accent has to actually move --color-background-brand-bold.
    await expect(solid('blue')).not.toBe(solid('red'))
  },
}

export const GrayColor: Story = {
  name: 'Gray color',

    <div className={docs.gridThirds}>

export const Appearance: Story = {
  render: () => (
    <div className={docs.gridHalves} style={{ gap: 'var(--space-4)' }}>
      <Theme appearance="light" style={{ borderRadius: 'var(--radius-panel)', background: 'var(--color-surface)', padding: 'var(--space-4)' }}>
        <Panel label="appearance=&quot;light&quot;" />
      </Theme>
      <Theme appearance="dark" style={{ borderRadius: 'var(--radius-panel)', background: 'var(--color-surface)', padding: 'var(--space-4)' }}>

export const TokenOverride: Story = {
  // Shows a consumer's own --color-background-brand-bold override; its contrast is the consumer's, not the kit's.
  parameters: { a11y: { test: 'off' } },
  name: 'Token override',
  render: () => (
    <div className={docs.gridHalves} style={{ gap: 'var(--space-4)' }}>

        <Panel label="default tokens" />
      </Theme>

        <Panel label="radius + brand overridden" />
      </Theme>
    </div>
  ),
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    const scope = canvas.getByText('radius + brand overridden').closest('div[style]')
    await expect(scope).toHaveStyle({ '--radius': '1.5rem' })
  },
}

export const Nested: Story = {
  render: () => (
    <Theme appearance="dark" style={{ borderRadius: 'var(--radius-panel)', background: 'var(--color-surface)', padding: 'var(--space-4)' }}>
      <div className={docs.stackWide} style={{ gap: 'var(--space-4)' }}>
        <Panel label="dark page" />
        <Theme appearance="light" style={{ borderRadius: 'var(--radius-panel)', background: 'var(--color-surface)', padding: 'var(--space-4)' }}>
          <Panel label="light island inside it" />
        </Theme>
      </div>
    </Theme>
  ),
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    const island = canvas.getByText('light island inside it').closest('.light')
    await expect(island).toBeInTheDocument()
    const bg = (el: Element) => getComputedStyle(el as HTMLElement).getPropertyValue('--color-surface').trim()
    // Compared against :root rather than a literal, so the assertion is about
    // the nested scope resolving to the light default — not about how the
    // generator happens to spell oklch().
    await expect(bg(island!)).toBe(bg(document.documentElement))
    await expect(bg(island!)).not.toBe(bg(island!.parentElement!.closest('.dark')!))
  },
}

/**
 * An accent or gray set on a light island inside a dark page takes the
 * island's appearance, not the page's: the nearest scope wins at any depth.
 */
export const NestedPalettes: Story = {
  render: () => (
    <Theme appearance="dark" accentColor="orange" grayColor="slate" data-testid="dark" style={{ background: 'var(--color-surface)', padding: 'var(--space-4)' }}>
      <Theme appearance="light" style={{ background: 'var(--color-surface)', padding: 'var(--space-4)' }}>
        <Theme accentColor="orange" grayColor="slate" data-testid="island">
          <Panel label="orange on slate, light, inside dark" />
          <Theme appearance="dark" style={{ padding: 'var(--space-2)' }}>
            <Theme accentColor="orange" grayColor="slate" data-testid="deep">
              <Panel label="and dark again inside that" />
            </Theme>
          </Theme>
        </Theme>
        <Theme accentColor="orange" grayColor="slate" appearance="dark" data-testid="same-element">
          <Panel label="accent and appearance on one element" />
        </Theme>
      </Theme>
    </Theme>
  ),
  play: async ({ canvas }) => {
    const v = (el: Element, name: string) => getComputedStyle(el).getPropertyValue(name).trim()
    const dark = canvas.getByTestId('dark')
    const island = canvas.getByTestId('island')
    for (const name of ['--color-text-brand', '--color-background-brand-bold', '--color-border-focused', '--color-text', '--color-text-subtlest', '--color-border-bold']) {
      // Light inside dark: the light palette, not the page's dark one.
      await expect(v(island, name)).not.toBe(v(dark, name))
      // Dark again one level down, and on the same element: the dark palette.
      await expect(v(canvas.getByTestId('deep'), name)).toBe(v(dark, name))
      await expect(v(canvas.getByTestId('same-element'), name)).toBe(v(dark, name))
    }
  },
}

# Foundations Foundations are the decisions every component inherits: color, type, spacing...
import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as OverviewStories from './Overview.stories'

<Meta of={OverviewStories} />

# Foundations

Foundations are the decisions every component inherits: color, type,
spacing, radius, elevation, cursors, and the breakpoints layouts respond
to. They live in **one file** — `src/tokens.css` — as CSS custom
properties.

There is no JavaScript theme object and no `ThemeProvider` that owns
values. A token is a CSS variable, which means the platform already knows
how to scope it, cascade it, inherit it and override it. Everything on
this page follows from that.

`tokens.css` is itself generated — see [Where the values come
from](#where-the-values-come-from) — but nothing downstream of it is.
**You** consume a plain stylesheet with no build step of your own.

## The three layers

| Layer | Where | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Raw value | `:root` / `.dark` in `tokens.css` | `--color-background-brand-bold: oklch(51.1% 0.262 276.966)` |
| Derived value | the `*` block in `tokens.css` | `--radius-control: max(…)` |
| Usage | a component's `.module.css` | `background: var(--color-background-brand-bold)` |

Components only ever read the variable. That is what makes a rebrand a
change to one file, and what keeps theme conditionals out of component CSS
entirely — the value behind `var(--color-background-brand-bold)` changes, the rule does not.

The derived layer is on `*` rather than `:root` on purpose: a custom
property that reads another one resolves where it is *declared*, so
putting these at the root would freeze them there and a `Theme` further
down the tree could not move them.

## Where the values come from

`tokens.css` is not written by hand. The source is a set of JSON files in
the [W3C design-token format](https://tr.designtokens.org/format/), and a
generator turns them into the stylesheet, the `Theme` component's list of
palettes, the swatches on the **Color** page, and an export for design
tools — four artefacts that used to be four chances to disagree with each
other.

Two things follow from that, and both are visible on other pages here.

**Nothing semantic holds a literal.** In the source,
`color-background-brand-bold` is `{accent.solid}` and `color-text` is
`{gray.950}` — references, not colours. Swapping a ramp moves everything downstream of it in one edit,
which is what makes the 17 accents and 9 grays on this page a
three-line change rather than a rewrite.

**The contrast numbers are measured, not claimed.** For each of the 17
accents the generator converts the ramp through OKLCH → sRGB → relative
luminance, computes the contrast of each candidate step against a white
and a black label, and takes the first that clears 4.5:1. The focus ring
is a separate measurement against the page at 3:1. The lowest passing
accent in the current set sits at **4.56:1** — close enough to the floor
that guessing would have missed it.

Edit a ramp so that no step can carry a readable label and the build
stops with the hue named. The accessibility claims on the
[Color](?path=/docs/foundations-colors--docs) page are therefore checks,
not documentation.

## The pages

- **[Color](?path=/docs/foundations-colors--docs)** — semantic tokens, the
  contrast measurements, and where every value comes from.
- **[Dark mode](?path=/docs/foundations-dark-mode--docs)** — how the two
  modes are declared and switched.
- **[Typography](?path=/docs/foundations-typography--docs)** — the
  role-based type scale, and the system font stack behind it.
- **[Spacing](?path=/docs/foundations-spacing--docs)** — six roles,
  one value each.
- **[Breakpoints](?path=/docs/foundations-breakpoints--docs)** — the
  responsive range, and the kit's lack of opinion about it.
- **[Radius](?path=/docs/foundations-radius--docs)** — four steps off one
  base, and what happens at the extremes.
- **[Shadows](?path=/docs/foundations-shadows--docs)** — elevation, and why
  dark mode needs its own alphas.
- **[Focus](?path=/docs/foundations-focus--docs)** — one ring, two
  offsets, and when to draw it inside.
- **[Motion](?path=/docs/foundations-motion--docs)** — three transition
  durations, one spinner speed, and reduced motion in one place.
- **[Layering](?path=/docs/foundations-layering--docs)** — four layers,
  and why every overlay shares one.
- **[Cursors](?path=/docs/foundations-cursors--docs)** — two tokens and one
  contested convention.

## Theming

Overriding tokens globally is just CSS — redeclare them after Zweihänder's
stylesheet loads:

```css
:root {
  --radius: 1rem;
  --color-background-brand-bold: oklch(0.55 0.2 264);
}
```

For anything narrower than the whole document, use `Theme`. It is a thin
wrapper that applies an appearance class and writes token overrides as
inline custom properties on one element, so everything inside it resolves
against those values.

```tsx
import { Theme } from 'zweihander/theme'

<Theme accentColor="violet" grayColor="slate" appearance="dark" radius="full-rounded">
  <Button>Inside a violet, slate, dark, rounder scope</Button>
</Theme>
```

Four settings, each independent:

| Prop | Values |
| --- | --- |
| `accentColor` | 17 hues — drives the brand tokens (`--color-background-brand-bold`, `--color-text-brand`, `--color-icon-brand`) and `--color-border-focused` |
| `grayColor` | 9 neutral ramps — drives backgrounds, text, borders |
| `appearance` | `light`, `dark`, `inherit` |
| `radius` | `sharp`, `rounded`, `full-rounded` |

### Accent color

The brand hue. Seventeen, all of them measured: the solid step and the
label colour are chosen per hue so every accent clears 4.5:1 for its own
label, which is why the warm hues below carry dark labels and the cool
ones carry white. The focus ring uses a step darker than the fill, because
the lighter solids miss the 3:1 a focus indicator needs.

<Canvas of={OverviewStories.AccentColor} />

### Gray color

The neutral ramp behind surfaces, text, borders and neutral fills. The
differences are subtle and cumulative; they read most clearly in dark
mode, which is how they are shown here.

<Canvas of={OverviewStories.GrayColor} />

### Radius

Covered on its own page, including why `full` pills a button but not a
text field: **[Radius](?path=/docs/foundations-radius--docs)**.

### Appearance

`appearance` takes `light`, `dark`, or `inherit` (the default, which
leaves the surrounding mode alone).

<Canvas of={OverviewStories.Appearance} />

### Token overrides

`tokens` takes any custom property, with or without the `--` prefix. It is
not limited to tokens Zweihänder defines — the component writes whatever
you pass onto the element, so a token your own components read works the
same way.

<Canvas of={OverviewStories.TokenOverride} />

Overrides cascade, so a nested `Theme` inherits what it does not restate.
Because they are inline styles they also beat any stylesheet rule, which
is what makes a scoped override reliable — and what makes `Theme` the
wrong tool for setting global defaults. Use CSS for those.

### Nesting

Scopes nest in either direction: a dark panel on a light page, or a light
island inside a dark one.

<Canvas of={OverviewStories.Nested} />

The light island works because `tokens.css` declares the light values on
`:root, .light`, not on `:root` alone. `.dark` is declared afterwards at
equal specificity, so the nearer scope's class is what an element inside
it resolves against.

An `accentColor` or `grayColor` inside a nested scope follows the same
rule. Each appearance sets two switches, `--use-light` and `--use-dark`,
and the palette scopes pick their light or dark values through them, so
the nearest appearance wins at any depth, on the same element too.

<Canvas of={OverviewStories.NestedPalettes} />

**One caveat.** If your own CSS branches on theme with a descendant
selector (`.dark .thing { … }`), that selector still matches inside a
light island nested in a dark ancestor, and will style it as dark.
Zweihänder's own CSS never branches on theme, so it is unaffected. Read
the tokens instead of matching on `.dark` and the problem does not arise.

## Installing

Both distribution paths carry the same tokens. Copy-source drops the
component's own source into your repo and merges these values into your
stylesheet; the npm package ships them as `zweihander/tokens.css`, which
you import after your base stylesheet.

The exact commands for either are in the
[repo README](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander).

import { Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'

<Meta title="Getting Started/Introduction" />

# Zweihänder

A front-end UI kit for React, documented here in Storybook. Components are
plain elements styled with CSS Modules against a layer of CSS custom
properties. There is no CSS framework, no primitive library, and one
runtime dependency.

<div style={{
  border: '1px solid var(--color-background-danger-bold)',
  borderRadius: 'var(--radius-panel)',
  padding: 'var(--space-4)',
  margin: 'var(--space-6) 0',
}}>

**Early stage — not production-ready.** Two components exist (Button, Text
Input). No design review has happened beyond the contrast measurements in
these docs, and no Figma file has been applied, so the palettes are chosen
for contrast rather than designed. **Expect breaking changes on any `0.x`
version bump.**

Fine to read, install, or borrow the setup from. Not ready to build a real
product on top of yet.

</div>

## What it is

The whole kit resolves against one stylesheet of custom properties. A
component never holds a colour, a size or a radius — it reads a token:

```css
.button {
  background: var(--color-background-brand-bold);
  border-radius: var(--radius-control);
  font-size: var(--text-body);
}
```

Three consequences follow, and most of these docs are about them:

- **Theming is scoping.** `<Theme accentColor="violet" appearance="dark">`
  redeclares tokens on a subtree; everything inside re-resolves. No
  context, no re-render, no theme object.
- **Rebranding is one file.** Change what `--color-background-brand-bold` means and every rule
  reading it moves. No component is touched.
- **There is no build step on your side.** No config, no content scanning,
  no plugin. It is a stylesheet.

## How to read these docs

**[Foundations](?path=/docs/foundations-overview--docs)** is the substance —
colour, type, spacing, radius, elevation, cursors, and the reasoning and
measurements behind each. Start with its Overview.

**[Components](?path=/docs/components-overview--docs)** is what exists so
far, plus the full category list of what does not.

Each topic has a hand-written page rather than a generated blurb, and they
are written as reference docs — what a token is *for*, where its value came
from, what the known gotchas are, and how to override it.

## Next

**[Installation](?path=/docs/getting-started-installation--docs)** — two
ways to consume the kit, and which to pick.

# Installation

Two ways to consume the kit. They ship the same components and the same
tokens; the difference is who owns the source afterwards.

| | Copy-source | npm package |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Source lives in | your repo | `node_modules` |
| Editing a component | edit the file | fork or override |
| Upgrading | re-run the CLI, review the diff | bump the version |
| Best when | you expect to customise | you want to version-pin |

**Pick copy-source unless you have a reason not to.** The kit is `0.x` and
incomplete; owning the source means a breaking change is a diff you read
rather than one that arrives.

## Copy-source

Components are served in the [shadcn CLI][cli] registry format, so the CLI
copies the source into your project and rewrites its imports to match your
path alias.

[cli]: https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/cli

The project needs a `components.json` — run `npx shadcn@latest init` first
if it has none. Then:

Or register the kit once and add components by name:

```json
{ "registries": { "@zweihander": "https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/{name}.json" } }
```

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @zweihander/button
```

`tokens` only needs adding once — every component depends on it, so the CLI
pulls it in with the first component anyway. Shared helpers (`utils`,
`icon`) resolve the same way, and the npm dependencies (`clsx`, and
`@base-ui/react` for components with behaviour) are installed for you.

Import the token layer once, at your app's entry:

```css
@import "./styles/zweihander-tokens.css";
```

The CLI prints where each file landed; the path above is relative to the
`src` your `components.json` points at.

**If your bundler needs CSS-module types**, add them once — Vite projects
already get this from `vite/client`:

```ts
declare module '*.module.css' {
  const classes: Record<string, string>
  export default classes
}
```

```css
@import "zweihander/tokens.css";  /* the token layer */
@import "zweihander/styles.css";  /* the component styles */
```

**Order matters** — the component styles read the tokens, so `tokens.css`
has to come first. Beyond those two lines there is nothing to configure.

`react` and `react-dom` are peer dependencies. `clsx` is the only runtime
dependency and installs with the package.

## Verifying it works

Render a Button inside a `Theme` and change the accent. If the button
follows, the token layer is loaded and scoping works:

```tsx
<Theme accentColor="violet">
  <Button>Violet</Button>
</Theme>
```

If the button renders unstyled, `styles.css` is missing (npm path) or the
component's `.module.css` did not come across (copy-source). If it renders
styled but in a **serif** face, the token layer is missing — components
declare `font-family: var(--font-sans)` explicitly, and with no tokens
that resolves to nothing.

## Using the theme

Both paths ship the same `Theme` component, which scopes four independent
settings to any subtree:

```tsx
<Theme accentColor="violet" grayColor="slate" appearance="dark" radius="full-rounded">
```

It writes custom properties, so it nests in either direction — a dark panel
on a light page, or a light island inside a dark one. The full write-up,
including what each setting moves and how to override tokens directly, is
in **[Foundations → Overview](?path=/docs/foundations-overview--docs)**.

## Contributing to the kit itself

```bash
git clone https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander
npm install
npm run storybook
```

Tokens are generated from `tokens/*.json` — run `npm run tokens` after
editing them, never edit the generated files. `npm run tokens:check` and
`node scripts/check-registry.mjs` both run in CI. The
[README](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander) has the rest.

# Components

Single, reusable UI components (atomic design's "molecules"). Reference list: [uiguideline.com/components](https://www.uiguideline.com/components).

Each component lives in `src/components/<category>/`, with its story set to
`Components/<Category>/<Component>`. Categories below — add a component to the
one it fits, or propose a new category if none fit.

| Category | Components |
| --- | --- |
| **Atomic Elements** | Divider ✅, Badge ✅, Avatar ✅, Tag ✅, Kbd ✅ |
| **Buttons** | Button ✅, Toggle Button ✅, Button Group ✅ |
| **Controls** | Color Picker ✅, Rating ✅, Slider ✅, Switch ✅, Checkbox ✅, Radio ✅ |
| **Data Display** | Calendar ✅, Table ✅, Card ✅, Collapse ✅ |
| **Inputs** | Field ✅, Search ✅, Number Input ✅, Text Input ✅, Password Input ✅, Textarea ✅, File Uploader ✅, Date Picker ✅, Select ✅, Combobox ✅ |
| **Loaders** | Spinner ✅, Progress Bar ✅, Skeleton ✅ |
| **Navigation** | Breadcrumbs ✅, Pagination ✅, Link ✅, Tabs ✅, Stepper ✅, Menu ✅, Menubar ✅ |
| **Notifications** | Alert ✅, Toast ✅, Inline Alert ✅ |
| **Overlays** | Modal ✅, Tooltip ✅, Popover ✅ |
| **States** | Empty State ✅, Error State ✅, Success State ✅ |

Unchecked = not built yet.

## How a component page reads

Every component page has the same three tabs, after Material 3, so the
answer you need is always in the same place.

| Tab | Answers | What is on it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Overview** | What is it? | One-line description, the main example, a gallery of variants with when to use each, the status, and Resources: the import line, the registry command, the source. |
| **Specs** | How is it built? | Anatomy (the real component with numbered parts), Measurements for every size, Color for every variant, States side by side, and the API table with live controls. Where Zweihänder departs from the reference spec, "Differences from the spec" says how. |
| **Guidelines** | How do I use it well? | When to use it, when to reach for something else, Do and Don't pairs rendered from real stories, and Accessibility: keyboard, roles and states, each line checked by a test. |

Every value on Specs is read live from the tokens, so it follows the theme
in the toolbar and cannot drift from the code. `npm run docs:check` fails CI
when a component page is missing a tab or a required section.

## Behaviour comes from Base UI

Components are styled with CSS Modules over the token layer; their
*behaviour* — focus, keyboard, ARIA — comes from
[Base UI](https://base-ui.com) (`@base-ui/react`) wherever it is more than
trivial. Button uses its `Button` for the focusable-while-loading state;
Toggle Button, the form controls, the overlays, Select, Combobox, Tabs and
Menu are built on its parts.

The reason is the same one that kept this kit from hand-rolling them: a
Modal needs a focus trap, scroll locking, an inert background and correct
restore-focus; Select and Combobox need typeahead, virtual focus and a
listbox ARIA contract; Menu and Tabs need roving tabindex. Those are not
lines of code, they are years of accumulated edge cases in screen readers
and browsers. Base UI is unstyled, so it carries none of that into the
look — the tokens still decide everything you can see.

Two conventions follow from it:

- **`render` instead of `asChild`.** Any component that renders an element
  you might want to replace takes a `render` prop — an element or a
  function — the same as Base UI's own parts and shadcn's.
- **Base UI's change handlers.** Components built on it expose its names:
  `onPressedChange`, `onCheckedChange`, `onValueChange`, `onOpenChange`.
  Components that wrap a real `<input>` (Text Input, Textarea, Search)
  keep the native `onChange(event)`.

Components with no behaviour worth the name — Divider, Badge, Avatar,
Tag, Kbd — are plain elements and do not import it.

## Resources

`<DocTabs>` takes exactly three `<DocTab>` children: `overview`, `specs`,
`guidelines`, in that order. The selected tab is kept in the address bar as
`&docTab=specs`, so a link can open on it.

## Anatomy

`<Anatomy>` takes the real component as children and a list of parts, each
found by a CSS selector inside it. A selector that finds nothing is called
out in the key.

  parts={[

  ]}
>
  <Story of={ButtonStories.WithIcons} />
</Anatomy>

## States

`<States>` shows one example per state. Hover, focus and pressed are forced
by storybook-addon-pseudo-states; a state that needs other props, like
disabled, passes its own `content`.

    { label: 'Enabled' },
    { label: 'Hover', pseudo: 'hover' },
    { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' },
    { label: 'Pressed', pseudo: 'active' },
    { label: 'Disabled', content: <Story of={ButtonStories.Disabled} /> },
  ]}
>
  <Story of={ButtonStories.Default} />
</States>

## When to use

`<DoDont>` sets a right and a wrong example side by side. In a real page both
come from stories (`<Story of={…} />`), the Don't one tagged `!dev`.

## When not to use

These blocks are for component docs. Foundations stay single pages.

<DoDont
  do={<Button>Save</Button>}
  doCaption="One primary button: the thing to do next."
  dont={
    <div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 'var(--space-2)' }}>
      <Button>Save</Button>
      <Button>Publish</Button>
    </div>
  }
  dontCaption="Two primary buttons compete for the same click."
/>

## Accessibility

Each block's own behaviour is tested in `DocBlocks.stories.tsx`: the tabs by
mouse and arrow keys, the anatomy markers by name, the token values across
themes, the state labels, and the Do / Don't words.
